impression.label: Left breast, core biopsy, invasive carcinoma NST:
impression.text: Oestrogen receptor POSITIVE (90%, strong); progesterone receptor POSITIVE (40%, moderate); HER2 NEGATIVE, IHC score 1+ (HER2-low); Ki-67 15%.

comment.text: HER2 1+ falls in the HER2-low category, which is relevant for eligibility for HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate therapy in the metastatic setting. Repeat biomarker testing on the excision specimen is advised if the result is discordant with morphology or if tumour heterogeneity is suspected.
HER2 ISH: not indicated. Surrogate molecular subtype: Luminal A-like (ER+, PR 20% or more, HER2-negative, Ki-67 low). Guideline: ASCO/CAP ER/PR 2020; ASCO/CAP HER2 2023 update.

ihcPanels.name: Colonic Adenocarcinoma, Mismatch Repair Deficient (MLH1 PMS2 Loss), BRAF V600E Positive, Ascending Colon (Right Hemicolectomy)
results: Diffuse cytoplasmic staining; normal mucosa negative

controls.External control:: Tonsil and known MMR-proficient colon stained appropriately.
controls.Internal control:: Non-neoplastic cells were positive for all four MMR proteins, so the loss in tumour cells is interpretable.

impression.label: Ascending colon adenocarcinoma, MMR IHC:
impression.text: Loss of MLH1 and PMS2 with intact MSH2 and MSH6, consistent with MISMATCH REPAIR DEFICIENCY (dMMR). BRAF V600E mutation-specific IHC POSITIVE.

comment.text: Combined MLH1/PMS2 loss with BRAF V600E positivity strongly favours a sporadic tumour due to MLH1 promoter hypermethylation; Lynch syndrome is unlikely. MLH1 promoter methylation testing may be done for confirmation if clinically indicated. A dMMR/MSI-H status is relevant for prognosis and for immune checkpoint inhibitor eligibility.
Lynch syndrome likelihood: low; findings favour sporadic MLH1 promoter hypermethylation.

Hepatocellular markers negative (excludes hepatocellular carcinoma). Differentials less likely: upper GI/pancreatobiliary (usually CK7 positive), lung, breast.

Highlights scattered small reactive T cells
Membranous in more than 30% of tumour cells
Nuclear in about 70% of tumour cells

Excludes CD5+ DLBCL and mantle cell lymphoma; CD30 negative

impression.label: Left cervical lymph node, excision:
impression.text: DIFFUSE LARGE B-CELL LYMPHOMA, NOT OTHERWISE SPECIFIED, GERMINAL CENTRE B-CELL (GCB) SUBTYPE (Hans algorithm: CD10+, BCL6+, MUM1-); BCL2 positive, MYC 20%, Ki-67 about 80%.

comment.text: Cell-of-origin by IHC is a surrogate for gene-expression profiling. Because the tumour is GCB type, MYC/BCL2/BCL6 FISH is recommended (WHO 5th edition / ICC 2022) to exclude a high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements. Staging with PET-CT and bone marrow assessment as clinically indicated.
Hans algorithm: mature B-cell lineage (CD20+, PAX5+, CD3-); step 1 CD10 positive, so step 2 (BCL6) not required; MUM1 negative (supportive). Dual expressor: no. EBV (EBER ISH): negative.

results: No nuclear or cytoplasmic staining in tumour cells

impression.label: Retroperitoneal mass, core biopsy:
impression.text: MALIGNANT SPINDLE CELL NEOPLASM WITH SMOOTH MUSCLE DIFFERENTIATION (SMA+, desmin+, h-caldesmon+; S100-, CD34-, CD117-, DOG1-, CK-, MDM2-), CONSISTENT WITH LEIOMYOSARCOMA.

comment.text: Co-expression of three smooth muscle markers with negative S100/SOX10, CD34, CD117/DOG1, cytokeratin and MDM2 supports leiomyosarcoma over schwannoma/MPNST, solitary fibrous tumour, GIST, sarcomatoid carcinoma and dedifferentiated liposarcoma. Grading on a core biopsy may underestimate the grade; final FNCLCC grade and margins on the resection specimen. Referral to a sarcoma multidisciplinary team is advised.
FNCLCC grade (biopsy, provisional): grade 2 (differentiation 2, mitoses 2, necrosis 1; total 5). Final grading on resection specimen.

results: Diffuse, strong nuclear (about 80% of tumour cells)
No nuclear staining in tumour cells (basal cells of bronchial epithelium positive)

controls.Internal control:: Benign bronchial basal cells (p40, CK5/6) and entrapped type II pneumocytes (TTF-1, Napsin A).

impression.label: Right upper lobe, bronchoscopic biopsy:
impression.text: NON-SMALL CELL CARCINOMA, FAVOUR ADENOCARCINOMA (TTF-1 positive, Napsin A positive, p40 negative).

comment.text: In small biopsies with solid morphology, the IASLC/WHO terminology 'NSCC, favour adenocarcinoma' is used when TTF-1 is positive and p40 is negative. The definitive subtype (e.g. solid adenocarcinoma) is assigned on resection. Remaining tissue has been preserved; reflex biomarker testing (molecular panel and PD-L1) is recommended for treatment planning.
Tissue stewardship: minimal two-marker panel used; tissue preserved for molecular testing. Molecular / predictive testing advised: EGFR, ALK, ROS1, KRAS, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK (NGS) and PD-L1 (22C3).

impression.label: Right breast, upper outer quadrant, core needle biopsy:
impression.text: Invasive breast carcinoma, NST, Grade 1. ER POSITIVE (95%, strong); PR POSITIVE (80%, strong); HER2 NEGATIVE, IHC score 0; Ki-67 10%. Surrogate molecular subtype: Luminal A-like.

comment.text: Therapy implications: Endocrine therapy is the mainstay (aromatase inhibitor in a postmenopausal patient). Chemotherapy is generally not indicated; a genomic assay (e.g. Oncotype DX) may be considered if node-positive or other high-risk features. HER2 score 0: not HER2-low; assess for HER2-ultralow if T-DXd is clinically contemplated at metastatic stage.
Specimen: ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy (14G, 4 cores). St Gallen criteria met: ER+, PR high (20% or more), HER2-negative, Ki-67 low (below 20%).
Ki-67 cut-offs are laboratory-dependent; 20% used here as the St Gallen low/high threshold. Ki-67 counted globally, hot-spots excluded (IKWG).
Surrogate subtyping by IHC approximates gene-expression intrinsic subtypes; correlate clinically. ER/PR positive at 1% or more (1 to 10% = ER-low); HER2 scored per ASCO/CAP 2023.

cases.name: Malignant - Ductal Carcinoma NST, Yokohama Category 5
cases.path: Cytopathology/FNAC/Breast/Neoplastic/Malignant - Ductal Carcinoma NST, Yokohama Category 5.dotx

PROCEDURE DETAILS.1.0: Palpation-guided fine needle aspiration (23G needle, 3 passes); needle rinse for cell block.
PROCEDURE DETAILS.2.0: Right breast lump, upper outer quadrant.
PROCEDURE DETAILS.3.0: 6 (3 air-dried Giemsa, 3 alcohol-fixed Pap). Cell block prepared.

1.0.text: Adequacy: Adequate and representative (IAC Yokohama criteria).
Cellularity: Highly cellular smears.
Architecture: Numerous loosely cohesive, crowded, overlapping three-dimensional clusters, with many dispersed single intact malignant cells. Occasional cells within fibrofatty stromal fragments.

Cell morphology: Moderately to markedly pleomorphic ductal epithelial cells, 2 to 3 times the size of benign ductal cells, with high N:C ratio, irregular nuclear membranes, coarse hyperchromatic chromatin and prominent nucleoli. Moderate amount of cytoplasm. Mitotic figures seen.
Myoepithelial cells: Bipolar bare nuclei and myoepithelial cells are absent.
Background: Necrotic debris and blood. No apocrine metaplasia, foam cells, mucin or signet-ring cells.

1.0.label: Right breast lump, FNAC:
1.0.text: Malignant – carcinoma, consistent with ductal carcinoma (no special type). IAC Yokohama System (2020): Category 5 – Malignant (risk of malignancy about 99 to 100%).
Invasion cannot be assessed on cytology; differentiation from high-grade DCIS requires histology. Correlation with the clinical (triple assessment) and imaging (BI-RADS 5) findings is concordant.

Recommend ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy for histological type, Nottingham grade and ER, PR, HER2 and Ki-67 assessment, and FNA of the palpable right axillary node for staging. Cell block retained for ancillary testing if required.

cases.name: Benign Reactive Lymphoid Hyperplasia
cases.path: Cytopathology/FNAC/Lymph Node/Non-neoplastic/Benign Reactive Lymphoid Hyperplasia.dotx

PROCEDURE DETAILS.1.0: Fine needle aspiration (23G needle, 2 passes). Aspirate: blood-mixed, whitish material.

1.0.text: Adequacy: Adequate, cellular and representative.

Cellularity and pattern: Smears are cellular and show a polymorphous population of lymphoid cells dominated by small mature lymphocytes, with admixed centrocytes, centroblasts, immunoblasts and occasional plasma cells.
Background: Scattered tingible body macrophages and lymphohistiocytic aggregates (germinal centre fragments) are seen. Lymphoglandular bodies are present in the background.
Atypical cells: No granulomas, necrosis, Reed–Sternberg-like cells, monomorphic atypical lymphoid population or metastatic malignant cells are seen.

1.0.label: Right posterior cervical lymph node, FNAC:
1.0.text: Benign – reactive lymphoid hyperplasia. Sydney System (2020): Category II – Benign (approximate risk of malignancy low, <5%).
Polymorphous lymphoid population with tingible body macrophages; ancillary studies are not required.
Clinical correlation and follow-up. Re-aspiration or excision biopsy if the node persists beyond 4–6 weeks or enlarges.

cases.name: Metastatic Keratinising Squamous Cell Carcinoma
cases.path: Cytopathology/FNAC/Lymph Node/Neoplastic/Metastatic Keratinising Squamous Cell Carcinoma.dotx

PROCEDURE DETAILS.1.0: Fine needle aspiration (22G needle, 2 passes). Aspirate: greyish-white, partly necrotic material.
PROCEDURE DETAILS.2.0: Right level II cervical lymph node.

1.0.text: Adequacy: Adequate.

Tumour cells: Smears are cellular and show malignant squamous cells in sheets, clusters and singly. Cells show marked pleomorphism, including polygonal, tadpole and spindle forms, with hyperchromatic, irregular nuclei with coarse chromatin.

Keratinisation and background: Keratinised cells with dense orangeophilic cytoplasm on Pap stain, keratin pearls and anucleate squames are seen. The background shows necrosis, keratinous debris and an inflammatory infiltrate.
Lymphoid cells: Residual lymphoid cells are scanty.

1.0.label: Right level II cervical lymph node, FNAC:
1.0.text: Positive for malignancy – metastatic keratinising squamous cell carcinoma. Sydney System (2020): Category V – Malignant (approximate risk of malignancy high, >95%).
Probable primary: oral cavity (tongue), on clinical correlation. p16 / HPV testing is advised if an oropharyngeal primary is suspected.
Biopsy of the tongue lesion and staging work-up.

cases.name: Rosai-Dorfman Disease
cases.path: Cytopathology/FNAC/Lymph Node/Neoplastic/Rosai-Dorfman Disease.dotx

PROCEDURE DETAILS.1.0: Fine needle aspiration (non-guided, 23G needle, 2 passes); needle rinse for cell block. Aspirate: whitish-grey, blood-mixed material.
PROCEDURE DETAILS.3.0: 6 (3 MGG, 2 Pap, 1 H&E); cell block prepared.

1.0.text: Adequacy: Adequate and representative.

Cellularity and background: Highly cellular smears with a polymorphous population of small lymphocytes, many mature plasma cells, scattered neutrophils and occasional eosinophils. No necrosis, granulomas or caseation.

Histiocytes: Numerous large histiocytes, singly and in loose clusters, with abundant pale to foamy, finely vacuolated cytoplasm and round to oval vesicular nuclei with a small distinct nucleolus. Binucleate and occasional multinucleate forms are present.
Emperipolesis: Many histiocytes contain intact lymphocytes and plasma cells within the cytoplasm, several surrounded by a clear halo (emperipolesis), best seen on MGG.
Atypical cells: Occasional large binucleate cells are present. No convincing Reed–Sternberg cells with macronucleoli, no sheets of atypical lymphoid cells and no cohesive epithelial clusters.

Cell block immunohistochemistry: S100 positive (nuclear and cytoplasmic in large histiocytes, highlighting engulfed lymphocytes); CD68 / CD163 positive; OCT2 positive; CD1a / Langerin negative; CD30 / CD15 negative in large cells; PAX5 / CD20 / CD3 mixed B and T cells with no aberrant population; pan-CK (AE1/AE3) negative; IgG4+ cells < 10/HPF, IgG4/IgG ratio < 40%.

1.0.label: Left cervical lymph node, FNAC:
1.0.text: Histiocytic proliferation with emperipolesis, consistent with Rosai–Dorfman disease (sinus histiocytosis with massive lymphadenopathy). S100+, CD68+, OCT2+, CD1a−. Sydney system: Benign (category II), with recommendation for excision.

The cytomorphology and immunoprofile support Rosai–Dorfman disease. As RDD is uncommon at this age and RDD-like changes may coexist with lymphoma (including Hodgkin lymphoma) or other neoplasms, a coexisting process cannot be fully excluded on FNA.

Excision biopsy of the most accessible node (preferably an inguinal node) is recommended to confirm the diagnosis and exclude a coexisting lymphoma. Suggest CBC, ESR, serum immunoglobulins and imaging to assess extranodal involvement.

cases.name: Tuberculous Granulomatous Lymphadenitis
cases.path: Cytopathology/FNAC/Lymph Node/Non-neoplastic/Tuberculous Granulomatous Lymphadenitis.dotx

PROCEDURE DETAILS.1.0: Fine needle aspiration (23G needle, 2 passes). Aspirate: cheesy, creamy-white material; part sent for CBNAAT / GeneXpert.
PROCEDURE DETAILS.2.0: Left supraclavicular / lower cervical matted lymph nodes.

1.0.text: Adequacy: Adequate.
Granulomas: Smears show multiple epithelioid cell granulomas: cohesive clusters of epithelioid histiocytes with elongated, slipper-shaped nuclei and pale cytoplasm.

Giant cells and background: Occasional Langhans-type multinucleated giant cells are present. The background shows abundant amorphous, granular eosinophilic caseous necrosis with degenerated inflammatory cells and a mixed lymphoid population.
Atypical cells: No atypical or malignant cells are seen.
Special stain: Ziehl–Neelsen (AFB) positive: occasional acid-fast bacilli (AFB 1+).

1.0.label: Left cervical lymph node, FNAC:
1.0.text: Necrotising granulomatous lymphadenitis with acid-fast bacilli, consistent with tuberculous lymphadenitis. Sydney System (2020): Category II – Benign.
Epithelioid granulomas with caseous necrosis, AFB positive (ZN); CBNAAT sent.
Correlate with CBNAAT / culture and clinical findings; manage per national TB programme guidelines.

cases.name: Benign Follicular Nodule (Colloid - Adenomatoid Nodule), Bethesda II
cases.path: Cytopathology/FNAC/Thyroid/Non-neoplastic/Benign Follicular Nodule (Colloid - Adenomatoid Nodule), Bethesda II.dotx

PROCEDURE DETAILS.1.0: USG-guided fine needle aspiration, 3 passes. Three aspirates received; adequate thin colloid visible on the slides grossly.
PROCEDURE DETAILS.3.0: Multiple (air-dried MGG and wet-fixed Papanicolaou smears).

1.0.text: Adequacy: Adequate (sufficient follicular cells and colloid).
The smears are cellular and show abundant thin watery colloid in the background, with occasional dense colloid fragments.

Follicular epithelial cells are arranged predominantly in flat monolayered sheets with a honeycomb arrangement and occasional small macrofollicular fragments. Nuclei are round, evenly spaced, with fine chromatin and inconspicuous nucleoli. Cytoplasm is moderate and delicate.

No nuclear features of papillary thyroid carcinoma are seen (no nuclear grooves, intranuclear cytoplasmic inclusions, nuclear crowding or overlapping, or powdery chromatin). No Hürthle-cell-predominant population, no atypical cells and no features of malignancy are identified. Findings are consistent with a benign follicular nodule (colloid / adenomatoid nodule).

1.0.label: Thyroid FNAC (USG-guided), right lobe nodule:
1.0.text: Bethesda Category II – Benign (benign follicular nodule / colloid nodule). The Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytopathology: approximate risk of malignancy 0–3%.
Ancillary studies are not required.
Clinical and sonographic follow-up as per ATA / local protocol. No immediate surgery is indicated on cytology alone.

cases.name: Endometrial Cells in a Woman 45 Years of Age or Older
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/Endometrial Cells in a Woman 45 Years of Age or Older.dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate; estimated more than 5,000 well-visualised, well-preserved squamous cells (LBC threshold met).

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Clean.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Other cells: Benign squamous and endocervical cells. No dyskaryosis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: Endometrial cells: Several small, tight, three-dimensional balls of exfoliated endometrial cells with scant cytoplasm and small round nuclei (about the size of an intermediate-cell nucleus), dark chromatin, moulding and occasional apoptotic debris. Nuclear features: No nuclear enlargement or prominent nucleoli to suggest atypical endometrial cells.

5.0: Other: endometrial cells in a woman 45 years of age or older (negative for squamous intraepithelial lesion)
7.0: None. Endometrial cells: Present; benign-appearing, exfoliated; patient postmenopausal
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Other: Endometrial cells present in a woman 45 years of age or older. Negative for squamous intraepithelial lesion.

1.0.text: Benign-appearing endometrial cells in a postmenopausal woman, reported under the TBS 2014 "Other" category as they can rarely indicate endometrial hyperplasia or carcinoma; obesity adds to her risk.

Recommend endometrial assessment (transvaginal ultrasound and/or endometrial sampling) per ASCCP, as she is postmenopausal; not needed in asymptomatic premenopausal women. Pap cytology is a screening test with false-negative results.
HPV test: hrHPV negative (co-test).

cases.name: High-grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion (HSIL)
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Neoplastic/High-grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion (HSIL).dotx

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Mild inflammation; no tumour diathesis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Numerous small, immature squamous cells are present singly, in loose sheets and in hyperchromatic crowded groups. They have a markedly increased nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, with dense metaplastic or lacy immature cytoplasm. Nuclei are hyperchromatic with evenly distributed coarse granular chromatin, prominent irregularity of the nuclear membrane with notches and grooves, and inconspicuous nucleoli. Nuclear size is variable, but the cells themselves are smaller than those of LSIL. No features suggestive of invasion are seen, such as macronucleoli, tadpole or fibre cells, marked keratinisation or a necrotic background.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: Endocervical / transformation zone cells present. Glandular cells are unremarkable.

5.0: Epithelial cell abnormality: squamous
9.0: High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL), encompassing moderate and severe dysplasia / CIS / CIN 2 and CIN 3; features suspicious for invasion not identified

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Epithelial cell abnormality – high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) (TBS 2014).

1.0.text: Urgent colposcopy with directed biopsy, or expedited treatment by loop electrosurgical excision (LEEP), is advised as per ASCCP 2019 guidelines for HSIL with HPV 16 positivity in a non-pregnant patient aged 25 years or older.
HPV test: HPV 16 positive (sample data).

cases.name: Low-grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion (LSIL) with HPV Cytopathic Effect
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Neoplastic/Low-grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion (LSIL) with HPV Cytopathic Effect.dotx

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Clean, with a mixed population of superficial and intermediate squamous cells.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Scattered intermediate and superficial squamous cells show nuclear enlargement more than three times the area of a normal intermediate cell nucleus, with mild hyperchromasia, slightly irregular nuclear outlines and occasional binucleation. Koilocytes are present, with sharply outlined perinuclear cavitation, a dense peripheral rim of cytoplasm and atypical (enlarged, hyperchromatic, raisinoid) nuclei. A few dyskeratotic cells with orangeophilic cytoplasm are also seen. No cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio of the HSIL type are seen.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: Endocervical / transformation zone cells present. Glandular cells are unremarkable.

5.0: Epithelial cell abnormality: squamous
7.0: None
9.0: Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL), encompassing HPV cytopathic effect / mild dysplasia / CIN 1

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Epithelial cell abnormality – low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL) with HPV cytopathic effect (TBS 2014).

1.0.text: Colposcopy is recommended (ASCCP 2019 risk-based management: LSIL with positive HPV). Correlate with clinical findings.
HPV test: high-risk HPV positive, non-16/18 (sample data).

cases.name: NILM with Actinomyces (IUD User)
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Actinomyces (IUD User).dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate; estimated 8,000 to 12,000 well-visualised squamous cells (conventional smear threshold met).
SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.3.0: Present (endocervical cells and squamous metaplastic cells).

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Mild neutrophilic inflammation. No sulphur granules with club formation in tissue fragments, and no necrosis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Superficial and intermediate cells with mild reactive change. No dyskaryosis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: Benign sheets with mild reactive change. No atypia.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.4.0: Several dark-staining "cotton-ball" (woolly) colonies composed of tangled, thin filamentous bacteria that radiate from a dense centre, showing acute-angle branching at the periphery. Neutrophils cling to the edges of the colonies.

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
6.0: Bacteria morphologically consistent with Actinomyces spp.
7.0: Reactive cellular changes associated with inflammation (mild); IUD in situ
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
INTERPRETATION / RESULT.2.0: Organisms: Bacteria morphologically consistent with Actinomyces spp.

1.0.text: Actinomyces-like organisms in an IUD user. No intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

Correlate clinically. In an asymptomatic woman, IUD removal and antibiotics are not required (ACOG); counsel her to report pelvic pain, fever or discharge. If symptoms of pelvic infection develop, evaluate for pelvic actinomycosis, treat and consider IUD removal. Routine screening per current guidelines. Pap cytology is a screening test with false-negative results.
HPV test: Not done.

cases.name: NILM with Atrophy
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Atrophy.dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate for an atrophic smear (Bethesda allows clinical judgement; estimated about 5,000 squamous cells).

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Clean, without the granular debris, blue blobs or inflammation of atrophic vaginitis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Parabasal cells: Predominantly parabasal cells in flat, cohesive monolayer sheets and singly. Oval nuclei, uniform in size, with fine, evenly distributed chromatin, smooth nuclear membranes and no nucleoli. N:C ratio higher than intermediate cells but uniform across the sheet. Some naked (stripped) nuclei. Other squamous cells: Few intermediate cells; superficial cells rare (atrophic maturation pattern).
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: Small benign sheets.

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
7.0: Non-neoplastic cellular variation: atrophy
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

1.0.text: Atrophic smear, physiological after the menopause. Parabasal cells show uniform nuclei with even chromatin and smooth membranes, with no features of HSIL. No diagnostic doubt.

No further action needed. If a future atrophic smear shows equivocal atypia, a short course of topical vaginal oestrogen and a repeat smear helps resolve it. Screening can stop at 65 after adequate negative prior screening per current guidelines. Pap cytology is a screening test with false-negative results.
HPV test: hrHPV negative (co-test).

cases.name: NILM with Atrophy with Inflammation (Atrophic Vaginitis)
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Atrophy with Inflammation (Atrophic Vaginitis).dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate for an atrophic smear (estimated about 5,000 squamous cells).
SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.3.0: Absent / insufficient (common in atrophy); not a reason for unsatisfactory reporting.
SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.4.0: Inflammation and granular debris obscure about 40% of cells; does not limit interpretation.

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Degenerative changes: "Blue blobs" (dark, degenerated parabasal cells or bare nuclei without discernible detail) and pseudoparakeratosis (degenerated parabasal cells with dense orangeophilic cytoplasm and pyknotic nuclei). Granular basophilic debris with many neutrophils and histiocytes, including multinucleated forms ("pseudodiathesis"). No malignant cells within the debris.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Parabasal cells: Sheets and single parabasal cells with uniform oval nuclei, even chromatin and smooth membranes. Other cells: Few intermediate cells. No dyskaryosis.

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
7.0: Atrophy with inflammation (atrophic vaginitis)
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

1.0.text: Atrophic vaginitis. The granular background, blue blobs and pseudoparakeratosis can mimic tumour diathesis or keratinising carcinoma, but there are no atypical cells.

Topical vaginal oestrogen should relieve symptoms. Repeat cytology after a short course only if there is diagnostic doubt. Blood-stained discharge after the menopause needs evaluation in its own right; her thin endometrium is reassuring, but persistent bleeding warrants endometrial sampling. Pap cytology is a screening test with false-negative results.
HPV test: hrHPV negative (reflex).

cases.name: NILM with Cellular Changes Consistent with Cytomegalovirus
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Cellular Changes Consistent with Cytomegalovirus.dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate; estimated more than 5,000 well-visualised, well-preserved squamous cells (LBC threshold met).
SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.3.0: Present (endocervical cells and squamous metaplastic cells).

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Mild lymphocytic and neutrophilic inflammation.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Unremarkable superficial and intermediate cells. No dyskaryosis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.4.0: Viral cytopathic effect: Scattered, markedly enlarged endocervical (glandular) cells (cytomegaly), each with a single large, dark basophilic intranuclear inclusion separated from the nuclear membrane by a clear halo ("owl's eye" appearance). Cytoplasm: Several infected cells contain multiple small, granular, basophilic to amphophilic cytoplasmic inclusions. Distinction from HSV: Infected cells are mainly single and mononucleate. No multinucleation or nuclear moulding.

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
7.0: Reactive cellular changes associated with inflammation (mild)
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
INTERPRETATION / RESULT.2.0: Organisms: Cellular changes consistent with cytomegalovirus.

1.0.text: Cytomegalovirus cytopathic effect in endocervical cells in an immunosuppressed woman. No intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

Suggest clinical correlation and liaison with the transplant team (CMV PCR/viral load if systemic infection is suspected). Screening should follow guidance for immunosuppressed women (more frequent intervals, as for women with HIV). Pap cytology is a screening test with false-negative results.
HPV test: hrHPV negative (co-test).

cases.name: NILM with Cellular Changes Consistent with Herpes Simplex Virus
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Cellular Changes Consistent with Herpes Simplex Virus.dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate; estimated more than 5,000 well-visualised, well-preserved squamous cells (LBC threshold met).
SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.4.0: Moderate inflammation and some necrotic debris, obscuring less than 50%; does not limit interpretation.

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Neutrophils, fibrin and degenerated cells from ulceration. No tumour diathesis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Other cells: Uninfected squamous and endocervical cells are unremarkable. No dyskaryosis or koilocytes.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.4.0: Viral cytopathic effect: Enlarged multinucleated squamous and metaplastic cells showing the "3 Ms": multinucleation, nuclear moulding and margination of chromatin against the nuclear membrane. Nuclear features: Many nuclei have a homogeneous, glassy "ground-glass" appearance. Others show dense eosinophilic intranuclear Cowdry type A inclusions surrounded by a clear halo (later-stage infection).

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
6.0: Cellular changes consistent with herpes simplex virus
7.0: Reactive cellular changes associated with inflammation
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
INTERPRETATION / RESULT.2.0: Organisms: Cellular changes consistent with herpes simplex virus.

1.0.text: Viral cytopathic changes typical of herpes simplex virus. These multinucleated cells are not dyskaryotic and must not be mistaken for HSIL. No intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

Suggest clinical correlation, confirmation by HSV PCR from a lesion if needed, antiviral therapy and screening for other sexually transmitted infections. In pregnancy, inform the obstetrician because of the risk of neonatal transmission. Routine screening per current guidelines. Pap cytology is a screening test with false-negative results.
HPV test: Not done (under 25 years).

cases.name: NILM with Fungal Organisms Consistent with Candida
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Fungal Organisms Consistent with Candida.dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate; estimated 8,000 to 12,000 well-visualised squamous cells (conventional smear threshold met).
SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.3.0: Present (endocervical cells and squamous metaplastic cells).
SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.4.0: Mild inflammation; less than 25% of cells obscured.

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Mild neutrophilic exudate. Lactobacilli reduced. No tumour diathesis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Superficial and intermediate cells, some with small perinuclear halos and mild reactive nuclear enlargement.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: Benign sheets. No atypia.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.4.0: Eosinophilic to grey-brown, segmented pseudohyphae with constrictions and budding yeast forms (3 to 7 micrometres). Pseudohyphae skewer stacked squamous cells ("shish-kebab" / spearing arrangement).

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
6.0: Fungal organisms morphologically consistent with Candida spp.
7.0: Reactive cellular changes associated with inflammation (mild)
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
INTERPRETATION / RESULT.2.0: Organisms: Fungal organisms morphologically consistent with Candida spp.

1.0.text: Candida spp. with mild reactive change. Speciation is not possible on cytology (pseudohyphae favour C. albicans).

Treat if symptomatic (asymptomatic colonisation does not need treatment); review glycaemic control. Routine screening per current guidelines. Pap cytology is a screening test with false-negative results.
HPV test: Not done.

cases.name: NILM with Glandular Cells Status Post Hysterectomy
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Glandular Cells Status Post Hysterectomy.dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate for a vault sample (lower thresholds acceptable after hysterectomy).

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Clean. No tumour diathesis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Intermediate and parabasal cells with mild atrophic pattern. No dyskaryosis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: Glandular cells: A few small, flat to slightly crowded groups of benign columnar glandular cells with basal, round to oval nuclei, fine chromatin, smooth membranes and inconspicuous nucleoli. Some have mucinous cytoplasm. No crowding, stratification, mitoses or feathering.

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
7.0: Benign-appearing glandular cells status post hysterectomy
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

1.0.text: Benign glandular cells in a vault smear after total hysterectomy. Possible origins include vaginal adenosis, glandular (mucinous) metaplasia from chronic irritation or radiation, prolapse of the fallopian tube into the vault, or a fistula. They carry no known increased risk of neoplasia. Confirm the hysterectomy was total, since endocervical cells would be expected after a supracervical one.

No follow-up for this finding. After total hysterectomy for benign disease with no history of CIN 2+ or cervical cancer, further cervical/vaginal screening is generally not recommended (ACS, USPSTF, ACOG).
HPV test: Not done.

cases.name: NILM with Keratotic Changes (Hyperkeratosis and Parakeratosis)
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Keratotic Changes (Hyperkeratosis and Parakeratosis).dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate; estimated more than 8,000 squamous cells (keratinised cells counted).
SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.3.0: Not identified (no endocervical or metaplastic cells); this does not make the sample unsatisfactory.

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Few neutrophils. No tumour diathesis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Hyperkeratosis: Many anucleate, mature polygonal squames with orangeophilic cytoplasm, some with a pale "ghost" nuclear space; occasional keratohyaline granules. Parakeratosis: Small, mature-looking squamous cells singly and in plaques, with dense orangeophilic cytoplasm and small, round, dark pyknotic nuclei. Nuclei are uniform, without enlargement, irregularity or hyperchromasia (no atypical parakeratosis). Other squamous cells: Superficial, intermediate and few parabasal cells. No dyskaryosis or tadpole/fibre cells.

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
7.0: Non-neoplastic cellular variation: keratotic changes (hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis)
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

1.0.text: Benign keratotic changes from chronic exposure and friction of the prolapsed cervix. No atypical parakeratosis or intraepithelial lesion.

Keratosis can mask an underlying lesion: biopsy any non-healing ulcer or visible abnormality, and examine the hysterectomy specimen. Consider hrHPV testing, as she was never screened. Pap cytology is a screening test with false-negative results.
HPV test: Not done.

cases.name: NILM with Lymphocytic (Follicular) Cervicitis
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Lymphocytic (Follicular) Cervicitis.dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate; estimated 8,000 to 12,000 well-visualised squamous cells (conventional smear threshold met).
SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.4.0: None significant; lymphoid cells form streaks but do not obscure epithelial cells.

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Lymphoid cells: Dense streaks and clusters of a polymorphous lymphoid population: predominantly small mature lymphocytes, with larger follicle-centre cells (centroblasts), occasional immunoblasts and plasma cells. Lymphoid cells are dispersed, not cohesive. Tingible-body macrophages: Scattered macrophages containing phagocytosed nuclear debris, confirming a reactive follicle.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Mixed parabasal, intermediate and superficial cells. No dyskaryosis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: Benign sheets.

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
7.0: Reactive cellular changes associated with lymphocytic (follicular) cervicitis
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
INTERPRETATION / RESULT.2.0: Reactive cellular changes associated with lymphocytic (follicular) cervicitis.

1.0.text: Lymphocytic (follicular) cervicitis. The small dark lymphoid cells can mimic HSIL, endometrial cells or lymphoma; the polymorphous population, lack of cohesion and tingible-body macrophages identify it as reactive.

Often linked to chronic Chlamydia trachomatis infection in younger women and common after the menopause. Consider chlamydia NAAT if risk factors or symptoms are present. Routine screening per current guidelines. Pap cytology is a screening test with false-negative results.
HPV test: hrHPV negative (co-test).

cases.name: NILM with Pregnancy-associated Changes (Decidual Cells, Arias-Stella Reaction)
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Pregnancy-associated Changes (Decidual Cells, Arias-Stella Reaction).dotx

PROCEDURE DETAILS.2.0: Cervix (broom device; no endocervical brush, as pregnant).

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate; estimated more than 5,000 well-visualised, well-preserved squamous cells (LBC threshold met).

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Decidual cells: Scattered large polygonal cells with abundant, finely granular to vacuolated, cyanophilic to amphophilic cytoplasm and large central vesicular nuclei with a single prominent nucleolus. N:C ratio low; chromatin fine, membranes smooth.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Navicular cells: Many boat-shaped, glycogenated intermediate cells with yellow cytoplasmic glycogen and folded borders (pregnancy-related maturation).
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: Arias-Stella reaction: A few endocervical cells with abundant clear to vacuolated cytoplasm and enlarged, hyperchromatic nuclei, some with intranuclear pseudoinclusions. They lie in small groups with low N:C ratio and no mitoses. Other cells: Normal endocervical sheets. No trophoblast seen. No dyskaryosis.

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
7.0: Non-neoplastic cellular variation: pregnancy-associated changes (decidual cells, Arias-Stella reaction)
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
INTERPRETATION / RESULT.2.0: Pregnancy-associated changes (decidual cells and Arias-Stella reaction).

1.0.text: Benign pregnancy-associated changes. Decidual cells can mimic HSIL or degenerating carcinoma, and Arias-Stella cells can mimic AGC or clear cell adenocarcinoma; the abundant cytoplasm, low N:C ratio and pregnancy context support benignity.
No intervention needed. Cytology is safe in pregnancy. Resume routine screening postpartum per current guidelines. Pap cytology is a screening test with false-negative results.
HPV test: Not done.

cases.name: NILM with Reactive Cellular Changes Associated with IUD
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Reactive Cellular Changes Associated with IUD.dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate; estimated more than 5,000 well-visualised, well-preserved squamous cells (LBC threshold met).

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Other findings: A few calcified psammoma-like concretions (debris). Mild neutrophilic inflammation. No Actinomyces-like organisms.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Unremarkable. No dyskaryosis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: Glandular clusters: Small three-dimensional clusters of 5 to 15 glandular cells with abundant cytoplasm containing large vacuoles, some displacing the nucleus into a signet-ring-like shape. Nuclei are mildly enlarged with fine chromatin and occasional prominent nucleoli. Single cells: Occasional isolated small cells with a high N:C ratio and scant cytoplasm, resembling HSIL cells, but with smooth nuclear membranes and fine chromatin and too few in number.

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
7.0: Reactive cellular changes associated with intrauterine contraceptive device (IUD)
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
INTERPRETATION / RESULT.2.0: Reactive cellular changes associated with intrauterine contraceptive device (IUD).

1.0.text: IUD-associated reactive change. Vacuolated glandular clusters can mimic adenocarcinoma, and single high-N:C cells can mimic HSIL; the IUD history and bland nuclear chromatin support a reactive process.

No action needed for the IUD. If there is diagnostic doubt in future, repeat cytology after IUD removal or replacement clarifies it. Routine screening per current guidelines. Pap cytology is a screening test with false-negative results.
HPV test: Not done.

cases.name: NILM with Reactive Cellular Changes Associated with Radiation
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Reactive Cellular Changes Associated with Radiation.dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate; more than 5,000 well-visualised squamous cells.
SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.3.0: Not identified (expected after radiotherapy); not required for adequacy.

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Few histiocytes and neutrophils. No tumour diathesis and no dyskaryotic cells with a raised N:C ratio.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Markedly enlarged squamous cells (cytomegaly) with proportionate enlargement of nucleus and cytoplasm, so the N:C ratio is preserved. Bizarre cell shapes are occasionally seen. Nuclear features: Bi- and multinucleation, fine or smudgy chromatin, smooth membranes, small nucleoli and some nuclear vacuolation. No coarse hyperchromasia. Cytoplasm: Two-tone polychromatic staining (cyanophilic and eosinophilic in the same cell) and cytoplasmic vacuolation, sometimes with engulfed neutrophils.

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
7.0: Reactive cellular changes associated with radiation
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
INTERPRETATION / RESULT.2.0: Reactive cellular changes associated with radiation.

1.0.text: Chronic radiation changes. The cells are large but the N:C ratio is preserved, with no hyperchromasia, single atypical cells or diathesis to suggest recurrent carcinoma or post-radiation dysplasia.
Continue oncology surveillance per protocol; cytology has limited sensitivity after radiation, and any new lesion needs biopsy. Pap cytology is a screening test with false-negative results.
HPV test: Not done.

cases.name: NILM with Reactive Cellular Changes, Typical Repair
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Reactive Cellular Changes, Typical Repair.dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate; estimated 8,000 to 12,000 well-visualised squamous cells (conventional smear threshold met).
SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.4.0: Mild inflammation and blood; less than 25% obscured.

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Mild acute inflammation and some fresh blood. Squamous cells mildly reactive.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: Repair sheets: Flat, cohesive, monolayer sheets of metaplastic and endocervical cells with well-defined borders. Cells are aligned in a streaming, "school-of-fish" pattern, with preserved nuclear polarity. Nuclear features: Enlarged round to oval nuclei with fine, evenly distributed pale chromatin, smooth membranes and one or more prominent nucleoli. Occasional normal mitoses. Neutrophils are scattered within the sheets. Absent worrying features: No single atypical cells, no nuclear overlapping or hyperchromasia, no irregular chromatin clearing, and no tumour diathesis.

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
7.0: Reactive cellular changes associated with inflammation, including typical repair
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
INTERPRETATION / RESULT.2.0: Reactive cellular changes associated with inflammation (includes typical repair).

1.0.text: Typical repair following cryocautery. Prominent nucleoli and mitoses can mimic invasive carcinoma, but the cohesive monolayer sheets, streaming, even chromatin and lack of single atypical cells and diathesis are diagnostic of repair. Atypical repair (marked pleomorphism, irregular chromatin, single cells) would be reported as ASC or AGC.
No further action; routine screening per current guidelines. Pap cytology is a screening test with false-negative results.
HPV test: Not done.

cases.name: NILM with Reactive Inflammatory Changes
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Reactive Inflammatory Changes.dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate.
SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.3.0: Endocervical and squamous metaplastic cells present.
SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.4.0: Moderate inflammation, partly obscuring (less than 50%); does not limit interpretation.

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Moderate acute inflammatory exudate, predominantly neutrophils, with neutrophils clustering on squamous cells ("polka-dot" pattern). No tumour diathesis or necrosis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Superficial, intermediate and occasional parabasal cells, some with mild nuclear enlargement (less than 1.5 times normal), smooth nuclear membranes, fine chromatin, small nucleoli and perinuclear halos, consistent with reactive change. No hyperchromasia or koilocytosis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: Sheets of endocervical cells with mild reactive nuclear enlargement and prominent nucleoli, maintaining a honeycomb arrangement. No crowding, stratification or feathering.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.4.0: Shift in flora with mixed coccobacilli and reduced lactobacilli; no clue cells. Candida, Trichomonas, Actinomyces and herpes changes not seen.

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
6.0: Shift in flora (not suggestive of bacterial vaginosis)
7.0: Reactive cellular changes associated with inflammation
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM).
INTERPRETATION / RESULT.2.0: Reactive cellular changes associated with inflammation (moderate, acute).

1.0.text: Moderate acute inflammation with reactive squamous and endocervical changes, possibly related to the intrauterine device or non-specific infection. No intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

Suggest clinical correlation, evaluation for an infective cause and treatment as indicated, then routine age-appropriate screening (cytology and/or HPV testing). Pap smear is a screening test with inherent false-negative rates.

cases.name: NILM with Shift in Flora Suggestive of Bacterial Vaginosis
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Shift in Flora Suggestive of Bacterial Vaginosis.dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate; estimated more than 5,000 well-visualised, well-preserved squamous cells (LBC threshold met).

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Inflammation: Sparse neutrophils, in keeping with bacterial vaginosis (not an inflammatory vaginitis).
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Superficial and intermediate cells with normal nuclear features. No koilocytes or dyskaryosis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: Benign sheets. No atypia.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.4.0: Filmy background of small coccobacilli. Numerous "clue cells": squamous cells carpeted by coccobacilli that blur the cell borders and overlie the nucleus. Lactobacilli are scanty to absent.

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
6.0: Shift in flora suggestive of bacterial vaginosis
7.0: None
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
INTERPRETATION / RESULT.2.0: Organisms: Shift in flora suggestive of bacterial vaginosis.

1.0.text: Clue cells and coccobacillary flora with loss of lactobacilli, suggestive of bacterial vaginosis. No intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

Cytology is suggestive only; correlate with clinical criteria (Amsel) or Gram stain (Nugent score). Treat if symptomatic (metronidazole or clindamycin per current CDC guidance); partner treatment is not routinely required. Routine screening per current guidelines. Pap cytology is a screening test with false-negative results.
HPV test: Not done.

cases.name: NILM with Squamous Metaplasia
cases.path: Cytopathology/PAP Smear/Female Genital Tract/Non-neoplastic/NILM with Squamous Metaplasia.dotx

SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.2.0: Adequate; estimated more than 5,000 well-visualised, well-preserved squamous cells (LBC threshold met).
SPECIMEN ADEQUACY.3.0: Present (abundant squamous metaplastic and endocervical cells).

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Clean. No organisms.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Immature metaplastic cells: Round to polygonal cells in loose cobblestone sheets and singly, with dense, cyanophilic cytoplasm and occasional cytoplasmic processes ("spider cells"). Central round nuclei with fine, evenly distributed chromatin, smooth nuclear membranes and inconspicuous nucleoli. N:C ratio moderate and uniform. Mature metaplastic cells: Cells approaching intermediate-cell size with more abundant cytoplasm and small regular nuclei.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: Squamous and endocervical cells: Normal squamous cells and benign endocervical sheets.

5.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
7.0: Non-neoplastic cellular variation: squamous metaplasia
9.0: None (no ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL or squamous cell carcinoma)

INTERPRETATION / RESULT.1.0: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

1.0.text: Squamous metaplasia, a normal physiological finding in the transformation zone, which also confirms that the zone was sampled. Metaplastic cells show no hyperchromasia or nuclear membrane irregularity to suggest ASC-H or HSIL.
Routine screening per current guidelines (e.g. primary hrHPV every 5 years or cytology every 3 years). Pap cytology is a screening test with false-negative results.

cases.name: Acute Myeloid Leukaemia
cases.path: Hematology/Bone Marrow Aspiration/Neoplastic/Acute Myeloid Leukaemia.dotx

PERIPHERAL BLOOD FINDINGS.6.0: Peripheral blood blasts 62%. Coagulation: PT, aPTT and fibrinogen within normal limits.

ASPIRATION DETAILS.1.0: Bone marrow aspiration (Leishman stain with myeloperoxidase cytochemistry); trephine biopsy reported separately.

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Adequate, particulate and markedly hypercellular.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Markedly hypercellular (particle cellularity about 90%).
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.5.0: Markedly suppressed; maturing forms 8%. Occasional hypogranular neutrophils.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.9.0: Blasts: sheets of myeloblasts make up 74% of all nucleated cells. They are medium to large, with a high nuclear-cytoplasmic ratio, fine nuclear chromatin, 1 - 3 prominent nucleoli and a scant to moderate rim of basophilic cytoplasm with occasional fine azurophilic granules. Auer rods are seen in some blasts. No faggot cells, and abnormal hypergranular promyelocytes are not seen.

1.0.text: Myeloperoxidase (MPO) cytochemistry: positive in over 3% of blasts (about 70%), confirming myeloid lineage.
Iron stores: adequate.

IMPRESSION.1.0: Markedly hypercellular marrow with 74% MPO-positive myeloblasts showing Auer rods, consistent with acute myeloid leukaemia. Final classification awaits immunophenotyping and genetic studies.

1.0.text: Lineage (provisional) myeloid; dysplasia in residual cells minimal (hypogranular neutrophils, micromegakaryocytes); APL features not seen (no hypergranular promyelocytes or faggot cells; coagulation normal). Provisional category: acute myeloid leukaemia, pending genetic classification (WHO 5th edition, 2022 / ICC 2022).
Advise urgent flow cytometry (expected CD34, CD117, CD13, CD33, HLA-DR and MPO positive; to exclude mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia).

Advise karyotype and FISH/RT-PCR for PML::RARA, RUNX1::RUNX1T1, CBFB::MYH11 and KMT2A rearrangements, and a molecular panel including NPM1, FLT3-ITD/TKD, CEBPA, TP53 and myelodysplasia-related genes (ASXL1, RUNX1 and others) for WHO/ICC classification and ELN 2022 risk.
Although APL features are absent, if PML::RARA is detected or coagulopathy develops, start ATRA immediately. Correlate with trephine biopsy. Urgent haematology referral is recommended.

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Markedly hypercellular (particle cellularity about 95%).

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.5.0: Markedly suppressed (5%); maturation normal in residual cells.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.9.0: Blasts: monotonous sheets of lymphoblasts make up 88% of all nucleated cells. They are small to medium sized (1.5 - 2 times a small lymphocyte), with a high nuclear-cytoplasmic ratio, scant agranular basophilic cytoplasm, finely dispersed to slightly condensed chromatin and inconspicuous to small nucleoli. Occasional cytoplasmic vacuoles. Auer rods are not seen.

5.0: 1 (metamyelocytes and band forms)

Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS): coarse granular to block positivity in a proportion of blasts.
Iron stores: adequate.

Flow cytometry (blast gate): CD19, CD22 and cytoplasmic CD79a positive; CD10 positive (bright); CD34 and TdT positive; CD20 partial dim positivity; surface immunoglobulin light chains negative; MPO, CD13, CD33 and CD117 negative; cytoplasmic CD3 and CD7 negative.

IMPRESSION.1.0: B-lymphoblastic leukaemia (precursor B-ALL, common-B phenotype); marrow blasts 88%.

1.0.text: Blast morphology: lymphoblasts (L1-type), no Auer rods; MPO negative, PAS block positivity. Lineage (flow cytometry): B-lymphoblastic, common-B (CD10 positive) phenotype. Residual haematopoiesis markedly suppressed. Genetics pending (karyotype and FISH/RT-PCR panel). Classification: B-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma, NOS (WHO 5th ed., pending genetics).

Final WHO/ICC subtype depends on genetics. Suggest karyotype with FISH or RT-PCR for ETV6::RUNX1, BCR::ABL1, KMT2A rearrangement, TCF3::PBX1 and iAMP21, plus DNA index or ploidy for high hyperdiploidy and hypodiploidy.

Keep a diagnostic immunophenotype on record for measurable residual disease (MRD) monitoring at the end of induction.

PERIPHERAL BLOOD FINDINGS.6.0: Marked leucocytosis with the full spectrum of granulocytic maturation, with peaks at myelocytes and segmented neutrophils (bimodal). Absolute basophilia and eosinophilia. Normocytic normochromic red cells; platelets increased. Differential: blasts 1%, promyelocytes 2%, myelocytes 14%, metamyelocytes 10%, band forms and neutrophils 52%, eosinophils 5%, basophils 6%, monocytes 3%, lymphocytes 7%.

ASPIRATION DETAILS.1.0: Bone marrow aspiration (trephine biopsy reported separately).

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Adequate, particulate and markedly hypercellular.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Markedly hypercellular (particle cellularity about 95%), with near-complete loss of fat spaces.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: About 13 : 1.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.5.0: Markedly increased, with orderly maturation and a predominance of myelocytes and mature forms. Blasts 2%. No significant dysplasia. Eosinophils and basophils increased.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.6.0: Increased, many small and hypolobated (dwarf megakaryocytes).
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.9.0: Occasional pseudo-Gaucher cells and sea-blue histiocytes. No parasites seen.

IMPRESSION.1.0: Markedly hypercellular marrow with granulocytic hyperplasia, basophilia, eosinophilia and dwarf megakaryocytes. Features are consistent with chronic myeloid leukaemia, BCR::ABL1-positive, in chronic phase (blasts under 10%; WHO 5th edition, 2022), subject to genetic confirmation.

1.0.text: Advise karyotype for t(9;22)(q34;q11.2) and additional chromosomal abnormalities, and FISH or RT-PCR for BCR::ABL1 with transcript type (e.g., e13a2 / e14a2).
Advise baseline quantitative BCR::ABL1 (IS) RT-qPCR for monitoring response to tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy.
Correlate with the trephine biopsy for fibrosis (reticulin) and blast distribution, and calculate the Sokal / ELTS risk score.
Clinical correlation is advised.

cases.name: Megaloblastic Erythroid Hyperplasia (Vitamin B12 Deficiency)
cases.path: Hematology/Bone Marrow Aspiration/Non-neoplastic/Megaloblastic Erythroid Hyperplasia (Vitamin B12 Deficiency).dotx

PERIPHERAL BLOOD FINDINGS.6.0: Oval macrocytes, tear drop cells, hypersegmented neutrophils. Reticulocyte count 0.6% (0.5 - 2.5%). Supportive tests: serum vitamin B12 85 pg/mL (low); folate normal; LDH 3,100 U/L.

ASPIRATION DETAILS.1.0: Bone marrow aspiration (Leishman and Perls' Prussian blue stains).

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Adequate, particulate and cellular.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Normocellular for age (particle cellularity about 50%).
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.3.0: Reversed, about 0.6 : 1.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.4.0: Hyperplastic with megaloblastic maturation. Erythroid precursors are enlarged and show nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony, with fine, open, sieve-like nuclear chromatin persisting into haemoglobinised (polychromatic and orthochromatic) stages. Occasional binucleate forms, nuclear budding and Howell-Jolly bodies are seen.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.5.0: Relatively reduced but maturing. Giant metamyelocytes and band forms are prominent. Hypersegmented neutrophils present. Blasts 1%.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.6.0: Adequate in number; occasional large hyperlobated forms.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.9.0: No blasts in excess, no ring sideroblasts, no metastatic or other abnormal cells.

5.0: 9 (including giant forms)

1.0.text: Perls' Prussian blue (iron stain): Storage iron increased (grade 4+). Ring sideroblasts not seen.

IMPRESSION.1.0: Normocellular marrow with megaloblastic erythroid hyperplasia, giant metamyelocytes and increased iron stores, consistent with megaloblastic anaemia. With the low serum B12, the picture fits vitamin B12 deficiency. No excess blasts or features of myelodysplastic neoplasm.

1.0.text: Megaloblastic change can mimic dysplasia and, in severe cases, an erythroid leukaemia; MDS should not be diagnosed until B12 and folate deficiency has been corrected.
Advise anti-intrinsic factor and anti-parietal cell antibodies to look for pernicious anaemia. Start B12 replacement promptly because of neurological symptoms, and avoid folate alone.
Expect a reticulocyte response in 5 - 7 days. Repeat marrow examination only if the counts do not recover.
