PERIPHERAL BLOOD FINDINGS.6.0: Normocytic normochromic red cells; normal leucocyte differential and morphology; adequate platelets. No immature or abnormal cells.

ASPIRATION DETAILS.1.0: Bone marrow aspiration under local anaesthesia (trephine biopsy reported separately).

MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.1.0: Adequate, particulate and cellular; spicules present.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.2.0: Normocellular for age (particle cellularity about 50%).
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.4.0: Normoblastic, with orderly maturation; no dyserythropoiesis.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.5.0: Normal, with orderly maturation to segmented neutrophils; blasts not increased.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.6.0: Adequate in number (2-3 per low-power field) with normal morphology and platelet budding.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS.9.0: No metastatic deposits, granulomas, storage cells or haemoparasites seen.

1.0.text: Perls' Prussian blue (iron stain): Storage iron present (grade 2+, normal). Sideroblasts present; no ring sideroblasts.

IMPRESSION.1.0: Normocellular marrow with normal trilineage haematopoiesis. No evidence of a haematological neoplasm or metastatic infiltration in the material examined.

1.0.text: Correlate with the trephine biopsy, which is better for detecting focal infiltrates and metastases.

cases.name: Chronic Myeloid Leukaemia, Chronic Phase
cases.path: Hematology/Bone Marrow Biopsy/Neoplastic/Chronic Myeloid Leukaemia, Chronic Phase.dotx

containers.text: Received 1 linear, grey-brown core of tissue labelled right posterior superior iliac spine, measuring 2.0 cm in length and 0.2 cm in diameter. The core is firm (bony); formalin-fixed and EDTA-decalcified.

1.0.sections: A1: entire core submitted after decalcification.

MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.1.0: Adequate; about 1.8 cm of evaluable marrow.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.2.0: Markedly hypercellular (about 95%), with near-complete loss of fat spaces.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.3.0: Reduced; residual small erythroid islands with normoblastic maturation.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.4.0: Markedly increased, with widening of the paratrabecular cuff of immature granulocytes (5-10 cells thick, normal 2-3) and orderly maturation to mature forms. Eosinophils are increased. Blasts not increased, with no clusters or sheets.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.5.0: Increased, small and hypolobated (dwarf megakaryocytes), scattered and in loose clusters.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.7.0: Scattered pseudo-Gaucher histiocytes. Normal bony trabeculae.

1.0.text: Reticulin: Mild increase in loose reticulin with focal intersections (MF-1).
Masson trichrome: No collagen fibrosis.
CD34: Blasts about 3% of cellularity, scattered singly; no clusters or sheets.
TdT: Negative (no lymphoblastic population).
MPO: Strongly positive granulocytic series.
CD61: Increased dwarf megakaryocytes.

1.0.label: Bone marrow trephine biopsy:
1.0.text: Markedly hypercellular marrow with granulocytic hyperplasia, dwarf megakaryocytes and mild reticulin fibrosis (MF-1), with no increase in blasts. Features are consistent with chronic myeloid leukaemia, BCR::ABL1-positive, in chronic phase (WHO 5th edition, 2022), subject to genetic confirmation.

Correlate with the aspirate, karyotype for t(9;22)(q34;q11.2) and BCR::ABL1 RT-PCR (transcript type and baseline IS level). Watch for MF-2/3 fibrosis, blast clusters or TdT-positive lymphoblasts on follow-up biopsies. Clinical correlation is advised.

cases.name: Metastatic Adenocarcinoma, Prostatic Origin (Bone Marrow Trephine)
cases.path: Hematology/Bone Marrow Biopsy/Neoplastic/Metastatic Adenocarcinoma, Prostatic Origin (Bone Marrow Trephine).dotx

containers.text: Received a single grey-white, firm core of bone measuring 1.8 x 0.2 cm, formalin-fixed and EDTA-decalcified.

MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.1.0: Adequate; about 1.6 cm of evaluable marrow space.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.2.0: About 70% of the marrow space is replaced by infiltrating tumour. Tumour cells: cohesive clusters, cords and small cribriform and microacinar glands of epithelial cells with moderate amphophilic to clear cytoplasm, round to oval nuclei with vesicular chromatin and prominent central nucleoli. Scattered mitoses. No haematopoietic origin features.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.3.0: Residual only, in small foci at the edge of the core; normoblastic, with normal maturation.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.4.0: Residual only, in small foci at the edge of the core; normal maturation.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.5.0: Present within the small foci of residual trilineage haematopoiesis.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.7.0: Tumour set in a desmoplastic stroma. Bony trabeculae are thickened and irregular, with new woven bone formation and prominent osteoblastic rimming (osteosclerotic reaction). No granulomas.

1.0.text: Reticulin: markedly increased, dense around tumour (MF-3 in involved areas).
Masson trichrome: collagen fibrosis in desmoplastic areas.
Pan-cytokeratin (AE1/AE3): strongly positive in tumour cells.
PSA: diffusely positive.
NKX3.1: diffuse nuclear positivity.
CK7 / CK20: negative / negative.
TTF-1, GATA3, CDX2: negative.
CD45 (LCA): negative in tumour; positive in residual haematopoietic cells.

1.0.label: Bone marrow trephine biopsy:
1.0.text: Metastatic adenocarcinoma with osteosclerotic reaction and marrow fibrosis; immunoprofile (PSA and NKX3.1 positive, CK7 and CK20 negative) is consistent with prostatic origin.

Synoptic summary: core 1.8 cm, adequate; marrow involvement present (about 70% of marrow space), diffuse and nodular pattern with desmoplasia; metastatic adenocarcinoma; osteosclerotic (osteoblastic) bone reaction; reticulin fibrosis MF-3 in involved areas; residual haematopoiesis focal, trilineage, normoblastic; favoured primary: prostate.
The leucoerythroblastic blood picture and dry tap are explained by marrow replacement and fibrosis.
Correlate with serum PSA, digital rectal examination and prostate imaging or biopsy for primary confirmation and grading. Gleason grading is not applied to metastatic deposits in marrow.
Bone scan or PSMA PET for staging is suggested, as clinically indicated.

cases.name: Normal Bone Marrow
cases.path: Hematology/Bone Marrow Biopsy/Non-neoplastic/Normal Bone Marrow.dotx

containers.text: Received a single grey-brown cylindrical core of bone measuring 1.8 cm in length and 0.2 cm in diameter, fixed in formalin and decalcified (EDTA).

1.0.sections: Entire specimen submitted in one cassette (A1).

MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.1.0: Adequate; about 1.6 cm of evaluable marrow with 12 intertrabecular spaces. No significant crush or decalcification artefact.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.3.0: Normal erythroid islands with orderly normoblastic maturation.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.4.0: Normal; paratrabecular precursors with orderly maturation towards the intertrabecular areas. No abnormally localised immature precursors (ALIP).
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.5.0: Adequate in number (2-3 per high-power field), evenly scattered, with normal size and nuclear lobation. No clustering.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.6.0: Scattered interstitial lymphocytes and plasma cells; no lymphoid aggregates or atypical infiltrates.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.7.0: Normal bony trabeculae; no osteosclerosis. No granulomas, necrosis, amyloid or metastatic deposits.

1.0.text: Reticulin: Fine scattered linear reticulin, MF-0 (European consensus grading)
Perls' iron: Storage iron present (normal)
CD34: Blasts under 2% of cellularity, scattered singly; no clusters
CD61: Megakaryocytes normal in number, morphology and distribution
Pan-cytokeratin: Negative; no metastatic carcinoma

1.0.label: Bone marrow trephine biopsy:
1.0.text: Normocellular marrow with normal trilineage haematopoiesis. No evidence of lymphoma, haematological neoplasm or metastatic malignancy. No fibrosis (MF-0).
Correlate with the paired aspirate findings. Clinical correlation is advised.

cases.name: Plasma Cell Myeloma, Kappa-restricted (Bone Marrow Trephine)
cases.path: Hematology/Bone Marrow Biopsy/Neoplastic/Plasma Cell Myeloma, Kappa-restricted (Bone Marrow Trephine).dotx

containers.text: Received a single grey-brown core of bone measuring 2.2 x 0.2 cm, formalin-fixed and EDTA-decalcified.

MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.1.0: Adequate; about 2.0 cm of evaluable marrow.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.6.0: Interstitial infiltrate with confluent nodules and sheets of plasma cells, replacing about 60% of cellularity. Cells are mature to intermediate, with eccentric nuclei, clock-face chromatin and perinuclear hof; occasional binucleate and plasmablastic forms with prominent nucleoli. No Dutcher or Russell body excess.
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION.7.0: Focal osteoclastic resorption of trabeculae. No amyloid-like deposits. No granulomas or metastatic deposits.

1.0.text: CD138: positive; plasma cells about 60% of marrow cellularity.
Kappa / lambda (ISH or IHC): kappa restricted (kappa : lambda over 20 : 1).
CD56: aberrant positivity in plasma cells.
CD19 / CD20: negative / negative.
Cyclin D1: negative.
Ki-67: about 10% in plasma cells.
Reticulin: mild increase, MF-1.
Congo red: negative for amyloid.

1.0.label: Bone marrow trephine biopsy:
1.0.text: Plasma cell myeloma: kappa-restricted clonal plasma cells about 60% of marrow cellularity, with an interstitial, nodular and diffuse pattern; fulfils IMWG criteria in the stated clinical context.

Synoptic summary: core 2.2 cm, adequate; cellularity about 70% (hypercellular for age); plasma cells (CD138) about 60% of cellularity; interstitial, nodular and diffuse (sheets) pattern; kappa light chain restricted; aberrant phenotype CD56 positive, CD19 negative; plasmablastic morphology occasional, not predominant; reticulin MF-1; amyloid not identified (Congo red negative). Myeloma-defining events (clinical): anaemia, hypercalcaemia, renal impairment, lytic bone lesions.
Correlate with the aspirate plasma cell count, serum free light chain ratio, beta-2 microglobulin, albumin and LDH for R-ISS staging.
Suggest FISH on CD138-selected cells for t(4;14), t(14;16), del(17p) and 1q gain or amplification for risk stratification.
Whole-body low-dose CT or PET-CT is suggested to map bone disease.

cases.name: Acute Leukaemia, Morphology Favouring AML
cases.path: Hematology/PS Comment/Neoplastic/Acute Leukaemia, Morphology Favouring AML.dotx

1.0.text: Haemoglobin 7.4 g/dL (reference 13.0 - 17.0 g/dL); MCV 90 fL (83 - 101 fL).
Normocytic normochromic red cells with mild anisocytosis. Occasional nucleated red cells (2 per 100 WBC).
Total leucocyte count 68,000 /cu mm (reference 4,000 - 10,000 /cu mm).

Differential leucocyte count (200 cells): blasts 62% (0%), promyelocytes 1%, myelocytes 2%, metamyelocytes 1%, neutrophils 12% (40 - 80%), lymphocytes 18% (20 - 40%), monocytes 3% (2 - 10%), eosinophils 1% (1 - 6%).

Marked leucocytosis with 62% blasts. Blasts are medium to large (2-3 times a small lymphocyte), with a high nuclear-cytoplasmic ratio, fine open chromatin, 1-3 prominent nucleoli and a moderate amount of agranular to finely granular basophilic cytoplasm. Occasional blasts show Auer rods. No faggot cells. Residual neutrophils show hypogranularity. Leukaemic hiatus is seen.
Platelet count 22,000 /cu mm (reference 1,50,000 - 4,10,000 /cu mm).
Severely reduced on smear; no clumps.
Not seen.

1.0.label: Peripheral smear:
1.0.text: Acute leukaemia, morphology favours acute myeloid leukaemia (blasts 62% with Auer rods), with anaemia and severe thrombocytopenia.
Urgent flow cytometry on peripheral blood (CD34, CD117, HLA-DR, MPO, CD13, CD33, CD64, CD14, CD19, cCD79a, CD3, cCD3, TdT) to confirm lineage.
Urgent coagulation screen (PT, APTT, fibrinogen, D-dimer) to exclude DIC; acute promyelocytic leukaemia must be actively excluded.

Bone marrow aspirate and trephine with MPO cytochemistry, karyotype, FISH and a molecular panel (NPM1, FLT3, CEBPA, RUNX1, TP53 and others) for WHO 5th edition / ICC classification and risk stratification.
Kindly correlate clinically and inform the treating clinician urgently.

cases.name: Anaemia of Chronic Disease
cases.path: Hematology/PS Comment/Non-neoplastic/Anaemia of Chronic Disease.dotx

1.0.text: Haemoglobin 9.8 g/dL (reference 12.0 - 15.0 g/dL); RBC count 3.6 x 10^6 /cu mm (3.8 - 4.8 x 10^6 /cu mm); PCV 30.2% (36 - 46%); MCV 84 fL (83 - 101 fL); MCH 27.2 pg (27 - 32 pg); MCHC 32.4 g/dL (31.5 - 34.5 g/dL); RDW-CV 13.8% (11.6 - 14.0%); reticulocyte count 0.6% (0.5 - 2.5%), an inappropriately low response.
Predominantly normocytic normochromic red cells with a minor population of mildly hypochromic cells. Mild rouleaux formation. No significant poikilocytosis, no fragments, no nucleated red cells.

Supportive studies: serum ferritin 310 ng/mL (reference 15 - 150 ng/mL; raised as an acute phase reactant); serum iron / TIBC 38 µg/dL / 220 µg/dL; transferrin saturation 17%; soluble transferrin receptor normal.
Total leucocyte count 8,900 /cu mm (reference 4,000 - 10,000 /cu mm).
Differential leucocyte count (100 cells): neutrophils 70% (40 - 80%), lymphocytes 22% (20 - 40%), monocytes 6% (2 - 10%), eosinophils 2% (1 - 6%), basophils 0% (0 - 2%).
Normal count; mild neutrophilia within range. No toxic changes or immature cells.
Platelet count 4.3 x 10^5 /cu mm (reference 1.5 - 4.1 x 10^5 /cu mm).
Mildly increased; normal morphology.
Not seen.

1.0.label: Peripheral smear:
1.0.text: Normocytic normochromic anaemia with rouleaux and reactive thrombocytosis, consistent with anaemia of chronic disease in the setting of rheumatoid arthritis.
Correlate with disease activity. Check renal function to exclude a contribution from chronic kidney disease.
If coexisting iron deficiency is suspected (ferritin under 100 ng/mL in inflammation), consider the soluble transferrin receptor / ferritin index. Treatment is directed at the underlying disease.

cases.name: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukaemia - Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma (CLL-SLL)
cases.path: Hematology/PS Comment/Neoplastic/Chronic Lymphocytic Leukaemia - Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma (CLL-SLL).dotx

1.0.text: Haemoglobin 12.8 g/dL (reference 13.0 - 17.0 g/dL); RBC count 4.3 x 10^6 /cu mm (4.5 - 5.5 x 10^6 /cu mm); PCV 38.6% (40 - 50%); MCV 90 fL (83 - 101 fL); MCH 29.8 pg (27 - 32 pg); MCHC 33.2 g/dL (31.5 - 34.5 g/dL); reticulocyte count 1.2% (0.5 - 2.5%).
Predominantly normocytic normochromic red cells. No spherocytes, no polychromasia, no red cell agglutination (no smear evidence of autoimmune haemolysis).
Total leucocyte count 42,600 /cu mm (reference 4,000 - 10,000 /cu mm); absolute lymphocyte count 35,800 /cu mm (1,000 - 3,000 /cu mm).

Differential leucocyte count (100 cells): neutrophils 14% (40 - 80%), lymphocytes (small mature) 82% (20 - 40%), prolymphocytes 2% (0%), monocytes 2% (2 - 10%), eosinophils 0% (1 - 6%), basophils 0% (0 - 2%).

Marked absolute lymphocytosis. The lymphocytes are small and mature-looking, slightly larger than red cells, with scanty cytoplasm, round nuclei and coarse, clumped (block-like, 'soccer ball') chromatin without visible nucleoli. Numerous smudge (basket) cells are seen. Prolymphocytes about 2% of lymphocytes (under 15%). Neutrophils show normal morphology.
Suggested Rai stage I / Binet A on clinical and smear data (to be confirmed clinically). Most likely category: mature B-cell neoplasm, morphology consistent with CLL.
Platelet count 1.9 x 10^5 /cu mm (reference 1.5 - 4.1 x 10^5 /cu mm).
Adequate in number; normal morphology.
Not seen.

1.0.label: Peripheral smear:
1.0.text: Absolute lymphocytosis of small mature lymphocytes with numerous smudge cells, morphologically consistent with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia / small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL), subject to flow cytometric confirmation.

Advise peripheral blood flow cytometry. The typical CLL immunophenotype is CD5+, CD19+, CD20 dim, CD23+, CD200+, with dim surface immunoglobulin light-chain restriction, and FMC7 and CD79b negative or weak (Matutes score 4 - 5). A sustained clonal B-cell count of at least 5 x 10^9/L is needed for a diagnosis of CLL.
If CD5+ and CD23 negative, exclude mantle cell lymphoma with cyclin D1 / SOX11 or t(11;14) FISH.
Before treatment, advise FISH for del(17p), del(11q), trisomy 12 and del(13q), TP53 mutation and IGHV mutational status. Direct antiglobulin test is advised if haemoglobin falls.

cases.name: Iron Deficiency Anaemia
cases.path: Hematology/PS Comment/Non-neoplastic/Iron Deficiency Anaemia.dotx

1.0.text: Haemoglobin 8.4 g/dL (reference 12.0 - 15.0 g/dL); RBC count 3.9 x 10^6 /cu mm (3.8 - 4.8 x 10^6 /cu mm); PCV 27.5% (36 - 46%); MCV 68 fL (83 - 101 fL); MCH 21.5 pg (27 - 32 pg); MCHC 30.5 g/dL (31.5 - 34.5 g/dL); RDW-CV 19.8% (11.6 - 14.0%); reticulocyte count 0.8% (0.5 - 2.5%).
Microcytic hypochromic red cells with marked anisopoikilocytosis. Pencil cells (elliptocytes), occasional target cells and tear drop cells. No basophilic stippling. No nucleated red cells.

Supportive iron studies: serum ferritin 6 ng/mL (reference 15 - 150 ng/mL); serum iron / TIBC 28 µg/dL / 465 µg/dL; transferrin saturation 6%. Mentzer index 17.4 (above 13, favours iron deficiency over thalassaemia trait).
Total leucocyte count 6,800 /cu mm (reference 4,000 - 10,000 /cu mm).
Differential leucocyte count (100 cells): neutrophils 62% (40 - 80%), lymphocytes 30% (20 - 40%), monocytes 5% (2 - 10%), eosinophils 3% (1 - 6%), basophils 0% (0 - 2%).
Normal in number and morphology. No immature cells.
Platelet count 4.6 x 10^5 /cu mm (reference 1.5 - 4.1 x 10^5 /cu mm).
Mildly increased (reactive thrombocytosis); normal morphology.
Not seen.

1.0.label: Peripheral smear:
1.0.text: Microcytic hypochromic anaemia with reactive thrombocytosis, consistent with iron deficiency anaemia.
Findings fit chronic blood loss from menorrhagia. Advise gynaecological evaluation and stool occult blood testing if indicated.
If ferritin is normal, consider haemoglobin electrophoresis (HPLC) to exclude beta thalassaemia trait. Repeat haemogram and reticulocyte count 2 - 4 weeks after starting iron therapy.

cases.name: Megaloblastic Anaemia (Vitamin B12 Deficiency)
cases.path: Hematology/PS Comment/Non-neoplastic/Megaloblastic Anaemia (Vitamin B12 Deficiency).dotx

1.0.text: Haemoglobin 7.6 g/dL (reference 13.0 - 17.0 g/dL); RBC count 2.1 x 10^6 /cu mm (4.5 - 5.5 x 10^6 /cu mm); PCV 24.0% (40 - 50%); MCV 114 fL (83 - 101 fL); MCH 36.2 pg (27 - 32 pg); MCHC 31.7 g/dL (31.5 - 34.5 g/dL); RDW-CV 21.5% (11.6 - 14.0%); reticulocyte count 0.7% (0.5 - 2.5%).

Marked anisopoikilocytosis with oval macrocytes, tear drop cells and occasional schistocytes. Howell-Jolly bodies and basophilic stippling seen. Occasional nucleated red cell with megaloblastic nuclear chromatin.
Supportive studies: serum vitamin B12 98 pg/mL (reference 200 - 900 pg/mL); serum folate 8.2 ng/mL (normal); LDH 2,850 U/L and indirect bilirubin 1.9 mg/dL (ineffective erythropoiesis).
Total leucocyte count 3,200 /cu mm (reference 4,000 - 10,000 /cu mm).
Differential leucocyte count (100 cells): neutrophils 56% (40 - 80%), lymphocytes 38% (20 - 40%), monocytes 4% (2 - 10%), eosinophils 2% (1 - 6%), basophils 0% (0 - 2%).
Leucopenia. Hypersegmented neutrophils present (over 5% with 5 lobes; occasional 6-lobed forms). No blasts.
Platelet count 0.95 x 10^5 /cu mm (reference 1.5 - 4.1 x 10^5 /cu mm).
Reduced; occasional large forms.
Not seen.

1.0.label: Peripheral smear:
1.0.text: Macrocytic anaemia with pancytopenia, oval macrocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils, suggestive of megaloblastic anaemia, consistent with vitamin B12 deficiency.
Dietary deficiency is likely; advise anti-intrinsic factor antibody testing to exclude pernicious anaemia. Neurological symptoms warrant prompt B12 replacement; do not give folate alone.
Expect a reticulocyte response in 5 - 7 days of treatment. Bone marrow examination is needed only if cytopenias fail to respond, to exclude MDS.

cases.name: Neutrophilic Leukaemoid Reaction
cases.path: Hematology/PS Comment/Non-neoplastic/Neutrophilic Leukaemoid Reaction.dotx

1.0.text: Haemoglobin 11.2 g/dL (reference 13.0 - 17.0 g/dL); MCV 86 fL (83 - 101 fL).
Normocytic normochromic red cells with mild anisocytosis. No nucleated red cells.
Total leucocyte count 62,000 /cu mm (reference 4,000 - 10,000 /cu mm).

Differential leucocyte count (200 cells): blasts 0%, promyelocytes 1%, myelocytes 6%, metamyelocytes 8%, band forms 18% (0 - 5%), neutrophils 58% (40 - 80%), lymphocytes 6% (20 - 40%), monocytes 3% (2 - 10%), eosinophils 0% (1 - 6%), basophils 0% (0 - 2%).

Marked neutrophilic leucocytosis with a left shift to myelocytes and promyelocytes (myelocytes fewer than metamyelocytes; no myelocyte bulge). Neutrophils show coarse toxic granulation, Döhle bodies and cytoplasmic vacuolation. No blasts. No basophilia or eosinophilia. No dysplasia.

Leukaemoid reaction versus CML: toxic granulation and Döhle bodies present (usually absent in CML); basophilia / eosinophilia absent (present in CML); metamyelocytes and band forms predominate, with no myelocyte bulge; no blasts; no splenomegaly; NAP score expected high (low in CML); BCR::ABL1 not expected (positive in CML).
Platelet count 4.2 x 10^5 /cu mm (reference 1.5 - 4.1 x 10^5 /cu mm).
Mildly increased (reactive), with normal morphology.
Not seen.

1.0.label: Peripheral smear:
1.0.text: Neutrophilic leukaemoid reaction with left shift and toxic changes, consistent with severe bacterial infection (pneumonia / sepsis). No evidence of leukaemia on the smear.
Correlate with blood culture, CRP / procalcitonin and the clinical course; the count is expected to settle with treatment of the infection.

Advise NAP score and repeat haemogram after treatment. If leucocytosis persists, or basophilia, splenomegaly or blasts appear, test for BCR::ABL1 to exclude CML, and consider CSF3R testing for chronic neutrophilic leukaemia.

cases.name: Normal Peripheral Blood Picture
cases.path: Hematology/PS Comment/Non-neoplastic/Normal Peripheral Blood Picture.dotx

1.0.text: No significant anisopoikilocytosis noted. Normocytic normochromic RBCs seen.
No increase in polychromatic cells or NRBCs seen.

Total leucocyte count and differential counts are within normal range. Normal segmentation and granulation noted within neutrophils, and lymphocytes appear normal in morphology. No atypical cells identified.
Adequate in smear, with normal morphology.
No platelet clumps seen.
Not identified.

1.0.label: Peripheral blood smear:
1.0.text: Normal peripheral blood picture.
Kindly correlate clinically.

diagnoses.name: Rheumatoid Synovitis, High-grade (Synovectomy)
diagnoses.path: Bone and Soft Tissue/Synovium/01 Inflammatory and Degenerative Arthritides

micro.text: Sections show high-grade chronic villous synovitis:
Lining: Synovial lining hyperplasia, up to 6–8 cell layers, with scattered multinucleated synoviocytes. Focal ulceration with surface fibrin.
Stroma: Markedly increased stromal cellularity with activated fibroblasts, oedema and many thick- and thin-walled new vessels. A rim of inflamed granulation tissue (pannus-like) is present in A10.

Infiltrate: Dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate forming band-like areas and many lymphoid follicles, several with germinal centres. Plasma cells are numerous, with Russell bodies. Neutrophils are scattered, mostly in the surface fibrin.
Rice bodies: Laminated eosinophilic fibrin with occasional entrapped cells. They are acellular centrally.

Negative findings: No granulomas, caseous necrosis or rheumatoid nodule. No crystals on polarisation. Polarisation also shows no steroid crystals or foreign material. No haemosiderin-laden sheets or giant cell tumour. No malignancy.
Special Stains / Immunohistochemistry:
Gram: No organisms
Ziehl–Neelsen: No acid-fast bacilli
PAS-D: No fungi; fibrin positive
CD20: Many B cells in follicles
CD68: Many lining and sublining macrophages
CD138: Numerous plasma cells (about 30%)
Polarised light: No crystals or foreign material

finalDiagnosis.label: Synovium, right knee, synovectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: High-grade chronic villous synovitis with lymphoid follicles, plasma cells, fibrin and rice bodies (Krenn synovitis score 9/9). Lympho-myeloid pathotype. Consistent with rheumatoid arthritis in this clinical setting.
No granulomas, crystals, organisms or neoplasm.

comment.text: The synovitis is high grade, with many lymphoid follicles and plasma cells. This fits the clinical diagnosis of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis. The histology is not specific on its own: psoriatic and other spondyloarthritis, Lyme and reactive arthritis can look similar. Correlate with clinical and serological findings.

Rice bodies occur in RA, but also in tuberculosis and atypical mycobacterial infection. ZN was negative and no granulomas were found. Please correlate with the mycobacterial culture and PCR on the fresh sample sent by the surgeon.
The lympho-myeloid pathotype has been linked to a response to B-cell-directed therapy (R4RA / PEAC studies). This information is optional and for clinical correlation.

containers.text: Received fresh, then fixed in formalin: multiple pieces of tan-red, villous and frond-like synovium, together 9.5 x 7.0 x 2.0 cm, weighing 42 g. Many villi are thickened and oedematous. Some surfaces are covered by yellow fibrinous material. Seven free, white, glistening, ovoid rice-like bodies, 2–5 mm, are present. No brown discolouration, chalky deposits, cartilage nodules or solid mass. A portion was sent fresh to microbiology by the surgeon.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A8 representative villous synovium, including fibrin-covered areas; A9 rice bodies; A10 deeper capsular tissue. Additional sections: 2 deeper levels on A2 and A5.

diagnoses.name: Osteoarthritis with Detritic Low-grade Synovitis
diagnoses.path: Bone and Soft Tissue/Synovium/01 Inflammatory and Degenerative Arthritides

micro.text: Sections show low-grade detritic synovitis:
Lining: Mild lining hyperplasia (2–3 layers).
Stroma: Mildly increased cellularity with fibrosis and focal oedema.
Infiltrate: Sparse perivascular lymphocytes.
Detritus: Multiple small fragments of hyaline cartilage and bone (detritus) embedded in the subsynovium, surrounded by foreign-body giant cells and fibrosis.
Negative findings: No crystals on polarisation (no urate, CPPD or steroid crystals). No haemosiderin sheets. No granulomas of infectious type. No neutrophilic infiltrate. No malignancy.

finalDiagnosis.label: Synovium, right knee, total knee arthroplasty:
finalDiagnosis.text: Low-grade chronic synovitis (Krenn synovitis score 3/9) with detritic synovitis (bone and cartilage detritus with foreign-body giant cell reaction), consistent with osteoarthritis.
No crystals, infection, inflammatory arthropathy or neoplasm.

comment.text: A Krenn score of 2–4 indicates low-grade synovitis, typical of osteoarthritis and other degenerative or post-traumatic joint disease. It helps exclude a high-grade inflammatory arthropathy.

Detritic synovitis reflects shedding of cartilage and bone fragments from the eroded joint surface. When detritus is abundant, consider a neuropathic (Charcot) joint or osteonecrosis. These are not suggested clinically here.

containers.text: Multiple fragments of tan-pink, partly fibrous synovium, 5.0 x 4.0 x 1.0 cm in aggregate. Some surfaces have small embedded white, gritty fragments up to 3 mm. No villous hypertrophy, brown pigmentation, chalky deposits or mass.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A3 representative synovium including the gritty areas (A3 decalcified briefly).

diagnoses.name: Tophaceous Gout with Synovitis
diagnoses.path: Bone and Soft Tissue/Synovium/02 Crystal Arthropathies

micro.text: Sections show multiple gouty tophi. These are amorphous, pale pink-grey, feathery deposits with radiating needle-shaped clefts. They are surrounded by palisading histiocytes, many foreign-body multinucleated giant cells and fibrous tissue.

Polarised light: In the ethanol-fixed tissue (B1) and the unstained sections, abundant needle-shaped crystals with strong negative birefringence (yellow when parallel to the slow axis of the compensator). The formalin-fixed sections retain only scattered birefringent needles, because formalin dissolves part of the urate.
Synovium: Lining hyperplasia of 3–4 layers, moderately increased stromal cellularity, and a moderate perivascular lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate. Foci of neutrophils around fresh deposits. Fibrosis.
Negative findings: No calcium pyrophosphate (rhomboid, weakly positive) crystals. No granulomas of infectious type. No organisms on Gram stain. No malignancy. Bone is not included.
Special Stains / Immunohistochemistry:
Polarised light (compensated): Needle-shaped, strongly negatively birefringent crystals
De Galantha (ethanol-fixed): Positive: black urate deposits
Gram: No organisms

finalDiagnosis.label: Tophus and synovium, left first MTP joint, debridement:
finalDiagnosis.text: Tophaceous gout. Monosodium urate crystal deposits (negatively birefringent needles; De Galantha positive) with a foreign-body giant cell reaction, and moderate chronic synovitis (Krenn 6/9) with focal acute inflammation.
No CPPD crystals, infection or malignancy.

comment.text: The features are diagnostic of tophaceous gout. Urate crystals dissolve in formalin and aqueous stains. The ethanol-fixed portion and unstained sections confirmed strongly negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals.

Gout can coexist with septic arthritis. No organisms or abscess were seen, but correlate with the microbiology culture if one was sent. Steroid injection crystals can mimic urate. There is no history of injection here, and the morphology is typical.

containers.text: Formalin: multiple pieces of grey-white to tan soft tissue, 4.2 x 3.0 x 1.5 cm in aggregate, with chalky white, toothpaste-like deposits on cut surface.
Absolute ethanol: one piece of chalky tissue, 1.2 x 0.8 x 0.6 cm.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A4 representative chalky deposits and synovium (formalin); B1 ethanol-fixed tissue processed through non-aqueous stages. B1 was also cut as an unstained deparaffinised section for polarisation.

diagnoses.name: CPPD Crystal Deposition Disease (Chondrocalcinosis)
diagnoses.path: Bone and Soft Tissue/Synovium/02 Crystal Arthropathies

micro.text: The meniscal fibrocartilage contains multiple purple-blue, granular, “chalky” crystal deposits, made up of small rhomboid and rod-shaped crystals about 1–10 µm. Many are surrounded by chondroid metaplasia and a mild histiocytic and giant cell reaction. The meniscus also shows myxoid degeneration and tears.
Polarised light: With the condenser lowered, many crystals show weak positive birefringence (blue when parallel to the slow axis of the compensator). Some are barely birefringent.

Synovium: Similar crystal deposits in the subsynovium. Lining 2–3 layers, mildly increased cellularity, sparse perivascular lymphocytes. Small fragments of cartilage and bone (detritus) with giant cells.
Negative findings: No needle-shaped negatively birefringent urate crystals. No amyloid on H&E. No infection or malignancy.
Special Stains / Immunohistochemistry:
Polarised light (compensated, condenser lowered): Rhomboid crystals, weakly positive birefringence
Alizarin red S: Weakly positive
Congo red: Negative (no amyloid)

finalDiagnosis.label: Menisci and synovium, right knee, total knee arthroplasty:
finalDiagnosis.text: Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (CPPD) crystal deposition (chondrocalcinosis) in meniscal fibrocartilage and synovium. Rhomboid, weakly positively birefringent crystals.
Degenerative meniscal tears and low-grade synovitis (Krenn 3/9) with detritus, in keeping with osteoarthritis. No urate crystals, infection or malignancy.

comment.text: The findings confirm CPPD deposition disease in the setting of osteoarthritis. CPPD crystals survive formalin fixation, unlike urate. They are often only weakly birefringent and are easier to see with the condenser lowered.

CPPD in a patient under 60, or with many joints affected, should prompt a search for a metabolic cause: hyperparathyroidism (present in this patient's history), haemochromatosis, hypomagnesaemia or hypophosphatasia.

containers.text: Medial and lateral menisci, 4.0 and 3.5 cm long. The fibrocartilage shows chalky white, linear and stippled deposits, with fraying of the inner rims.
Synovium, multiple tan pieces, 5.0 x 3.0 x 1.0 cm in aggregate, with focal white chalky specks. Bone and cartilage are in a separate container (reported separately).

exampleGross.sections: A1–A3 menisci (cross-sections through the deposits); B1–B3 synovium.

diagnoses.name: Tuberculous Synovitis
diagnoses.path: Bone and Soft Tissue/Synovium/03 Infective Arthritis

micro.text: Sections show chronic granulomatous synovitis:
Granulomas: Numerous coalescent epithelioid granulomas with central caseous necrosis. They contain Langhans-type and foreign-body giant cells, with a peripheral cuff of lymphocytes and plasma cells.
Synovium: Lining hyperplasia with focal ulceration and fibrin, inflamed granulation tissue, and fibrinous rice bodies.
Negative findings: No crystals on polarisation. No fungi on GMS. No foreign material. No malignancy.
Special Stains / Molecular Tests:
Ziehl–Neelsen: Rare acid-fast bacilli
Auramine–rhodamine: Scanty fluorescent bacilli
GMS / PAS-D: No fungi
Polarised light: No crystals or foreign material

finalDiagnosis.label: Synovium, left knee, arthroscopic biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Chronic necrotising (caseating) granulomatous synovitis with rice bodies. Acid-fast bacilli seen on Ziehl–Neelsen. Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex DNA detected (Xpert MTB/RIF; rifampicin resistance not detected). Consistent with tuberculous synovitis.
No fungi, crystals or malignancy.

comment.text: Caseating granulomas with acid-fast bacilli and a positive molecular test confirm tuberculous synovitis. Acid-fast bacilli are often scanty in joint tissue, so a negative ZN does not exclude TB. Culture with drug-susceptibility testing is pending and will be reported as an addendum.

Other granulomatous causes considered: atypical mycobacteria (especially hand tenosynovitis), fungal infection (GMS negative), sarcoidosis (non-necrotising), rheumatoid nodule and foreign-body reaction. Rice bodies also occur in RA, but with this histology TB is the diagnosis.
Notify the case per national TB programme requirements.

containers.text: Received in formalin: multiple grey-tan to yellow, friable synovial fragments, 3.0 x 2.5 x 0.8 cm in aggregate, with focal cheesy yellow areas. Numerous rice bodies, 1–4 mm. Separate fresh tissue was sent to microbiology for mycobacterial culture and Xpert MTB/RIF.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A4 entire synovium; A5 rice bodies.

diagnoses.name: Septic Arthritis, Acute Suppurative Synovitis
diagnoses.path: Bone and Soft Tissue/Synovium/03 Infective Arthritis

micro.text: Sections show acute suppurative synovitis:
Surface: Ulcerated synovium covered by thick fibrinopurulent exudate with sheets of neutrophils and necrotic debris.
Subsynovium: Dense neutrophilic infiltrate extending into the subsynovium, with microabscesses, oedema, congested vessels and haemorrhage. Early granulation tissue at the base.
Organisms: Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in clusters within the exudate and in neutrophils.
Negative findings: No crystals on polarisation (urate or CPPD). No granulomas. No fungi. No malignancy. No cartilage or bone is included.
Special Stains / Immunohistochemistry:
Gram: Gram-positive cocci in clusters
PAS-D / GMS: No fungi
Ziehl–Neelsen: No acid-fast bacilli
Polarised light: No crystals

finalDiagnosis.label: Synovium, right knee, arthrotomy and debridement:
finalDiagnosis.text: Acute suppurative synovitis with fibrinopurulent exudate and microabscesses. Gram-positive cocci in clusters, in keeping with septic arthritis (Staphylococcus aureus on culture).
No crystals, granulomas or malignancy.

comment.text: The histology shows acute septic (pyogenic) arthritis, which matches the culture of methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus. Septic arthritis is an emergency: cartilage destruction can start within days.
Crystals were specifically searched for, because gout or CPPD can coexist with infection or mimic it. None were seen. Treatment follows microbiology and orthopaedic advice.

containers.text: Received in formalin: multiple fragments of red-tan, oedematous synovium, 5.5 x 4.0 x 1.2 cm in aggregate. The surfaces are covered by yellow-green purulent fibrinous exudate. No chalky deposits, rice bodies or mass. Tissue for culture was sent directly from theatre.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A5 representative synovium with exudate.

diagnoses.name: Periprosthetic Joint Infection, SLIM Type II (Revision TKA)
diagnoses.path: Bone and Soft Tissue/Synovium/04 Prosthesis Related

micro.text: Frozen section results were telephoned to the surgeon. The permanent sections confirm them.

Interface membranes (1, 2, 6): Granulation-tissue-like synovial-like interface membrane with oedema, neovascularisation and a mixed infiltrate. Neutrophils infiltrate the tissue (not only the surface fibrin), with plasma cells and lymphocytes. On permanent sections the neutrophil count is 64 in 10 high-power fields (0.3 mm² each, the 10 most infiltrated fields; CD15 confirmed). Small focal microabscess in 2A.

Particles: Scattered birefringent polyethylene fragments in a few giant cells, and occasional cement-related vacuoles with radiopaque granules. These cover less than 5% of the area, below the SLIM type I threshold (20%).
Neosynovium / capsule (3–5): Fibrosis and mild chronic inflammation, with fewer neutrophils (below threshold).
Negative findings: No ALVAL-type perivascular lymphoid cuffs. No granulomas. No organisms on Gram stain. No malignancy.
Frozen Section Neutrophil Counts:
FS1 – femoral interface membrane: Fields counted: 5 HPF (x400); Neutrophils per HPF (5 most cellular fields): 12, 9, 15, 8, 11 (all 5 or more).
FS2 – tibial interface membrane: Fields counted: 5 HPF (x400); Neutrophils per HPF (5 most cellular fields): 7, 6, 10, 5, 9 (all 5 or more).
FS3 – posterior capsule / neosynovium: Fields counted: 5 HPF (x400); Neutrophils per HPF (5 most cellular fields): 3, 2, 4, 1, 2 (below threshold).
Special Stains / Immunohistochemistry:
CD15: Highlights tissue-infiltrating neutrophils; used for the 10 HPF count
Gram: No organisms seen
Polarised light: Scattered birefringent polyethylene particles
CD68: Macrophages, focally particle-laden

finalDiagnosis.label: Periprosthetic tissues, left knee, revision TKA:
finalDiagnosis.text: Synovial-like interface membrane, infectious type (SLIM type II). 64 neutrophils in 10 HPF (Morawietz threshold 23 or more), CD15 confirmed; frozen section positive (Feldman: 5 or more neutrophils per HPF in 5 HPF). Findings support periprosthetic joint infection.
Minor polyethylene and cement particles (less than 5%). No ALVAL, granulomas or malignancy.

comment.text: Intraoperative frozen section (communicated to the operating surgeon): POSITIVE for acute inflammation consistent with infection. FS1 and FS2 had 5 or more neutrophils per HPF in 5 HPF. FS3 (capsule) was below threshold.

The histology meets the Feldman and Morawietz/Krenn thresholds for infection. It is a confirmatory criterion in the EBJIS 2021 definition and scores 3 points in ICM 2018. Neutrophils were counted only within tissue, excluding surface fibrin.

Low-virulence organisms (for example Cutibacterium acnes or coagulase-negative staphylococci) may need prolonged culture (up to 14 days). Final interpretation should combine these findings with the culture results.

containers.text: Six containers, labelled 1–6, each with tan-grey membranous tissue 1.0–3.5 cm in greatest dimension. Separate tissue samples (5) were sent to microbiology from theatre. Container labelled 1 (femoral interface): soft, grey-yellow membranes with focal fibrin. No black discolouration.
Labelled 2 (tibial interface): soft, grey-yellow membranes with focal fibrin and small amounts of white flaky debris. No black discolouration.
Labelled 3 (posterior capsule): tan-grey membranous tissue. No black discolouration.
Labelled 4 (lateral gutter neosynovium): tan-grey membranous tissue. No black discolouration.
Labelled 5 (medial gutter neosynovium): tan-grey membranous tissue. No black discolouration.
Labelled 6 (tibial canal tissue): tan-grey membranous tissue. No black discolouration.

exampleGross.sections: Frozen sections FS1 (container 1), FS2 (container 2) and FS3 (container 3), with frozen remnants submitted as A1–A3. Permanent sections: 1A–1B, 2A–2B, 3A, 4A, 5A, 6A (all tissue submitted).

diagnoses.name: Wear-particle Interface Membrane, SLIM Type I
diagnoses.path: Bone and Soft Tissue/Synovium/04 Prosthesis Related

micro.text: Sections show a wear-particle-induced synovial-like interface membrane:
Macrophage reaction: Sheets of foamy and granular macrophages, and many foreign-body multinucleated giant cells. They make up about 50–60% of the tissue area.

Particles: (1) Polyethylene: abundant, colourless, strongly birefringent slivers and flakes, mostly macroparticles larger than 5 µm in giant cells and microparticles 0.5–5 µm in histiocytes. This is the dominant particle type. (2) Metal: fine black, non-birefringent, Perls-negative granules in histiocytes (minor, about 10% of particle burden), consistent with debris from the CoCr head and taper. (3) Occasional round empty vacuoles with radiopaque granules, from PMMA bone cement with contrast agent (zirconium dioxide).
Inflammation and other changes: Fibrosis and focal necrosis. Lymphocytes are sparse, with no perivascular lymphoid cuffs (no ALVAL). Neutrophils: 4 in 10 HPF (below the threshold of 23).
Negative findings: No granulomas of infectious type. No organisms. No malignancy.
Special Stains / Immunohistochemistry:
Polarised light: Abundant strongly birefringent polyethylene particles
Perls Prussian blue: Negative in black particles (metal, not haemosiderin)
CD68: Sheets of particle-laden macrophages
CD15: 4 neutrophils in 10 HPF
Gram: No organisms

finalDiagnosis.label: Periprosthetic tissues, right hip, revision THA:
finalDiagnosis.text: Synovial-like interface membrane, wear-particle-induced type (SLIM type I). Abundant polyethylene macro- and microparticles with a foreign-body macrophage and giant cell reaction, minor metal particles and occasional bone-cement particles.
Neutrophils 4 in 10 HPF (below threshold): no histological evidence of infection. No ALVAL. No malignancy.

comment.text: The findings are those of particle disease. Polyethylene wear debris drives macrophage activation and periprosthetic osteolysis, leading to aseptic loosening. Particles were classified by polarised light (polyethylene birefringent; metal opaque and non-birefringent) and morphology.
The neutrophil count is below the infection threshold and cultures are negative, which supports aseptic loosening. The minor metal debris does not show an ALVAL-type reaction.
Please correlate with retrieval analysis of the explanted liner if performed.

containers.text: Acetabular interface membrane, multiple fragments of grey-white to tan, rubbery tissue, 4.5 x 3.5 x 1.0 cm in aggregate, with gritty white flecks and focal grey-black staining.
Pseudocapsule, 5.0 x 3.0 x 0.8 cm, with grey discolouration of the inner surface.
Osteolytic lesion contents (curettings), 2.0 x 1.5 x 0.5 cm, soft and tan-grey. The explanted liner is not received (retained by the hospital for retrieval analysis).

exampleGross.sections: A1–A4, B1–B2, C1 (all tissue).

diagnoses.name: Tenosynovial Giant Cell Tumour, Diffuse Type (Knee)
diagnoses.path: Bone and Soft Tissue/Synovium/05 Tumours and Tumour-like Lesions

micro.text: Sections show diffuse tenosynovial giant cell tumour:
Architecture: Infiltrative sheets and villonodular expansions of synovium with cleft-like and pseudoalveolar spaces.

Cell types: (1) A mixed population of small histiocytoid mononuclear cells. (2) Larger epithelioid mononuclear cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, eccentric reniform nuclei and a peripheral rim of haemosiderin granules. (3) Scattered osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells, fewer than in localized TGCT. (4) Sheets of foamy macrophages. (5) Abundant haemosiderin deposits. (6) Lymphocytes.

Mitoses and margin: Mitoses up to 3 per 10 HPF, with no atypical forms. No necrosis, marked atypia or sarcomatous areas (no features of malignant TGCT). The tumour extends to the inked deep margin of B.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
Desmin: Positive in a subset of large dendritic and epithelioid cells
Clusterin: Positive in large mononuclear cells
CD68 / CD163: Positive in histiocytoid cells and giant cells
Ki-67: About 5%
Perls: Abundant haemosiderin

finalDiagnosis.label: Synovium and posterior mass, left knee, total synovectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Tenosynovial giant cell tumour, diffuse type (formerly pigmented villonodular synovitis), with extra-articular extension into the popliteal fossa. No features of malignancy.
Lesion present at the inked deep margin of the posterior specimen (piecemeal resection).

comment.text: The diagnosis is diffuse-type TGCT. It is a locally aggressive neoplasm driven by CSF1 rearrangement in a minority of the cells, which recruit a large reactive macrophage population (the landscape effect). Recurrence after synovectomy is common (about 20–50%), especially with extra-articular disease and positive margins as here.

Systemic CSF1R inhibitors (for example pexidartinib or vimseltinib) are options for recurrent or unresectable disease, after multidisciplinary discussion. Haemosiderotic synovitis (haemophilia, recurrent haemarthrosis) and synovial haemangioma were considered. They do not show sheets of neoplastic mononuclear cells with desmin-positive dendritic cells.

containers.text: Anterior synovium: multiple fragments of shaggy, villous and nodular synovium, 9.0 x 6.0 x 2.5 cm in aggregate, 58 g, rust-brown to yellow-tan, with matted fronds and firm nodules up to 2.2 cm.
Posterior and popliteal tissue: nodular mass with attached synovium, 5.5 x 4.0 x 3.0 cm, poorly circumscribed. Cut surface is variegated yellow, brown and grey-white. No necrosis.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A8 representative villi and nodules; B1–B6 posterior mass including the deep soft-tissue margin (inked).

diagnoses.name: Tenosynovial Giant Cell Tumour, Localized Type (Finger)
diagnoses.path: Bone and Soft Tissue/Synovium/05 Tumours and Tumour-like Lesions

micro.text: Sections show a lobulated, well-circumscribed tumour with a fibrous capsule and collagenous septa, consisting of:

Cell types: (1) Small round to ovoid histiocytoid mononuclear cells. (2) Larger epithelioid mononuclear cells with a peripheral rim of haemosiderin. (3) Numerous evenly spaced osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells. (4) Clusters of xanthomatous foamy macrophages. (5) Haemosiderin. (6) Hyalinised collagen.
Mitoses and atypia: Mitoses 2 per 10 HPF, with no atypical forms. No necrosis or significant atypia.
Margins: The tumour is close to (0.5 mm) but does not reach the inked surface. The satellite nodule is completely excised.

finalDiagnosis.label: Mass, volar right index finger, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Tenosynovial giant cell tumour, localized type (giant cell tumour of tendon sheath), 2.2 cm. Margins clear (closest 0.5 mm).

comment.text: Localized TGCT is benign. The local recurrence rate is about 4–30%, higher with satellite nodules, incomplete excision, and lesions at the distal interphalangeal joint or with bone erosion. Close margins and a satellite nodule are noted here, so clinical follow-up is advised.

The morphology is classic: lobulated architecture, mixed mononuclear cells, giant cells, foam cells and haemosiderin. Immunohistochemistry is not needed. Differential diagnoses considered include fibroma of tendon sheath, giant cell reparative granuloma and xanthoma.

containers.text: A well-circumscribed, lobulated, firm nodule, 2.2 x 1.5 x 1.1 cm, with a thin fibrous capsule. A small satellite nodule, 0.3 cm, is attached. The outer surface is inked. Cut surface: variegated yellow, tan and rust-brown, with fibrous septa. No necrosis or haemorrhage.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted, A1–A4 (serial slices including the inked margins and the satellite nodule).

diagnoses.name: Synovial Chondromatosis
diagnoses.path: Bone and Soft Tissue/Synovium/05 Tumours and Tumour-like Lesions

micro.text: Sections show primary synovial chondromatosis:
Nodules: Multiple nodules of hyaline cartilage, both within the subsynovial connective tissue (B) and free (A). They are covered by a thin layer of synovium.
Chondrocytes: Arranged in clusters (clonal clustering). Some are mildly enlarged and binucleated, with moderate cellularity. This degree of atypia is acceptable in chondromatosis.
Ossification: Several free bodies show peripheral and central enchondral ossification, with fatty marrow in the larger bodies.

Negative findings: No sheets of chondrocytes with loss of clustering. No myxoid change, necrosis, or spindling at the periphery of lobules. No permeation of bone. Mitoses absent. Synovium shows mild chronic inflammation (Krenn 2/9). No concentric growth rings around a central osteochondral fragment (against secondary loose bodies).

finalDiagnosis.label: Loose bodies and synovium, right knee, arthroscopic excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Synovial chondromatosis (primary), with ossification of loose bodies. No features of malignancy.

comment.text: Primary synovial chondromatosis is a benign, locally recurrent cartilaginous neoplasm of synovium, characterised by FN1::ACVR2A (or ACVR2A::FN1) fusions. Recurrence after synovectomy is about 15–20%. Malignant transformation to synovial chondrosarcoma is rare (about 5% or less in long-standing disease).

Secondary chondromatosis (loose bodies from osteoarthritis or osteochondral fracture) was considered. Its bodies are fewer and larger, show concentric growth rings around an osteochondral core, and lack chondrocyte clustering. Imaging and histology here favour the primary type.

containers.text: About 85 loose bodies, 0.2–1.2 cm, smooth, glistening, white-blue, cartilaginous, several with a gritty centre. Total weight 38 g.
Synovium, multiple fragments 4.0 x 3.0 x 1.0 cm in aggregate, with numerous small attached cartilaginous nodules up to 0.4 cm.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A3 representative loose bodies (bisected; after brief decalcification of A3); B1–B4 synovium with attached nodules.

diagnoses.name: Lipoma Arborescens
diagnoses.path: Bone and Soft Tissue/Synovium/05 Tumours and Tumour-like Lesions

micro.text: Sections show many villous synovial projections whose subsynovial tissue is replaced by mature adipose tissue. The adipocytes are uniform, without atypia, lipoblasts or atypical stromal cells.
Synovium: Lining 2–3 cells thick. Mild fibrosis and mild perivascular lymphoplasmacytic inflammation (Krenn 3/9: lining 1, stroma 1, infiltrate 1).
Negative findings: No haemosiderin sheets, giant cell tumour, crystals, cartilage nodules or malignancy.

finalDiagnosis.label: Synovium, left knee suprapatellar pouch, arthroscopic synovectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Lipoma arborescens (villous lipomatous proliferation of the synovium) with low-grade chronic synovitis (Krenn 3/9). No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Lipoma arborescens is a benign, probably reactive, villous lipomatous proliferation of synovium. It is usually in the suprapatellar pouch of the knee and associated with osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis or previous trauma. It is not a true neoplasm. MRI shows fat signal in all sequences, which is characteristic.
Differential diagnoses include synovial (intra-articular) lipoma, which is a solitary circumscribed mass, and diffuse TGCT and synovial haemangioma, which are excluded morphologically.

containers.text: Multiple yellow, soft, villous, frond-like (tree-like) fragments of synovium, 6.5 x 5.0 x 2.0 cm in aggregate, weighing 28 g. The fronds are up to 1.5 cm long. Cut surface is yellow and fatty. They float in formalin. No brown discolouration, chalky deposits, cartilage nodules or solid mass.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A5 representative fronds.

diagnoses.name: Acute Lactational Mastitis with Breast Abscess
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/01 Acute and Infective Mastitis

micro.text: Sections show an abscess wall: central suppurative necrosis with dense sheets of neutrophils, nuclear debris and fibrin, surrounded by oedematous granulation tissue with proliferating capillaries, macrophages, lymphocytes and plasma cells. Breast lobules at the periphery show lactational change: distended acini lined by cells with vacuolated cytoplasm and hobnail nuclei, with intraluminal secretion. Several lobules are infiltrated by neutrophils (acute lobulitis) with milk stasis.
Clusters of Gram-positive cocci are seen in the necrotic debris on Gram stain. No granulomas, organisms of other types, foreign material or squamous metaplasia. No epithelial atypia or malignancy.
Special Stains, IHC and Microbiology:
Gram stain (tissue): Gram-positive cocci in clusters within the necrotic centre
PAS / GMS: No fungal elements
Ziehl–Neelsen: No acid-fast bacilli
Pus culture (aerobic): Staphylococcus aureus, heavy growth; methicillin-sensitive (MSSA): sensitive to cloxacillin, cefazolin, clindamycin, co-trimoxazole; resistant to penicillin
Anaerobic culture: No anaerobes isolated

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast, abscess wall, incision and drainage:
finalDiagnosis.text: Acute suppurative lactational (puerperal) mastitis with breast abscess. Gram-positive cocci in clusters on tissue Gram stain; culture: Staphylococcus aureus (methicillin-sensitive). Background lactational change. No granulomas. No evidence of malignancy.

comment.text: Lactational mastitis with abscess is usually caused by S. aureus (including MRSA in some settings), which enters through nipple fissures and milk stasis. Treat according to culture sensitivity. Breastfeeding or expressing from the affected side is generally encouraged. Pregnancy-associated breast carcinoma, including inflammatory carcinoma, can mimic infection. If the erythema or a mass persists after drainage and antibiotics, repeat imaging and core biopsy are advised. No malignancy is seen in this specimen.

containers.text: Received multiple irregular, soft, grey-yellow to haemorrhagic tissue fragments in aggregate 3.5 x 3.0 x 1.0 cm, with adherent purulent material. No discrete firm or gritty areas.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in cassettes A1–A4.

diagnoses.name: Zuska Disease, Recurrent Subareolar Abscess (SMOLD) with Fistula
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/01 Acute and Infective Mastitis

micro.text: Several lactiferous ducts show squamous metaplasia extending well beyond their normal short squamous-lined terminal segment, deep into the subareolar duct system (squamous metaplasia of lactiferous ducts, SMOLD). The ducts are plugged by laminated keratin. One metaplastic duct has ruptured: free keratin flakes in the periductal stroma provoke a foreign-body giant cell reaction with neutrophilic microabscesses and chronic inflammation.

A sinus tract, lined partly by granulation tissue and partly by ingrowing squamous epithelium, runs from the ruptured duct to the areolar skin surface (periareolar mammary duct fistula). Periductal fibrosis and plasma cells are present. Squamous epithelium shows reactive changes only, without dysplasia or invasive carcinoma. No caseating granulomas or organisms on special stains.
Special Stains, IHC and Microbiology:
Gram stain: Mixed Gram-positive cocci and occasional Gram-negative bacilli in keratin debris
Ziehl–Neelsen: No acid-fast bacilli
PAS / GMS: No fungal elements
Culture (tract swab): Mixed anaerobes (Peptostreptococcus spp., Bacteroides fragilis group) with coagulase-negative staphylococci
p16 / p53: Not required (no squamous atypia)

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast, subareolar ducts and fistula tract, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Recurrent subareolar abscess with squamous metaplasia of lactiferous ducts (SMOLD), keratin plugging, duct rupture with keratin-induced foreign-body giant cell reaction, and periareolar mammary duct fistula (Zuska disease). No dysplasia or malignancy.

comment.text: Zuska disease is strongly associated with smoking. Keratin plugs obstruct and rupture metaplastic lactiferous ducts, which leads to recurrent abscesses and fistulas. Recurrence is common unless the whole metaplastic duct system and tract are excised; smoking cessation is advised. The differential includes periductal mastitis/duct ectasia, tuberculous sinus (no caseating granulomas; ZN negative) and squamous cell carcinoma (no atypia). Excision margins of the duct complex are free of squamous-metaplastic ducts in sections examined.

containers.text: Received a cone of subareolar tissue 4.5 x 3.5 x 2.5 cm with an ellipse of areolar skin 2.0 x 0.8 cm bearing a 0.3 cm punctum. A probe passed from the punctum enters a 2.2 cm sinus tract leading to a dilated major duct beneath the nipple base. The tract is lined by grey granular tissue and contains cheesy white keratinous debris. No discrete mass.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A3 sinus tract with skin opening (longitudinal); A4–A6 major ducts at nipple base (cross-sections); A7–A8 surrounding tissue.

diagnoses.name: Tuberculous Mastitis
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/01 Acute and Infective Mastitis

micro.text: Cores show breast tissue replaced by numerous confluent epithelioid cell granulomas with central caseous (amorphous, eosinophilic, granular) necrosis, rimmed by epithelioid histiocytes, Langhans-type multinucleated giant cells, lymphocytes and fibroblasts. Granulomas involve both lobules and interlobular stroma, without a strict lobulocentric distribution. Residual ducts and lobules are compressed and infiltrated by inflammatory cells.
Ziehl–Neelsen stain shows rare acid-fast bacilli within the caseous necrosis. No cystic lipid vacuoles, foreign material, vasculitis or fungal elements. No atypia or malignancy.
Special Stains, IHC and Microbiology:
Ziehl–Neelsen: Rare acid-fast bacilli (1–2 per 50 oil-immersion fields) within caseous necrosis
GMS / PAS: No fungal elements
Gram stain: No bacteria
GeneXpert MTB/RIF Ultra (core in saline): MTB DETECTED, medium; rifampicin resistance NOT detected
Mycobacterial culture (liquid MGIT): Pending (final report to follow)
Pan-cytokeratin: Not required (no atypical epithelial cells)

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast lump, core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Necrotising (caseating) granulomatous mastitis with Langhans giant cells and rare acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl–Neelsen stain; GeneXpert MTB/RIF Ultra: Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex DETECTED, rifampicin resistance not detected. Consistent with tuberculous mastitis. No evidence of malignancy.

comment.text: Breast tuberculosis is uncommon but well recognised in endemic regions, often with a sinus and axillary lymphadenopathy, and it can mimic carcinoma clinically and radiologically. Caseous necrosis, AFB and a positive GeneXpert confirm the diagnosis. Idiopathic granulomatous lobular mastitis (lobulocentric, no caseation, special stains and molecular tests negative), fungal infection, sarcoidosis and CNGM were considered and are not favoured. Anti-tubercular therapy according to national programme (NTEP) guidelines and notification are advised. Follow up the mycobacterial culture and drug-susceptibility testing.

containers.text: Received four grey-white to cheesy yellow cores, 0.8–1.6 cm long, 0.1 cm diameter, partly friable.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A2.

diagnoses.name: Fungal Mastitis (Aspergillus)
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/01 Acute and Infective Mastitis

micro.text: Sections show a necrotising suppurative and granulomatous abscess: central necrosis and neutrophilic microabscesses surrounded by epithelioid histiocytes, foreign-body and Langhans-type giant cells and granulation tissue. Within the necrosis and giant cells are numerous fungal hyphae that are narrow (3–6 µm), of uniform width, regularly septate and show repeated acute-angle (about 45°) dichotomous branching. Focal angioinvasion with hyphae in the wall of a small vessel and thrombosis.
No broad, pauciseptate ribbon-like hyphae, yeasts or pseudohyphae. Fungal elements are highlighted by GMS and PAS. No acid-fast bacilli. Residual breast lobules show no atypia; no malignancy.
Special Stains, IHC and Microbiology:
GMS (Grocott): Numerous septate hyphae with acute-angle dichotomous branching
PAS / PAS-D: Fungal walls positive
Ziehl–Neelsen: No acid-fast bacilli
Gram stain: No bacteria
KOH mount (fresh tissue): Septate branching hyphae
Fungal culture (SDA): Aspergillus fumigatus (blue-green colonies; uniseriate conidiophores), confirmed by MALDI-TOF
Bacterial culture: No growth

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast, abscess wall, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Necrotising suppurative and granulomatous fungal mastitis with abscess, with septate acute-angle branching hyphae (GMS/PAS positive) and focal angioinvasion; culture: Aspergillus fumigatus. No evidence of malignancy.

comment.text: Fungal mastitis is rare and seen mainly in immunosuppressed patients. Candida is more common with lactation and nipple infection; Aspergillus causes invasive disease in the immunocompromised. Hyphal morphology suggests but cannot reliably distinguish Aspergillus from other hyaline septate moulds (Fusarium, Scedosporium); culture confirms A. fumigatus here. Mucorales were excluded (broad, pauciseptate, right-angle branching hyphae not seen). Look for disseminated aspergillosis; antifungal therapy (e.g. voriconazole, monitoring tacrolimus interaction) with infectious diseases input is advised. No malignancy.

containers.text: Received irregular grey-brown to black-tinged necrotic tissue with abscess wall, aggregate 4.0 x 3.2 x 1.5 cm. Cut surface shows a 2.5 cm cavity with friable necrotic lining and focal greenish-black flecks.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A6.

diagnoses.name: Actinomycotic Mastitis
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/01 Acute and Infective Mastitis

micro.text: Sections show chronic suppurative inflammation with multiloculated abscesses, dense fibrosis and granulation tissue lining a sinus tract. Several abscesses contain characteristic granules: rounded to lobulated colonies 150–400 µm across with a basophilic centre of tangled filaments and a radiating eosinophilic club-like periphery (Splendore–Hoeppli phenomenon). Neutrophils surround the granules, with an outer zone of foamy histiocytes, plasma cells and occasional giant cells.

Gram stain shows delicate Gram-positive, beaded, branching filamentous bacilli within the granules, also highlighted by GMS. Modified Fite (modified acid-fast) stain is negative, which is against Nocardia. No caseating granulomas, fungal hyphae or malignancy.
Special Stains, IHC and Microbiology:
Gram stain: Gram-positive, thin, branching filamentous bacilli within granules
GMS: Filaments highlighted (bacterial filaments <1 µm wide)
Modified Fite / modified ZN: Negative (against Nocardia)
Ziehl–Neelsen: No acid-fast bacilli
PAS: No fungal hyphae; granule periphery PAS-positive
Anaerobic culture (granules, 10 days): Actinomyces turicensis identified by MALDI-TOF; mixed anaerobic flora
Aerobic culture: Coagulase-negative staphylococci (likely skin contaminant)

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast, abscess and sinus tract, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Chronic suppurative (actinomycotic) mastitis with multiloculated abscesses, sinus tract and sulphur granules containing Gram-positive branching filamentous bacteria (modified Fite negative); culture: Actinomyces turicensis. No evidence of malignancy.

comment.text: Primary breast actinomycosis is rare. It presents as recurrent abscesses and sinuses that mimic carcinoma, tuberculosis or Zuska disease. Sulphur granules with Gram-positive branching filaments that are modified acid-fast negative favour Actinomyces over Nocardia; culture is often negative but was positive here. Botryomycosis (granules of cocci/bacilli) and fungal mycetoma are excluded morphologically. Prolonged penicillin-based therapy (weeks to months) is usually needed. No malignancy.

containers.text: Received a fibrofatty tissue piece 5.5 x 4.0 x 3.0 cm with a skin ellipse 3.0 x 1.2 cm bearing a 0.4 cm sinus opening. Sectioning shows a 2.8 cm multiloculated cavity lined by shaggy yellow granulation tissue, containing pus with several pinpoint yellow 'sulphur' granules (up to 1 mm), and surrounded by dense fibrosis.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A2 sinus tract with skin; A3–A7 abscess cavity wall with granules; A8 peripheral fibrosis.

diagnoses.name: Filarial Mastitis (Wuchereria bancrofti)
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/01 Acute and Infective Mastitis

micro.text: Sections show dilated lymphatic channels containing transverse and oblique sections of adult nematodes with a thin smooth cuticle, a thin muscle layer and paired uterine tubes packed with coiled microfilariae, consistent with a gravid adult female filarial worm. Some worm segments are degenerated and calcified. Surrounding the worms is eosinophil-rich granulomatous inflammation with epithelioid histiocytes, foreign-body giant cells, eosinophilic microabscesses, Charcot–Leyden crystals and Splendore–Hoeppli material, with lymphangitis and fibrosis.
Free microfilariae in tissue are sheathed, with nuclear columns not extending to the tip of the tail, consistent with Wuchereria bancrofti. Breast lobules show no atypia. No malignancy.
Special Stains, IHC and Microbiology:
PAS: Microfilarial sheath and worm cuticle highlighted
Giemsa (tissue): Sheathed microfilariae; nuclei do not extend to tail tip
Ziehl–Neelsen / GMS: No acid-fast bacilli; no fungi
Peripheral blood night smear (Giemsa): Sheathed microfilariae of W. bancrofti (body nuclei clear of tail tip)
Filarial antigen (ICT, W. bancrofti CFA): Positive
Absolute eosinophil count: 1,450/µL (raised)

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast lump, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Filarial mastitis: adult female filarial worm with sheathed microfilariae within dilated lymphatics, with eosinophil-rich granulomatous lymphangitis, consistent with Wuchereria bancrofti (correlating with positive night blood smear and filarial antigen test). No evidence of malignancy.

comment.text: Filarial infestation of the breast is uncommon. It occurs in endemic regions and may mimic carcinoma clinically and on mammography (calcified worms). W. bancrofti microfilariae are sheathed with no nuclei at the tail tip, unlike Brugia malayi, which has terminal and subterminal tail nuclei. Zoonotic Dirofilaria repens (subcutaneous nodule, a worm with a thick, longitudinally ridged cuticle and usually no circulating microfilariae) is the main morphological differential. Antifilarial treatment (DEC with albendazole, per national programme) is advised. No malignancy.

containers.text: Received a fibrofatty tissue piece 4.0 x 3.0 x 2.5 cm. Sectioning shows a 1.6 cm ill-defined, firm, grey-white nodule containing tiny tortuous, thread-like, cream-white structures within dilated channels.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A4 nodule entirely; A5 surrounding tissue.

diagnoses.name: Syphilitic Mastitis (Secondary Syphilis)
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/01 Acute and Infective Mastitis

micro.text: The areolar epidermis shows erosion with psoriasiform hyperplasia, exocytosis of neutrophils and spongiosis; no Paget cells. The dermis and underlying subareolar breast tissue show a dense, perivascular and periductal inflammatory infiltrate rich in plasma cells, with lymphocytes and histiocytes and ill-formed non-necrotising granulomas. Vessels show endothelial swelling and proliferation with narrowed lumina (endarteritis obliterans). The plasma cell-rich inflammation surrounds and infiltrates ducts (periductal mastitis pattern).

Treponemal immunohistochemistry demonstrates numerous spirochetes in the lower epidermis, around vessels and around ducts. No acid-fast bacilli or fungi. No atypical epithelial cells, Paget cells, carcinoma or lymphoma.
Special Stains, IHC and Serology:
Treponema pallidum IHC: Numerous spiral organisms in epidermis, perivascular and periductal tissue
Warthin–Starry: Spirochetes demonstrated (concordant with IHC)
CK7 / CAM5.2: No intraepidermal (Paget) cells; positive in ducts only
Kappa / lambda (ISH): Polytypic plasma cells
Ziehl–Neelsen / GMS: Negative
Serology (clinical): RPR reactive 1:64; TPHA positive; HIV-1/2 non-reactive

finalDiagnosis.label: Left nipple-areolar lesion with subareolar tissue, incisional biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Plasma cell-rich perivascular and periductal mastitis with endarteritis obliterans, psoriasiform epidermal change and numerous spirochetes on Treponema pallidum immunohistochemistry; serology RPR reactive (1:64) and TPHA positive. Consistent with syphilitic mastitis in secondary syphilis. No Paget disease or malignancy.

comment.text: Syphilitic involvement of the breast is rare. It is described as a nipple-areolar chancre, as secondary-stage lesions, and as tertiary gummas that mimic carcinoma. Plasma cell-rich inflammation with endarteritis should prompt treponemal IHC, which is more sensitive and specific than silver stains. Paget disease and carcinoma (no CK7-positive intraepidermal cells or invasive tumour), tuberculosis, lymphoma (polytypic) and periductal mastitis are excluded. Treatment (benzathine penicillin), partner notification and screening for other sexually transmitted infections are advised. A pregnancy test is advised because of the risk of congenital syphilis.

containers.text: Received a wedge of skin and subareolar tissue 2.5 x 1.5 x 1.2 cm with an eroded, indurated skin surface 1.2 x 0.8 cm. Cut surface is firm and grey-white without a discrete mass.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A3 (perpendicular to skin).

diagnoses.name: Periductal Mastitis with Duct Ectasia
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/02 Periductal and Granulomatous Lobular Mastitis

micro.text: Several large subareolar ducts are markedly dilated and contain inspissated eosinophilic secretion, cholesterol clefts and numerous foamy histiocytes, some laden with golden-brown lipofuscin pigment ('ochrocytes'). The duct epithelium is attenuated or focally lost, and foamy histiocytes infiltrate the duct wall.

There is periductal chronic inflammation rich in plasma cells and lymphocytes, with marked periductal concentric fibrosis and elastosis. Some ducts are obliterated by fibrous tissue with a residual ring of elastic tissue (obliterative mastitis). Coarse rod-like calcifications in duct lumina correspond to the mammographic finding. No squamous metaplasia, granulomas or organisms. Duct epithelium lacks atypia; no intraductal papilloma, DCIS or invasive carcinoma.
Special Stains, IHC and Microbiology:
Gram / ZN / GMS: No organisms
Elastic van Gieson: Periductal elastosis; residual elastic rings around obliterated ducts
CD68: Not required (foamy macrophages morphologically evident)
Discharge culture: No significant growth

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast, major subareolar ducts, total duct excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Mammary duct ectasia with periductal (plasma cell-rich) mastitis, periductal fibrosis, focal obliterative mastitis and intraductal calcifications. No intraductal papilloma, atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Duct ectasia with periductal mastitis (plasma cell mastitis when plasma cells dominate) commonly causes nipple discharge, retraction and retroareolar calcification. These features can clinically and radiologically mimic carcinoma; rod-like calcifications correspond to inspissated secretions. Periductal mastitis in young smokers overlaps with the Zuska/SMOLD spectrum, though no squamous metaplasia is seen here. Intraductal papilloma and DCIS, the main causes of pathological discharge, are excluded in this complete duct excision.

containers.text: Received a cone of subareolar tissue 4.0 x 3.5 x 2.0 cm, the apex marked with a suture (nipple side). Sectioning shows multiple dilated ducts up to 0.5 cm containing thick, pasty, yellow-green secretion, with periductal fibrous thickening. No discrete mass.

exampleGross.sections: A1 apex (nipple side) en face; A2–A7 serial sections of duct complex; A8 base.

diagnoses.name: Idiopathic Granulomatous Lobular Mastitis
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/02 Periductal and Granulomatous Lobular Mastitis

micro.text: The cores show a lobulocentric granulomatous inflammation: lobules are expanded and effaced by non-caseating granulomas composed of epithelioid histiocytes and Langhans and foreign-body type multinucleated giant cells, admixed with lymphocytes, plasma cells, occasional eosinophils and numerous neutrophils forming small microabscesses within the granulomas. Residual acini are entrapped at the centre of the inflamed lobules. Inflammation extends into the interlobular stroma in places.

There is no caseous necrosis, no cystic lipid vacuoles rimmed by neutrophils (against CNGM), no vasculitis, no foreign material and no duct-centred squamous metaplasia. Extensive special stains for organisms are negative. No epithelial atypia or malignancy.
Special Stains, IHC and Microbiology:
Ziehl–Neelsen: No acid-fast bacilli (multiple levels)
Modified Fite: Negative
GMS / PAS: No fungal elements
Gram stain (including Brown–Hopps): No bacteria; specifically no Gram-positive bacilli in vacuoles
GeneXpert MTB/RIF Ultra: MTB NOT detected
Bacterial culture (including prolonged, lipid-enriched): No growth at 7 days
Mycobacterial culture: No growth at 6 weeks
Fungal culture: No growth

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast mass, core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Non-caseating, lobulocentric granulomatous mastitis with neutrophilic microabscesses; special stains, GeneXpert and cultures negative for organisms. In the clinical context, consistent with idiopathic granulomatous lobular mastitis. No evidence of malignancy.

comment.text: IGLM is a diagnosis of exclusion, typically in parous women within a few years of pregnancy or lactation, sometimes with hyperprolactinaemia. Tuberculosis (caseation, AFB, GeneXpert), fungal and other infections, CNGM (lipid vacuoles with Gram-positive bacilli, which should be sought specifically), sarcoidosis, GPA and foreign-body reaction have been excluded as far as possible on this sample. It mimics carcinoma clinically and radiologically, and no malignancy is seen. Management options include observation, steroids, methotrexate or limited surgery; clinicoradiological follow-up is advised.

containers.text: Received five grey-white to tan cores, 1.0–1.8 cm long.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A2.

diagnoses.name: Cystic Neutrophilic Granulomatous Mastitis (Corynebacterium)
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/02 Periductal and Granulomatous Lobular Mastitis

micro.text: Sections show suppurative lipogranulomas with a distinctive pattern: clear, round to oval, empty-appearing cystic (lipid) vacuoles of varying size, each rimmed by a cuff of neutrophils, surrounded by an outer layer of epithelioid histiocytes and Langhans-type giant cells, and then a mixed infiltrate of lymphocytes and plasma cells. The process is centred on lobules and extends into the surrounding fat.

On Gram stain (Brown–Hopps), sparse Gram-positive bacilli are seen within several of the clear vacuoles; they are easily missed and only detected after examining multiple vacuoles at high power. No caseous necrosis, acid-fast bacilli, fungi, foreign material or vasculitis. No atypia or malignancy.
Special Stains, IHC and Microbiology:
Gram stain (Brown–Hopps): Sparse Gram-positive bacilli within clear lipid vacuoles
Ziehl–Neelsen: No acid-fast bacilli
GMS / PAS: No fungal elements
Bacterial culture (blood agar with 1% Tween 80, 5 days): Corynebacterium kroppenstedtii (lipophilic), identified by MALDI-TOF
16S rRNA PCR (tissue): Corynebacterium kroppenstedtii detected
GeneXpert MTB/RIF Ultra: MTB NOT detected

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast mass, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Cystic neutrophilic granulomatous mastitis (CNGM): suppurative lipogranulomas with neutrophil-rimmed lipid vacuoles containing Gram-positive bacilli; culture and 16S rRNA PCR: Corynebacterium kroppenstedtii. No evidence of malignancy.

comment.text: CNGM is a distinctive form of granulomatous lobular mastitis associated with lipophilic Corynebacterium species, especially C. kroppenstedtii. The organisms reside in lipid vacuoles and are sparse, so careful Gram staining is needed; routine cultures are often negative unless lipid-enriched media and prolonged incubation are used. Differentials are idiopathic granulomatous lobular mastitis (no vacuole-associated bacilli), tuberculosis and fat necrosis. Prolonged therapy with lipophilic antibiotics (e.g. doxycycline, clarithromycin, rifampicin or co-trimoxazole, per microbiology advice) is usually recommended. No malignancy.

containers.text: Received a fibrofatty tissue piece 4.5 x 3.5 x 2.5 cm. Sectioning shows a 2.8 cm ill-defined, firm, tan-yellow area containing multiple small cystic spaces (0.1–0.4 cm) with turbid yellow fluid. No discrete solid mass.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A6 lesion entirely; A7 peripheral tissue.

diagnoses.name: Fat Necrosis of Breast
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/03 Fat Necrosis and Foreign Body Reaction

micro.text: Sections show established fat necrosis: anucleate, ghost-like necrotic adipocytes; numerous lipid-laden foamy macrophages; multinucleated foreign-body giant cells around lipid spaces; lipid (oil) cysts lined by histiocytes; and membranous (lipomembranous) change with crenated, eosinophilic, arabesque-like linings. There is haemosiderin deposition, organising fibrosis with chronic inflammation, and dystrophic calcification at the periphery of the oil cyst.
No atypical cells, carcinoma, organisms, foreign material or granulomas of infectious type. Background breast shows fibrocystic change.
Special Stains and IHC:
Perls (Prussian blue): Haemosiderin-laden macrophages present
CD68: Foamy and giant cells positive (histiocytic)
Pan-cytokeratin (AE1/AE3): Negative in foamy cells and stroma (excludes infiltrating carcinoma, including histiocytoid lobular carcinoma)
Microbiology: Not required

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast lump, wire-guided excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Fat necrosis with oil cyst, lipomembranous change, foamy macrophages, giant cells, haemosiderin, fibrosis and dystrophic calcification (lesion 1.9 cm). Concordant with imaging. No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Fat necrosis commonly follows trauma, surgery or radiotherapy and can closely mimic carcinoma clinically and radiologically (spiculation, skin tethering, calcification). The specimen radiograph confirms the targeted calcified lesion was excised, and the histology is concordant. Foamy histiocytes are keratin-negative, excluding histiocytoid (lobular) carcinoma. Silicone granuloma and CNGM are excluded (no refractile vacuoles or Gram-positive bacilli).

containers.text: Received a wire-localised fibrofatty specimen 5.0 x 4.0 x 3.0 cm, oriented with sutures (short superior, long lateral) and inked. A 1.9 x 1.6 x 1.4 cm ill-defined, firm, yellow-white area with chalky flecks and a central 0.6 cm oily cyst is present 1.0 cm from the nearest (deep) margin. Specimen radiograph confirms the lesion and calcification.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A6 lesion entirely with inked margins; A7–A8 surrounding tissue.

diagnoses.name: Silicone Foreign Body Granulomatous Reaction, Implant Capsule
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/03 Fat Necrosis and Foreign Body Reaction

micro.text: A: The capsule is composed of dense, hyalinised collagen with synovial-like metaplasia of the inner lining, focal dystrophic calcification and patchy chronic inflammation.
