The capsule and adjacent breast parenchyma contain numerous clear, round vacuoles of varying size (Swiss-cheese pattern), within and between foamy histiocytes and foreign-body multinucleated giant cells. The vacuoles contain faintly refractile, non-birefringent material consistent with silicone. There is surrounding fibrosis and lymphocytic infiltration (silicone granulomatous mastitis / siliconoma).
B: The lymph node shows sinus and parenchymal infiltration by vacuolated histiocytes and giant cells containing silicone (silicone lymphadenopathy). No carcinoma.

C: Fluid cytology shows foamy macrophages and occasional lymphocytes; no atypical large cells. No large atypical lymphoid cells in capsule, effusion or node; no squamous lining or atypia of the capsule; no malignancy.
IHC, Special Studies and Microbiology:
CD68: Vacuolated histiocytes and giant cells positive
CD30: Negative in capsule, effusion cell block and node (only rare scattered small activated lymphocytes)
ALK: Negative
Pan-cytokeratin (AE1/AE3): Negative in histiocytes; no carcinoma or squamous lining
Polarised light: Silicone non-birefringent; scant birefringent fragments (implant shell)
Effusion culture: No growth

finalDiagnosis.label: A–C. Right breast implant capsule with ruptured implant, axillary lymph node and peri-implant fluid:
finalDiagnosis.text: Fibrous implant capsule with synovial metaplasia, calcification and silicone foreign-body granulomatous reaction extending into adjacent breast tissue (silicone granulomatous mastitis), consistent with implant rupture and capsular contracture. Silicone lymphadenopathy in the axillary node. Peri-implant fluid: foamy macrophages only. CD30 negative; no evidence of breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma or other malignancy.

comment.text: Silicone leaking from ruptured implants, or injected directly, causes foreign-body granulomas (siliconomas) in breast tissue and draining nodes that may mimic carcinoma clinically and on imaging. The capsule and effusion were evaluated for BIA-ALCL (associated mainly with textured implants; CD30 positive large cells) and for implant-associated squamous cell carcinoma; neither is present. Fat necrosis and infectious granulomas are the main histological differentials. Injected free silicone produces a similar picture without a capsule.

containers.text: Intact capsule 13 x 11 x 5 cm, thickened up to 0.4 cm, enclosing a collapsed silicone implant with a 3 cm shell tear and free sticky silicone gel. Capsule inner surface is shaggy and yellow-tan, with focal calcified plaques; no discrete mass or nodule. Separately, adherent breast tissue (3 x 2 x 1 cm) with gel-infiltrated yellow areas. Implant (13 cm) described and returned to theatre records.
Lymph node 1.6 x 1.2 x 1.0 cm, cut surface yellow-white, glistening.
20 mL straw-coloured fluid.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A12 capsule (anterior, posterior, superior, inferior, lateral, medial, and calcified plaques); A13–A14 adherent breast tissue with gel; B1–B2 node; C: cytospin and cell block.

diagnoses.name: Lymphocytic (Diabetic) Mastopathy
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/04 Immune Mediated and Systemic Mastitis

micro.text: Cores show dense, hyalinised, keloid-like collagenous stroma containing scattered plump epithelioid fibroblasts (myofibroblasts) with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm. Atrophic lobules and ducts are infiltrated and surrounded by a dense, mature, small lymphocytic infiltrate (lymphocytic lobulitis and ductitis). Prominent perivascular lymphocytic cuffing is seen around small vessels. A few germinal centres are present.

There is no granulomatous inflammation, necrosis, abscess or organisms. Lymphocytes are small and mature without atypia, lymphoepithelial destruction or sheets. The epithelioid stromal cells are cytokeratin-negative. No in situ or invasive carcinoma.
Immunohistochemistry:
CD20: Predominant B lymphocytes in lobular and perivascular aggregates
CD3: Scattered T lymphocytes (minority)
Kappa / lambda (ISH): Polytypic plasma cells (no light-chain restriction)
Pan-cytokeratin (AE1/AE3): Negative in epithelioid stromal cells (excludes infiltrating carcinoma); positive in residual epithelium
SMA: Epithelioid fibroblasts focally positive (myofibroblastic)
IgG4: Occasional positive plasma cells (<5/HPF)

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast mass, core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Lymphocytic (diabetic) mastopathy: keloid-like stromal fibrosis with epithelioid fibroblasts, B-cell predominant lymphocytic lobulitis, ductitis and perivascular cuffing. Polytypic. No evidence of lymphoma or carcinoma.

comment.text: Diabetic (lymphocytic) mastopathy typically occurs in long-standing type 1 diabetes with microvascular complications. It may be bilateral and recurrent, and forms hard masses with marked acoustic shadowing that mimic carcinoma. The differential includes MALT lymphoma (excluded: polytypic, no lymphoepithelial lesions or atypical sheets), infiltrating lobular carcinoma (stromal epithelioid cells keratin-negative), IgG4-related mastitis (IgG4 not increased) and autoimmune lymphocytic mastitis. If concordant with imaging, excision is usually unnecessary; follow-up is advised.

containers.text: Received five firm, white, fibrous cores 0.6–1.4 cm long (fragmented).

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A2.

diagnoses.name: IgG4-related Sclerosing Mastitis
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/04 Immune Mediated and Systemic Mastitis

micro.text: Sections show a nodular sclerosing mastitis with marked lobular atrophy and loss of lobules. There is a dense, diffuse lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with scattered reactive lymphoid follicles and a few eosinophils. The fibrosis is storiform (cartwheel), with plump fibroblasts arranged in whorls. Several medium-sized veins are obliterated by the lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate (obliterative phlebitis), highlighted on elastic stain.
No granulomas, neutrophilic microabscesses, necrosis, organisms or emperipolesis. Plasma cells are mature and polytypic. No atypical lymphoid infiltrate or carcinoma.
Special Stains, IHC and Serology:
IgG4: IgG4-positive plasma cells: average 85 per HPF (mean of 3 hotspot HPFs; field 0.237 mm²)
IgG: IgG-positive plasma cells: average 140 per HPF
IgG4/IgG ratio: About 61% (>40%)
Kappa / lambda (ISH): Polytypic
CD20 / CD3: Mixed B (follicles) and T cells, normal distribution
S100 / CD1a: Negative (no Rosai–Dorfman cells or Langerhans cells)
Elastic van Gieson: Obliterative phlebitis confirmed
ZN / GMS / Gram: No organisms
Serum IgG4 (clinical): 312 mg/dL (raised)

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast mass, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: IgG4-related sclerosing mastitis: dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, storiform fibrosis and obliterative phlebitis with IgG4-positive plasma cells averaging 85/HPF and an IgG4/IgG ratio of about 61%. Polytypic. No evidence of lymphoma or carcinoma.

comment.text: The histology, tissue IgG4 counts (well above commonly used thresholds) and IgG4/IgG ratio above 40%, together with raised serum IgG4 and submandibular gland involvement, support IgG4-related disease. Increased IgG4 plasma cells alone are not specific; they can occur in IGLM, other chronic mastitides, Rosai–Dorfman disease and lymphoma. Differentials excluded here are MALT lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation (polytypic), Rosai–Dorfman disease (S100 negative), IGLM (no granulomas) and diabetic mastopathy. Rheumatology referral for systemic evaluation and steroid therapy is advised.

containers.text: Received a firm fibrofatty specimen 4.5 x 3.5 x 3.0 cm containing a 2.8 x 2.4 x 2.0 cm well-defined, rubbery, homogeneous grey-white nodule. No necrosis, cyst or calcification.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A6 nodule entirely; A7 interface with surrounding tissue.

diagnoses.name: Sarcoidosis of Breast
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/04 Immune Mediated and Systemic Mastitis

micro.text: Cores show numerous well-formed, tight, non-necrotising epithelioid granulomas with few surrounding lymphocytes ('naked' granulomas). They are distributed in the interlobular stroma and within and around lobules, without a specific lobulocentric predilection, and some are confluent with surrounding concentric hyaline fibrosis. Langhans-type giant cells contain asteroid bodies and Schaumann (calcified, laminated) bodies.

There is no caseous necrosis, neutrophilic microabscesses, cystic lipid vacuoles, vasculitis or birefringent foreign material on polarisation. Special stains for organisms are negative. No atypical epithelial cells or carcinoma; no lymphoma.
Special Stains, IHC and Microbiology:
Ziehl–Neelsen: No acid-fast bacilli
GMS / PAS: No fungal elements
Gram stain: No bacteria
Polarised light: No birefringent foreign material (Schaumann bodies may show small calcium oxalate crystals)
GeneXpert MTB/RIF Ultra: MTB NOT detected
Mycobacterial and fungal culture: No growth (final)
Serum ACE (clinical): 98 U/L (raised)

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast mass, core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Non-necrotising, well-formed epithelioid granulomatous inflammation with asteroid and Schaumann bodies; special stains, GeneXpert and cultures negative. In the context of known systemic sarcoidosis, consistent with sarcoidosis of the breast. No evidence of malignancy.

comment.text: Breast involvement in sarcoidosis is rare and usually occurs in patients with known systemic disease, as here. It remains a diagnosis of exclusion. Tuberculosis and fungal infection (special stains, GeneXpert and cultures negative), IGLM (lobulocentric, neutrophil-rich, looser granulomas), foreign-body reaction and GPA are not favoured. Sarcoid-like granulomatous reactions can occur adjacent to or draining carcinoma or lymphoma, so radiology-pathology concordance and follow-up imaging are advised. No malignancy is seen in these cores.

containers.text: Received four grey-white cores, 1.0–1.5 cm long.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A2.

diagnoses.name: Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis of Breast
diagnoses.path: Breast/01 Mastitis/04 Immune Mediated and Systemic Mastitis

micro.text: Cores show irregular, geographic zones of 'dirty' basophilic necrosis containing neutrophilic nuclear debris, bordered by palisading epithelioid histiocytes and scattered multinucleated giant cells. The surrounding mixed inflammatory infiltrate includes neutrophils, lymphocytes, plasma cells and eosinophils, with neutrophilic microabscesses.

Several small arteries and veins show necrotising vasculitis, with transmural inflammation, fibrinoid necrosis and disruption of the elastic lamina (highlighted on EVG). No well-formed sarcoid-type granulomas, caseation of tuberculous type, organisms or foreign material. Residual lobules are entrapped; no atypia or malignancy.
Special Stains, IHC and Microbiology:
Elastic van Gieson: Destruction of the elastic lamina in small vessels (vasculitis)
Ziehl–Neelsen: No acid-fast bacilli
GMS / PAS: No fungal elements
Gram stain: No bacteria
GeneXpert MTB/RIF Ultra: MTB NOT detected
Bacterial, mycobacterial and fungal cultures: No growth (final)
Serum ANCA (received after biopsy): c-ANCA (cytoplasmic) positive on IIF; anti-PR3 152 IU/mL (positive); anti-MPO negative
Pan-cytokeratin (AE1/AE3): Highlights entrapped benign epithelium only

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast mass, core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Necrotising granulomatous inflammation with geographic basophilic necrosis, palisading histiocytes, giant cells and necrotising small-vessel vasculitis; special stains, GeneXpert and cultures negative. With PR3/c-ANCA positivity and sinonasal, pulmonary and renal involvement, consistent with granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) of the breast. No evidence of malignancy.

comment.text: Breast involvement by GPA is rare and may be the presenting feature. It mimics carcinoma or abscess clinically. The triad of geographic necrosis, granulomatous inflammation and vasculitis, with infection excluded (tuberculosis and fungi in particular), supports the diagnosis in the right clinical and serological context. Differentials include tuberculosis, fungal infection, IGLM, sarcoidosis and other vasculitides (eosinophilic GPA, polyarteritis nodosa). Urgent rheumatology/nephrology referral is advised given renal involvement. No malignancy.

containers.text: Received five grey-white to tan cores with yellow friable areas, 0.8–1.6 cm long.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A3, with levels.

diagnoses.name: Fibrocystic Change, Non-proliferative
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/01 Benign Epithelial Proliferations

micro.text: Cores show fibrous stroma with multiple variably dilated ducts and cysts. Cysts are lined by flattened attenuated epithelium or by apocrine cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm, apical snouts and round, uniform nuclei with small nucleoli (apocrine metaplasia without atypia). Some cysts contain foamy histiocytes and proteinaceous secretion. There is mild duct ectasia and dense stromal fibrosis.

Lobules show mild adenosis without sclerosis. There is no epithelial hyperplasia beyond two cell layers, no columnar cell lesion and no atypia. A few calcium oxalate crystals (birefringent under polarised light) are present in an apocrine cyst. No in situ or invasive carcinoma.

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast, core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Fibrocystic change: cysts with apocrine metaplasia without atypia, duct ectasia and stromal fibrosis. Non-proliferative. No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Fibrocystic change without epithelial proliferation does not increase breast cancer risk. Calcium oxalate (weddellite) crystals, typical of apocrine cysts, are colourless and need polarisation to be seen. If calcifications were the target, check that the specimen radiograph shows them. Atypical apocrine lesions, papilloma within a cyst and intracystic carcinoma were considered and are not present. Imaging is concordant; return to routine care.

containers.text: Received four grey-white to tan fibrous cores, 0.8–1.5 cm long.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A2.

diagnoses.name: Usual Ductal Hyperplasia, Florid
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/01 Benign Epithelial Proliferations

micro.text: Several ducts and TDLUs are filled and distended by a florid epithelial proliferation with irregular, slit-like, peripherally placed fenestrations. The cells are heterogeneous, with overlapping, oval to spindled nuclei that vary in size and shape and stream in parallel with the long axis of the bridges. Bridges are thin and stretched, and nuclei are unevenly distributed. Scattered myoepithelial and apocrine cells are admixed. No rigid cribriform spaces, monotonous cell population or micropapillae.
Calcifications are present within secretions in the hyperplastic ducts and in the adjacent stroma. Background shows fibrocystic change. No atypia, in situ or invasive carcinoma.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
CK5/6: Mosaic (heterogeneous) positivity in the proliferating cells
ER: Heterogeneous: variable intensity in a minority of cells
p63: Myoepithelial cells retained at the periphery of involved ducts

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast, stereotactic vacuum-assisted biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Florid usual ductal hyperplasia with associated microcalcifications; fibrocystic change. No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: The heterogeneous cell population, streaming, irregular peripheral fenestrations, mosaic CK5/6 and heterogeneous ER support UDH. Atypical ductal hyperplasia and low-grade DCIS show monotonous cells, rigid architecture, diffuse strong ER and CK5/6 negativity. The target calcifications are explained, so no further surgery is needed.

containers.text: Received twelve tan-yellow cores, 1.0–2.0 cm, cores with calcifications submitted separately.

exampleGross.sections: A1 (calcification-containing cores), A2–A3 remaining cores; levels x3.

diagnoses.name: Sclerosing Adenosis
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/01 Benign Epithelial Proliferations

micro.text: Cores show a lobulocentric proliferation of compressed and distorted acini and tubules in a swirling, whorled arrangement within fibrous stroma, more cellular at the centre with elongated, compressed glands at the periphery. A distinct myoepithelial layer surrounds the glands, which have small, inconspicuous lumina. The lobular (organoid) architecture is maintained at low power.

Punctate calcifications are present within gland lumina. There is no cytological atypia, perineural or intravascular pseudo-invasion, columnar cell change or lobular neoplasia. No in situ or invasive carcinoma.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
p63: Nuclear positivity in a continuous myoepithelial layer around all glands
SMMHC: Myoepithelial cells positive around all glands
Calponin: Positive around glands
E-cadherin: Membranous positivity (no lobular neoplasia)

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast, core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Sclerosing adenosis with intraluminal microcalcifications. No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Sclerosing adenosis mimics invasive carcinoma, particularly tubular carcinoma, on imaging and histology. The lobulocentric architecture and an intact myoepithelial layer around all glands on p63/SMMHC/calponin exclude invasion. Atypical ductal hyperplasia, DCIS or lobular neoplasia involving sclerosing adenosis can mimic invasion and were specifically excluded.

containers.text: Received five grey-white cores, 1.0–1.6 cm.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A2; levels x3.

diagnoses.name: Apocrine Adenosis
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/01 Benign Epithelial Proliferations

micro.text: The cores contain a lobulocentric sclerosing adenosis in which most glands are lined by apocrine cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm, apical snouts and round nuclei with single small nucleoli. Nuclei are uniform, without enlargement beyond three times the size of benign apocrine nuclei, prominent multiple nucleoli or necrosis. A myoepithelial layer surrounds the glands.
No atypical apocrine proliferation, apocrine DCIS or invasive carcinoma. No calcifications.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
Androgen receptor (AR): Diffuse nuclear positivity in apocrine cells
GCDFP-15: Positive
ER: Negative in apocrine cells
p63 / SMMHC: Myoepithelial layer retained around glands

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast, core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Apocrine adenosis (sclerosing adenosis with apocrine metaplasia) without atypia. No malignancy.

comment.text: Apocrine cells are normally ER-negative and AR/GCDFP-15-positive, so ER negativity is not a sign of malignancy here. Atypical apocrine adenosis (marked nuclear enlargement, prominent nucleoli) would warrant excision. Apocrine DCIS and invasive apocrine carcinoma are excluded by the absence of atypia and the retained myoepithelial layer.

containers.text: Received four tan cores, 0.9–1.4 cm.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1.

diagnoses.name: Microglandular Adenosis
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/01 Benign Epithelial Proliferations

micro.text: Haphazard, infiltrative proliferation of small, round, uniform glands with open lumina, scattered in fibrous stroma and permeating adipose tissue, without lobulocentric organisation. The glands are lined by a single layer of cuboidal cells with clear to amphophilic vacuolated cytoplasm and bland, round nuclei without nucleoli. Lumina contain dense eosinophilic, PAS-positive, diastase-resistant colloid-like secretion. No myoepithelial layer is identified, but each gland is enclosed by a basement membrane.

There is no atypical microglandular adenosis (no complex architecture, cell stratification or nuclear atypia) and no carcinoma arising in MGA. The biopsy site is identified. All margins are clear; the closest is inferior at 0.7 cm.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
S100: Diffuse strong positivity in glandular cells
ER / PR: Negative
HER2: Score 0
EMA: Negative
p63 / SMMHC / calponin: Negative (no myoepithelial cells)
Laminin / collagen IV: Continuous basement membrane ring around each gland
PAS-D: Luminal secretions positive
Ki-67: About 3%

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast, wire-guided wide local excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Microglandular adenosis, 1.6 cm, without atypia or associated carcinoma (S100+, ER/PR/HER2 negative, myoepithelial markers negative, intact laminin/collagen IV basement membrane). Margins clear (closest 0.7 cm, inferior). Biopsy site present.

comment.text: MGA is a rare, infiltrative glandular proliferation without myoepithelium that mimics tubular carcinoma. Tubular carcinoma is ER-positive, S100-negative, has angulated glands and lacks a basement membrane. Many MGA-associated carcinomas are triple-negative and share genetic alterations, so MGA is regarded as a non-obligate precursor. Complete excision with clear margins is recommended; it has been achieved here.

containers.text: Received an oriented fibrofatty specimen 5.5 x 4.5 x 3.0 cm (short suture superior, long lateral), inked. A 1.7 x 1.3 x 1.2 cm ill-defined, firm, grey-white area containing the biopsy clip lies 0.8 cm from the nearest (inferior) margin.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A8 lesion entirely with margins; A9–A10 margins away from lesion (shaves).

diagnoses.name: Tubular Adenosis
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/01 Benign Epithelial Proliferations

micro.text: The cores show a non-lobulocentric proliferation of elongated, narrow, tortuous tubules, many cut longitudinally, arranged haphazardly in fibrous stroma and focally extending into fat. Tubules are lined by bland luminal cells with a distinct outer myoepithelial layer; some lumina contain eosinophilic secretion and calcifications. No angulated tubules with apical snouts or desmoplastic stroma.
No atypia, in situ or invasive carcinoma.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
p63: Myoepithelial nuclei present around all tubules
Calponin / SMMHC: Positive around tubules
ER: Heterogeneous in luminal cells

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast, core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Tubular adenosis with luminal microcalcifications. No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Tubular adenosis is an uncommon adenosis variant whose haphazard, fat-infiltrating tubules mimic tubular carcinoma and microglandular adenosis. Myoepithelial markers around every tubule exclude tubular carcinoma. Unlike microglandular adenosis, a myoepithelial layer is present. Rare examples harbour DCIS, which is excluded here.

containers.text: Received four grey-white cores, 1.0–1.5 cm.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1; levels x3.

diagnoses.name: Radial Scar
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/01 Benign Epithelial Proliferations

micro.text: The fragments contain a stellate lesion with a central fibroelastotic core containing small, entrapped, distorted tubules, from which ducts and lobules radiate. The radiating ducts show mild usual ductal hyperplasia, cysts, apocrine metaplasia and adenosis. The entrapped glands retain a myoepithelial layer. Reconstructed size about 9 mm.
No atypical ductal hyperplasia, lobular neoplasia, DCIS or invasive (tubular) carcinoma in the entirely examined material.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
p63 / SMMHC: Myoepithelial layer around entrapped central tubules
CK5/6: Mosaic in UDH; myoepithelial cells positive
Elastic van Gieson: Central elastosis

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast, vacuum-assisted excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Radial scar (about 9 mm) with mild usual ductal hyperplasia, adenosis and cysts. No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Radial scars and complex sclerosing lesions mimic carcinoma radiologically and histologically. The central glands are infiltrative-looking but retain myoepithelium, excluding tubular carcinoma. Without atypia, removal by VAE is generally sufficient (NHSBSP B3 pathway). If atypia had been present, surgical excision would be advised.

containers.text: Received multiple cores and fragments of fibrofatty tissue in aggregate 4.0 x 3.0 x 1.5 cm (4.2 g).

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A6.

diagnoses.name: Columnar Cell Change and Columnar Cell Hyperplasia
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/01 Benign Epithelial Proliferations

micro.text: Several TDLUs show variably dilated acini lined by columnar epithelial cells with apical cytoplasmic snouts and luminal secretion. In some, the lining is one to two cell layers thick (columnar cell change). In others, it is stratified to more than two layers with mild crowding and small tufts (columnar cell hyperplasia). Nuclei are ovoid, basally oriented and perpendicular to the basement membrane, with no monotonous rounding, loss of polarity or prominent nucleoli.
Secretory calcifications are present in the lumina of the dilated acini. No flat epithelial atypia, atypical ductal hyperplasia, lobular neoplasia or carcinoma.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
ER: Diffuse positivity in columnar cells
CK5/6: Negative in columnar cells; myoepithelial cells positive

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast, stereotactic vacuum-assisted biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Columnar cell change and columnar cell hyperplasia without atypia, with associated microcalcifications. No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Columnar cell lesions are common in calcification biopsies. Without atypia they carry minimal risk and need no excision. Flat epithelial atypia, defined by low-grade monotonous rounded nuclei with loss of polarity, and the related ADH, lobular neoplasia and tubular carcinoma were specifically looked for and are absent. Like low-grade neoplasia, columnar cell lesions are ER-positive and CK5/6-negative, so this IHC pattern does not on its own indicate atypia.

containers.text: Received ten tan-yellow cores 1.0–1.8 cm; calcification cores submitted separately.

exampleGross.sections: A1 (calcification cores), A2–A3 remaining; levels x3.

micro.text: Several TDLUs show dilated acini lined by one to several layers of columnar to cuboidal cells with low-grade, monotonous, round to ovoid nuclei, evenly spaced, with loss of the normal perpendicular orientation (loss of polarity), slightly increased nuclear-cytoplasmic ratio and inconspicuous to small nucleoli. Apical snouts and luminal secretions with calcifications are present. The atypical cells form flat layers or minimal mounds without complex architecture (no rigid bridges, bars, micropapillae or cribriform spaces).
This is flat epithelial atypia. Adjacent TDLUs show columnar cell change without atypia. No ADH, lobular neoplasia, DCIS or invasive (tubular) carcinoma is seen on multiple levels.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
ER: Diffuse strong positivity in atypical cells
CK5/6: Negative in atypical cells (myoepithelium positive)
E-cadherin: Retained (no lobular neoplasia)

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast, stereotactic vacuum-assisted biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Flat epithelial atypia with associated microcalcifications; background columnar cell change. No ADH, lobular neoplasia or malignancy identified.

comment.text: FEA is a low-risk, non-obligate precursor that is clonally related to low-grade neoplasia. It is often associated with ADH, lobular neoplasia and tubular carcinoma (the 'Rosen triad'). Upgrade on excision is low when FEA is pure and the calcifications have been removed. Management should be decided at MDT: further VAE of the area per NHSBSP B3 guidance, or excision if residual calcifications or discordance.

containers.text: Received twelve tan cores 1.0–2.0 cm; calcification cores separate.

exampleGross.sections: A1 (calcification cores), A2–A4 remaining; levels x3.

micro.text: Two adjacent ducts (in a single core, aggregate extent 1.8 mm) are partially involved by a proliferation of monotonous, evenly spaced small cells with round, uniform, hyperchromatic nuclei. The cells form rigid bridges and punched-out cribriform spaces, with polarisation of cells around the spaces, and a residual population of polarised columnar cells at the periphery. The features are qualitatively those of low-grade DCIS but quantitatively insufficient (partial involvement, two ducts, <2 mm), and are classified as atypical ductal hyperplasia.
Calcifications are present in the atypical proliferation. Background shows columnar cell change and flat epithelial atypia. No necrosis, lobular neoplasia or invasive carcinoma.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
ER: Diffuse strong positivity in the atypical cells
CK5/6: Negative in atypical cells (residual myoepithelium positive)
p63: Myoepithelial layer intact around involved ducts
E-cadherin: Membranous (ductal phenotype)

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast, stereotactic core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Atypical ductal hyperplasia (focal, two ducts, 1.8 mm) with microcalcifications; background columnar cell change and flat epithelial atypia. No in situ or invasive carcinoma in sampled tissue.

comment.text: On a core, ADH may be the edge of a low-grade DCIS. Given residual calcifications, a 1.2 cm target and a B3 lesion with atypia, diagnostic wire-guided excision is recommended. Differential: low-grade DCIS (more than 2 mm or 2 fully involved spaces) and UDH (heterogeneous cells, CK5/6 mosaic). ADH increases the long-term risk of breast cancer in either breast, so MDT discussion of chemoprevention and surveillance is advised.

containers.text: Received six grey-white cores 1.0–1.5 cm.

exampleGross.sections: A1 (calcification cores), A2 remaining; levels x3.

diagnoses.name: Lobular Neoplasia, ALH and Classic LCIS

micro.text: Several lobules are involved by a proliferation of small, uniform, discohesive cells with round nuclei, inconspicuous nucleoli, scant pale cytoplasm and occasional intracytoplasmic vacuoles (type A cells). In some lobules the cells fill and distend more than half of the acini (classic lobular carcinoma in situ, LCIS). In others they partially fill acini without distension (atypical lobular hyperplasia, ALH). Pagetoid spread beneath the native ductal epithelium is seen in an adjacent duct.

There is no pleomorphic or florid LCIS: no marked nuclear pleomorphism, necrosis, or confluent massive acinar expansion. The target calcifications lie in adjacent sclerosing adenosis and benign acini. No invasive lobular or ductal carcinoma.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
E-cadherin: Loss of membranous expression in lobular neoplastic cells (normal luminal and myoepithelial cells retained)
p120 catenin: Diffuse cytoplasmic staining in neoplastic cells (membranous in normal cells)
ER: Diffuse strong positivity
HER2: Score 0
Ki-67: Low (about 2%)
p63: Myoepithelial cells retained around involved acini

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast, stereotactic vacuum-assisted biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Lobular neoplasia: atypical lobular hyperplasia and classic lobular carcinoma in situ (E-cadherin negative, p120 cytoplasmic, ER positive); calcifications in adjacent sclerosing adenosis. No pleomorphic/florid LCIS or invasive carcinoma.

comment.text: Classic lobular neoplasia is both a risk indicator and a non-obligate precursor of invasive lobular carcinoma. When concordant with imaging, as here, surgical excision is not routinely required. Pleomorphic or florid LCIS would need excision to clear margins. E-cadherin loss with cytoplasmic p120 distinguishes lobular from solid low-grade ductal neoplasia. Long-term surveillance and discussion of risk-reducing endocrine therapy are advised.

containers.text: Received twelve tan cores 1.0–2.0 cm; calcification cores separate.

exampleGross.sections: A1 (calcification cores), A2–A4 remaining; levels x3.

micro.text: A dilated large duct contains an arborising papillary lesion with fibrovascular cores covered by an inner luminal epithelial layer and an outer myoepithelial layer throughout. There is mild usual ductal hyperplasia between fronds and focal apocrine metaplasia. Focal stromal sclerosis and haemorrhage are present at the base. No monotonous cell population, cribriform or micropapillary atypical proliferation, or loss of myoepithelium.
The surrounding duct wall shows no invasion or entrapped glands. The duct margins at both ends are free of papilloma.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
p63: Continuous myoepithelial layer along fibrovascular cores and duct wall
CK5/6: Mosaic positivity in epithelium; myoepithelium positive
ER: Heterogeneous

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast, microdochectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Intraductal papilloma (central, solitary), 1.0 cm, without atypia, with mild usual ductal hyperplasia. Completely excised. No malignancy.

comment.text: A central papilloma is the commonest cause of single-duct bloodstained discharge. With no atypia and complete excision, no further treatment is needed. Papilloma with ADH or DCIS (monotonous cells, CK5/6 negative, ER diffuse) and encapsulated or solid papillary carcinoma (no myoepithelium within fronds) were excluded.

containers.text: Received a cone of subareolar tissue 3.5 x 2.0 x 1.5 cm with a lacrimal probe in a duct. Opening along the probe reveals a dilated duct containing a friable, tan, papillary lesion 1.0 x 0.7 x 0.6 cm, attached to the duct wall at one point.

exampleGross.sections: A1 nipple-end margin; A2–A5 papilloma with duct (entire); A6 deep end.

micro.text: Multiple papillomas are present in peripheral (TDLU-related) ducts over a 2.8 cm area, each with fibrovascular cores lined by luminal and myoepithelial cells, accompanied by UDH and sclerosing adenosis. Within one papilloma, a focus of monotonous, evenly spaced cells with round nuclei forms rigid bridges and cribriform spaces, measuring 2 mm in greatest extent. This is papilloma with atypical ductal hyperplasia; under WHO criteria a focus ≥3 mm would be classified as papilloma with DCIS.

Calcifications are present in the papillomas. There is no DCIS outside the papillomas and no invasive carcinoma. All margins clear; closest anterior 0.4 cm (benign papilloma); ADH focus 1.2 cm from the nearest margin. Biopsy site present.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
CK5/6: Negative in the atypical focus; mosaic in the remaining papilloma epithelium
ER: Diffuse strong in atypical focus; heterogeneous elsewhere
p63: Myoepithelial cells present along cores, including beneath the atypical focus

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast, wire-guided excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Multiple peripheral intraductal papillomas (over 2.8 cm), one with atypical ductal hyperplasia (focus 2 mm), with associated calcifications. No DCIS or invasive carcinoma. Margins clear.

comment.text: Peripheral papillomas are more often multiple and associated with atypia, DCIS or invasive carcinoma than central papillomas, and carry higher recurrence and risk. WHO 5th edition classifies an atypical low-grade ductal proliferation within a papilloma as ADH when it is under 3 mm, and as papilloma with DCIS when it is 3 mm or more. The atypical focus here is 2 mm and has been completely excised.

containers.text: Received an oriented fibrofatty specimen 6.0 x 5.0 x 3.0 cm, inked. Multiple small tan papillary nodules (0.3–0.7 cm) are seen in dilated ducts over a 3.0 cm area; biopsy cavity with clip. Closest margin (anterior) 0.5 cm.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A12 entire lesional area with margins; A13–A14 shave margins.

micro.text: A well-circumscribed, pushing lesion composed of closely packed, uniform, small round tubules with small lumina, lined by a single layer of bland luminal epithelial cells and an outer myoepithelial layer. There is scant intervening stroma containing small vessels and a few lymphocytes. A thin fibrous pseudocapsule is present. Focal areas at the edge show fibroadenoma-like stroma.
No atypia, mitotic activity of note, necrosis or carcinoma.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
p63: Myoepithelial cells around all tubules
CK5/6: Myoepithelial cells positive; luminal cells negative

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast lump, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Tubular adenoma, 2.5 cm. No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Tubular adenoma is a benign, well-circumscribed adenoma of young women. It may be related to fibroadenoma (transitional areas are common) and is treated by simple excision. Differentials include fibroadenoma (more stroma), lactating adenoma (secretory change) and tubular carcinoma (infiltrative angulated tubules without myoepithelium).

containers.text: Received an oval, well-circumscribed nodule 2.5 x 2.0 x 1.6 cm with smooth outer surface. Cut surface is homogeneous, tan-yellow, soft and slightly lobulated, without slit-like spaces.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A5 representative sections including capsule.

micro.text: The cores show a lobulated, circumscribed proliferation of closely packed acini and tubules showing marked secretory (lactational) change: cuboidal cells with abundant vacuolated cytoplasm, hobnail nuclei protruding into lumina and abundant intraluminal secretion. Myoepithelial cells are attenuated but present. Scant intervening stroma.

One core shows an area of coagulative (infarct-type) necrosis with ghost outlines of glands and surrounding haemorrhage, a recognised change in lactating adenoma. No nuclear pleomorphism, atypical mitoses or carcinoma.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
p63: Attenuated but present myoepithelial layer
Ki-67: Moderately increased (about 10%), in keeping with lactation
Pan-cytokeratin: Ghost glands in infarcted area outlined

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast mass, core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Lactating adenoma with focal infarction. No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Lactating adenoma arises in pregnancy or lactation and may represent a tubular adenoma or fibroadenoma with superimposed secretory change. Infarction can cause pain and a suspicious imaging appearance. Pregnancy-associated breast carcinoma must be excluded; there is no pleomorphism or invasion here. Hobnail lactational cells should not be mistaken for atypia.

containers.text: Received four soft, tan-pink cores, 1.0–1.5 cm.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1.

micro.text: A well-circumscribed nodule lies within a duct whose wall forms a thick fibrous capsule. It consists of compressed and distorted tubules and glands embedded in a dense, central, hyalinised and partly calcified fibrous stroma. Glands are lined by bland luminal cells, frequently showing apocrine metaplasia, with an outer myoepithelial layer. At the periphery, entrapped glands within the capsule mimic invasion but retain myoepithelial cells. Residual papillary fronds are seen focally.
No atypia, DCIS or invasive carcinoma. Margins clear (closest 0.3 cm).
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
p63 / SMMHC: Myoepithelial layer around all glands, including entrapped peripheral glands
CK5/6: Mosaic; myoepithelium positive
ER: Heterogeneous; apocrine cells negative
AR / GCDFP-15: Apocrine cells positive

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast nodule, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Ductal adenoma, 1.3 cm, with apocrine metaplasia and central sclerosis. No atypia or malignancy. Margins clear.

comment.text: Ductal adenoma is a well-circumscribed benign glandular proliferation within a duct. It is closely related to, and may represent, a sclerosed intraductal papilloma. Entrapped glands in the thick sclerotic wall can mimic invasive carcinoma, but they keep myoepithelial cells. Apocrine cells with nucleoli should not be over-called as atypia.

containers.text: Received a fibrofatty specimen 3.5 x 3.0 x 2.0 cm containing a firm, white, well-circumscribed nodule 1.3 x 1.2 x 1.0 cm with a thick fibrous rim and gritty centre. Closest margin 0.3 cm.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A4 nodule entirely with margins.

micro.text: A well-circumscribed, lobulated tumour composed of ducts and tubules lined by luminal epithelial cells, surrounded by and merging with sheets and cords of myoepithelial cells (plasmacytoid, spindled and clear), which blend into abundant chondromyxoid stroma. There are foci of mature hyaline cartilage, with focal ossification and calcification. Myoepithelial cells show no significant atypia.

There are no mitoses beyond 1 per 10 HPF, no necrosis and no infiltrative growth. No carcinomatous component (no atypical epithelial nests or matrix-producing metaplastic carcinoma). Margins clear, closest 0.4 cm.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
CK7 / CAM5.2: Luminal ductal cells positive
p63 / SOX10 / S100: Myoepithelial and stromal-merging cells positive
SMA / calponin: Myoepithelial cells positive
PLAG1: Nuclear positivity in myoepithelial component
ER: Focal in luminal cells
Ki-67: About 2%

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast subareolar mass, wide local excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Pleomorphic adenoma (benign mixed tumour), 1.9 cm, with chondroid metaplasia and ossification. No atypia or malignancy. Margins clear (closest 0.4 cm).

comment.text: Pleomorphic adenoma of the breast is rare, usually subareolar, and morphologically identical to its salivary counterpart. On core biopsy it can be mistaken for matrix-producing metaplastic carcinoma. Circumscription, bland cytology, low proliferation and PLAG1 expression support the diagnosis. Other differentials are adenomyoepithelioma and mucinous carcinoma. Complete excision with clear margins is recommended.

containers.text: Received a fibrofatty specimen 4.5 x 4.0 x 3.0 cm containing a lobulated, firm, glistening grey-white to bluish nodule 1.9 x 1.6 x 1.5 cm with a gritty area. Closest margin 0.4 cm.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A6 nodule entirely with margins.

micro.text: A lobulated, circumscribed biphasic tumour composed of tubules and glands lined by luminal epithelial cells, surrounded by a prominent proliferation of polygonal myoepithelial cells with clear to eosinophilic cytoplasm forming solid nests and sheets, separated by fibrous septa. Some areas show papillary (intraductal papilloma-like) and tubular growth patterns.

Myoepithelial cells are cytologically bland; mitoses up to 1 per 10 HPF (0.4 per mm²); no necrosis, marked atypia, infiltrative border or carcinomatous overgrowth. Margins clear (closest deep 0.6 cm).
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
CK7 / EMA: Luminal cells positive
ER: Positive in luminal cells (about 70%)
p63 / SMA / calponin / CK5/6: Myoepithelial cells positive
S100: Myoepithelial cells patchy positive
Ki-67: About 3%

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast mass, wide local excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Adenomyoepithelioma, benign, 2.2 cm, tubular and papillary patterns, without atypia or carcinoma. Margins clear (closest 0.6 cm).

comment.text: Adenomyoepithelioma is a biphasic tumour of luminal and myoepithelial cells. ER-positive AMEs often harbour PIK3CA/AKT1 mutations. ER-negative AMEs more often have HRAS Q61 mutations and a greater risk of malignant transformation. The distinction from malignant AME (AME with carcinoma) depends on atypia, mitoses, necrosis and infiltration, none of which are present. Differentials include intraductal papilloma with myoepithelial hyperplasia, pleomorphic adenoma and adenoid cystic carcinoma. Complete excision is recommended.

containers.text: Received an oriented fibrofatty specimen 5.0 x 4.5 x 3.5 cm, inked, containing a lobulated, firm, tan-white mass 2.2 x 2.0 x 1.8 cm. Closest margin (deep) 0.6 cm.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A8 mass entirely with margins.

diagnoses.name: Nipple Adenoma
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/06 Tumours of the Nipple

micro.text: Beneath the nipple epidermis is a well-demarcated proliferation of ducts showing florid papillomatosis with florid usual ductal hyperplasia, adenosis with compressed glands and areas of sclerosing papillomatosis with pseudo-infiltrative glands in a sclerotic stroma. A myoepithelial layer is present around ducts and glands. Squamous cysts are seen near the surface, where ductal epithelium replaces the eroded epidermis and extends onto the skin surface.
There are no Paget cells in the adjacent epidermis, no atypia, necrosis, DCIS or invasive carcinoma. The deep margin is involved focally by benign papillomatosis (0 mm); peripheral margins clear.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
p63 / CK5/6: Myoepithelial layer around glands; CK5/6 mosaic in UDH
CK7: Glandular epithelium positive; no intraepidermal (Paget) cells
ER: Heterogeneous
HER2: Not required (no atypia)

finalDiagnosis.label: Right nipple, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Nipple adenoma (florid papillomatosis of the nipple), 0.8 cm, with surface erosion. No atypia, Paget disease or malignancy. Deep margin focally involved by benign lesion.

comment.text: Nipple adenoma causes erosion and discharge that mimic Paget disease clinically. Pseudo-infiltrative glands in the sclerosing areas mimic invasive carcinoma. Retained myoepithelium and the absence of intraepidermal CK7-positive Paget cells exclude these. Syringomatous tumour (infiltrative tubules and squamous nests in nipple stroma) is the other differential. A benign involved margin carries a small recurrence risk.

containers.text: Received a wedge of nipple skin and subcutaneous tissue 1.5 x 1.2 x 1.0 cm, with an eroded red skin surface 0.6 cm. Cut surface: a firm, grey-white, 0.8 cm nodule beneath the eroded epidermis, 0.1 cm from the deep margin.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A3 (perpendicular to skin, margins inked).

diagnoses.name: Syringomatous Tumour of Nipple
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/06 Tumours of the Nipple

micro.text: An ill-defined, infiltrative proliferation of small tubules, cords and nests, many comma- or tadpole-shaped, with occasional keratinous (squamous) cysts. It infiltrates the dermis, the smooth muscle bundles of the nipple and the subareolar stroma, with focal perineural infiltration, in a desmoplastic to sclerotic stroma. The tubules are lined by two cell layers in many places: inner cuboidal cells and outer basaloid/squamoid cells. Cytology is bland, mitoses are rare and there is no necrosis.
No DCIS. The lesion does not involve breast lobules beyond the subareolar region. All margins clear (closest deep 0.2 cm).
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
p63 / CK5/6: Outer layer of tubules and squamous nests positive
ER / PR: Negative
CK7: Inner luminal cells positive
HER2: Score 0
Ki-67: About 3%
CEA / EMA: Highlight lumina

finalDiagnosis.label: Left nipple-areolar complex, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Syringomatous tumour of the nipple, 1.3 cm, infiltrating nipple smooth muscle with perineural involvement. No carcinoma. Margins clear (closest deep 0.2 cm).

comment.text: Syringomatous tumour is a locally infiltrative but non-metastasising tumour of the nipple-areolar region. It recurs if incompletely excised. It is morphologically similar to low-grade adenosquamous carcinoma, which arises in breast parenchyma rather than the nipple. Tubular carcinoma (ER-positive, no p63-positive cells, no squamous elements) and nipple adenoma (circumscribed, true myoepithelium) are the main differentials. Clear margins are recommended; the close deep margin warrants clinical follow-up.

containers.text: Received a nipple-areolar complex with subareolar tissue, 4.0 x 3.5 x 2.5 cm, oriented, inked. Beneath the nipple is a firm, ill-defined, grey-white lesion 1.3 x 1.0 x 1.0 cm extending into subareolar tissue; closest margin (deep) 0.3 cm.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A6 lesion entirely with margins; A7 areolar skin margins.

diagnoses.name: Fibroadenoma
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/07 Fibroepithelial Tumours and Hamartomas

micro.text: The cores show a biphasic fibroepithelial lesion with both intracanalicular (ducts compressed into slit-like, curvilinear spaces) and pericanalicular (ducts with open lumina surrounded by stroma) patterns. The ducts are lined by bland luminal and myoepithelial cells. The stroma is uniformly distributed, of low to moderate cellularity, with no atypia, no stromal mitoses and no periductal stromal condensation or leaf-like fronds.
Complex features are absent: no cysts >3 mm, sclerosing adenosis, epithelial calcifications or papillary apocrine change. No atypia or malignancy.

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast mass, core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Fibroadenoma (simple). No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Fibroadenoma is the commonest benign breast tumour of young women. A complex fibroadenoma has cysts over 3 mm, sclerosing adenosis, epithelial calcifications or papillary apocrine change; it carries a slightly higher long-term risk and is more common in older patients. None of these are present. On a core, phyllodes tumour cannot always be excluded: stromal hypercellularity, mitoses, stromal overgrowth or leaf-like architecture would warrant a B3 category and excision, and none are seen.

containers.text: Received three grey-white, firm cores, 1.2–1.6 cm.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1.

diagnoses.name: Juvenile (Cellular) Fibroadenoma
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/07 Fibroepithelial Tumours and Hamartomas

micro.text: A well-circumscribed fibroepithelial tumour with a predominantly pericanalicular pattern. The stroma is uniformly and diffusely hypercellular, composed of bland spindle cells without nuclear atypia, with 1 mitosis per 10 HPF (0.4 per mm²), and no periductal condensation, stromal overgrowth or leaf-like architecture. The ducts show florid epithelial hyperplasia with a gynaecomastoid (micropapillary, tapering) pattern, lined by luminal and myoepithelial cells.
No necrosis, heterologous elements or infiltrative border. No atypia or malignancy.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
Ki-67 (stroma): About 3%
CD34: Stromal cells positive (non-specific)
p63: Myoepithelial cells intact

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast mass, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Juvenile (cellular) fibroadenoma, 7.2 cm (105 g), with gynaecomastoid epithelial hyperplasia. No features of phyllodes tumour. No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Juvenile fibroadenoma occurs mainly in adolescents. It may grow rapidly and become large ('giant' if over 5 cm or 500 g), but it remains benign. The main differential is benign phyllodes tumour: a pericanalicular pattern, uniform rather than periductally accentuated stromal cellularity, few mitoses, and no stromal overgrowth or leaf-like fronds favour juvenile fibroadenoma. Simple enucleation is adequate.

containers.text: Received a well-circumscribed, encapsulated, ovoid mass 7.2 x 6.0 x 4.5 cm, 105 g. Cut surface is bulging, tan-white, homogeneous and fleshy, without clefts, haemorrhage or necrosis.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A10 (one block per cm of maximum dimension plus capsule).

diagnoses.name: Phyllodes Tumour, Benign
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/07 Fibroepithelial Tumours and Hamartomas

micro.text: A fibroepithelial tumour with exaggerated intracanalicular, leaf-like architecture, with fronds of stroma covered by bilayered epithelium projecting into cleft-like spaces. The stroma shows mild hypercellularity with periepithelial (subepithelial) condensation and mild nuclear atypia. Mitoses number 1.5 per mm² (about 3 per 10 HPF of 0.5 mm diameter) in the most active areas. There is no stromal overgrowth (stroma without epithelium in a ×4 objective field) and no malignant heterologous elements. The border is well defined and pushing.
Margins clear; closest superior 0.2 cm.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
Ki-67 (stroma): About 5% (hotspot 8%)
CD34: Stromal cells positive
Pan-cytokeratin / p63: Negative in stroma (excludes metaplastic carcinoma); epithelium/myoepithelium positive

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast mass, wide local excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Phyllodes tumour, benign (WHO 5th edition criteria), 5.4 cm. Margins clear (closest superior 0.2 cm).

comment.text: WHO 5th edition grades phyllodes tumours on border, stromal cellularity, atypia, mitoses and overgrowth. Benign tumours have mild cellularity and atypia, fewer than 2.5 mitoses/mm², no overgrowth and a well-defined border. Borderline tumours have 2.5 to under 5 mitoses/mm² and/or focal permeation. Malignant tumours have 5 or more mitoses/mm², marked atypia and overgrowth. Cellular fibroadenoma is the main differential; leaf-like architecture and periepithelial condensation favour phyllodes here. Clear margins are adequate for benign PT; re-excision of close margins is not usually required.

containers.text: Received an oriented specimen 8.0 x 7.0 x 5.0 cm, inked, containing a well-circumscribed, lobulated, firm, tan-white mass 5.4 x 4.8 x 4.0 cm with a bulging whorled cut surface and leaf-like clefts. No haemorrhage or necrosis. Closest margin (superior) 0.3 cm.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A12 mass (one block per cm plus all interfaces with margins).

diagnoses.name: Hamartoma of Breast
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/07 Fibroepithelial Tumours and Hamartomas

micro.text: A well-circumscribed, encapsulated lesion composed of a disorganised mixture of normal-appearing breast elements: lobules, ducts, dense fibrous stroma and mature adipose tissue in varying proportions. The lobules are well formed and separated by fibrous stroma, in contrast to the surrounding breast. There are areas of pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia, fibrocystic change and focal apocrine metaplasia.
No fibroadenomatous or phyllodes architecture, smooth muscle bundles, epithelial atypia or malignancy.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
p63: Myoepithelium intact around lobules and ducts
CD34: Stromal/PASH cells positive
Desmin / SMA: No smooth muscle bundles (not myoid hamartoma)

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast mass, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Breast hamartoma, 4.2 cm, with pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia and fibrocystic change. No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Breast hamartoma is a circumscribed mass of disorganised normal breast components. It is best recognised radiologically ('breast within a breast'), and core biopsy is often non-diagnostic because it shows normal-looking tissue. Differentials include fibroadenoma, phyllodes tumour, lipoma and PASH. Multiple hamartomas should prompt consideration of Cowden (PTEN hamartoma tumour) syndrome. Any carcinoma arising in a hamartoma is reported as such; none is present.

containers.text: Received a well-circumscribed, ovoid mass with a thin capsule 4.2 x 3.5 x 2.5 cm. Cut surface is variegated with yellow fatty areas and grey-white fibrous areas.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A6 representative sections including capsule.

diagnoses.name: Myoid Hamartoma of Breast
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/07 Fibroepithelial Tumours and Hamartomas

micro.text: A circumscribed lesion composed of breast lobules and ducts, fibrous stroma and fat, admixed with prominent interlacing bundles of mature smooth muscle cells. These cells have eosinophilic fibrillary cytoplasm and blunt-ended, cigar-shaped nuclei, without atypia, mitoses or necrosis. The smooth muscle bundles surround and separate lobules.
Glandular elements have intact myoepithelium and show focal apocrine metaplasia. No atypia or malignancy.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
Desmin: Smooth muscle bundles positive
h-caldesmon / SMA: Positive
CD34: Negative in smooth muscle (against myofibroblastoma)
p63: Negative in smooth muscle bundles (not myoepithelial); positive in ductal myoepithelium
ER / PR: Positive in smooth muscle and epithelium

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast mass, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Myoid hamartoma, 2.7 cm. No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Myoid hamartoma is a hamartoma variant with prominent smooth muscle; the origin of the muscle is debated (vascular or myoepithelial). Differentials: leiomyoma (no glandular elements), myofibroblastoma (CD34-positive, desmin-positive spindle cells with collagen bands), adenomyoepithelioma (p63-positive myoepithelial proliferation) and fibroadenoma or phyllodes tumour with smooth muscle metaplasia. Excision is curative.

containers.text: Received a firm, well-circumscribed mass 2.7 x 2.3 x 2.0 cm with a whorled, grey-white cut surface and scattered yellow fat.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A5 lesion entirely.

diagnoses.name: Pseudoangiomatous Stromal Hyperplasia (Tumoral PASH)
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/08 Mesenchymal Tumours and Tumour-like Lesions

micro.text: Dense, collagenous, keloid-like stroma contains a complex network of anastomosing, empty, slit-like pseudovascular spaces. They are lined by discontinuous, bland, flat spindle cells (myofibroblasts) and contain no red blood cells. The spaces separate lobules and ducts without destroying them. Some areas show fascicular myofibroblastic proliferation. No nuclear atypia, mitoses, endothelial tufting, dissection of fat, or necrosis.
Lobules and ducts are benign with intact myoepithelium. No atypia or malignancy.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
CD34: Lining spindle cells positive
PR: Positive in spindle cells
SMA: Patchy positive
CD31 / ERG: Negative in cells lining slit-like spaces (not endothelial)
D2-40: Negative

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast mass, core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia (tumoral PASH). No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: PASH is a hormonally responsive myofibroblastic stromal proliferation, often incidental, occasionally forming a mass (tumoral PASH). The main differential is low-grade angiosarcoma, which has true vascular channels containing red cells, dissects fat and lobules, and is CD31/ERG-positive. Myofibroblastoma and phyllodes stroma are other differentials. PASH is benign; follow-up is appropriate if concordant.

containers.text: Received four firm, white cores 1.2–1.7 cm.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1.

diagnoses.name: Myofibroblastoma of Breast
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/08 Mesenchymal Tumours and Tumour-like Lesions

micro.text: A well-circumscribed, pushing tumour composed of bland, uniform spindle cells arranged in short, haphazard fascicles separated by thick, hyalinised collagen bands, with interspersed mature adipocytes. Nuclei are oval with fine chromatin; no significant atypia, mitoses (<1 per 10 HPF) or necrosis. There is a mild mast cell infiltrate.
No breast ducts or lobules are entrapped within the lesion (male breast). No malignancy.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
CD34: Diffuse positive
Desmin: Diffuse positive
ER / PR / AR: Positive
Rb (retinoblastoma protein): Loss of nuclear expression (13q14 deletion surrogate)
SMA: Focal
STAT6: Negative (against solitary fibrous tumour)
Pan-cytokeratin / p63: Negative (excludes spindle cell metaplastic carcinoma)
S100: Negative
β-catenin: Cytoplasmic only (against fibromatosis)

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast (male) mass, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Myofibroblastoma, 2.9 cm (CD34+, desmin+, Rb loss). No malignancy.

comment.text: Mammary myofibroblastoma most often occurs in older men and postmenopausal women. It belongs to the 13q/Rb-deleted family with spindle cell lipoma and cellular angiofibroma. Variants (epithelioid, lipomatous, myxoid, infiltrative) can cause diagnostic difficulty. Differentials: spindle cell metaplastic carcinoma (keratin/p63-positive), solitary fibrous tumour (STAT6), fibromatosis (nuclear β-catenin), PASH and schwannoma (S100). Excision is curative.

containers.text: Received a well-circumscribed, unencapsulated, firm, rubbery mass 2.9 x 2.4 x 2.0 cm with a whorled, grey-pink cut surface and yellow flecks.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A5 lesion entirely.

diagnoses.name: Angiolipoma of Breast
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/08 Mesenchymal Tumours and Tumour-like Lesions

micro.text: A thinly encapsulated lesion of mature adipocytes of uniform size, admixed with clusters of small, capillary-sized, thin-walled vessels, more numerous at the subcapsular periphery (vascular component about 25%). Many capillaries contain fibrin microthrombi. Endothelial cells are flat and bland, without multilayering, mitoses or atypia.
The lesion is subcutaneous and does not involve breast parenchyma. No lipoblasts, atypical stromal cells or malignancy.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
CD31 / ERG: Capillary endothelium positive
MDM2: Negative (no atypical lipomatous features)

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast subcutaneous nodule, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Angiolipoma, 1.7 cm, completely excised. No malignancy.

comment.text: Angiolipoma is a benign, often tender subcutaneous lipoma variant with capillaries containing characteristic fibrin thrombi. A conventional lipoma lacks the vascular component. Within breast parenchyma, the key differential is well-differentiated angiosarcoma, which is infiltrative, dissects lobules and fat, and shows endothelial atypia and, when radiation-associated, MYC amplification. Atypical lipomatous tumour (MDM2) is excluded.

containers.text: Received an encapsulated, ovoid, yellow nodule 1.7 x 1.3 x 1.0 cm with a thin capsule. Cut surface is yellow with red-tan speckled areas, more prominent at the periphery.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A3 nodule entirely.

diagnoses.name: Cavernous Haemangioma and Perilobular Haemangioma
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/08 Mesenchymal Tumours and Tumour-like Lesions

micro.text: A well-circumscribed lesion composed of dilated, thin-walled, congested vascular channels of varying size (cavernous pattern), lined by a single layer of flat, bland endothelium, separated by fibrous septa. Some channels contain organising thrombi with phleboliths (calcifications). There is no anastomosing network, endothelial multilayering, tufting, nuclear atypia, mitoses or dissection of breast lobules or fat.
Separately, an incidental perilobular haemangioma (1.5 mm, a microscopic cluster of small capillaries in and around a lobule) is present. Margins clear.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
CD31 / ERG: Endothelium positive
MYC: Negative
Ki-67: Very low in endothelium (<2%)
D2-40: Negative (blood vascular)

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast, wire-guided excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Cavernous haemangioma, 0.9 cm, with thrombosis and phleboliths; incidental perilobular haemangioma (1.5 mm). No atypia or malignancy. Margins clear.

comment.text: Benign vascular lesions of the breast include perilobular haemangioma, which is microscopic and usually incidental, haemangiomas (capillary, cavernous, venous) and angiomatosis. Because a well-differentiated angiosarcoma can look deceptively bland on a core, vascular lesions on core are usually excised. Small size, circumscription, no anastomosing or dissecting channels, no endothelial atypia and MYC negativity support a benign diagnosis.

containers.text: Received an oriented fibrofatty specimen 4.0 x 3.5 x 2.5 cm, inked, containing a circumscribed, dark red, spongy nodule 0.9 x 0.8 x 0.6 cm with biopsy track. Closest margin 0.8 cm.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A4 nodule entirely; A5–A6 surrounding tissue.

diagnoses.name: Atypical Vascular Lesion, Post-radiotherapy
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/08 Mesenchymal Tumours and Tumour-like Lesions

micro.text: The superficial and mid dermis contains a circumscribed, wedge-shaped proliferation of thin-walled, dilated, anastomosing vascular channels, some with a lymphatic appearance and small papillary projections, lined by a single layer of flat to slightly hobnailed endothelial cells. There is no endothelial multilayering, no significant nuclear atypia or hyperchromasia, no mitoses, no dissection of collagen bundles into the deep dermis or subcutis, and no haemorrhage or 'blood lakes'.

Background shows radiation dermatitis (dermal fibrosis, atypical radiation fibroblasts, telangiectasia). Both papules show the same appearance. Margins clear (closest 0.4 cm). No angiosarcoma and no recurrent carcinoma.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
CD31 / ERG: Endothelium positive
D2-40 (podoplanin): Positive (lymphatic phenotype)
MYC (IHC): Negative in endothelial nuclei
MYC FISH: Not amplified (MYC/CEP8 ratio 1.0)
Pan-cytokeratin: Negative (no recurrent carcinoma)

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast skin (irradiated field), excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Atypical vascular lesion, lymphatic type, two papules (3 and 4 mm), MYC negative by IHC and FISH. No angiosarcoma. Margins clear.

comment.text: Atypical vascular lesions arise in irradiated skin, usually 3 to 6 years after radiotherapy. They are small, superficial and circumscribed, and lack MYC amplification. Post-radiation angiosarcoma, by contrast, is typically larger, infiltrative and multilayered, with atypia, mitoses and MYC amplification or overexpression in most cases. AVLs are mostly benign, but a small risk of progression and overlap with well-differentiated angiosarcoma justify complete excision and close follow-up.

containers.text: Received an ellipse of skin 3.0 x 1.2 cm with subcutis to 0.8 cm, bearing two pink-tan papules (0.3 and 0.4 cm), 0.4 cm apart; closest peripheral margin 0.5 cm.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A4 (transverse, margins inked).

diagnoses.name: Granular Cell Tumour of Breast
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/08 Mesenchymal Tumours and Tumour-like Lesions

micro.text: An infiltrative, poorly circumscribed tumour composed of sheets, nests and cords of large polygonal cells with abundant, coarsely granular eosinophilic cytoplasm and small, round, centrally placed nuclei. The cells infiltrate between breast lobules, fat and around small nerves, with desmoplastic stroma. Pustulo-ovoid bodies of Milian are present. No overlying pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia (deep location).

Fanburg-Smith criteria (necrosis, spindling, vesicular nuclei with large nucleoli, mitoses >2/10 HPF at ×200, high N:C ratio, pleomorphism): none present (0/6), so benign. Margins clear (closest anterior 0.3 cm).
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
S100: Diffuse strong (nuclear and cytoplasmic)
SOX10: Diffuse nuclear
CD68: Granular cytoplasmic positivity
Inhibin-α: Positive
PAS-D: Cytoplasmic granules positive (diastase-resistant)
Pan-cytokeratin / ER: Negative (excludes carcinoma, including apocrine carcinoma)

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast mass, wide local excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Granular cell tumour, benign (0 of 6 Fanburg-Smith criteria), 1.6 cm. Margins clear (closest 0.3 cm).

comment.text: Granular cell tumour is a Schwann cell-derived neoplasm that often arises from intramammary cutaneous nerve branches. Clinically and radiologically it closely mimics carcinoma: hard, spiculated, with skin retraction. Keratin negativity with S100/SOX10/inhibin positivity excludes carcinoma, including apocrine and histiocytoid lobular types. Atypical (1–2 criteria) and malignant (3 or more) granular cell tumours are rare. Complete excision is curative.

containers.text: Received an oriented specimen 5.0 x 4.0 x 3.0 cm, inked, with a firm, ill-defined, tan-yellow mass 1.6 x 1.4 x 1.2 cm with a gritty cut surface; closest margin (anterior) 0.4 cm.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A6 mass entirely with margins.

diagnoses.name: Schwannoma of Breast
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/08 Mesenchymal Tumours and Tumour-like Lesions

micro.text: An encapsulated spindle cell tumour with alternating hypercellular Antoni A areas, which show nuclear palisading and Verocay bodies, and hypocellular, loose, myxoid Antoni B areas with microcysts. Blood vessels are thick-walled and hyalinised. Scattered degenerative nuclear atypia ('ancient' change) is present, without mitoses or necrosis.
No entrapped breast epithelium within the tumour. No malignancy.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
S100: Diffuse strong positivity
SOX10: Diffuse nuclear positivity
EMA: Perineurial capsule positive
CD34: Patchy in Antoni B areas
Neurofilament: No axons within tumour (against neurofibroma)
Pan-cytokeratin: Negative

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast mass, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Schwannoma, 2.1 cm, with degenerative ('ancient') change. No malignancy.

comment.text: Schwannoma of the breast is rare and arises from intramammary nerves. Differentials: neurofibroma (unencapsulated, mixed cells with axons, S100 patchy; consider NF1), myofibroblastoma (CD34/desmin), spindle cell metaplastic carcinoma (keratin) and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour (excluded). Degenerative atypia without mitoses does not indicate malignancy.

containers.text: Received an encapsulated, ovoid, firm, tan-yellow nodule 2.1 x 1.7 x 1.5 cm with a glistening cut surface and a small cystic area.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A4 nodule entirely including capsule.

diagnoses.name: Nodular Fasciitis of Breast
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/08 Mesenchymal Tumours and Tumour-like Lesions

micro.text: The cores show a proliferation of plump, uniform myofibroblasts arranged in short, irregular fascicles and a loose 'tissue culture-like' pattern in a myxoid to focally collagenous stroma. The stroma contains microcysts, extravasated red blood cells, lymphocytes and scattered osteoclast-like giant cells. Mitoses are readily found (6 per 10 HPF) but are all typical. There is no nuclear pleomorphism, hyperchromasia or necrosis.
Entrapped ducts at the edge are benign. No atypical epithelial cells and no malignancy.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
SMA: Diffuse positive (tram-track pattern)
Desmin: Negative
CD34: Negative
Pan-cytokeratin / p63 / CK5/6: Negative (excludes spindle cell metaplastic carcinoma)
β-catenin: Cytoplasmic only (no nuclear staining; against fibromatosis)
S100 / SOX10: Negative
Ki-67: About 10%
USP6 break-apart FISH: Rearrangement detected (split signals in 34% of nuclei)

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast mass, core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Nodular fasciitis (USP6 gene rearrangement detected by FISH). No malignancy.

comment.text: Nodular fasciitis is a rapidly growing, self-limited myofibroblastic proliferation driven by USP6 fusions (most often MYH9::USP6). In the breast it mimics carcinoma or sarcoma, and the brisk mitoses can be alarming. Differentials: spindle cell metaplastic carcinoma (keratin/p63-positive, must be excluded in any breast spindle cell lesion), fibromatosis (nuclear β-catenin, long fascicles), myofibroblastoma and phyllodes stroma. Spontaneous regression is common.

containers.text: Received four soft, grey-pink cores, 0.8–1.4 cm.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1; block A1 used for FISH.

diagnoses.name: Desmoid-type Fibromatosis of Breast
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/08 Mesenchymal Tumours and Tumour-like Lesions

micro.text: The cores show an infiltrative proliferation of uniform, bland spindle cells (fibroblasts/myofibroblasts) arranged in long, sweeping fascicles in a collagenous stroma with keloid-like collagen in places and thin-walled, slit-like vessels with perivascular oedema. The cells have pale, vesicular, ovoid nuclei with small nucleoli and no hyperchromasia or pleomorphism; mitoses 1 per 10 HPF.
The lesion infiltrates adipose tissue and surrounds and entraps breast lobules, which remain benign, and skeletal muscle fibres (pectoralis) at the edge of one core. No necrosis or malignancy.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
β-catenin: Nuclear positivity in lesional cells (diffuse, variable intensity)
SMA: Positive (myofibroblastic)
Desmin: Focal
Pan-cytokeratin (AE1/AE3), 34βE12, CK5/6, p63: Negative (excludes fibromatosis-like metaplastic carcinoma)
CD34 / S100 / STAT6: Negative
ER: Negative in spindle cells
CTNNB1 sequencing: Exon 3 mutation c.121A>G (p.T41A) detected

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast mass, core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Desmoid-type fibromatosis (nuclear β-catenin positive, CTNNB1 p.T41A mutation), infiltrating breast parenchyma and skeletal muscle. No malignancy.

comment.text: Breast fibromatosis usually arises from pectoral fascia and has been associated with trauma, surgery and implants. It mimics carcinoma clinically and radiologically. The most important differential is low-grade fibromatosis-like metaplastic carcinoma, which needs a broad keratin panel and p63; all are negative here. Others are nodular fasciitis (USP6), myofibroblastoma and scar. Current consensus favours initial active surveillance over upfront surgery, given high recurrence and frequent spontaneous stabilisation.

containers.text: Received five firm, white, fibrous cores 1.0–1.8 cm.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A2.

diagnoses.name: Leiomyoma of Nipple
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/08 Mesenchymal Tumours and Tumour-like Lesions

micro.text: Beneath the nipple epidermis is a well-circumscribed, unencapsulated tumour composed of interlacing fascicles of smooth muscle cells with abundant eosinophilic fibrillary cytoplasm and blunt-ended, cigar-shaped nuclei with perinuclear vacuoles. There is no nuclear atypia, no mitoses (0 per 10 HPF) and no necrosis. It merges focally with the native smooth muscle of the nipple-areolar complex.
Overlying epidermis is unremarkable. Deep margin is close (0.1 cm) but clear.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
Desmin / h-caldesmon / SMA: Diffuse positive
ER / PR: Positive
Pan-cytokeratin / S100: Negative

finalDiagnosis.label: Left nipple nodule, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Leiomyoma of the nipple, 0.8 cm, without atypia or mitoses. Margins clear.

comment.text: Leiomyomas of the breast most often arise from the smooth muscle of the nipple-areolar complex. Differentials include leiomyosarcoma (atypia, mitoses, necrosis; none here), myoid hamartoma (contains glandular elements), myofibroblastoma (CD34-positive) and dermatomyofibroma. Pain is a recognised feature. Excision is curative.

containers.text: Received a wedge of nipple skin and subcutis 1.4 x 1.0 x 0.9 cm with a firm, white, whorled, well-circumscribed nodule 0.8 cm beneath the skin; closest (deep) margin 0.1 cm.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A2.

diagnoses.name: Gynaecomastia, Florid Phase
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/09 Gynaecomastia and Miscellaneous Lesions

micro.text: Breast tissue with ducts but no lobules. Ducts show epithelial hyperplasia with characteristic micropapillary tufts that taper toward the lumen (gynaecomastoid hyperplasia), with a myoepithelial layer. They are surrounded by a cuff of oedematous, cellular, loose periductal stroma with increased vascularity and chronic inflammation (florid/proliferative phase). Areas of pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia are present. The outer stroma is dense and hyalinised in places.
No atypia, no in situ or invasive carcinoma.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
CK5/6: Mosaic positivity in hyperplastic epithelium (usual-type pattern)
ER: Positive (heterogeneous to strong)
AR: Positive
p63: Myoepithelium intact

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast (male), subcutaneous mastectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Gynaecomastia, florid (proliferative) phase, with gynaecomastoid ductal hyperplasia and pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia. No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Gynaecomastia has an early florid phase (epithelial hyperplasia with cellular oedematous periductal stroma) and a late fibrous phase (hyalinised stroma, inactive ducts). The florid features fit the 8-month history and the drug association (spironolactone). Gynaecomastoid hyperplasia shows usual-type CK5/6 mosaicism. Atypia or DCIS, which can rarely arise and would be CK5/6-negative, has been excluded.

containers.text: Received a disc of fibrofatty tissue 7.0 x 6.0 x 2.0 cm, 48 g, with a firm, rubbery, grey-white central retroareolar area 4.0 x 3.5 x 1.5 cm, without a discrete mass.
Liposuction aspirate (fat) not submitted.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A8 representative sections of the fibrous area; A9 fat.

diagnoses.name: Mucocele-like Lesion
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/09 Gynaecomastia and Miscellaneous Lesions

micro.text: Multiple dilated ducts and cysts are distended by mucin and lined by flat to cuboidal benign epithelium with an outer myoepithelial layer. Several cysts have ruptured, with pools of extravasated acellular mucin dissecting the stroma. Within the extravasated mucin are occasional detached strips of bland epithelium that retain myoepithelial cells, together with coarse calcifications.
There are no floating clusters of atypical epithelial cells, no ADH or DCIS in the cyst linings and no mucinous carcinoma. Background shows columnar cell change.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
p63 / CK5/6: Myoepithelial cells present along cyst linings and within detached epithelial strips
ER: Heterogeneous in lining epithelium
Alcian blue / PAS: Extracellular mucin positive

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast, stereotactic vacuum-assisted biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Mucocele-like lesion without atypia, with extravasated acellular mucin and associated calcifications; background columnar cell change. No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Mucocele-like lesions consist of mucin-filled cysts that rupture, releasing mucin into the stroma. Detached epithelial strips with myoepithelial cells favour an MLL over mucinous carcinoma, which has floating clusters of neoplastic epithelium without myoepithelium. MLLs may coexist with ADH, DCIS or mucinous carcinoma. Without atypia and with the calcifications removed, as here, upgrade is uncommon and surveillance is reasonable.

containers.text: Received twelve tan, partly gelatinous cores 1.0–2.0 cm; calcification cores separate.

exampleGross.sections: A1 (calcification cores), A2–A4 remaining; levels x3.

diagnoses.name: Collagenous Spherulosis
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/09 Gynaecomastia and Miscellaneous Lesions

micro.text: Several ducts involved by usual ductal hyperplasia, and adjacent sclerosing adenosis, contain numerous rounded, cribriform-like intraluminal spaces. Each space is filled by an eosinophilic to pale, fibrillary or laminated spherule of basement membrane material, some with a central star-like pattern, and is rimmed by flattened myoepithelial cells. Some spherules are calcified, corresponding to the mammographic target.
The surrounding epithelium is heterogeneous, with streaming and overlapping nuclei (UDH). No monotonous cribriform proliferation, lobular neoplasia or adenoid cystic carcinoma. No malignancy.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
p63 / calponin / SMMHC: Myoepithelial cells rim each spherule
Collagen IV: Spherules positive (basement membrane material)
CD117 (c-KIT): Negative in epithelial cells (against adenoid cystic carcinoma)
E-cadherin: Membranous (no lobular neoplasia)
CK5/6: Mosaic in surrounding UDH
ER: Heterogeneous

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast, stereotactic core needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Collagenous spherulosis involving usual ductal hyperplasia and sclerosing adenosis, with calcified spherules. No atypia or malignancy.

comment.text: Collagenous spherulosis is a benign, usually incidental finding in UDH, papillomas and sclerosing adenosis. Its cribriform-like appearance must not be mistaken for cribriform DCIS, whose spaces are lined by luminal cells, with monotonous ER-diffuse, CK5/6-negative cells, or for adenoid cystic carcinoma (infiltrative, CD117-positive, MYB-NFIB). Collagenous spherulosis colonised by LCIS also occurs, which E-cadherin excludes here.

containers.text: Received six grey-white cores 1.0–1.6 cm.

exampleGross.sections: A1 (calcification cores), A2 remaining; levels x3.

diagnoses.name: Juvenile Papillomatosis
diagnoses.path: Breast/02 Benign Lesions/09 Gynaecomastia and Miscellaneous Lesions

micro.text: A localised lesion composed of numerous cysts and dilated ducts, many lined by apocrine metaplastic or flattened epithelium, some containing foamy histiocytes (duct stasis).
