There is florid usual ductal hyperplasia with papillomatosis, sclerosing adenosis and periductal fibrosis. Cell populations are heterogeneous, with streaming and irregular fenestrations.
Foci of necrosis within hyperplastic ducts are absent; there is no atypical ductal hyperplasia, DCIS or invasive carcinoma. Margins clear (closest 0.4 cm).
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
CK5/6: Mosaic in hyperplastic epithelium
ER: Heterogeneous
p63: Myoepithelium intact throughout

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast mass, excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Juvenile papillomatosis, 4.2 cm, with florid usual ductal hyperplasia, papillomatosis, cysts with apocrine metaplasia and sclerosing adenosis. No atypia or malignancy. Margins clear.

comment.text: Juvenile papillomatosis is an uncommon localised proliferative lesion in young women, with a characteristic 'Swiss cheese' gross appearance. It is associated with a family history of breast cancer and a possibly increased later risk of carcinoma for the patient (especially with bilateral or recurrent disease) and her relatives. Differentials: fibrocystic change in older women, juvenile fibroadenoma and papillary carcinoma. Complete excision and long-term follow-up are advised; referral for genetic or family-history risk assessment is reasonable.

containers.text: Received a fibrofatty specimen 6.0 x 5.0 x 3.5 cm containing a firm, ill-defined lesion 4.2 x 3.5 x 2.5 cm with numerous cysts (0.1–0.8 cm) containing clear to brown fluid, giving a 'Swiss cheese' appearance. Closest margin 0.5 cm.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A10 lesion with margins.

diagnoses.name: Invasive Breast Carcinoma, No Special Type

micro.text: Sections show an invasive carcinoma composed of irregular glands, tubules and solid nests of moderately pleomorphic cells with vesicular nuclei and small nucleoli, infiltrating a desmoplastic stroma. Gland formation is present in about 35% of the tumour (score 2), nuclear pleomorphism is moderate (score 2) and there are 11 mitoses per 10 HPF (score 2), Nottingham grade 2 (6/9). There is no lobular, mucinous, micropapillary or other special-type component; the tumour is of no special type.

Intermediate-grade DCIS of cribriform and solid patterns with focal necrosis and microcalcifications is admixed with the invasive carcinoma, forming about 10% of the tumour; it does not extend beyond the invasive carcinoma. Lymphovascular invasion is not identified. Margins are clear, the closest being the posterior margin at 4 mm (invasive) and 5 mm (DCIS). The biopsy site shows haemosiderin, fat necrosis and a foreign-body reaction around the clip.
All three sentinel lymph nodes are free of metastatic carcinoma on three H&E levels (0/3).
Immunohistochemistry / Biomarkers:
Diagnostic immunohistochemistry / ancillary studies:

E-cadherin: Strong, complete membranous staining in the invasive carcinoma (performed because of focal single-file growth; supports IBC-NST and excludes lobular carcinoma; the WHO 6th edition category 'IBC-NST with lobular features' is not needed)
p63 / calponin: Myoepithelial cells absent around invasive glands; retained around DCIS
Breast biomarkers (CAP Breast Biomarker Template v1.6.2.0):
Testing performed on: Block A3 of this resection
Estrogen receptor (ER): Positive (greater than 10% of cells demonstrate nuclear positivity): 95%, average intensity Strong (3+). Allred score 8/8 (proportion 5 + intensity 3).
Progesterone receptor (PgR): Positive (greater than or equal to 1% of cells demonstrate nuclear positivity): 80%, average intensity Strong (3+). Allred score 8/8.

HER2 by IHC: Negative (Score 1+): incomplete membrane staining that is faint / barely perceptible and in greater than 10% of tumour cells (about 40%). Falls in the HER2-low category used in DESTINY-Breast04.
HER2 by ISH: Not performed (not required for IHC 1+).
Final HER2 status: HER2 NEGATIVE (IHC 1+, HER2-low)
Ki-67 proliferative index: 15% of invasive tumour nuclei (global scoring, International Ki67 in Breast Cancer Working Group method; clone 30-9).

HER2 IHC comment: CAP standardized comment: In the DESTINY-Breast 04 and 06 trials, "HER2 low" was IHC Score 1+ or 2+ / ISH negative, and "HER2 ultralow" was HER2 IHC Score of 0 (pattern 0+) with membrane staining that is incomplete and faint / barely perceptible in less than or equal to 10% of tumour cells. Breast cancers with these staining patterns may be eligible for treatment with trastuzumab-deruxtecan in the metastatic setting (but those with no staining, IHC "null" pattern 0, are currently excluded). WHO 6th edition recommends specifying the IHC 0 staining pattern (0 / absent versus 0+ / with membrane staining); use of the terms HER2-low and HER2-ultralow is not required.

Fixation / methods: Cold ischaemia time 35 minutes; 10% neutral buffered formalin fixation 28 hours (meets ASCO/CAP requirements; no decalcification). Clones: ER SP1, PgR 1E2, HER2 4B5 (Ventana PATHWAY, FDA-approved); ASCO/CAP scoring criteria; internal and external controls stain as expected.
Prior biopsy biomarkers: Core biopsy (prior case, illustrative accession): ER 90% strong, PgR 70%, HER2 IHC 1+, Ki-67 15%; concordant with the resection.

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast, wire-guided wide local excision and sentinel lymph node biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Invasive carcinoma of no special type (ductal), Nottingham grade 2 (6/9), 18 mm, with intermediate-grade DCIS (no EIC). Lymphovascular invasion not identified. All margins clear (closest posterior 4 mm). Sentinel lymph nodes negative (0/3). HER2 negative (IHC 1+, HER2-low); ER and PgR positive. pT1c pN0 (sn); AJCC anatomic stage IA; pathological prognostic stage IA.

comment.text: Luminal-type (ER/PgR positive, HER2-negative) grade 2 invasive carcinoma of no special type, completely excised with clear margins and negative sentinel nodes. The HER2 IHC 1+ result places the tumour in the HER2-low category, which is relevant only in the metastatic setting.

A multigene assay (e.g. 21-gene recurrence score) may be considered by the treating team; for T1-2 N0 ER-positive HER2-negative cancers a recurrence score below 11 assigns AJCC prognostic stage IA (already the stage here). Discussion at the breast multidisciplinary meeting is recommended.

containers.text: Received in formalin a wire-guided wide local excision of the left breast, orientated with a short suture superior and a long suture lateral, and inked superior blue, inferior green, medial yellow, lateral red, anterior orange and posterior (deep) black. It measures 65 mm (medial to lateral) x 55 mm (superior to inferior) x 35 mm (anterior to posterior) and weighs 58 g. The localisation wire enters anteriorly. The specimen radiograph accompanying the specimen shows the lesion and the marker clip within the specimen. Serial slicing from medial to lateral into 12 slices shows a firm, stellate, grey-white tumour measuring 18 x 15 x 12 mm in slices 6 to 8, with gritty cut surface. The marker clip is retrieved at the tumour edge. Distances from the tumour: posterior 4 mm, anterior 6 mm, lateral 9 mm, superior 12 mm, inferior 15 mm, medial 20 mm. The remaining tissue is fibrofatty with no other lesion.
Sentinel lymph nodes: three nodes labelled as blue and hot, measuring 6, 11 and 15 mm, each sliced at 2 mm intervals perpendicular to the long axis.

exampleGross.sections: A1 medial margin en face; A2-A3 slices with tumour and posterior margin; A4-A5 tumour with anterior and superior margins; A6 tumour with lateral margin; A7 clip site; A8-A9 tumour (for biomarkers, A3 selected); A10 inferior margin; A11-A12 background tissue. B1-B3 sentinel nodes 1-3, entirely submitted, three levels each.

diagnoses.name: Invasive Breast Carcinoma NST, Medullary Pattern

micro.text: Sections show a well-circumscribed invasive carcinoma with a pushing border, growing in syncytial sheets (more than 75% of the tumour) of large, highly pleomorphic cells with vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli and indistinct cell borders. There is no gland formation (score 3), nuclear pleomorphism is marked (score 3) and there are 32 mitoses per 10 HPF (score 3), Nottingham grade 3 (9/9). Atypical mitoses and apoptotic bodies are frequent.

A dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate permeates the stroma and the edge of the tumour (stromal TILs 70%). No DCIS, gland formation or neuroendocrine morphology is seen. Lymphovascular invasion is not identified. Margins are clear (closest deep 6 mm). Background breast shows mild fibrocystic change.
Two sentinel lymph nodes show reactive follicular hyperplasia with no metastatic carcinoma (0/2).
Immunohistochemistry / Biomarkers:
Diagnostic immunohistochemistry / ancillary studies:
CK5/6 and EGFR: Positive (basal-like immunophenotype)
AE1/AE3: Positive in tumour cells; highlights syncytial sheets
GATA3: Positive (moderate, 60% of cells): supports breast origin
CD3 / CD8 / CD20: TILs predominantly CD3+ CD8+ T cells, with scattered CD20+ B cells and plasma cells
PD-L1 (22C3): Not performed on this specimen; may be requested if metastatic disease develops
p63 / SMMHC: No myoepithelial layer around tumour nests (invasive)
Breast biomarkers (CAP Breast Biomarker Template v1.6.2.0):
Testing performed on: Block A3 of this resection
Estrogen receptor (ER): Negative (less than 1%). Internal control (normal ducts) present and stains as expected. Allred score 0.
Progesterone receptor (PgR): Negative (less than 1%). Internal control present and stains as expected. Allred score 0.
HER2 by IHC: Negative (Score 0): no membrane staining detected (0 / absent membrane staining). HER2-null pattern (not HER2-low or HER2-ultralow).
HER2 by ISH: Not performed (not required for IHC 0).
Final HER2 status: HER2 NEGATIVE (IHC 0, null)
Ki-67 proliferative index: 75% of invasive tumour nuclei (global scoring, International Ki67 in Breast Cancer Working Group method; clone 30-9).

Fixation / methods: Cold ischaemia time 35 minutes; 10% neutral buffered formalin fixation 28 hours (meets ASCO/CAP requirements; no decalcification). Clones: ER SP1, PgR 1E2, HER2 4B5 (Ventana PATHWAY, FDA-approved); ASCO/CAP scoring criteria; internal and external controls stain as expected.

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast, wide local excision and sentinel lymph node biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Invasive carcinoma of no special type (ductal) with medullary pattern, Nottingham grade 3 (9/9), 24 mm, with stromal TILs 70%. No DCIS or lymphovascular invasion. Margins clear (closest deep 6 mm). Sentinel lymph nodes negative (0/2). Triple-negative: ER negative, PgR negative, HER2 negative (IHC 0, null); Ki-67 75%. pT2 pN0 (sn); AJCC anatomic stage IIA; pathological prognostic stage IIA.

comment.text: Triple-negative, basal-like, TIL-rich carcinoma with medullary pattern. Per WHO 6th edition and CAP v4.11.0.0 this is reported as IBC-NST with a specific morphologic pattern (medullary pattern) rather than as 'medullary carcinoma'. High stromal TILs are associated with a better prognosis and response to therapy in triple-negative disease. The association with a germline BRCA1 variant is typical.

Other specific morphologic patterns of NST listed by CAP include 'with neuroendocrine differentiation' and 'osteoclast-like stromal giant cell-rich'. In WHO 6th edition, IBC-NST with neuroendocrine differentiation requires moderate to strong, or diffuse weak but unequivocal, neuroendocrine marker expression; large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma is regarded as part of this pattern and not as a separate entity, and the unified neuroendocrine neoplasm model is no longer applied to breast. Routine neuroendocrine staining of IBC-NST is not recommended, and it was not performed here because there was no neuroendocrine morphology.
The HER2 IHC 0 (null) result means the tumour does not fall in the HER2-low or HER2-ultralow categories. Referral to medical oncology and genetics is recommended.

diagnoses.name: Invasive Lobular Carcinoma, Classic
diagnoses.path: Breast/03 Carcinomas/02 Invasive Lobular and Mixed Carcinoma

micro.text: Sections show an invasive carcinoma composed of small, discohesive, monotonous cells with scant cytoplasm and uniform round nuclei, infiltrating in single files and as single cells and arranged in a targetoid pattern around ducts, with minimal stromal reaction. Occasional intracytoplasmic lumina and signet-ring cells are present. There is no gland formation (score 3), nuclei are mildly enlarged with mild variability (score 2), and mitoses are scant, 3 per 10 HPF (score 1): Nottingham grade 2 (6/9).

Classic lobular carcinoma in situ involves multiple lobules within and around the tumour. Lymphovascular invasion is not identified. The nipple and skin are uninvolved. The deep margin is clear by 8 mm.

Metastatic lobular carcinoma is present in both sentinel nodes and in 2 of 12 non-sentinel axillary nodes (4/14), with a subtle sinusoidal and diffuse single-cell pattern best seen on cytokeratin stain; the largest deposit measures 9 mm, with 1.5 mm of extranodal extension in one node.
Immunohistochemistry / Biomarkers:
Diagnostic immunohistochemistry / ancillary studies:
E-cadherin: Complete loss of membranous staining in invasive and in situ cells (normal ducts positive as internal control)
p120 catenin: Diffuse cytoplasmic staining (lobular pattern)
AE1/AE3 (nodes): Highlights subtle single-cell nodal involvement
GATA3: Positive
Breast biomarkers (CAP Breast Biomarker Template v1.6.2.0):
Testing performed on: Block A5 of this resection
Estrogen receptor (ER): Positive (greater than 10% of cells demonstrate nuclear positivity): 98%, average intensity Strong (3+). Allred score 8/8 (proportion 5 + intensity 3).
Progesterone receptor (PgR): Positive (greater than or equal to 1% of cells demonstrate nuclear positivity): 60%, average intensity Moderate (2+). Allred score 6/8.

HER2 by IHC: Negative (Score 0+): membrane staining that is incomplete and is faint / barely perceptible and in less than or equal to 10% of tumour cells (0+ / with membrane staining), about 5% of cells. Falls in the HER2-ultralow category used in DESTINY-Breast06.
HER2 by ISH: Not performed (not required for IHC 0+).
Final HER2 status: HER2 NEGATIVE (IHC 0+, ultralow)
Ki-67 proliferative index: 8% of invasive tumour nuclei (global scoring, International Ki67 in Breast Cancer Working Group method; clone 30-9).

HER2 IHC comment: CAP standardized comment: In the DESTINY-Breast 04 and 06 trials, "HER2 low" was IHC Score 1+ or 2+ / ISH negative, and "HER2 ultralow" was HER2 IHC Score of 0 (pattern 0+) with membrane staining that is incomplete and faint / barely perceptible in less than or equal to 10% of tumour cells. Breast cancers with these staining patterns may be eligible for treatment with trastuzumab-deruxtecan in the metastatic setting (but those with no staining, IHC "null" pattern 0, are currently excluded). WHO 6th edition recommends specifying the IHC 0 staining pattern (0 / absent versus 0+ / with membrane staining); use of the terms HER2-low and HER2-ultralow is not required.

Fixation / methods: Cold ischaemia time 35 minutes; 10% neutral buffered formalin fixation 28 hours (meets ASCO/CAP requirements; no decalcification). Clones: ER SP1, PgR 1E2, HER2 4B5 (Ventana PATHWAY, FDA-approved); ASCO/CAP scoring criteria; internal and external controls stain as expected.

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast, simple total mastectomy, sentinel lymph node biopsy and axillary lymph node dissection:
finalDiagnosis.text: Invasive lobular carcinoma, classic, Nottingham grade 2 (6/9), 55 mm, with classic LCIS. E-cadherin lost. No lymphovascular invasion. Nipple and skin not involved. Margins clear (closest deep 8 mm). Metastatic carcinoma in 4 of 14 axillary lymph nodes (largest 9 mm; ENE 1.5 mm). ER positive, PgR positive, HER2 negative (IHC 0+, ultralow). pT3 pN2a; AJCC anatomic stage IIIA; pathological prognostic stage IB.

comment.text: Classic invasive lobular carcinoma with E-cadherin loss. Size was determined by correlating gross mapping, microscopy and MRI because ILC is often grossly inconspicuous. The pT3 pN2a cancer is anatomic stage IIIA but, because it is grade 2, ER/PgR-positive and HER2-negative, its AJCC pathological prognostic stage is IB (a downstaging of more than one group, as AJCC 8th edition allows for favourable biology).
The HER2 IHC 0+ (with membrane staining) result falls in the HER2-ultralow category; see the CAP standardized comment. Classic LCIS at or near margins does not require re-excision.

diagnoses.path: Breast/03 Carcinomas/02 Invasive Lobular and Mixed Carcinoma

micro.text: Sections show an invasive carcinoma with a discohesive single-file and sheet-like (alveolar-solid) growth pattern composed of large cells with abundant eosinophilic to apocrine-like cytoplasm and markedly pleomorphic nuclei (more than four times the size of lymphocytes) with prominent nucleoli. There is no gland formation (score 3), nuclear pleomorphism is marked (score 3) and there are 12 mitoses per 10 HPF (score 2): Nottingham grade 3 (8/9).

Pleomorphic LCIS with central comedo-type necrosis and calcification fills adjacent lobules. Focal lymphovascular invasion is present in one block (A8). The inferior shave contains no carcinoma; the final inferior margin is 1.5 mm from invasive carcinoma (no tumour in the shave). The anterior shave contains pleomorphic LCIS 0.5 mm from its new margin; invasive carcinoma is not present in the shave.
One of three sentinel nodes contains a 4 mm macrometastasis of pleomorphic lobular carcinoma without extranodal extension (1/3).
Immunohistochemistry / Biomarkers:
Diagnostic immunohistochemistry / ancillary studies:
E-cadherin: Loss of membranous staining (invasive and in situ components)
p120 catenin: Diffuse cytoplasmic staining
Androgen receptor: Positive (80%)
GCDFP-15: Focally positive (apocrine-like cytology)
p63 / SMMHC: Myoepithelium absent around invasive cells, retained around pleomorphic LCIS
Breast biomarkers (CAP Breast Biomarker Template v1.6.2.0):
Testing performed on: Block A4 of this resection
Estrogen receptor (ER): Positive (greater than 10% of cells demonstrate nuclear positivity): 60%, average intensity Moderate (2+). Allred score 6/8 (proportion 4 + intensity 2).
Progesterone receptor (PgR): Negative (less than 1%). Internal control present and stains as expected. Allred score 0.
HER2 by IHC: Equivocal (Score 2+): weak to moderate complete membrane staining observed in greater than 10% of tumour cells (about 60%). Reflex ISH performed on the same block.

HER2 by ISH: Negative (not amplified, Group 5 result). Average HER2 signals/cell 3.1; average CEP17 signals/cell 2.2; HER2/CEP17 ratio 1.41. Number of observers 2; 40 invasive tumour cells counted. Dual-probe ISH (ASCO/CAP 2023 criteria).
Final HER2 status: HER2 NEGATIVE (IHC 2+, ISH not amplified; HER2-low category)
Ki-67 proliferative index: 35% of invasive tumour nuclei (global scoring, International Ki67 in Breast Cancer Working Group method; clone 30-9).

HER2 IHC comment: CAP standardized comment: In the DESTINY-Breast 04 and 06 trials, "HER2 low" was IHC Score 1+ or 2+ / ISH negative, and "HER2 ultralow" was HER2 IHC Score of 0 (pattern 0+) with membrane staining that is incomplete and faint / barely perceptible in less than or equal to 10% of tumour cells. Breast cancers with these staining patterns may be eligible for treatment with trastuzumab-deruxtecan in the metastatic setting (but those with no staining, IHC "null" pattern 0, are currently excluded). WHO 6th edition recommends specifying the IHC 0 staining pattern (0 / absent versus 0+ / with membrane staining); use of the terms HER2-low and HER2-ultralow is not required.

Pleomorphic LCIS close to a margin (0.5 mm) is managed similarly to DCIS by many centres; correlation with the surgical plan and multidisciplinary discussion regarding further anterior margin excision is suggested. exampleGross.sections: A1 skin; A2-A7 each margin; A8-A10 tumour (A9 for biomarkers); A11-A12 background. B1-B3 sentinel nodes, entirely, three levels each.

micro.text: Sections show a well-circumscribed invasive carcinoma composed entirely of small clusters, trabeculae and occasional cribriform nests of low-grade tumour cells floating in abundant pools of extracellular mucin separated by thin fibrovascular septa; cellularity is low (type A, hypocellular). No conventional NST component is present (mucinous component 100%). Tubule formation is under 10% (score 3), nuclei are small and uniform (score 1) and mitoses are 2 per 10 HPF (score 1): Nottingham grade 1 (5/9).

Minor low-grade micropapillary DCIS is present at the periphery. No lymphovascular invasion. The closest epithelium is 3 mm from the posterior margin; a dissecting acellular mucin pool lies 0.5 mm from the posterior margin. Both sentinel nodes are negative (0/2).
Immunohistochemistry / Biomarkers:
Diagnostic immunohistochemistry / ancillary studies:
Synaptophysin / chromogranin: Negative (in keeping with hypocellular type A; neuroendocrine staining is optional and not required for the diagnosis)
MUC2: Positive in extracellular mucin and tumour cells
p63 / SMMHC: Absent around tumour clusters (excludes mucocele-like lesion with in situ carcinoma)
GATA3: Positive
Breast biomarkers (CAP Breast Biomarker Template v1.6.2.0):
Testing performed on: Block A3 of this resection
Estrogen receptor (ER): Positive (greater than 10% of cells demonstrate nuclear positivity): 100%, average intensity Strong (3+). Allred score 8/8 (proportion 5 + intensity 3).
Progesterone receptor (PgR): Positive (greater than or equal to 1% of cells demonstrate nuclear positivity): 70%, average intensity Moderate (2+). Allred score 7/8.
HER2 by IHC: Negative (Score 0): no membrane staining detected (0 / absent membrane staining). HER2-null pattern (not HER2-low or HER2-ultralow).
HER2 by ISH: Not performed (not required for IHC 0).
Final HER2 status: HER2 NEGATIVE (IHC 0, null)
Ki-67 proliferative index: 5% of invasive tumour nuclei (global scoring, International Ki67 in Breast Cancer Working Group method; clone 30-9).

Fixation / methods: Cold ischaemia time 35 minutes; 10% neutral buffered formalin fixation 28 hours (meets ASCO/CAP requirements; no decalcification). Clones: ER SP1, PgR 1E2, HER2 4B5 (Ventana PATHWAY, FDA-approved); ASCO/CAP scoring criteria; internal and external controls stain as expected.

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast, central wide local excision and sentinel lymph node biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Mucinous carcinoma (pure, 100% mucinous, hypocellular type A), Nottingham grade 1 (5/9), 28 mm, with minor low-grade DCIS. No lymphovascular invasion. Carcinoma 3 mm from the closest (posterior) margin; acellular mucin 0.5 mm from the posterior margin. Sentinel lymph nodes negative (0/2). ER and PgR positive, HER2 negative (IHC 0, null). pT2 pN0 (sn); AJCC anatomic stage IIA; pathological prognostic stage IA.

comment.text: Pure mucinous carcinoma (at least 90% mucinous) has a favourable prognosis; tumours with 10-90% mucinous component are classified as mixed. The size includes the mucin pools containing tumour cells. The T2 N0 tumour is anatomic stage IIA but pathological prognostic stage IA because of its low grade and receptor profile.

WHO 6th edition reserves mucinous carcinoma for grade 1-2 tumours with a favourable biomarker profile; mucin-producing carcinomas with high nuclear grade, ER negativity or HER2 positivity are classified as IBC-NST with mucin production. A prominent micropapillary pattern, if present, is noted but not designated a separate subtype; metastasis to the breast should be excluded clinically. Acellular mucin near (but not at) a margin is reported descriptively; acellular mucin at the margin is usually not regarded as a positive margin, but practice varies and surgical correlation is advised. HER2 IHC 0 (null).

containers.text: Received a central wide local excision of the right breast, orientated with a short suture superior and a long suture lateral, and inked superior blue, inferior green, medial yellow, lateral red, anterior orange and posterior (deep) black, measuring 70 x 60 x 35 mm (68 g). Sentinel lymph nodes: two nodes, 9 and 11 mm.

exampleGross.sections: A1-A6 each margin; A7-A10 tumour, including posterior margin (A8 for biomarkers); A11 background. B1-B2 sentinel nodes, entirely, three levels each.

micro.text: Sections show an invasive carcinoma composed of small, hollow or morular clusters of tumour cells lacking fibrovascular cores, each lying within a clear stromal space (retraction artefact), with reversed polarity ('inside-out' arrangement). The micropapillary pattern forms about 95% of the tumour. True tubules are under 10% (score 3), nuclear pleomorphism is moderate (score 2) and mitoses are 14 per 10 HPF (score 2): Nottingham grade 2 (7/9). Psammomatous calcifications are present.

Extensive lymphovascular invasion is present in four blocks, including focal tumour emboli in dermal lymphatics of the overlying skin (no direct skin invasion). Micropapillary DCIS forms about 5%. Margins are clear (deep 6 mm). The nipple is uninvolved.
Metastatic micropapillary carcinoma is present in 12 of 21 axillary nodes, including 1 of 2 level III nodes; the largest deposit measures 18 mm, with extranodal extension in 3 nodes (maximum 4 mm).
Immunohistochemistry / Biomarkers:
Diagnostic immunohistochemistry / ancillary studies:
EMA (MUC1): Reverse polarity: staining of the stroma-facing (outer, 'inside-out') surface of the micropapillary clusters
CD31 / D2-40: Confirm true lymphovascular invasion (D2-40-positive endothelium) in addition to retraction spaces; dermal lymphatic emboli confirmed
GATA3: Positive (supports breast origin, versus ovarian serous or urothelial micropapillary carcinoma)
PAX8 / WT1: Negative
Breast biomarkers (CAP Breast Biomarker Template v1.6.2.0):
Testing performed on: Block A6 of this resection
Estrogen receptor (ER): Positive (greater than 10% of cells demonstrate nuclear positivity): 80%, average intensity Strong (3+). Allred score 8/8 (proportion 5 + intensity 3).
Progesterone receptor (PgR): Positive (greater than or equal to 1% of cells demonstrate nuclear positivity): 20%, average intensity Moderate (2+). Allred score 5/8.

HER2 by IHC: Equivocal (Score 2+): moderate to intense but incomplete (basolateral, U-shaped 'inside-out') membrane staining in about 70% of tumour cells, the pattern recognised by CAP in HER2-amplified micropapillary carcinomas. Reflex ISH performed.

HER2 by ISH: Positive (amplified, Group 1 result in greater than 10% of cell population). Average HER2 signals/cell 6.2; average CEP17 signals/cell 2.3; HER2/CEP17 ratio 2.7. Number of observers 2; 40 invasive tumour cells counted. Heterogeneity not identified. Dual-probe ISH (ASCO/CAP 2023 criteria).
Final HER2 status: HER2 POSITIVE (IHC 2+, ISH amplified)
Ki-67 proliferative index: 30% of invasive tumour nuclei (global scoring, International Ki67 in Breast Cancer Working Group method; clone 30-9).

Fixation / methods: Cold ischaemia time 35 minutes; 10% neutral buffered formalin fixation 28 hours (meets ASCO/CAP requirements; no decalcification). Clones: ER SP1, PgR 1E2, HER2 4B5 (Ventana PATHWAY, FDA-approved); ASCO/CAP scoring criteria; internal and external controls stain as expected.

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast, simple total mastectomy and axillary lymph node dissection (levels I-III):
finalDiagnosis.text: Invasive micropapillary carcinoma (more than 90%, micropapillary 95%), Nottingham grade 2 (7/9), 35 mm, with extensive lymphovascular invasion including dermal lymphatics (not inflammatory carcinoma). Margins clear (closest deep 6 mm). Metastatic carcinoma in 12 of 21 axillary lymph nodes including level III (largest 18 mm; ENE up to 4 mm). ER positive (80%), PgR positive (20%), HER2 positive (IHC 2+, ISH amplified). pT2 pN3a; AJCC anatomic stage IIIC; pathological prognostic stage IIIA.

comment.text: Invasive micropapillary carcinoma has a high propensity for lymphovascular invasion and nodal metastasis. Ten or more positive axillary nodes, or level III involvement, defines pN3a, so the anatomic stage is IIIC. Because the tumour is grade 2, ER/PgR-positive and HER2-positive, the AJCC pathological prognostic stage is IIIA.

Dermal lymphovascular invasion without the clinical findings of inflammatory carcinoma (erythema and oedema of at least one-third of the skin) does not change the T category. HER2 is positive by ISH (Group 1) after an equivocal IHC result with the basolateral pattern typical of micropapillary carcinoma; HER2-targeted therapy should be considered.

micro.text: Sections show an invasive keratinising squamous cell carcinoma with nests and sheets of polygonal cells with intercellular bridges, keratin pearls and individual cell keratinisation, surrounding a central cyst. The tumour directly invades the dermis and ulcerates the epidermis; there is no in situ squamous carcinoma of the overlying epidermis (excluding a cutaneous primary). Gland formation absent (score 3), marked pleomorphism (score 3), 13 mitoses per 10 HPF (score 2): Nottingham grade 3 (8/9).
Focal lymphovascular invasion. The nipple is uninvolved. Margins are clear (skin edge 15 mm, deep 12 mm). Metastatic squamous carcinoma in 1 of 16 axillary nodes (7 mm, no ENE).

Diagnostic immunohistochemistry / ancillary studies:
p40 / p63: Diffuse strong nuclear positivity
CK5/6: Diffusely positive
GATA3: Focally positive (supports breast origin)
p16: Patchy (not block-type); HPV-associated metastatic SCC not favoured
Overlying epidermis: No squamous dysplasia or in situ carcinoma (supports a breast parenchymal primary)

Testing performed on: Block A7 of this resection

finalDiagnosis.text: Metaplastic carcinoma, squamous cell type (keratinising), Nottingham grade 3 (8/9), 42 mm, directly invading the skin with macroscopic ulceration (pT4b). comment.text: Primary squamous cell carcinoma of the breast is a metaplastic carcinoma; metastasis from another site (skin, lung, cervix, head and neck) and extension of a cutaneous SCC must be excluded clinically and pathologically. comment.text: Classification note: WHO 6th edition defines malignant adenomyoepithelioma as an AME with carcinoma arising from the epithelial cells, the myoepithelial cells or both, and broadly retains the previous AME classification scheme. CAP v4.11.0.0 lists spindle cell, squamous, heterologous/matrix-producing, mixed and two low-grade metaplastic subtypes; because this carcinoma has mixed spindle and epithelioid myoepithelial-type morphology arising in an AME, it is reported under 'Metaplastic carcinoma, other type (specify)'. Alternatives some pathologists would choose: 'Metaplastic carcinoma, spindle cell' (WHO 6th edition notes myoepithelial-derived carcinomas usually resemble spindle cell metaplastic carcinoma) or 'Other histologic type not listed: malignant adenomyoepithelioma'. Metaplastic carcinoma with osteoclast-like giant cells was not chosen for this slot because CAP classifies osteoclast-like stromal giant cell-rich carcinoma as a specific morphologic pattern of NST.
AJCC 8th: pT3 pN0(sn) is anatomic stage IIB; grade 3 triple-negative biology gives pathological prognostic stage IIIA. Size refers to the malignant component only.

diagnoses.path: Breast/03 Carcinomas/05 Papillary and Salivary Gland Type Carcinomas

micro.text: Sections show multiple expansile, rounded, solid cellular nodules with delicate fibrovascular cores, composed of low-grade, monotonous, oval to spindle cells with granular eosinophilic cytoplasm, palisading around vessels, with focal intracytoplasmic mucin. The rounded nodules lack a myoepithelial layer but have smooth, circumscribed contours (solid papillary carcinoma in situ pattern). At the posterior aspect, the tumour forms jagged, irregular, geographic nests infiltrating desmoplastic stroma and fat over 14 mm, diagnostic of invasive solid papillary carcinoma. Tubule formation under 10% (score 3), nuclei score 1, mitoses 3 per 10 HPF (score 1): Nottingham grade 1 (5/9).
No lymphovascular invasion. Invasive margins clear (posterior 6 mm); in situ SPC 3 mm from the medial margin. Sentinel nodes negative (0/2).
Immunohistochemistry / Biomarkers:
Diagnostic immunohistochemistry / ancillary studies:
Synaptophysin / chromogranin A / INSM1: Diffusely positive (neuroendocrine differentiation)
GATA3: Positive
p63 / SMMHC / CK5/6: Myoepithelial layer absent around both the rounded nodules and the jagged invasive nests; CK5/6 negative in tumour cells (excludes UDH)
Collagen IV: Continuous basement membrane around the rounded nodules; absent around invasive nests
Breast biomarkers (CAP Breast Biomarker Template v1.6.2.0):
Testing performed on: Block A6 (invasive component) of this resection
Estrogen receptor (ER): Positive (greater than 10% of cells demonstrate nuclear positivity): 100%, average intensity Strong (3+). Allred score 8/8 (proportion 5 + intensity 3).
Progesterone receptor (PgR): Positive (greater than or equal to 1% of cells demonstrate nuclear positivity): 90%, average intensity Strong (3+). Allred score 8/8.

HER2 by IHC: Negative (Score 1+): incomplete membrane staining that is faint / barely perceptible and in greater than 10% of tumour cells (about 20%). Falls in the HER2-low category used in DESTINY-Breast04.
HER2 by ISH: Not performed (not required for IHC 1+).
Final HER2 status: HER2 NEGATIVE (IHC 1+, HER2-low)
Ki-67 proliferative index: 8% of invasive tumour nuclei (global scoring, International Ki67 in Breast Cancer Working Group method; clone 30-9).

HER2 IHC comment: CAP standardized comment: In the DESTINY-Breast 04 and 06 trials, "HER2 low" was IHC Score 1+ or 2+ / ISH negative, and "HER2 ultralow" was HER2 IHC Score of 0 (pattern 0+) with membrane staining that is incomplete and faint / barely perceptible in less than or equal to 10% of tumour cells. Breast cancers with these staining patterns may be eligible for treatment with trastuzumab-deruxtecan in the metastatic setting (but those with no staining, IHC "null" pattern 0, are currently excluded). WHO 6th edition recommends specifying the IHC 0 staining pattern (0 / absent versus 0+ / with membrane staining); use of the terms HER2-low and HER2-ultralow is not required.

Fixation / methods: Cold ischaemia time 35 minutes; 10% neutral buffered formalin fixation 28 hours (meets ASCO/CAP requirements; no decalcification). Clones: ER SP1, PgR 1E2, HER2 4B5 (Ventana PATHWAY, FDA-approved); ASCO/CAP scoring criteria; internal and external controls stain as expected.

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast, central wide local excision and sentinel lymph node biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Invasive solid papillary carcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation, Nottingham grade 1 (5/9), invasive component 14 mm, arising in solid papillary carcinoma in situ (whole lesion 30 mm). No lymphovascular invasion. Margins clear (invasive closest posterior 6 mm; in situ SPC medial 3 mm). Sentinel lymph nodes negative (0/2). ER and PgR positive, HER2 negative (IHC 1+, HER2-low). pT1c pN0 (sn); AJCC anatomic stage IA; pathological prognostic stage IA.

comment.text: Staging note: per WHO 6th edition and AJCC/CAP, solid papillary carcinoma composed of circumscribed nodules with smooth contours is classified and staged as in situ disease (pTis) even in the absence of myoepithelial cells. WHO 6th edition separates invasive SPC (ragged, jagged geographic nests, as here; the invasive SPC is measured for pT, 14 mm, pT1c) from SPC in situ with invasion (where only the accompanying conventional invasive carcinoma, e.g. mucinous or NST, is typed, graded and measured).

Neuroendocrine marker expression is common in SPC; WHO 6th edition regards SPC as a distinct special type that should not be classified as a neuroendocrine tumour or carcinoma. HER2 IHC 1+ (HER2-low).

micro.text: Sections of the mapped tumour bed show residual invasive carcinoma of no special type arranged as solid nests, sheets and cords with marked nuclear pleomorphism, prominent nucleoli and brisk mitoses (21 per 10 HPF), scattered within hyalinised, oedematous fibrous stroma with foamy macrophages, haemosiderin and chronic inflammation, consistent with partial treatment response. The largest contiguous focus measures 28 mm; tumour cellularity across the 50 x 40 mm bed averages about 30%. A small amount of residual high-grade solid DCIS is present (about 5% of the residual carcinoma). Stromal TILs about 10%.

Extensive lymphovascular invasion is present within the breast. The skin sections show numerous tumour emboli within dilated dermal and subdermal lymphatics (D2-40 positive endothelium) in 7 of 9 skin blocks, including skin of the lower inner quadrant far from the tumour bed, with dermal oedema; tumour does not directly infiltrate the dermis or epidermis and there is no ulceration. Four of 16 axillary lymph nodes contain residual metastatic carcinoma (largest deposit 9 mm, clipped node) with peritumoural fibrosis; one shows 1.5 mm extranodal extension. Two further nodes show fibrotic scars with histiocytes, consistent with regressed metastasis (counted as negative) (4/16).

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast and axilla, modified radical mastectomy after neoadjuvant therapy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Inflammatory carcinoma (clinical cT4d): residual invasive breast carcinoma of no special type, Nottingham grade 3 (9/9), largest contiguous focus 28 mm within a 50 x 40 mm tumour bed with partial treatment response; minor residual high-grade DCIS. Extensive lymphovascular invasion, including extensive dermal lymphatic tumour emboli. Margins clear (closest posterior 6 mm). Residual metastatic carcinoma in 4 of 16 axillary lymph nodes (largest 9 mm, ENE 1.5 mm). ER negative, PgR negative, HER2 positive (IHC 3+), Ki-67 30% (residual). RCB-III (RCB score 3.882). ypT4d ypN2a; post-therapy anatomic stage IIIB.

comment.text: Inflammatory carcinoma is a clinical diagnosis (AJCC 8th / CAP v4.11.0.0): T4d requires clinical erythema and oedema involving at least one-third of the breast skin, which were documented at presentation (about two-thirds) and still about one-third pre-operatively. The dermal lymphatic tumour emboli seen here support but are neither necessary nor sufficient for T4d: emboli without the clinical signs are recorded only as dermal lymphovascular invasion and the tumour is staged by size, and their absence (common in small punch biopsies) does not exclude inflammatory carcinoma. The patient keeps the inflammatory carcinoma designation after neoadjuvant therapy, even if the skin changes resolve.

Staging note: ypT is based on residual tumour size and extent. ypT4d is recorded here because the clinical inflammatory skin changes persisted at surgery. If they had resolved completely, ypT would follow the residual size (28 mm, ypT2), with the inflammatory (cT4d) designation still recorded. Practice varies, so stage with the treating team. The AJCC pathological prognostic stage does not apply after neoadjuvant therapy.

Response: partial response with residual disease in breast and nodes, RCB-III (score 3.882), a high-risk category. HER2 status is retained in the residual tumour (IHC 3+). Residual HER2-positive disease after neoadjuvant therapy is relevant for adjuvant treatment (for example trastuzumab emtansine), but that decision rests with the oncology team. Pre-treatment core biomarkers are listed in the Biomarker section.

diagnoses.name: Paget Disease of Nipple with Underlying DCIS
diagnoses.path: Breast/03 Carcinomas/07 Paget Disease of the Nipple

micro.text: The nipple epidermis contains numerous large atypical cells with abundant pale to amphophilic cytoplasm, large vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli, single and in nests at all levels of the epidermis, most concentrated along the basal layer, with no dermal invasion: Paget disease of the nipple. The process extends 3 mm into the areolar epidermis. The nipple dermis shows chronic inflammation and the surface is eroded.

The major lactiferous ducts and the retroareolar ducts are filled and expanded by high-grade DCIS (nuclear grade III) of solid and comedo type with central necrosis and calcifications, in continuity with the intraepidermal Paget cells. The DCIS spans at least 45 mm in sequential blocks. Myoepithelial cells around the involved ducts are intact on p63 / calponin; no invasion or microinvasion is seen in the entirely submitted lesion with levels. Margins are clear (closest posterior 11 mm).
Two sentinel lymph nodes are negative for metastatic carcinoma (0/2).
Immunohistochemistry / Biomarkers:
Diagnostic immunohistochemistry / ancillary studies:
CK7: Strong diffuse cytoplasmic positivity in intraepidermal Paget cells and in the underlying DCIS (keratinocytes negative)
CAM5.2 (low-molecular-weight cytokeratin): Positive in Paget cells
GATA3: Strong nuclear positivity in Paget cells and DCIS (mammary origin)

HER2 (4B5): Strong complete circumferential membrane staining (3+) in Paget cells and in the underlying DCIS (diagnostic use only: ASCO/CAP HER2 scoring is validated for invasive carcinoma, not DCIS or Paget disease)
p63 and CK5/6: Negative in Paget cells; positive in the surrounding keratinocytes (excludes pagetoid squamous cell carcinoma in situ / Bowen disease)
S100, SOX10 and Melan-A: Negative in Paget cells; highlight only scattered native melanocytes (excludes melanoma in situ)
PAS-diastase / mucicarmine: Occasional Paget cells contain PAS-diastase-resistant, mucicarmine-positive intracytoplasmic mucin; no melanin pigment within tumour cells
p63 / calponin (DCIS): Intact myoepithelial layer around all involved ducts sampled: no invasion
Breast biomarkers (CAP Breast Biomarker Template v1.6.2.0, DCIS):
Testing performed on: Block A9 of this resection (DCIS, retroareolar)
Estrogen receptor (ER): Negative (less than 1%) in DCIS and Paget cells. Internal control (normal ducts) present and stains as expected. Allred score 0.
Progesterone receptor (PgR): Negative (less than 1%). Internal control present and stains as expected. Allred score 0.
HER2: Not reported as a predictive biomarker (HER2 testing of DCIS is not part of ASCO/CAP or CAP DCIS reporting); the diagnostic HER2 IHC (3+) is listed above

Fixation / methods: Cold ischaemia time 30 minutes; 10% neutral buffered formalin fixation 30 hours (meets ASCO/CAP requirements; no decalcification). Clones: ER SP1, PgR 1E2 (Ventana); ASCO/CAP ER/PgR scoring; internal and external controls stain as expected.

finalDiagnosis.label: Left breast and sentinel lymph nodes, simple total mastectomy and sentinel lymph node biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Paget disease of the nipple with underlying high-grade ductal carcinoma in situ (nuclear grade III, solid and comedo types with central necrosis and calcifications), extent at least 45 mm, involving the major lactiferous ducts. No invasive carcinoma or microinvasion. Margins clear (closest posterior 11 mm). Two sentinel lymph nodes negative (0/2). DCIS ER negative, PgR negative. pTis (DCIS) pN0 (sn); AJCC stage 0.

comment.text: The intraepidermal cells are glandular (CK7, CAM5.2 and GATA3 positive, with intracytoplasmic mucin) and HER2 3+, in continuity with the underlying ER-negative high-grade DCIS. This is the typical profile of mammary Paget disease. Pagetoid squamous cell carcinoma in situ (p63 / CK5/6 negative here) and melanoma in situ (S100 / SOX10 / Melan-A negative here) are excluded. Benign Toker cells are also CK7 positive, but they are cytologically bland and HER2 negative.

Staging rule (AJCC 8th; CAP DCIS v4.5.0.1): Paget disease with underlying DCIS is staged by the DCIS as pTis (DCIS). pTis (Paget) is used only when no DCIS or invasive carcinoma is present in the underlying breast parenchyma. Because the whole lesion was submitted and showed no invasion, the CAP DCIS protocol applies rather than the invasive protocol.

HER2 IHC was done for diagnosis. ASCO/CAP HER2 scoring applies only to invasive carcinoma, so this result is not a predictive biomarker. ER/PgR testing on DCIS is reported as in the CAP Biomarker Template.

An ill-defined area of firm grey-white, gritty tissue with comedo-like yellow material on pressure extends from just beneath the nipple towards 12 o'clock over 45 x 30 mm, 11 mm from the posterior margin. The rest is fibro-fatty with fibrocystic change. Specimen radiograph: calcifications in slices 7-10.
Sentinel lymph nodes: two nodes, 9 and 14 mm.

diagnoses.name: Paget Disease of Nipple with Underlying Invasive Carcinoma
diagnoses.path: Breast/03 Carcinomas/07 Paget Disease of the Nipple

micro.text: The nipple epidermis is permeated by large atypical cells with abundant pale cytoplasm and pleomorphic vesicular nuclei, singly and in clusters, without dermal invasion: Paget disease of the nipple. The major lactiferous ducts contain high-grade solid and comedo DCIS with central necrosis and calcifications, continuous with DCIS that extends through the retroareolar ducts to the invasive tumour (DCIS extent at least 65 mm).

At 12 o'clock there is an invasive carcinoma of no special type, 16 mm, made of solid nests and cords with few glands (less than 10%, score 3), markedly pleomorphic nuclei (score 3) and 14 mitoses per 10 HPF (score 2): Nottingham grade 3 (8/9). Focal lymphovascular invasion is present (two vessels, A13). There is no dermal lymphatic invasion and no invasion of the nipple stroma. Margins are clear (invasive carcinoma 9 mm, DCIS 7 mm, both posterior).

One of three sentinel lymph nodes contains a 1.2 mm subcapsular micrometastasis (more than 200 cells, confirmed with AE1/AE3) without extranodal extension; the other two are negative (1/3, micrometastasis).
Immunohistochemistry / Biomarkers:
Diagnostic immunohistochemistry / ancillary studies:
CK7: Strong diffuse cytoplasmic positivity in intraepidermal Paget cells and in the underlying DCIS (keratinocytes negative)
CAM5.2 (low-molecular-weight cytokeratin): Positive in Paget cells
GATA3: Strong nuclear positivity in Paget cells and DCIS (mammary origin)

HER2 (4B5): Strong complete circumferential membrane staining (3+) in Paget cells and in the underlying DCIS (diagnostic use only: ASCO/CAP HER2 scoring is validated for invasive carcinoma, not DCIS or Paget disease)
p63 and CK5/6: Negative in Paget cells; positive in the surrounding keratinocytes (excludes pagetoid squamous cell carcinoma in situ / Bowen disease)
S100, SOX10 and Melan-A: Negative in Paget cells; highlight only scattered native melanocytes (excludes melanoma in situ)
p63 / calponin: Absent around invasive nests; intact around DCIS and the lactiferous ducts (no nipple stromal invasion)
AE1/AE3 (sentinel node 2): Confirms a 1.2 mm cohesive tumour deposit (micrometastasis)
Breast biomarkers (CAP Breast Biomarker Template v1.6.2.0):
Testing performed on: Block A12 of this resection (invasive carcinoma)
Estrogen receptor (ER): Positive (greater than 10% of cells demonstrate nuclear positivity): 40%, average intensity Moderate (2+). Allred score 6/8 (proportion 4 + intensity 2).
Progesterone receptor (PgR): Negative (less than 1%). Internal control present and stains as expected. Allred score 0.
HER2 by IHC: Positive (Score 3+): circumferential membrane staining that is complete, intense and in greater than 10% of tumour cells (about 90%), homogeneous; clustered heterogeneity not identified.
HER2 by ISH: Not performed (not required for IHC 3+).
Final HER2 status: HER2 POSITIVE (IHC 3+)
Ki-67 proliferative index: 35% of invasive tumour nuclei (global scoring, International Ki67 in Breast Cancer Working Group method; clone 30-9).

Fixation / methods: Cold ischaemia time 35 minutes; 10% neutral buffered formalin fixation 28 hours (meets ASCO/CAP requirements; no decalcification). Clones: ER SP1, PgR 1E2, HER2 4B5 (Ventana PATHWAY, FDA-approved); ASCO/CAP scoring criteria; internal and external controls stain as expected.

finalDiagnosis.label: Right breast and sentinel lymph nodes, simple total mastectomy and sentinel lymph node biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Paget disease of the nipple with underlying invasive breast carcinoma of no special type, Nottingham grade 3 (8/9), 16 mm, at 12 o'clock, and extensive high-grade DCIS (at least 65 mm) involving the lactiferous ducts and nipple. Focal lymphovascular invasion; no dermal lymphatic invasion. Margins clear (closest posterior: invasive 9 mm, DCIS 7 mm). Micrometastasis (1.2 mm) in 1 of 3 sentinel lymph nodes. ER positive (40%, moderate), PgR negative, HER2 positive (IHC 3+), Ki-67 35%. pT1c pN1mi (sn); AJCC anatomic stage IB; pathological prognostic stage IA.

comment.text: Paget disease of the nipple with an underlying invasive carcinoma is staged by the invasive carcinoma (largest invasive focus 16 mm, pT1c). Paget disease is still reported (nipple status: Paget's disease present), but it does not change pT and is not pT4b. Pure intraepidermal spread does not count as skin invasion or ulceration (AJCC 8th; CAP v4.11.0.0 Note H). Nipple involvement may matter for surgical planning but does not change pT.

The Paget cells, DCIS and invasive carcinoma share a HER2-positive phenotype, which is typical of mammary Paget disease (CK7, GATA3 positive; p63 / CK5/6, S100 / SOX10 / Melan-A negative). Staging note: a micrometastasis only gives pN1mi (sn). T1 N1mi M0 is anatomic stage IB, and grade 3, ER positive, PgR negative, HER2 positive gives pathological prognostic stage IA.

containers.text: Received a right simple total mastectomy, inked anterior-superior blue, anterior-inferior green and posterior (deep) black, 610 g, 240 x 200 x 50 mm, with a 170 x 75 mm skin ellipse bearing a nipple (11 mm) and areola (38 mm). The nipple is flattened, red and crusted over 9 mm; no ulceration elsewhere. Serial slicing (17 slices) shows a firm, irregular, grey-white tumour, 16 x 14 x 12 mm, at 12 o'clock, 25 mm from the nipple and 9 mm from the posterior margin. Gritty grey-white streaks with comedo-like material extend from the tumour to the nipple base over a total of 65 mm. The rest is fibro-fatty.
Sentinel lymph nodes: three nodes, 7 to 15 mm.

exampleGross.sections: A1-A3 nipple (perpendicular, entirely) and areola; A4-A5 lactiferous ducts; A6-A11 retroareolar ducts towards the tumour in sequence; A12-A15 tumour, entirely (A12 biomarkers); A16-A19 tissue beyond the tumour to map DCIS extent; A20-A21 posterior margin; A22 skin edge; A23-A26 quadrants. B1-B2 sentinel node 1; B3 sentinel node 2; B4 sentinel node 3; all entirely, three levels.

diagnoses.name: Paget Disease of Nipple without Underlying Carcinoma
diagnoses.path: Breast/03 Carcinomas/07 Paget Disease of the Nipple

micro.text: The nipple epidermis contains numerous large atypical cells with abundant pale cytoplasm, large pleomorphic vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli, singly and in small nests at all levels of the epidermis, concentrated along the basal layer, with surface erosion and crusting: Paget disease of the nipple. The process extends 4 mm into the areolar epidermis, reaching to within 1.5 mm of the lateral (3 o'clock) skin margin. There is no dermal invasion; the dermis shows chronic inflammation and a healing punch biopsy tract.

The lactiferous duct orifices, the lactiferous sinuses and the retroareolar ducts and lobules, all entirely submitted and examined on three levels, show no ductal carcinoma in situ, no atypical intraductal proliferation and no invasive carcinoma; there is duct ectasia only. Cytokeratin 7 shows no Paget cells beyond the epidermis apart from occasional bland Toker cells (HER2 negative) at the nipple base.
Immunohistochemistry / Biomarkers:
Diagnostic immunohistochemistry / ancillary studies:
CK7: Strong diffuse cytoplasmic positivity in intraepidermal Paget cells and in the underlying DCIS (keratinocytes negative)
CAM5.2 (low-molecular-weight cytokeratin): Positive in Paget cells
GATA3: Strong nuclear positivity in Paget cells and DCIS (mammary origin)

HER2 (4B5): Strong complete circumferential membrane staining (3+) in Paget cells and in the underlying DCIS (diagnostic use only: ASCO/CAP HER2 scoring is validated for invasive carcinoma, not DCIS or Paget disease)
p63 and CK5/6: Negative in Paget cells; positive in the surrounding keratinocytes (excludes pagetoid squamous cell carcinoma in situ / Bowen disease)
S100, SOX10 and Melan-A: Negative in Paget cells; highlight only scattered native melanocytes (excludes melanoma in situ)
PAS-diastase / mucicarmine: Occasional Paget cells contain PAS-diastase-resistant, mucicarmine-positive intracytoplasmic mucin; no melanin pigment within tumour cells
CK7 (lactiferous ducts and dermis): No atypical CK7-positive cells in the dermis or lactiferous sinuses; a few bland CK7-positive, HER2-negative Toker cells at the nipple base
Breast biomarkers (CAP Breast Biomarker Template v1.6.2.0, DCIS):
Testing performed on: Block A2 of this resection (intraepidermal Paget cells; no parenchymal disease)
Estrogen receptor (ER): Negative (less than 1%) in Paget cells. Internal control (benign lactiferous duct epithelium) present and stains as expected. Allred score 0.
Progesterone receptor (PgR): Negative (less than 1%). Internal control present and stains as expected. Allred score 0.
HER2: Not reported as a predictive biomarker (not validated for Paget disease / DCIS); the diagnostic HER2 IHC (3+) is listed above

Fixation / methods: Cold ischaemia time 30 minutes; 10% neutral buffered formalin fixation 30 hours (meets ASCO/CAP requirements; no decalcification). Clones: ER SP1, PgR 1E2 (Ventana); ASCO/CAP ER/PgR scoring; internal and external controls stain as expected.

finalDiagnosis.label: Left nipple-areola complex with retroareolar tissue, central excision:
finalDiagnosis.text: Paget disease of the nipple (intraepidermal, high-grade cytology), 10 mm on the nipple with 4 mm areolar extension, without underlying ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive carcinoma in the entirely submitted lactiferous ducts and retroareolar breast tissue. Closest margin: lateral (areolar skin) 1.5 mm from Paget cells; deep margin clear. Paget cells ER negative, PgR negative, HER2 IHC 3+ (diagnostic). pTis (Paget); pN not assigned; AJCC stage 0 (with cN0 cM0).

comment.text: pTis (Paget) is used only for Paget disease without DCIS or invasive carcinoma in the underlying breast parenchyma (AJCC 8th; CAP DCIS v4.5.0.1). That requires an excision with the lactiferous ducts and retroareolar tissue submitted entirely, together with clinical and radiological correlation (normal mammogram, ultrasound and MRI here). A nipple punch or wedge biopsy alone diagnoses Paget disease but cannot exclude underlying carcinoma, so pT should not be assigned on a punch. Pure Paget disease is uncommon: most cases have underlying DCIS and/or invasive carcinoma, which may lie deeper than this cone. Continued imaging surveillance is advised.

The immunoprofile (CK7, CAM5.2, GATA3 positive, HER2 3+, ER negative; p63, CK5/6, S100, SOX10, Melan-A negative; intracytoplasmic mucin) confirms mammary Paget disease and excludes pagetoid Bowen disease and melanoma in situ. The atypical cells are separate from the scattered bland, HER2-negative Toker cells.

Margin: CAP DCIS margin categories are applied to the intraepidermal disease. The lateral areolar skin margin is 1.5 mm from Paget cells (1 to 2 mm category). Re-excision versus radiotherapy is for the multidisciplinary team. The HER2 and ER results here are for diagnosis only.

containers.text: Received a left central excision, orientated with a stitch at 12 o'clock and inked: skin edge (areolar margin) red, deep (retroareolar) margin black. It comprises a disc of skin 48 x 45 mm with a central nipple (12 mm) and areola (38 mm), and a cone of retroareolar breast tissue 30 mm deep (total 48 x 45 x 32 mm; 28 g). The nipple surface is red and crusted over 10 mm, reaching close to the 3 o'clock (lateral) areolar edge. A previous punch biopsy site is visible at the nipple tip. Serial slicing shows the lactiferous ducts converging on the nipple base; there is no mass, no gritty tissue and no comedo-like material. The retroareolar tissue is fibro-fatty with mildly ectatic ducts.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted: A1-A4 nipple (perpendicular sections through the nipple and lactiferous ducts, including the punch site); A5-A8 areola with radial skin margins at 12, 3, 6 and 9 o'clock (3 o'clock lateral margin in A6); A9-A14 retroareolar cone in sequence including the deep margin. Three levels on all blocks.

diagnoses.name: Uterine Leiomyomas and Adenomyosis (TAH-BSO)
diagnoses.path: Female Genital Tract/Uterus/01 Myometrium - Leiomyoma and Adenomyosis

micro.text: The five myometrial nodules are usual-type (conventional) leiomyomas: intersecting fascicles of cytologically bland spindle cells with cigar-shaped nuclei, fine chromatin and inconspicuous nucleoli, with eosinophilic fibrillary cytoplasm. Mitotic figures are scarce (up to 1 per 10 HPF). There is no coagulative tumour-cell necrosis, no significant cytologic atypia and no myxoid or epithelioid change. The surrounding myometrium is compressed but not invaded. The submucosal nodule is covered by attenuated proliferative endometrium.

The myometrium shows diffuse adenomyosis: endometrial glands of proliferative type accompanied by endometrial stroma, deep within the myometrium, more than 2 mm from the endomyometrial junction and involving more than half the wall thickness (deepest focus 18 mm from the junction in a 28 mm anterior wall). Some foci show haemorrhage and haemosiderin. There is no stromal neoplasia.

The endometrium is proliferative, without hyperplasia, polyp, atypical hyperplasia or carcinoma. The cervix shows chronic cervicitis with mature squamous metaplasia; the transformation zone is present; no CIN or invasive carcinoma. Both ovaries contain follicular cysts; no endometriosis or neoplasm. Both tubes are histologically unremarkable.

finalDiagnosis.label: Uterus, cervix, bilateral tubes and ovaries, total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: 1. Uterus: multiple (five) usual-type leiomyomas (largest 48 mm, intramural anterior; also intramural, submucosal and subserosal). 2. Uterus: diffuse adenomyosis. 3. Endometrium: proliferative, no hyperplasia or malignancy. 4. Cervix: chronic cervicitis; no dysplasia. 5. Fallopian tubes and ovaries: no significant abnormality (follicular cysts).

comment.text: Usual-type leiomyoma is a benign smooth-muscle tumour. The diagnosis rests on the absence of the Stanford criteria for malignancy (significant cytologic atypia, coagulative tumour-cell necrosis, and elevated mitotic activity). None of these is present here, so there is no indication for a diagnosis of leiomyosarcoma or of smooth-muscle tumour of uncertain malignant potential (STUMP). Immunohistochemistry (desmin, SMA, h-caldesmon) is not required when the morphology is typical; it can be used if a differential of endometrial stromal tumour or other spindle-cell lesion arises.

Adenomyosis is defined by endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium, conventionally more than one low-power field (about 2–2.5 mm) beneath the endomyometrial junction. Diffuse deep involvement, as here, correlates with the clinical dysmenorrhoea and heavy bleeding. Coexistence of leiomyomas and adenomyosis is common.
No residual endometrium of concern: the pre-operative sampling and the hysterectomy endometrium are concordant (proliferative). No further pathologic follow-up is required for these benign findings.

containers.text: Received an intact uterus with attached cervix, 420 g, 145 (fundus to ectocervix) x 95 (cornu to cornu) x 70 mm. The serosa is smooth and glistening with a 12 mm bosselated, firm, white subserosal nodule on the right lateral wall. The cervix is 32 mm long with a transverse slit os; ectocervix 28 mm diameter. The endometrial cavity is triangular, 55 mm long, and distorted by a 15 mm pedunculated, firm, white submucosal nodule on the posterior wall. The endometrium is 3–4 mm thick, tan and uniform. The myometrium is up to 28 mm thick anteriorly and 25 mm posteriorly, trabeculated and mottled with soft haemorrhagic foci of adenomyosis, most marked in the posterior wall. Within the myometrium there are four additional circumscribed, firm, white, whorled nodules without necrosis, haemorrhage or softening: anterior intramural 48 x 40 x 35 mm; fundal intramural 22 mm; posterior intramural 18 mm; and the right subserosal 12 mm already noted (five leiomyomas in total). Right ovary 30 x 20 x 15 mm and left ovary 28 x 18 x 14 mm, both with a few thin-walled cysts up to 8 mm; no solid mass. Each fallopian tube is about 55 mm long with fimbriae, no adhesions or dilatation. Parametrial soft tissue is scant and unremarkable.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A2 cervix (anterior and posterior lips through transformation zone); A3–A4 anterior endomyometrium full thickness; A5–A6 posterior endomyometrium full thickness (including deepest adenomyosis); A7–A9 largest (anterior) leiomyoma, representative (including interface with myometrium); A10 submucosal leiomyoma entirely; A11 fundal, A12 posterior intramural and A13 subserosal leiomyomas, representative; A14 lower uterine segment; A15 right cornu; B1 right ovary; B2 right tube; C1 left ovary; C2 left tube.

diagnoses.name: Leiomyoma, Usual Type (Myomectomy)
diagnoses.path: Female Genital Tract/Uterus/01 Myometrium - Leiomyoma and Adenomyosis

micro.text: Sections show a usual-type leiomyoma: intersecting fascicles of cytologically bland smooth-muscle cells with elongated blunt-ended nuclei, fine chromatin and eosinophilic cytoplasm, separated by hyalinised collagen in places. Mitotic count 1 per 10 HPF (field diameter 0.55 mm). No coagulative tumour-cell necrosis, no significant cytologic atypia, no epithelioid or myxoid areas, and no intravascular growth. The attached rim is non-neoplastic myometrium. The inked enucleation surface abuts compressed leiomyoma or myometrium without a separate soft-tissue cuff (expected for myomectomy).
Immunohistochemistry confirms smooth-muscle differentiation (desmin, SMA and h-caldesmon diffusely positive; CD10 negative), supporting leiomyoma over endometrial stromal tumour.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
Desmin: Diffuse cytoplasmic positivity
SMA (smooth muscle actin): Diffuse cytoplasmic positivity
h-Caldesmon: Diffuse cytoplasmic positivity
CD10: Negative (excludes endometrial stromal tumour)
Ki-67: Low (less than 5% of nuclei)

finalDiagnosis.label: Uterus, laparoscopic myomectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Usual-type (conventional) leiomyoma, 70 mm, intact enucleation. No atypia, coagulative necrosis or raised mitotic activity. Desmin / SMA / h-caldesmon positive.

comment.text: The morphology and immunoprofile are those of a usual-type leiomyoma. Stanford criteria for leiomyosarcoma (diffuse moderate-to-severe atypia, coagulative tumour-cell necrosis, and mitotic count typically 10 or more per 10 HPF in the most active area, with nuances by subtype) are not met. Mitotically active leiomyoma (raised mitoses without atypia or necrosis) and STUMP are not suggested here.

Myomectomy removes the fibroid for symptoms and fertility preservation; 'margins' are the enucleation plane and are not interpreted as in cancer resection. Recurrence of fibroids elsewhere in the uterus is a clinical possibility and is unrelated to this specimen's histology.
If future hysterectomy tissue shows an atypical smooth-muscle tumour, correlation with this myomectomy (and any morcellation history — none here; specimen received intact) would be relevant.

containers.text: Received an intact, firm, ovoid mass, 98 g, 70 x 55 x 48 mm, with a smooth, bosselated, white cut surface showing a classic whorled pattern. A thin rim of pink myometrium (up to 2 mm) is attached over about one-third of the surface (enucleation plane). No softening, yellow necrosis, haemorrhage or cystic change. The outer surface is inked.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted after serial slicing at 8–10 mm: A1–A8 representative slices including the enucleation surface and the attached myometrial rim (A3 and A5 for IHC).

diagnoses.name: Adenomyosis with Incidental Leiomyoma (TLH)
diagnoses.path: Female Genital Tract/Uterus/01 Myometrium - Leiomyoma and Adenomyosis

micro.text: The myometrium is extensively involved by adenomyosis: proliferative-type to inactive endometrial glands accompanied by endometrial stroma, irregularly distributed from just beneath the endomyometrial junction to within 2 mm of the posterior serosa. Many foci show recent haemorrhage and haemosiderin-laden macrophages, correlating with the clinical dysmenorrhoea. There is associated smooth-muscle hyperplasia of the myometrium. No stromal sarcoma or carcinoma arising in adenomyosis.

The endometrium is thin and inactive / weakly proliferative with stromal decidualisation consistent with levonorgestrel IUS effect. No hyperplasia, polyp or malignancy. The 8 mm posterior nodule is a usual-type leiomyoma (bland spindle cells, no atypia, no coagulative necrosis, mitoses 0–1 per 10 HPF). The cervix shows mild chronic inflammation only; no dysplasia.
Fallopian tubes and ovaries were not submitted (conserved).

finalDiagnosis.label: Uterus and cervix, total laparoscopic hysterectomy (adnexa retained):
finalDiagnosis.text: 1. Diffuse extensive adenomyosis (near full-thickness, particularly posterior wall). 2. Incidental usual-type leiomyoma, 8 mm, intramural. 3. Endometrium: inactive / progestogen (LNG-IUS) effect; no hyperplasia or malignancy. 4. Cervix: no significant abnormality. 5. Levonorgestrel IUS retrieved.

comment.text: This specimen is adenomyosis-predominant: the clinical bulk and pain are explained by diffuse deep adenomyosis rather than by the tiny incidental leiomyoma. Adenomyosis can coexist with fibroids; when fibroids are minimal, imaging (thickened junctional zone) and the trabeculated haemorrhagic myometrium are the clues.

Carcinoma or endometrial stromal sarcoma arising in adenomyosis is rare; none is present after representative full-thickness sampling including the deepest foci. The LNG-IUS effect accounts for the inactive endometrium and should not be mistaken for atrophy of postmenopausal type in this premenopausal patient.
Ovaries and tubes were conserved and are not assessed pathologically; any future adnexal pathology would be a separate specimen.

containers.text: Received an intact uterus with cervix, 185 g, 95 (fundus to ectocervix) x 70 x 55 mm. The uterus is symmetrically enlarged and globular. The serosa is smooth. The cervix is 28 mm long with a pinpoint os. The endometrial cavity contains a retrieved levonorgestrel IUS (arms intact; submitted in a separate container). The endometrium is thin (1–2 mm), pale. The myometrium is markedly thickened (up to 32 mm posteriorly, 28 mm anteriorly), firm, trabeculated and mottled with soft brown haemorrhagic foci of adenomyosis that approach the serosa posteriorly. A single, firm, white, 8 mm intramural nodule is present in the posterior wall, without necrosis. No adnexa are included.
Levonorgestrel intrauterine system (IUS) retrieved from the endometrial cavity, arms intact, received in a separate container. Photographed and described; no tissue.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A2 cervix (anterior and posterior through transformation zone); A3–A5 anterior endomyometrium full thickness (including serosa); A6–A9 posterior endomyometrium full thickness to serosa (deepest adenomyosis); A10 lower uterine segment; A11 cornual regions; A12 incidental leiomyoma entirely; A13 endometrium additional; separate: IUS photographed and described (no tissue).

micro.text: Sections show abundant endometrium with crowded proliferative-type glands of variable size and shape, including irregularly branched and cystically dilated glands, set in cellular proliferative stroma. The gland-to-stroma ratio is increased in most fragments, but the glands remain separated by stroma; there is no cribriforming, gland confluence or back-to-back glands.

The glandular epithelium is pseudostratified columnar with elongated, cigar-shaped nuclei and mitotic activity, cytologically identical to the background proliferative glands. There is no rounding, vesicular change, loss of polarity or prominent nucleoli to define a cytologically altered population. Focal tubal (ciliated) metaplasia and a small squamous morule are present. Areas of stromal breakdown with fibrin thrombi and collapsing stroma reflect anovulatory bleeding.
No secretory change, polyp, atypical hyperplasia or carcinoma is identified on levels.

finalDiagnosis.label: Endometrium, Pipelle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Endometrial hyperplasia without atypia (WHO 2020), with focal tubal and squamous morular metaplasia and stromal breakdown. No atypical hyperplasia / EIN or carcinoma identified.

comment.text: WHO 2020 two-tier terminology: 'hyperplasia without atypia' replaces simple and complex hyperplasia without atypia. It is a non-clonal response to unopposed oestrogen, fitting the obesity / anovulation context here. The risk of progression to carcinoma is low (about 1–3% over 20 years). Most cases regress once the oestrogen excess is removed or progestin is given.

Management (for clinical correlation, per RCOG/BSGE 2016 and current practice): address risk factors such as weight. First-line treatment is a levonorgestrel intrauterine system (LNG-IUS), or continuous oral progestogen if the IUS is declined. Repeat endometrial sampling at least every 6 months, with discharge after two consecutive negative biopsies. Re-biopsy promptly if bleeding persists or recurs. Hysterectomy is not first-line but may be considered for progression, failed treatment or persistent symptoms.

Differentials considered: disordered proliferative endometrium, where gland irregularity is focal and the gland:stroma ratio is not markedly raised; endometrial polyp, which shows fibrous stroma and thick-walled vessels, absent here; metaplasias, which are present only focally and are not the dominant change; and atypical hyperplasia / EIN, excluded because there is no cytologically distinct crowded gland population. If a lesion is seen later on imaging, targeted sampling (hysteroscopy) is advised.

containers.text: Received in a container labelled with the patient's details and 'endometrial pipelle': multiple soft, tan-red mucoid tissue fragments and blood clot, aggregate 25 x 20 x 4 mm (about 0.8 mL tissue).

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A2 (filtered through a fine mesh bag). Three levels examined.

micro.text: Sections show fragments of proliferative endometrium in which there are discrete regions of markedly crowded glands, with gland area exceeding stromal area and only thin intervening stroma, each region measuring more than 1 mm. The glands are tubular and branched, focally nearly back-to-back, without cribriform bridging, solid sheets, villoglandular architecture or desmoplastic stroma.

The lesional epithelium is cytologically different from the background glands: nuclei are enlarged and rounded with vesicular chromatin, loss of polarity and conspicuous small nucleoli, with focal mucinous and eosinophilic change. The background glands are proliferative, with cigar-shaped nuclei, and focally show hyperplasia without atypia. Mitoses are present in lesional glands; there is no necrosis.
Immunohistochemistry shows loss of PAX2 and PTEN in the lesional glands, with retention in the background glands; MMR proteins are intact and p53 is wild-type. No carcinoma is identified.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
PAX2: Loss of nuclear expression in the crowded atypical glands; retained in background non-lesional glands (supports clonal EIN)
PTEN: Loss of cytoplasmic/nuclear staining in lesional glands; retained in background glands and stroma (internal control)

MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6 (MMR proteins): Intact nuclear expression in lesional glands (MMR proficient). Lynch-pattern loss not seen; MMR testing is not mandatory on AH but is useful when a hysterectomy is likely
p53: Wild-type (scattered, variable nuclear staining)
ER / PR: Diffusely positive in lesional glands (relevant if fertility-sparing progestin therapy is chosen)

finalDiagnosis.label: Endometrium, Pipelle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Atypical hyperplasia / endometrioid intraepithelial neoplasia (AH/EIN), WHO 2020. PAX2 and PTEN loss in lesional glands; MMR proteins intact (proficient); p53 wild-type. No carcinoma identified in this sample.

comment.text: AH/EIN is a clonal premalignant lesion: crowded glands with gland area greater than stroma, a cytologically distinct population compared with the background, lesion size greater than 1 mm, and exclusion of benign mimics and carcinoma. Loss of PAX2 (about 70–80% of EIN) and of PTEN (about 40–60%) in lesional glands supports the diagnosis, but retained staining does not exclude it.

A biopsy samples only part of the endometrium. In hysterectomies done after an AH/EIN biopsy, concurrent endometrioid carcinoma is found in roughly 25–40% (up to about 40% in the GOG-167 series), usually low grade and superficial. Total hysterectomy, with BSO according to age and clinical decision, is therefore the standard recommendation (ACOG/SGO and RCOG/BSGE guidance). Frozen section and lymphadenectomy are not routine for AH alone.

Fertility-sparing option, for selected patients who want future pregnancy, after MDT counselling: progestin therapy (LNG-IUS preferred, or oral progestogen), pelvic MRI to exclude myoinvasion or adnexal disease, and endometrial sampling every 3 months until two consecutive negative results. Hysterectomy is advised after childbearing or if the lesion persists or progresses. Weight reduction and PCOS management are advised. ER/PR positivity supports, but does not guarantee, response to progestin.

MMR: intact here, so no evidence of Lynch-pattern loss. Because of the family history of colorectal cancer, genetic counselling may still be considered, and universal MMR or MSI testing is recommended on any subsequent carcinoma.

containers.text: Received in a container labelled 'endometrial biopsy': multiple tan-pink soft fragments, aggregate 20 x 15 x 3 mm.

exampleGross.sections: Entirely submitted in A1–A2. Three levels; IHC on A1.

diagnoses.name: Residual Atypical Hyperplasia - EIN, No Carcinoma (TLH-BSO)

micro.text: Multifocal residual atypical hyperplasia / EIN is present at the fundus and posterior wall: crowded tubular and branched glands with gland area exceeding stroma, focally back-to-back, lined by cytologically altered cells with rounded vesicular nuclei and small nucleoli that differ from the adjacent proliferative glands. Focal mucinous and morular metaplasia. Background endometrium is proliferative with hyperplasia without atypia elsewhere.

After complete submission of the endometrium and levels on all lesional blocks, there is no endometrioid carcinoma: no confluent cribriform or solid growth, no maze-like architecture, no desmoplastic stromal response and no myometrial invasion. The endomyometrial junction is smooth. No lymphovascular space involvement (LVSI does not apply to AH/EIN).

The myometrium is unremarkable. The cervix shows chronic cervicitis without CIN or extension of hyperplasia. The fallopian tubes, including fimbriae examined per SEE-FIM, show no STIC; the ovaries show corpora albicantia and inclusion cysts.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
PAX2 (block A7): Loss in lesional crowded glands; retained in background glands
MMR (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6): Intact on prior biopsy (not repeated)

finalDiagnosis.label: Uterus, cervix, bilateral tubes and ovaries, total laparoscopic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: 1. Endometrium: residual atypical hyperplasia / endometrioid intraepithelial neoplasia (AH/EIN), multifocal (fundus and posterior wall), with background hyperplasia without atypia. No carcinoma identified (entire endometrium examined). 2. Myometrium: no significant abnormality. 3. Cervix: chronic cervicitis; no dysplasia. 4. Fallopian tubes and ovaries: no significant abnormality.

comment.text: The hysterectomy confirms the biopsy diagnosis of AH/EIN. No carcinoma was found after the whole endometrium was submitted. That is the expected outcome in about 60–75% of such cases; the remainder harbour concurrent carcinoma.

Atypical hyperplasia is not a cancer, so no FIGO stage, histologic grade or LVSI assessment applies. No adjuvant therapy is indicated on pathological grounds. Morcellation was not used, which preserved the specimen for complete assessment.
MMR proteins were intact on the prior biopsy. Any future carcinoma, or a strong family history, would warrant Lynch syndrome assessment.

containers.text: Received an intact uterus with cervix and attached adnexa, 135 g. Uterus 85 (fundus to ectocervix) x 55 x 40 mm. Serosa smooth. Cervix 30 mm long, ectocervix 25 mm, unremarkable. The uterus is opened bivalved. The endometrium is tan, velvety and thickened up to 6 mm, most marked at the fundus and on the posterior wall; no exophytic mass, polyp or ulceration. Myometrium 18 mm thick, uniform, without nodules or trabeculation. Right tube 60 mm and right ovary 25 x 15 x 10 mm; left tube 55 mm and left ovary 22 x 14 x 10 mm; all grossly unremarkable.

exampleGross.sections: Entire endometrium submitted with the underlying inner myometrium in mapped full-thickness strips (A3–A14: anterior A3–A5, fundus A6–A8, posterior A9–A12, cornua A13–A14); A15 lower uterine segment; A1–A2 cervix (anterior and posterior lips); B1–B2 right ovary and tube (fimbria entirely, SEE-FIM); C1–C2 left ovary and tube (fimbria entirely). Three levels on lesional blocks.

micro.text: All three pieces show similar features, consistent with haemorrhoids:

Vascular changes: Expanded submucosa (and subepithelial stroma beneath the anoderm at the external ends) containing clusters of markedly dilated, congested, thin-walled venous channels and thick-walled vessels with irregular smooth-muscle walls. Loose oedematous stroma with scattered haemosiderin-laden macrophages.

Thrombosis: 7 o'clock (B): a laminated thrombus with lines of Zahn showing early organisation (ingrowth of granulation tissue and fibroblasts from the wall) and early recanalisation, with recent haemorrhage into the surrounding stroma. 11 o'clock (C): an older organised and recanalised thrombus, which matches the small grey nodule seen grossly.
Haemorrhage: Recent interstitial haemorrhage in B, and patchy recent haemorrhage elsewhere.

Surface epithelium: Anorectal (colorectal-type) columnar mucosa at the internal ends; anal transitional zone epithelium; non-keratinising squamous epithelium of the anoderm; keratinised hair-bearing perianal skin at the external end of A and B. In B there is a focal surface erosion with fibrinopurulent exudate and granulation tissue. The rectal mucosa shows mild prolapse-type changes: mild crypt distortion, fibromuscular obliteration of the lamina propria, and mild chronic inflammation.

Negative findings: No viral cytopathic changes (koilocytes). No anal squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL/HSIL; AIN). No glandular dysplasia. No atypical melanocytic proliferation. No Paget cells. No malignancy. Granulomas and parasites are absent.

finalDiagnosis.label: Anal canal, haemorrhoidectomy (3, 7 and 11 o'clock pedicles):
finalDiagnosis.text: Haemorrhoids (mixed internal and external). Dilated, congested vascular channels, with a recent thrombus showing early organisation (7 o'clock) and an old organised, recanalised thrombus (11 o'clock). Focal surface erosion. Mild chronic inflammation.
Negative for HPV-related changes, squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL/HSIL), dysplasia and malignancy.
