comment.text: The features are those of haemorrhoids, which are dilated vascular cushions of the anal canal. They include thrombosis at different stages, which matches the acute painful episode at 7 o'clock.
Differential diagnoses considered and excluded on histology:
Fibroepithelial polyp / skin tag: Fibrovascular stroma covered by squamous epithelium, without the dilated vascular channels seen here.
Mucosal prolapse / inflammatory cloacogenic polyp: Only mild prolapse-type change is present, with no polyp.
Condyloma acuminatum: No papillomatosis or koilocytes.
Anal squamous intraepithelial lesion (AIN): Not identified. Incidental HSIL is uncommon but important, particularly in high-risk groups.
Anorectal melanoma and other malignancies: Not identified. These are rare incidental findings.

Routine histological examination of haemorrhoidectomy specimens is still common practice, although its yield is low. Unexpected findings occur in only a small proportion of cases (most often anal squamous intraepithelial lesion, and rarely carcinoma or melanoma). Some centres submit these specimens selectively, based on clinical risk factors and the surgeon's findings. Here all pedicles were small enough to be submitted entirely, so sampling is complete.
No further action is needed from a pathology point of view. Clinical follow-up is as per the surgical team.

containers.text: Received in formalin, labelled with the patient's name and 'haemorrhoids x 3', three separate tan-purple, polypoid, wedge-shaped tissue pieces. Each is covered partly by smooth pink-tan mucosa and partly by grey-white skin at the external end. Each piece is bisected along its long axis. 3 o'clock: 2.2 x 1.4 x 1.0 cm. Mucosa-covered, with a 0.5 cm skin strip at the external end. Cut surface: spongy, with dilated blood-filled vessels. No thrombus. No mass, ulcer or pigmented lesion.

7 o'clock: 3.0 x 2.0 x 1.4 cm. Mucosa and skin covered, with a 0.6 cm area of dusky surface erosion. Cut surface: dilated vessels with a 1.1 cm dark red-brown, laminated, firm thrombus beneath the skin and transitional zone. No mass or pigmented lesion.
11 o'clock: 2.0 x 1.2 x 0.9 cm. Mucosa-covered. Cut surface: spongy, with dilated vessels and a 0.3 cm pale-grey nodule (fibrosed vessel). No mass or pigmented lesion.

exampleGross.sections: Each pedicle is submitted entirely in longitudinal sections that include the mucosa-skin junction: A1–A2 (3 o'clock), B1–B3 (7 o'clock, including the thrombus and the eroded surface), C1–C2 (11 o'clock).

micro.text: Sections show appendix with patchy mucosal erosions and a neutrophilic infiltrate concentrated in the mucosa and submucosa, with early extension of neutrophils into the inner circular layer of the muscularis propria at a few foci. Crypt abscesses are focal. The outer muscularis and serosa show vascular congestion and mild oedema without a fibrinopurulent exudate. There is no transmural necrosis, no perforation and no periappendiceal abscess.
No granuloma, parasite, diverticulum or neoplasm is identified. The proximal resection margin shows intact mucosa without active neutrophilic inflammation.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Early acute (catarrhal) appendicitis. Neutrophilic inflammation involving mucosa, submucosa and early muscularis propria; no serositis, gangrene or perforation. Proximal resection margin free of active inflammation. No neoplasm identified.

comment.text: Early / catarrhal appendicitis denotes acute neutrophilic inflammation that has not yet become fully transmural with fibrinopurulent periappendicitis. Neutrophils within the muscularis propria support the diagnosis of acute appendicitis over mucosal-only (uncertain significance) change. Clinical-radiologic correlation is advised.

containers.text: Received a vermiform appendix measuring 6.5 cm in length and 0.7 cm in maximum diameter, with a short mesoappendix. The serosal surface is mildly congested and dull over the distal third; no fibrinopurulent exudate, perforation or gangrene is identified. The proximal surgical margin is unremarkable. On cut section the wall is up to 0.25 cm thick. The lumen contains scant faecal material. No faecolith or tumour is seen.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal resection margin (en face); representative transverse sections from proximal, middle and distal appendix including tip (entire specimen submitted).

diagnoses.name: Acute Suppurative Phlegmonous Appendicitis with Periappendicitis

micro.text: Sections show appendix with mucosal ulceration and a dense transmural infiltrate of neutrophils extending through the mucosa, submucosa and muscularis propria into the serosa. The lumen contains neutrophils, necrotic debris and fibrin. The submucosal and serosal vessels are congested, with fibrinopurulent exudate over the serosal surface and periappendiceal fat (acute serositis / periappendicitis). Lymphoid hyperplasia is mild.
There is no granuloma, no parasite or ova, no dysplasia and no evidence of neoplasm. The proximal resection margin is viable, with no active inflammation. No gangrene or perforation is identified.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Acute suppurative (phlegmonous) appendicitis with acute serositis (periappendicitis). No perforation, gangrene or neoplasm identified. Proximal resection margin free of inflammation.

containers.text: Received a vermiform appendix measuring 7 cm in length and 1 cm in maximum diameter. The serosal surface is congested and dull, with fibrinopurulent exudate over the distal half. The mesoappendix is oedematous and congested. The proximal surgical margin is unremarkable. On cut section, the wall is thickened (0.3 cm) and the lumen contains purulent material and faecal matter. No faecolith, perforation or tumour is identified.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal resection margin, and representative transverse sections from the proximal, middle and distal parts of the appendix, including the mesoappendix. Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Sections from the distal appendix show full-thickness coagulative necrosis of the wall with loss of nuclear staining, ghost outlines of muscularis propria, and dense neutrophilic debris with bacterial colonies. Viable mucosa is absent in necrotic segments. Adjacent viable wall shows dense transmural neutrophilic inflammation extending into the serosa and mesoappendix with fibrinopurulent periappendicitis.

No frank full-thickness perforation defect with luminal continuity to the periappendiceal space is demonstrated in the sections examined, although mural necrosis is extensive (gangrenous appendicitis). The proximal resection margin shows viable tissue with mild acute inflammation confined to the mucosa; the muscularis and serosa at the margin are viable. No granuloma, parasite or neoplasm is identified. A faecolith is present.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Gangrenous appendicitis with acute periappendicitis and faecolith. No frank perforation or neoplasm identified. Proximal resection margin viable.

comment.text: Gangrenous appendicitis indicates transmural necrosis. Distinction from perforated appendicitis requires demonstration of a full-thickness defect; none was identified grossly or microscopically in this sample. Clinical correlation for peritonitis remains important.

containers.text: Received a vermiform appendix measuring 8.5 cm in length and 1.4 cm in maximum diameter, with attached oedematous mesoappendix. The distal two-thirds of the serosa is dull, green-black and friable, with fibrinopurulent exudate. No frank perforation hole is identified on careful inspection. The proximal 2 cm is congested but pink and viable. On cut section the distal wall is thinned, necrotic and green-black; the lumen contains foul purulent material and a faecolith measuring 0.8 cm. No tumour is seen.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal resection margin; sections through viable-gangrenous transition; distal necrotic wall and faecolith bed; mesoappendix. Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Sections confirm full-thickness perforation of the appendiceal wall with discontinuity of mucosa, muscularis propria and serosa, and direct communication with a periappendiceal abscess cavity lined by granulation tissue, neutrophils and fibrin. The appendiceal wall adjacent to the perforation shows transmural neutrophilic inflammation and foci of coagulative necrosis (gangrene). Fibrinopurulent serositis extends widely over the serosa and into the mesoappendix.

The proximal resection margin is viable and free of active transmural inflammation. No granuloma, parasite or neoplasm is identified. Bacterial colonies are present within the abscess and necrotic wall.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix with periappendiceal soft tissue, appendicectomy and drainage:
finalDiagnosis.text: Perforated appendicitis with periappendiceal abscess and adjacent gangrene. Proximal resection margin viable. No neoplasm identified.

containers.text: Received an appendix measuring 7.5 cm in length and 1.5 cm in maximum diameter, with adherent periappendiceal soft tissue and abscess cavity wall. The mid-portion of the appendix shows a 0.6 cm full-thickness perforation with ragged edges and surrounding green-black necrosis. The serosa is coated with thick fibrinopurulent exudate. Attached soft tissue contains a cavity filled with creamy yellow pus measuring approximately 3 cm. The proximal margin appears viable. On cut section the lumen communicates with the perforation. A faecolith 0.7 cm is present near the perforation site. No tumour is identified.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal resection margin; perforation site with adjacent wall; abscess wall / periappendiceal soft tissue; tip; mesoappendix. Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Sections show appendix with marked mural fibrosis, granulation tissue, haemosiderin and foamy macrophage collections (xanthogranulomatous change). Scattered non-caseating granulomas and multinucleated giant cells are present, some related to residual faecal material / foreign-body type. Residual mixed chronic inflammation is present; neutrophils are scant. Serosa shows dense fibrous adhesions without active fibrinopurulent exudate. No ongoing abscess cavity in this specimen.
No parasites, diverticula or neoplasm. Special stains for AFB and fungi negative. Proximal margin shows fibrosis without active inflammation.
Special Stains / Immunohistochemistry:
ZN: No acid-fast bacilli
GMS / PAS: No fungi

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, interval appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Interval (post-antibiotic) appendicitis: organising mural fibrosis, granulation tissue, xanthogranulomatous inflammation and non-caseating granulomas, consistent with treated complicated appendicitis. No residual abscess, active perforation or neoplasm.

comment.text: Granulomas in interval appendicectomy specimens are well recognised after antibiotic therapy for perforated / phlegmonous appendicitis and do not equate to Crohn disease or TB by themselves. Negative special stains and the clinical history of successful non-operative management support an interval/post-therapy pattern. Still exclude infection and IBD if clinically discordant.

containers.text: Received an appendix measuring 6 cm in length and 0.9 cm in maximum diameter with dense fibrous adhesions. Serosa white and fibrotic; no fresh exudate, perforation or gangrene. On cut section wall thickened and fibrotic (0.45 cm); lumen obliterated distally. No faecolith or tumour. Yellow xanthogranulomatous foci in the wall.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal margin; mid-wall; obliterated tip; adhesive serosa. Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Sections show appendix with residual mucosal ulceration in healing phase, mixed acute and chronic inflammatory infiltrate (neutrophils, lymphocytes, plasma cells and histiocytes) extending into the muscularis propria, and prominent granulation tissue with early fibrosis in the submucosa and serosa. Serosal fibrous adhesions and organising fibrinous exudate are present (organising periappendicitis). Neutrophils are fewer than in florid acute appendicitis.
No well-formed granulomas, parasites, diverticula or neoplasm. The proximal resection margin shows mild chronic inflammation without active neutrophilic transmural disease.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Subacute / resolving appendicitis with organising periappendicitis. No perforation, gangrene or neoplasm. Proximal margin free of active transmural inflammation.

comment.text: The histologic picture of mixed acute-chronic inflammation with granulation tissue and organising serositis is consistent with partially treated or naturally resolving acute appendicitis. Distinction from interval (post-abscess antibiotic) appendicitis is clinical; granulomas are more typical of the latter.

containers.text: Received an appendix measuring 6.8 cm in length and 0.9 cm in maximum diameter. The serosa is dull and shows patchy fibrous adhesions and residual fibrinous exudate, without frank pus. No perforation or gangrene. On cut section the wall is thickened (0.35 cm) and fibrotic; the lumen is narrowed and contains scant mucoid material. No faecolith or tumour.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal margin; proximal, mid and distal transverse sections including tip and adhesions. Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Sections show appendix with mural fibrosis, submucosal and muscular hypertrophy, and a chronic inflammatory infiltrate of lymphocytes, plasma cells and eosinophils within the wall. Occasional scattered neutrophils are present in the mucosa without a dense transmural neutrophilic infiltrate. Lymphoid hyperplasia is moderate. The distal tip shows fibrous obliteration with neural proliferation. Serosa shows fibrous thickening and adhesions without active fibrinopurulent exudate.
No granuloma, parasite, diverticulum, active gangrene, perforation or neoplasm. The proximal resection margin shows mild chronic inflammation only.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Features consistent with recurrent / chronic appendicitis (mural fibrosis, chronic inflammation, fibrous adhesions; no florid acute transmural appendicitis). Distal fibrous obliteration. No neoplasm.

comment.text: Chronic / recurrent appendicitis is a clinicopathologic diagnosis. Histology typically shows fibrosis and chronic inflammation without (or with only mild) acute neutrophilic transmural disease. Correlation with episodic clinical history is required. Differential includes neurogenic appendicopathy and incidental fibrous obliteration.

containers.text: Received an appendix measuring 7.2 cm in length and 0.8 cm in maximum diameter. The serosa shows dull white fibrous thickening and adhesions without fresh fibrinopurulent exudate. No perforation or gangrene. On cut section the wall is fibrotic (up to 0.4 cm); the distal lumen is obliterated by firm white tissue over 1.5 cm. No faecolith or tumour.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal margin; mid-appendix; obliterated tip (longitudinal). Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Sections of residual appendix show mucosal ulceration and dense transmural neutrophilic inflammation extending to the serosa with fibrinopurulent periappendicitis, identical to native acute appendicitis. A faecolith is present. The prior distal resection / staple line shows fibrosis and suture granulomas. No gangrene or frank perforation in the levels examined.
Proximal caecal cuff margin shows viable caecal mucosa with mild acute inflammation; muscularis propria at this margin is viable. No granuloma of Crohn/TB type, parasite or neoplasm.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendiceal stump, completion appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Stump appendicitis (acute suppurative appendicitis of residual appendiceal stump) with periappendicitis and faecolith. Proximal caecal margin viable. No neoplasm.

comment.text: Stump appendicitis is a recognised complication of residual appendiceal stump, especially if long. Imaging and surgical history are critical. Completion excision is both diagnostic and therapeutic.

containers.text: Received a residual appendiceal stump measuring 2.8 cm in length and 1.2 cm in diameter, with a staple / suture line at the prior distal cut end and a proximal caecal cuff 0.8 cm. Serosa congested with fibrinopurulent exudate. No frank free perforation. On cut section wall thickened; lumen contains a 0.5 cm faecolith and pus. Mucosa ulcerated. No tumour.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal (caecal) margin; mid-stump; prior distal suture line; faecolith bed. Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Sections show appendix with deep mucosal ulceration, mixed acute and chronic inflammation extending into the muscularis propria, and endothelial and stromal cells with characteristic cytomegalovirus cytopathic effect: marked cellular enlargement, intranuclear basophilic inclusions with halo (owl-eye) and granular cytoplasmic inclusions. Vasculitis-like endothelial injury and focal crypt epithelial inclusions are present. Mild fibrinous serositis is noted without perforation.
No granuloma, parasite, diverticulum or neoplasm. Proximal margin shows mild inflammation without viral inclusions in the levels examined.
Special Stains / Immunohistochemistry:
CMV immunohistochemistry (DDG9/CCH2): Positive nuclear (and granular cytoplasmic) staining in endothelial, stromal and epithelial cells; numerous positive cells in ulcer bed
HSV-1/2 immunohistochemistry: Negative
Adenovirus immunohistochemistry: Negative
GMS / PAS: No fungi identified

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) appendicitis with mucosal ulceration and mural inflammation, in an immunosuppressed renal transplant recipient. CMV immunohistochemistry positive. No perforation or neoplasm.

comment.text: CMV appendicitis occurs in immunosuppressed hosts (transplant, HIV, high-dose steroids). Correlation with systemic CMV PCR and antiviral therapy (infectious diseases / transplant team) is essential. Neutropenic paucicellular injury and other opportunistic infections should remain in the clinical differential.

containers.text: Received an appendix measuring 7.5 cm in length and 1.0 cm in maximum diameter. Serosa congested with focal fibrinous exudate; no perforation or gangrene. On cut section mucosa extensively ulcerated and haemorrhagic; wall oedematous (0.3 cm). No faecolith or tumour.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal margin; ulcerated mid and distal appendix; tip. Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Sections show appendix with mucosal erosions and a mixed inflammatory infiltrate including neutrophils extending into the muscularis propria (acute appendicitis), accompanied by numerous tissue and luminal eosinophils. The lumen contains multiple cross-sections of Enterobius vermicularis (lateral alae, characteristic eggs). Mild fibrinous serosal reaction is present without frank periappendiceal abscess.
No granuloma, gangrene, perforation, diverticulum or neoplasm. Proximal resection margin viable without active inflammation.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Acute appendicitis associated with Enterobius vermicularis infestation. Mild periappendiceal serosal reaction. No perforation, gangrene or neoplasm. Proximal margin free of inflammation.

comment.text: Enterobius vermicularis may be incidental or associated with appendiceal inflammation. Antihelminthic treatment for the patient and close contacts is recommended. Distinguish from purely eosinophilic appendicitis without neutrophilic muscularis involvement (see related sample 08).

containers.text: Received an appendix measuring 5.5 cm in length and 0.8 cm in maximum diameter. Serosa mildly congested over the distal half; no frank fibrinopurulent coat, perforation or gangrene. On opening, multiple white thread-like worms (up to 1 cm) fill the lumen. Wall mildly thickened. No faecolith or tumour.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal margin; mid and distal sections with luminal worms; tip. Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Sections show chronic active transmural appendicitis with abscesses, sinus tracts and dense fibrosis. Within abscess cavities are classic actinomycotic (sulfur) granules: basophilic colonies of filamentous bacteria with peripheral eosinophilic Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon, surrounded by neutrophils. Gram stain highlights Gram-positive branching filaments. The inflammation extends to periappendiceal soft tissue. Mucosa shows ulceration; muscularis is disrupted by abscesses.
No caseating granulomas typical of tuberculosis. No parasites or neoplasm. Proximal resection margin shows fibrosis and chronic inflammation without sulfur granules in the sections examined.
Special Stains / Immunohistochemistry:
Gram stain: Gram-positive branching filamentous bacteria within sulfur granules
GMS: Highlights filamentous organisms
ZN: Negative for acid-fast bacilli
PAS: Filaments positive

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix with periappendiceal soft tissue, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Actinomycosis of the appendix with chronic active transmural appendicitis, periappendiceal abscess and sinus tracts. Sulfur granules with Gram-positive branching filaments consistent with Actinomyces species. No neoplasm.

comment.text: Pelvic/abdominal actinomycosis is associated with long-term IUCD use. Prolonged antibiotic therapy and IUCD removal (gynaecology) are typically required in addition to surgery. Culture and/or molecular confirmation can be pursued if fresh tissue was submitted. Differential of filamentous bacteria includes Nocardia (partially acid-fast; ZN negative here).

containers.text: Received an appendix measuring 9 cm in length and 1.8 cm in maximum diameter, densely adherent to periappendiceal soft tissue. Serosa shows thick yellow-white exudate and sinus-like tracts. A 2 cm abscess cavity in attached soft tissue contains yellow granular (sulfur granule) material. No frank free perforation to the peritoneal cavity identified after dissection. Wall markedly thickened and fibrotic. No tumour mass distinct from the inflammatory process. Proximal margin viable.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal margin; abscess with sulfur granules; multiple wall levels; sinus tracts. Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Sections show appendix with mucosal ulceration, transmural lymphoid aggregates, fissuring-type inflammation and numerous non-caseating epithelioid granulomas within the wall and mesoappendix, some with Langhans-type giant cells. A mixed acute and chronic inflammatory infiltrate extends through the muscularis propria to the serosa (periappendicitis). No caseous necrosis. No parasites, foreign material, diverticula or neoplasm.

Special stains for acid-fast bacilli and fungi are negative (see below). Proximal resection margin shows mild chronic inflammation with one non-caseating granuloma in the submucosa; no active neutrophilic transmural disease at the margin ink.
Special Stains / Immunohistochemistry:
Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN): No acid-fast bacilli identified
GMS / PAS: No fungal organisms identified
Gram stain: No filamentous bacteria / sulfur granules

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Granulomatous appendicitis (non-caseating) with transmural chronic active inflammation and periappendicitis. Special stains negative for AFB and fungi. No perforation or neoplasm.

comment.text: Differential diagnosis of granulomatous appendicitis includes idiopathic granulomatous appendicitis, Crohn disease, Yersinia infection, tuberculosis, foreign-body reaction and interval (post-therapy) appendicitis. Negative ZN/GMS reduce likelihood of TB/fungi but do not exclude mycobacterial or Yersinia infection (consider PCR / serology / culture if clinically indicated). Clinical and endoscopic evaluation of the ileocolon is advised to assess for Crohn disease. Isolated granulomatous appendicitis may remain idiopathic and not progress to Crohn disease in a substantial subset of patients.

containers.text: Received an appendix measuring 8 cm in length and 1.2 cm in maximum diameter with oedematous mesoappendix. Serosa is congested with patchy fibrinous exudate; no perforation. On cut section wall thickened (0.4 cm); lumen narrowed. Mucosa shows aphthoid-like erosions. No faecolith or tumour. No fat wrapping of ileum in this specimen (ileum not submitted).

exampleGross.sections: Proximal margin; multiple transverse levels including erosions and mesoappendix. Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Sections show appendix with a dense eosinophilic infiltrate in the lamina propria and submucosa, focally extending into the muscularis propria, without a significant neutrophilic component and without mucosal ulceration or transmural suppuration. The lumen contains cross-sections of adult nematodes with characteristic lateral alae and intestinal tract morphology diagnostic of Enterobius vermicularis; eggs with flattening on one side are also present.
No serositis, gangrene, perforation, granuloma or neoplasm. Proximal resection margin unremarkable. Background lymphoid tissue is preserved.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Eosinophilic appendicitis associated with Enterobius vermicularis infestation. No neutrophilic acute appendicitis, perforation or neoplasm.

comment.text: Enterobius is often an incidental luminal finding; when accompanied by tissue eosinophilia it supports eosinophilic appendicitis / parasitic association. Antihelminthic therapy for the patient and household contacts is recommended. Neutrophilic transmural acute appendicitis is not present in this sample.

containers.text: Received an appendix measuring 6 cm in length and 0.6 cm in maximum diameter. Serosa is glistening and unremarkable; no exudate, perforation or gangrene. On cut section the lumen contains several white thread-like worms measuring up to 0.8 cm. Wall thickness normal. No faecolith or tumour.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal margin; mid-appendix with luminal contents; tip. Entire specimen and worms submitted.

micro.text: Sections from the distal appendix show haemorrhagic infarction with mucosal and mural necrosis, haemorrhage into the wall, and a relatively sparse neutrophilic response at the interface with viable tissue (ischaemic pattern rather than primary suppurative appendicitis). Ghost outlines of crypts and muscularis are present. Mesoappendiceal muscular artery shows occlusive organising thrombus / embolus with early organisation.

Proximal appendix shows mucosal haemorrhage and congestion without dense transmural suppuration. Mild reactive serosal fibrin is present. No granuloma, parasite, diverticulum or neoplasm. Proximal resection margin is viable.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Ischaemic appendicitis (haemorrhagic infarction of distal appendix) secondary to occlusive mesoappendiceal arterial thrombus/embolus, in a patient with atrial fibrillation. Proximal margin viable. No neoplasm.

comment.text: Ischaemic appendicitis is uncommon and may be embolic (AF), thrombotic or related to volvulus/hernia. The histologic clue is infarction with relatively few neutrophils compared with classic suppurative appendicitis, plus vascular occlusion. Clinical vascular work-up may be indicated.

containers.text: Received an appendix measuring 8 cm in length and 1.3 cm in maximum diameter. The distal half is dusky purple-black and flabby; proximal appendix is congested but viable. Serosa dull without thick purulent coat. No frank perforation hole. On cut section distal mucosa is haemorrhagic and necrotic; lumen contains blood-stained fluid. A thromboembolus is identified in a mesoappendiceal artery on careful sectioning. No faecolith or tumour.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal margin; viable-ischaemic transition; distal necrotic wall; mesoappendiceal vessels. Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Sections show extensive mucosal ulceration and necrosis with marked oedema and haemorrhage of the submucosa. Inflammatory cells are strikingly paucicellular relative to the degree of tissue injury: neutrophils are virtually absent, consistent with the patient's profound neutropenia. Sparse mononuclear cells and karyorrhectic debris are present. Bacterial colonies are prominent on the ulcer surface and within necrotic mucosa (bacterial overgrowth).

The muscularis propria shows oedema and focal myocytolysis without a dense neutrophilic infiltrate. Mild serosal congestion and fibrin are present. No CMV inclusions identified on H&E in this sample. No granuloma, parasite, diverticulum or neoplasm. Proximal margin viable with mild oedema.
Special Stains / Immunohistochemistry:
Gram stain: Abundant mixed bacteria on ulcer surface
GMS / PAS: No fungal organisms identified
CMV immunohistochemistry: Negative (no nuclear positivity)

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Neutropenic (paucicellular) appendicitis with extensive mucosal ulceration, bacterial overgrowth and absent neutrophilic infiltrate, in the setting of chemotherapy-induced neutropenia. CMV immunohistochemistry negative. No perforation or neoplasm.

comment.text: In neutropenic patients, appendicitis (and typhlitis) may lack the classic neutrophilic transmural infiltrate; diagnosis rests on mucosal injury, clinical neutropenia and exclusion of opportunistic infection (CMV, fungi). Multidisciplinary management is essential.

containers.text: Received an appendix measuring 7 cm in length and 1.1 cm in maximum diameter. The serosa is congested and dull with focal haemorrhage; scant fibrinous exudate. No frank perforation. On cut section the mucosa is extensively ulcerated and haemorrhagic; the wall is oedematous. Lumen contains necrotic debris. No faecolith or tumour.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal margin; ulcerated mid and distal sections; tip. Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Sections confirm acquired appendiceal diverticula: herniation of mucosa and submucosa through gaps in the muscularis propria. One diverticulum shows mucosal ulceration, transmural neutrophilic inflammation centred on the diverticulum, and fibrinopurulent periappendicitis (diverticulitis of the appendix). Adjacent non-diverticular appendix shows lesser degrees of acute inflammation. No frank free perforation of the diverticulum into the peritoneal cavity in the sections examined, although the wall is markedly thinned.
No granuloma, parasite or neoplasm. Proximal resection margin viable without active inflammation.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Diverticular appendicitis (acute diverticulitis of acquired appendiceal diverticula) with periappendicitis. No free perforation or neoplasm. Proximal margin free of inflammation.

comment.text: Appendiceal diverticulitis may mimic or cause appendicitis and carries a higher risk of perforation than conventional appendicitis in some series. Acquired diverticula lack a full muscularis propria coat. Exclude coexistent neoplasm if diverticula are associated with mucin or mass lesions.

containers.text: Received an appendix measuring 7.8 cm in length and 1.1 cm in maximum diameter. Serosa congested with fibrinopurulent exudate over the mid-portion; no free perforation. On cut section two thin-walled diverticula (0.4 and 0.5 cm) protrude from the mesenteric border through the muscularis; one diverticulum contains a small faecolith and shows mural thinning and surrounding suppuration. Wall elsewhere thickened. No tumour.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal margin; diverticula with adjacent wall; non-diverticular appendix; tip. Entire specimen submitted.

diagnoses.name: Fibrous Obliteration of Appendiceal Tip, Incidental

micro.text: Sections show an otherwise unremarkable appendix without mucosal ulceration, without neutrophilic inflammation in any layer, and without serositis. The tip shows fibrous obliteration of the lumen by bland collagenous tissue with scant fibroblasts and few residual nerves — incidental fibrous obliteration of the tip (not neurogenic appendicopathy-dominant; neural proliferation is minimal).
No granuloma, parasite, diverticulum, dysplasia or neoplasm. Proximal resection margin normal.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, incidental appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Fibrous obliteration of the tip of the appendix. No acute or chronic appendicitis, parasite or neoplasm. Incidental finding.

comment.text: Fibrous obliteration of the appendiceal tip is a common incidental ageing / involutional change and is not acute appendicitis. It is included here as a related non-inflammatory sample for comparison with neurogenic appendicopathy and chronic/recurrent appendicitis.

containers.text: Received an appendix measuring 5.8 cm in length and 0.5 cm in maximum diameter. Serosa smooth and glistening throughout; no congestion, exudate, perforation or gangrene. On cut section the distal 1.8 cm shows solid white fibrous obliteration of the lumen; proximal lumen patent and empty. No faecolith, mucin or tumour.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal margin; mid-appendix; obliterated tip (longitudinal). Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Tip shows fibrous obliteration of the lumen by collagenous tissue with entrapped nerves and sparse fibroblasts — fibrous obliteration / neuroma of the tip (non-neoplastic). No dysplasia, no NET, no mucinous neoplasm. Proximal appendix unremarkable. No acute appendicitis.

Classification note: Fibrous obliteration / neuroma of the appendiceal tip is a non-neoplastic, tumour-like / involutional change (not a WHO neoplastic entity). Included as a related sample commonly encountered in appendicectomy specimens.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, incidental appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Fibrous obliteration (neuroma) of the tip of the appendix. Non-neoplastic. No acute appendicitis or neoplasm.

comment.text: Fibrous obliteration / tip neuroma is a common incidental ageing or involutional change and is not a WHO neoplastic tumour. Included as a tumour-like related sample for differential with true neural neoplasms and with neurogenic appendicopathy.

containers.text: Appendix 5.5 cm × 0.5 cm. Distal 2.0 cm shows solid white fibrous obliteration of the lumen (neuroma / fibrous obliteration of tip); proximal lumen patent. No tumour mass distinct from obliteration.

exampleGross.sections: Obliterated tip longitudinal; mid; proximal margin. Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Sections show no mucosal ulceration and no neutrophilic infiltrate in the mucosa, submucosa or muscularis propria (no acute appendicitis). The distal tip shows fibrous obliteration of the lumen with a proliferation of S100-positive spindle cells in a neurofibroma-like / neuromodular pattern, with intertwined nerve twigs and scattered neuroendocrine cells — features of neurogenic appendicopathy (neuroma of the appendix / neurogenic appendicopathy).
Serosa unremarkable. No granuloma, parasite, diverticulum or neoplasm (no NET mass). Proximal margin normal.
Special Stains / Immunohistochemistry:
S100: Highlights neural proliferation obliterating the tip
SOX10: Positive in spindle neural cells
Synaptophysin: Highlights scattered entrapped neuroendocrine cells
Neurofilament: Highlights axons within the neural proliferation

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Neurogenic appendicopathy (neuromuscular / neural proliferative obliteration of the tip) without acute appendicitis. No neoplasm, perforation or parasite.

comment.text: Neurogenic appendicopathy may be found in patients with RIF pain and a grossly normal appendix. It is distinct from acute appendicitis (no neutrophils in muscularis propria) and from incidental fibrous obliteration without a prominent neural component. Clinical correlation for alternative causes of pain remains appropriate.

containers.text: Received an appendix measuring 6.2 cm in length and 0.5 cm in maximum diameter. Serosa smooth and glistening; no congestion, exudate, perforation or gangrene. On cut section the distal 2 cm of lumen is obliterated by firm white tissue; proximal lumen patent. No faecolith or tumour nodule.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal margin; mid-appendix; obliterated tip (longitudinal). Entire specimen submitted.

diagnoses.name: Hyperplastic Polyp of Appendix
diagnoses.path: Gastrointestinal/Appendix/03 Benign Polyps and Mesenchymal Tumours

micro.text: Sections show a sessile mucosal polyp of the appendix composed of elongated crypts with serration confined to the upper crypt / luminal aspect, with preserved overall crypt architecture, non-dilated bases and no horizontal growth along the muscularis mucosae. Goblet cells and absorptive cells are present; nuclei are small, basally oriented, without cytologic dysplasia.

Background appendix shows mild acute mucosal and submucosal neutrophilic inflammation consistent with early acute appendicitis. No serrated dysplasia, conventional adenoma, mucinous neoplasm, or invasive carcinoma. Muscularis mucosae intact. Proximal resection margin free of polyp and of dysplasia.

Classification note (WHO Classification of Tumours, Digestive System Tumours, 6th edition, 2026): Appendiceal benign epithelial tumours include serrated lesions/polyps, conventional appendiceal adenoma (separate entry), and mucinous adenoma (reinstated). The present case is reported as hyperplastic polyp of the appendix (appendiceal serrated lesions and polyps). Appendiceal mucinous neoplasms (AMN/LAMN/HAMN) are classified as malignant epithelial tumours in the 6th edition and are not used for this diagnosis.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Hyperplastic polyp of the appendix (0.4 cm), without dysplasia. Mild early acute appendicitis. Proximal resection margin free of polyp. No mucinous neoplasm or invasive carcinoma.

comment.text: In WHO Digestive System Tumours, 6th edition (2026), appendiceal serrated lesions and polyps are grouped under benign epithelial tumours. Hyperplastic polyps show superficial serration without the architectural distortion of sessile serrated lesion. Complete appendicectomy is curative for this incidental polyp; clinical correlation for colorectal serrated polyposis is not required on this solitary small lesion alone.

containers.text: Received a vermiform appendix measuring 7.0 cm in length and 0.8 cm in maximum diameter, with a short mesoappendix. Serosa mildly congested over the distal half; no perforation or gangrene. Proximal surgical margin unremarkable. On cut section the lumen of the mid-appendix contains a sessile, flat mucosal nodule / polypoid mucosal thickening measuring 0.4 cm in greatest dimension, without mucin extrusion or mural thickening elsewhere. No faecolith.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal margin en face; polyp entirely submitted in sequential sections; tip and representative mid-appendix. Entire specimen submitted.

diagnoses.name: Inflammatory Fibroid Polyp of Appendix
diagnoses.path: Gastrointestinal/Appendix/03 Benign Polyps and Mesenchymal Tumours

micro.text: Inflammatory fibroid polyp: loose fibrovascular proliferation with eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate, onion-skin whorling of spindle cells around vessels, and bland spindle cells. No atypia. Mucosa intact without dysplasia. IFP of the appendix is uncommon but reported; more typical in stomach/ileum. Margins free. No acute appendicitis.

Classification note: Inflammatory fibroid polyp of the appendix is a benign mesenchymal / neural tumour (not an epithelial neoplasm in the WHO Digestive System Tumours, 6th edition, 2026 epithelial chapter). Reported here as an illustrative indolent appendix mass.
Immunohistochemistry:
CD34: Positive in spindle cells
PDGFRA: Positive (illustrative; mutation testing not performed in this sample)
CD117 / DOG1: Negative
S100: Negative
Desmin: Negative

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Inflammatory fibroid polyp of the appendix, 1.4 cm, benign. No epithelial neoplasia. Margins free.

comment.text: IFP is PDGFRA-associated in many GI sites; appendiceal examples are uncommon. Exclude GIST and inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour by morphology and IHC. Complete local excision (appendicectomy) is typically adequate.

containers.text: Appendix 7.0 cm × 0.8 cm. At the base, a submucosal / mural polypoid lesion 1.4 cm, grey-tan, centred in submucosa, mucosa stretched over surface. No necrosis.

exampleGross.sections: Entire polypoid lesion with base of appendix; tip.

diagnoses.name: Leiomyoma of Appendix
diagnoses.path: Gastrointestinal/Appendix/03 Benign Polyps and Mesenchymal Tumours

micro.text: Well-circumscribed fascicular smooth-muscle tumour continuous with muscularis propria: blunt-ended spindle cells, eosinophilic cytoplasm, no atypia, no necrosis, mitoses 0/10 HPF — leiomyoma. No GIST-like morphology. No epithelial neoplasia. Margins free.

Classification note: Leiomyoma of the appendix is a benign mesenchymal / neural tumour (not an epithelial neoplasm in the WHO Digestive System Tumours, 6th edition, 2026 epithelial chapter). Reported here as an illustrative indolent appendix mass.
Immunohistochemistry:
Desmin: Diffuse positive
SMA: Diffuse positive
CD117 / DOG1: Negative
S100: Negative

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Leiomyoma of the appendix, 0.9 cm, benign. No epithelial neoplasm. Margins free.

comment.text: IHC excludes GIST (CD117/DOG1 negative). Appendiceal leiomyoma is benign; appendicectomy is curative in this sample.

containers.text: Appendix 5.8 cm × 0.6 cm. Firm grey-white mural nodule 0.9 cm arising from muscularis propria; whorled cut surface. Mucosa intact.

exampleGross.sections: Entire nodule; representative appendix.

diagnoses.name: Lipoma of Appendix
diagnoses.path: Gastrointestinal/Appendix/03 Benign Polyps and Mesenchymal Tumours

micro.text: Mature adipose tissue expanding the submucosa without encapsulation or atypia — lipomatous hypertrophy of the appendix (lipoma-like). No lipoblasts. No epithelial neoplasia in appendix. No acute appendicitis.

Classification note: Lipoma / lipomatous hypertrophy of the appendix is a benign mesenchymal / neural tumour (not an epithelial neoplasm in the WHO Digestive System Tumours, 6th edition, 2026 epithelial chapter). Reported here as an illustrative indolent appendix mass.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, incidental appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Lipomatous hypertrophy (lipoma-like fatty infiltration) of the appendiceal submucosa. No epithelial neoplasm or appendicitis.

comment.text: Lipomatous hypertrophy of the appendix is usually incidental and benign. Discrete encapsulated lipomas are uncommon; either pattern is non-malignant. Colon primary reported separately.

containers.text: Appendix 6.0 cm × 1.0 cm. Diffuse submucosal yellow fatty thickening maximally 0.8 cm thick over 2.5 cm length (lipomatous hypertrophy); no discrete encapsulated lipoma separate from wall. Mucosa intact; no tumour at tip.

exampleGross.sections: Representative fatty wall; tip; proximal.

diagnoses.name: Schwannoma of Appendix
diagnoses.path: Gastrointestinal/Appendix/03 Benign Polyps and Mesenchymal Tumours

micro.text: Well-circumscribed spindle-cell tumour of Antoni A / Antoni B pattern with Verocay bodies, wavy nuclei, and hyalinised vessels — schwannoma. No atypia, no necrosis, mitoses scarce (<1/10 HPF). Mucosa and muscularis propria partly attenuated but no epithelial neoplasia. Mild incidental acute appendicitis. Margins of resection free of tumour (appendicectomy).

Classification note: Schwannoma of the appendix is a benign mesenchymal / neural tumour (not an epithelial neoplasm in the WHO Digestive System Tumours, 6th edition, 2026 epithelial chapter). Reported here as an illustrative indolent appendix mass.
Immunohistochemistry:
S100: Diffuse strong nuclear and cytoplasmic positive
SOX10: Positive
Desmin: Negative
DOG1 / CD117: Negative

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Schwannoma of the appendix, 1.2 cm, benign. Mild acute appendicitis. Margins free. No epithelial neoplasm.

comment.text: Appendiceal schwannoma is rare; IHC (diffuse S100/SOX10) distinguishes it from GIST, leiomyoma, and neurofibroma. Complete excision by appendicectomy is usually curative.

containers.text: Appendix 6.5 cm × 0.8 cm. Well-circumscribed, firm, grey-white mural nodule 1.2 cm in mid-appendix, centred in wall; mucosa intact over lesion. No necrosis.

exampleGross.sections: Entire nodule with margins of surrounding wall; tip; proximal margin.

diagnoses.name: Sessile Serrated Lesion of Appendix without Dysplasia

micro.text: Sections show a sessile serrated lesion of the appendix: crypts with serration extending to the bases, dilated L- or inverted T-shaped crypt bases, and horizontal growth along the muscularis mucosae. Cytologic dysplasia is absent (no conventional adenomatous change; no serrated dysplasia).
Background mild acute appendicitis. No invasive carcinoma. Muscularis mucosae intact beneath the lesion. Proximal margin negative.

Classification note (WHO Classification of Tumours, Digestive System Tumours, 6th edition, 2026): Appendiceal benign epithelial tumours include serrated lesions/polyps, conventional appendiceal adenoma (separate entry), and mucinous adenoma (reinstated). The present case is reported as sessile serrated lesion / serrated polyp of the appendix without dysplasia. Appendiceal mucinous neoplasms (AMN/LAMN/HAMN) are classified as malignant epithelial tumours in the 6th edition and are not used for this diagnosis.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Sessile serrated lesion (serrated polyp) of the appendix, 0.7 cm, without dysplasia. Mild acute appendicitis. Margins free. No invasive carcinoma.

comment.text: Appendiceal SSL is reported under WHO 6th edition benign appendiceal serrated lesions and polyps. Wording "without dysplasia" parallels colorectal SSL reporting. Appendicectomy is typically curative for a confined SSL without dysplasia.

containers.text: Received an appendix measuring 6.8 cm × 0.9 cm with congested serosa. On opening, a flat, sessile mucosal lesion measuring 0.7 cm is present in the proximal third, with subtle mucosal thickening; no mucin pools or mural soft-tissue mass.

exampleGross.sections: Proximal margin; entire sessile lesion submitted sequentially; tip. Entire specimen submitted.

diagnoses.name: Sessile Serrated Lesion of Appendix with Dysplasia

micro.text: Sections show a sessile serrated lesion with architectural features of SSL (basal crypt dilatation, serration to crypt bases, horizontal growth). Within the lesion there is a discrete focus of cytologic dysplasia (nuclear enlargement, stratification, loss of polarity) involving approximately 30% of the lesion — reported as sessile serrated lesion with dysplasia (low-grade cytologic dysplasia in this illustrative example).
No high-grade dysplasia and no invasive carcinoma. Muscularis mucosae intact. Mild acute appendicitis elsewhere. Margins free of SSL and of dysplasia.

Classification note (WHO Classification of Tumours, Digestive System Tumours, 6th edition, 2026): Appendiceal benign epithelial tumours include serrated lesions/polyps, conventional appendiceal adenoma (separate entry), and mucinous adenoma (reinstated). The present case is reported as sessile serrated lesion of the appendix with dysplasia. Appendiceal mucinous neoplasms (AMN/LAMN/HAMN) are classified as malignant epithelial tumours in the 6th edition and are not used for this diagnosis.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Sessile serrated lesion of the appendix with dysplasia (1.1 cm); no high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma. Mild acute appendicitis. Margins free.

comment.text: SSL with dysplasia is recognised in colorectal WHO practice and is used here by analogy for the appendix under "serrated lesions and polyps." Exact subtype labelling in the published WHO 6th appendix chapter should be confirmed against the Blue Book text; dysplasia grade terminology (presence vs low-/high-grade) may vary by institutional protocol. Complete excision by appendicectomy with negative margins is documented.

containers.text: Appendix 7.2 cm × 1.0 cm. Flat sessile mucosal lesion 1.1 cm in mid-appendix with tan mucosal thickening; no mucin extrusion through wall.

exampleGross.sections: Entire lesion and margins submitted; tip. Entire specimen submitted.

diagnoses.name: Tubular Adenoma of Appendix, Low-grade Dysplasia

micro.text: Sections show a conventional tubular adenoma of the appendix resembling its colorectal counterpart: crowded tubules lined by dysplastic epithelium with elongated, hyperchromatic, pseudostratified nuclei, retained polarity, and no cribriform or solid growth — low-grade dysplasia. Villous architecture <25%.
No high-grade dysplasia or invasion. Muscularis mucosae intact. Mild acute appendicitis. Margins free.

Classification note (WHO Classification of Tumours, Digestive System Tumours, 6th edition, 2026): Appendiceal benign epithelial tumours include serrated lesions/polyps, conventional appendiceal adenoma (separate entry), and mucinous adenoma (reinstated). The present case is reported as conventional tubular adenoma of the appendix (new separate entry in WHO 6th edition). Appendiceal mucinous neoplasms (AMN/LAMN/HAMN) are classified as malignant epithelial tumours in the 6th edition and are not used for this diagnosis.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Conventional tubular adenoma of the appendix, 0.6 cm, with low-grade dysplasia. No high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma. Mild acute appendicitis. Margins free.

comment.text: WHO 6th edition (2026) introduces a separate entry for conventional appendiceal adenoma analogous to colorectal conventional adenoma. Appendicectomy with clear margins is typically curative for this confined lesion.

containers.text: Appendix 6.5 cm × 0.8 cm. Pedunculated / sessile mucosal polyp 0.6 cm in distal appendix; stalk / base within mucosa. No mucin pools.

exampleGross.sections: Polyp entirely submitted with base; proximal margin; tip.

diagnoses.name: Tubulovillous Adenoma of Appendix, Low-grade Dysplasia

micro.text: Conventional tubulovillous adenoma: mixture of tubular and villous architecture (villous component estimated 40–50%), lined by epithelium with low-grade dysplasia (elongated hyperchromatic nuclei, preserved polarity). No high-grade dysplasia or invasion. Intact muscularis mucosae. Mild acute appendicitis. Margins free.

Classification note (WHO Classification of Tumours, Digestive System Tumours, 6th edition, 2026): Appendiceal benign epithelial tumours include serrated lesions/polyps, conventional appendiceal adenoma (separate entry), and mucinous adenoma (reinstated). The present case is reported as conventional tubulovillous adenoma of the appendix. Appendiceal mucinous neoplasms (AMN/LAMN/HAMN) are classified as malignant epithelial tumours in the 6th edition and are not used for this diagnosis.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Conventional tubulovillous adenoma of the appendix, 1.2 cm, low-grade dysplasia. No high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma. Mild acute appendicitis. Margins free.

comment.text: Architecture is classified as for colorectal conventional adenomas (tubular / tubulovillous / villous). WHO 6th edition lists conventional appendiceal adenoma as a benign epithelial entity separate from mucinous adenoma and from AMN.

containers.text: Appendix 7.5 cm × 1.0 cm. Sessile-polypoid mucosal lesion 1.2 cm with soft villiform surface in mid-distal appendix. No mucin extrusion.

exampleGross.sections: Entire lesion with base; margins; tip. Entire specimen submitted.

diagnoses.name: Villous Adenoma of Appendix, Low-grade Dysplasia

micro.text: Conventional villous adenoma (>75% villous architecture) with low-grade dysplasia. No circumferential mucinous neoplastic epithelium of mucinous-adenoma type; no pushing invasion or mucin dissecting wall (not LAMN/AMN). Intact muscularis mucosae. No high-grade dysplasia or carcinoma. Margins free. No acute appendicitis.

Classification note (WHO Classification of Tumours, Digestive System Tumours, 6th edition, 2026): Appendiceal benign epithelial tumours include serrated lesions/polyps, conventional appendiceal adenoma (separate entry), and mucinous adenoma (reinstated). The present case is reported as conventional villous adenoma of the appendix. Appendiceal mucinous neoplasms (AMN/LAMN/HAMN) are classified as malignant epithelial tumours in the 6th edition and are not used for this diagnosis.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Conventional villous adenoma of the appendix, 1.8 cm, low-grade dysplasia. No high-grade dysplasia, mucinous adenoma, AMN, or invasive carcinoma. Margins free.

comment.text: Villous conventional adenoma must be distinguished from mucinous adenoma (circumferential mucinous epithelium with intact MM) and from LAMN/AMN (malignant in WHO 6th ed). Appendicectomy is documented as complete in this sample.

containers.text: Appendix 8.0 cm × 1.3 cm (tip dilated). Soft villiform mucosal lesion 1.8 cm filling distal lumen; wall not gelatinously thickened; no extracopy mucin.

exampleGross.sections: Entire distal lesion with wall; proximal margin; mesoappendix. Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Conventional tubulovillous adenoma with foci of high-grade dysplasia: complex cribriform architecture, marked nuclear pleomorphism, loss of polarity, and atypical mitoses, still confined by intact muscularis mucosae without invasion into submucosa. Background low-grade dysplasia in tubular areas. Mild acute appendicitis. Margins free of adenoma and of high-grade dysplasia.

Classification note (WHO Classification of Tumours, Digestive System Tumours, 6th edition, 2026): Appendiceal benign epithelial tumours include serrated lesions/polyps, conventional appendiceal adenoma (separate entry), and mucinous adenoma (reinstated). The present case is reported as conventional appendiceal adenoma with high-grade dysplasia. Appendiceal mucinous neoplasms (AMN/LAMN/HAMN) are classified as malignant epithelial tumours in the 6th edition and are not used for this diagnosis.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Conventional tubulovillous adenoma of the appendix with high-grade dysplasia (0.9 cm); no invasive carcinoma. Mild acute appendicitis. Margins free.

comment.text: High-grade dysplasia in a conventional appendiceal adenoma remains a non-invasive (intraepithelial) process when muscularis mucosae is intact. Thorough sampling of the base is essential to exclude invasion. Multidisciplinary correlation and consideration of colonoscopy for synchronous colorectal neoplasia are suggested.

containers.text: Appendix 6.9 cm × 0.9 cm. Sessile mucosal polyp 0.9 cm, firm, grey-tan; no serosal mucin.

exampleGross.sections: Entire polyp with deep base and muscularis; margins. Entire specimen submitted.

micro.text: Sections show circumferential mucinous neoplastic epithelium lining the appendiceal lumen, with tall columnar mucin-rich cells and low-grade cytologic atypia, strictly confined to the mucosa and completely surrounded by an intact, continuous muscularis mucosae. No pushing invasion through muscularis mucosae, no mucin dissecting the wall, and no loss of the lamina propria–muscularis mucosae complex as required for LAMN/AMN.
No high-grade cytology, no infiltrative invasion, and no extra-appendiceal mucin. Proximal margin free of neoplastic epithelium. No acute appendicitis.

Classification note (WHO Classification of Tumours, Digestive System Tumours, 6th edition, 2026): Appendiceal benign epithelial tumours include serrated lesions/polyps, conventional appendiceal adenoma (separate entry), and mucinous adenoma (reinstated). The present case is reported as mucinous adenoma (reinstated benign entity; intact muscularis mucosae). Appendiceal mucinous neoplasms (AMN/LAMN/HAMN) are classified as malignant epithelial tumours in the 6th edition and are not used for this diagnosis.

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, appendicectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Mucinous adenoma of the appendix: circumferential mucinous neoplastic epithelium confined to the mucosa and completely surrounded by intact muscularis mucosae. No features of LAMN/AMN/HAMN. Proximal margin free. Appendicectomy is considered curative for this benign entity (WHO 6th edition, 2026).

comment.text: WHO Digestive System Tumours, 6th edition (2026) reinstates mucinous adenoma as a benign epithelial tumour distinct from appendiceal mucinous neoplasms. Critical criteria: mucosa-confined circumferential mucinous neoplastic epithelium completely surrounded by intact muscularis mucosae. Any breach of muscularis mucosae, mural mucin, or loss of the MM framework warrants classification as AMN/LAMN (malignant category) rather than mucinous adenoma. Entire submission of the appendix is recommended when "mucocele" is suspected.

micro.text: The dilated appendix is lined by a villiform to flattened, undulating proliferation of mucinous columnar epithelium with tall cells, basally located, mildly enlarged, elongated nuclei and only mild atypia (low-grade cytology). The lamina propria and muscularis mucosae are lost and replaced by hyalinised fibrosis with dystrophic calcification. The neoplasm shows a broad pushing front and abuts the muscularis propria without infiltrative (destructive) invasion or desmoplasia.

Acellular mucin dissects into the muscularis propria but does not extend into the subserosa or mesoappendix. The serosa is intact; no mucin or neoplastic epithelium on the serosal surface. No high-grade cytological features (no marked nuclear pleomorphism, full-thickness stratification, cribriforming or brisk mitoses). No signet-ring cells.

The proximal non-dilated segment shows normal appendiceal mucosa; the stapled base margin is free of neoplastic epithelium and mucin. The mesoappendiceal margin is free. No lymph nodes in the specimen.

comment.text: In the WHO 6th edition, LAMN and HAMN are classified as malignant epithelial neoplasms because they can spread to the peritoneum. Mucinous adenoma is reserved for lesions confined to the mucosa with an intact muscularis mucosae; here the muscularis mucosae is lost, so this is LAMN. A LAMN confined by the muscularis propria with no extra-appendiceal mucin is staged Tis(LAMN). The risk of recurrence or pseudomyxoma peritonei is very low after complete appendicectomy with a negative base margin. Right hemicolectomy and lymph node staging are not usually needed. Follow-up per institutional protocol.

comment.text: HAMN has the pushing architecture of LAMN but high-grade cytology. It is classified with malignant epithelial neoplasms in the WHO 6th edition. Pseudomyxoma peritonei and mucinous carcinoma peritonei are discussed in WHO under peritoneal metastases, and the peritoneal disease is graded separately: low grade (G1), high grade (G2), or high grade with signet-ring cells (G3). The grade of the peritoneal disease drives prognosis and AJCC stage grouping (M1b G1 = IVA; M1b G2/G3 = IVB). Ovarian deposits are CK7−/CK20+/SATB2+/PAX8−, which supports appendiceal origin over a primary ovarian mucinous tumour.

micro.text: The appendiceal wall is concentrically infiltrated, beneath largely intact mucosa, by goblet cell adenocarcinoma. About 60% of the tumour has the low-grade pattern: tubules and tight clusters of goblet cells with crescentic nuclei, admixed with scattered Paneth-like and endocrine cells, infiltrating the wall without significant desmoplasia. About 40% has the high-grade pattern: single infiltrating goblet or signet-ring-like cells, complex anastomosing and cribriform aggregates, and solid sheets, with desmoplastic stroma and increased mitoses.

Grade by loss of tubular/clustered growth (CAP/WHO three-tier): G2 (low-grade pattern 50–75%). Tumour infiltrates through the muscularis propria into the mesoappendix (pT3); the serosa is not involved. Perineural invasion is prominent. Lymphovascular invasion is not identified and there are no tumour deposits. The base margin is uninvolved and all margins are negative. Sixteen lymph nodes are negative. No conventional adenocarcinoma or well-differentiated NET component.

CDX2: Positive

comment.text: In the WHO 6th edition, goblet cell adenocarcinoma is the prototype amphicrine-like carcinoma. It is staged as a carcinoma, not as a neuroendocrine tumour, and its prognosis is worse than NET but slightly better than conventional appendiceal adenocarcinoma. Grade depends on the proportion of the low-grade tubular/clustered pattern (G1 >75%, G2 50–75%, G3 <50%) and should be reported as a percentage. GCA is not a MiNEN: neuroendocrine cells are admixed within the same glands, not a separate component.

comment.text: Medullary carcinoma is a solid, syncytial carcinoma with abundant TILs. It is typically dMMR, calretinin-positive and shows reduced CDX2/CK20, so it may be mistaken for a neuroendocrine carcinoma, which is excluded here with negative synaptophysin and chromogranin. Loss of MLH1/PMS2 with BRAF V600E strongly suggests sporadic MLH1 promoter hypermethylation; MLH1 promoter methylation testing is recommended to complete Lynch syndrome screening. dMMR status is prognostically favourable and predicts response to immune checkpoint inhibitors.

finalDiagnosis.text: Metastatic undifferentiated carcinoma (pM1b). pT4b pN2 pM1b, stage IVB (AJCC Version 9).

comment.text: Undifferentiated carcinoma lacks morphological or immunohistochemical evidence of a specific line of differentiation beyond keratin expression. The WHO 6th edition redefines undifferentiated carcinoma of the digestive tract to include carcinoma with mesenchymal differentiation (sarcomatoid features). SMARCB1 and SMARCA4 are retained and MMR is intact. Loss of either SWI/SNF protein would favour an SWI/SNF-deficient undifferentiated (often rhabdoid) carcinoma, and dMMR would favour a medullary-type tumour. Melanoma, lymphoma, sarcoma, GIST and NEC were excluded by IHC. Prognosis is poor; oncology referral is recommended.
