micro.text: The tumour has two morphologically and immunophenotypically distinct components. Component 1 (about 60% of tumour) is an invasive adenocarcinoma of colonic type, moderately differentiated (G2), with cribriform glands and dirty necrosis, arising from a surface conventional adenoma. Component 2 (about 40%) is a large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma forming solid nests and trabeculae with peripheral palisading, comedonecrosis, 40 mitoses/2 mm² and a Ki-67 of about 65%. Each component makes up at least 30% of the tumour, which meets MiNEN criteria. The components are largely separate (adenocarcinoma superficial, LCNEC deep), with a narrow transition zone.

The LCNEC component penetrates the visceral peritoneum and is present at the serosal surface (pT4a). Lymphovascular invasion is present, involving the LCNEC component. Perineural invasion is not identified. No tumour deposits. All margins negative; caecal orifice free. Zero of twenty lymph nodes involved.
Immunohistochemistry:
CK20 (adenocarcinoma): Positive
CDX2 (adenocarcinoma): Positive
SATB2 (adenocarcinoma): Positive
CK7: Negative (both components)
Synaptophysin (LCNEC component): Positive (diffuse); negative in adenocarcinoma
Chromogranin A (LCNEC component): Positive (patchy)
INSM1 (LCNEC component): Positive
Ki-67 (LCNEC component): About 65%
Mitotic count (LCNEC component): 40 mitoses / 2 mm²
Ki-67 (adenocarcinoma): About 45%
p53: Aberrant in both components (supports clonal relationship)
MMR proteins (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6): Intact nuclear expression

finalDiagnosis.label: Appendix, right colon and terminal ileum, right hemicolectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Mixed neuroendocrine–non-neuroendocrine neoplasm (MiNEN) of the appendix: colonic-type adenocarcinoma, G2 (about 60%), and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (about 40%; Ki-67 about 65%), each at least 30%, 3.6 cm, with the NEC component penetrating the visceral peritoneum (pT4a) and showing lymphovascular invasion. Margins negative. 0 of 20 lymph nodes involved (pN0). pT4a pN0 (cM0), stage IIB (AJCC Version 9).

comment.text: MiNEN requires each component to make up at least 30% of the tumour. The type, proportion and grade/proliferation of each component should be recorded. MiNEN is distinct from goblet cell adenocarcinoma, an amphicrine-like carcinoma with admixed endocrine cells, and from an adenocarcinoma with scattered neuroendocrine cells. Behaviour is usually driven by the high-grade NEC component, so systemic therapy planning should consider it.

items.label: Tumor Site
items.value: Proximal appendix; base involved; caecal orifice uninvolved

items.label: Histologic Type
items.value: Mixed neuroendocrine–non-neuroendocrine neoplasm (MiNEN): adenocarcinoma, colonic type (~60%) + large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (~40%); each component ≥30%

items.label: Histologic Grade
items.value: Adenocarcinoma component G2 (moderately differentiated); LCNEC component high grade by definition (Ki-67 65%, 40 mitoses/2 mm²)

items.label: Tumor Extent
items.value: Penetrates visceral peritoneum (LCNEC component at serosal surface)

items.label: Peritoneal Involvement (Grade of Peritoneal Mucinous Disease)
Proximal Margin (Appendiceal Base / Ileal)
items.value: Ileal margin negative; caecal orifice uninvolved (0.6 cm)

items.label: pM Category
items.value: Not applicable - pM cannot be determined from the submitted specimen(s)

items.label: Ancillary Studies
items.value: Component-specific IHC as tabulated; p53 aberrant in both; MMR proficient

containers.text: Right hemicolectomy (ileum 8 cm, colon 16 cm). The proximal appendix contains a firm mass 3.6 x 2.8 x 2.4 cm, with a gritty grey-white portion near the mucosa and a fleshy, tan, necrotic portion deeper in the wall reaching a puckered serosal surface. The base is involved, but the caecal orifice is free (0.6 cm). Twenty lymph nodes.

exampleGross.sections: Entire tumour submitted with mapping (A5–A16): mucosal/grey-white areas (A5–A9), fleshy deep areas with serosa (A10–A14), base/orifice (A15–A16). A1 ileal margin; A2 colonic margin; A3 mesenteric margin; A17–A24 lymph nodes (20).

micro.text: All three biopsies consist of colorectal mucosa with abundant underlying submucosa (about 40-50% of the thickness). There is no squamous or anal transitional epithelium, and no skeletal muscle.

Despite examination of all serial levels, no ganglion cells are identified in the submucosa of any biopsy. The submucosa contains numerous thick nerve trunks (at least 4 per biopsy), measuring 45-65 µm in diameter. The muscularis mucosae is mildly thickened. There is no enterocolitis.

Calretinin shows complete absence of immunoreactive nerve fibrils in the lamina propria, muscularis mucosae and submucosa; the only positive cells are scattered granular mast cells (CD117-positive). External control is satisfactory.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:

Calretinin (paraffin): Negative: no calretinin-immunoreactive nerve fibrils in lamina propria, muscularis mucosae or submucosa; no positive ganglion cells. Scattered granular calretinin-positive mast cells noted (not counted as fibrils; CD117-positive). External positive control (ganglionic colon) stains appropriately
S100: Highlights thickened submucosal nerve trunks (up to 65 µm); no ganglion cell bodies outlined
CD117 (c-kit): Confirms that the calretinin-positive round cells are mast cells

finalDiagnosis.label: Rectum, suction biopsies at 2, 3 and 4 cm above the dentate line:
finalDiagnosis.text: Consistent with Hirschsprung disease: no ganglion cells in adequate submucosa (all levels examined), hypertrophic submucosal nerve trunks (45-65 µm) and absent calretinin-immunoreactive mucosal innervation.

comment.text: The combination of aganglionosis in three adequate biopsies taken at 2-4 cm above the dentate line, submucosal nerve hypertrophy and a negative calretinin pattern is diagnostic of Hirschsprung disease in this clinical setting. Biopsy height and adequacy exclude the physiological hypoganglionic zone as a cause.
Calretinin-positive mast cells are a known pitfall. They were identified as mast cells by morphology and CD117, and were not read as nerve fibrils.

A rectal biopsy cannot show how long the aganglionic segment is. The extent is defined by the contrast enema and by intraoperative levelling biopsies with frozen section before or during pull-through.

containers.text: Received in formalin, labelled 2 cm: a single tan, ovoid mucosal fragment, 3 x 3 x 1 mm. Placed on a sponge, orientated on edge (mucosa perpendicular).
Received in formalin, labelled 3 cm: a single tan, ovoid mucosal fragment, 4 x 3 x 1 mm. Placed on a sponge, orientated on edge (mucosa perpendicular).
Received in formalin, labelled 4 cm: a single tan, ovoid mucosal fragment, 4 x 3 x 1.5 mm. Placed on a sponge, orientated on edge (mucosa perpendicular).

exampleGross.sections: A (2 cm), B (3 cm), C (4 cm): each entirely embedded on edge; serial sections, about 75 levels per block; H&E on every fifth level; unstained levels retained for IHC (calretinin on levels from the middle of each block).

diagnoses.name: Suction Rectal Biopsy, Ganglion Cells Present (Hirschsprung Excluded)

micro.text: Both biopsies show colorectal mucosa with adequate submucosa (about one-third to one-half of the thickness). Several submucosal ganglia containing mature ganglion cells are present in both biopsies, recognisable on H&E by abundant amphophilic cytoplasm, eccentric vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli, accompanied by satellite glial cells.

Submucosal nerve trunks are of normal calibre (less than 40 µm). The mucosa is unremarkable. Calretinin shows a normal pattern, with abundant fine, beaded fibrils in the lamina propria and muscularis mucosae and positive ganglion cells.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
Calretinin (paraffin): Positive: numerous fine, beaded calretinin-immunoreactive nerve fibrils in lamina propria and muscularis mucosae; submucosal ganglion cells positive. Normal pattern

finalDiagnosis.label: Rectum, suction biopsies at 2 and 3 cm above the dentate line:
finalDiagnosis.text: Ganglion cells present in the submucosa, with normal calretinin-immunoreactive mucosal innervation. No hypertrophic nerves. Hirschsprung disease excluded at the levels biopsied.

comment.text: Finding ganglion cells in an adequate rectal biopsy taken at least 2 cm above the dentate line excludes Hirschsprung disease at that level. Because aganglionosis always runs continuously upward from the anal end, this excludes the condition altogether. The one exception is the debated ultrashort segment, which lies below the standard biopsy height. A normal calretinin pattern supports this.

If symptoms persist, consider functional constipation, internal anal sphincter achalasia (absent rectoanal inhibitory reflex on manometry with ganglionic biopsies), anorectal malformation or other dysmotility.

containers.text: Received in formalin, labelled 2 cm: one tan fragment, 4 x 3 x 1 mm. Orientated on edge.
Received in formalin, labelled 3 cm: one tan fragment, 3 x 3 x 1 mm. Orientated on edge.

exampleGross.sections: A (2 cm), B (3 cm): each entirely embedded on edge; serial sections, about 60 levels; H&E every fifth level; calretinin on A.

diagnoses.name: Suction Rectal Biopsy, Inadequate for Hirschsprung Assessment

micro.text: Biopsy A consists of anal transitional zone epithelium and squamous mucosa with underlying lamina propria and a small amount of submucosa containing occasional thick nerves. This level lies within the physiological hypoganglionic zone, so the absence of ganglion cells here is not interpretable.

Biopsy B consists of colorectal mucosa and muscularis mucosae with only a thin sliver of submucosa (less than 10% of the thickness). No ganglion cells are seen, but the submucosa is insufficient to assess the submucosal plexus. Calretinin shows sparse lamina propria fibrils, a non-diagnostic pattern in this small, distal sample.
Immunohistochemistry / Special Stains:
Calretinin (paraffin): Sparse fibrils in lamina propria of the colorectal-type mucosa only; no submucosa available to assess ganglia. Interpretation limited (distal / anal transitional zone level)

finalDiagnosis.label: Rectum, suction biopsies labelled 1 cm and 2 cm from the anal verge:
finalDiagnosis.text: Inadequate for the diagnosis or exclusion of Hirschsprung disease: biopsy A is too low (anal transitional / squamous mucosa, physiological hypoganglionic zone) and biopsy B contains insufficient submucosa. No ganglion cells identified, but this is not diagnostic. Repeat biopsy recommended.

comment.text: Adequacy criteria (ERNICA 2020; Gastro 2009 IWG): biopsies at least 2 cm above the dentate line (about 3 cm from the anal orifice), at least 3 mm in diameter, with submucosa forming at least about one-third of the specimen. The distal 1-2 cm above the dentate line normally has few or no ganglia and coarse nerves. Biopsies from there, or biopsies made of mucosa alone, can produce a false-positive diagnosis of aganglionosis.

Recommendation: repeat 2-3 suction biopsies at 2, 3 and 4 cm above the dentate line, labelled by distance. If repeated suction biopsies remain inadequate, consider an open or full-thickness rectal biopsy.

containers.text: Received labelled '1 cm': one grey-white fragment, 3 x 2 x 0.5 mm; thin, with little visible submucosa. Orientated on edge as far as possible.
Received labelled '2 cm': one tan fragment, 2 x 2 x 0.5 mm; thin, with little visible submucosa. Orientated on edge as far as possible.

exampleGross.sections: A (1 cm), B (2 cm): entirely embedded; serial sections, about 50 levels each; H&E every fifth level; calretinin on B.

micro.text: Frozen section diagnoses (communicated to the surgeon by telephone): L1 aganglionic with hypertrophic nerves; L2 aganglionic with hypertrophic nerves; L3 rare small ganglion cells, sparse, with thick nerves, suggestive of transition zone, not suitable for anastomosis; L4 ganglion cells present at normal density, no hypertrophic nerves; L5 ganglion cells present in myenteric and submucosal plexuses, no hypertrophic nerves.

Permanent sections confirm the frozen diagnoses. In L3 the myenteric ganglia are small and sparse (hypoganglionosis), with intermuscular nerves of 40-55 µm, consistent with transition zone; Hu C/D highlights the few neurons. L4 and L5 show normal ganglion cell density and calretinin-positive fibres.
Levelling Results: Frozen Section and Permanent:

L1: Rectum, 3 cm above dentate line (seromuscular): Frozen section result (intraoperative): Aganglionic; hypertrophic nerve trunks between muscle layers; Permanent sections / IHC: Confirmed aganglionic; nerves up to 70 µm; calretinin negative.
L2: Rectosigmoid junction (seromuscular): Frozen section result (intraoperative): Aganglionic; hypertrophic nerves; Permanent sections / IHC: Confirmed aganglionic; calretinin negative.

L3: Mid sigmoid (seromuscular): Frozen section result (intraoperative): Rare small ganglion cells; sparse; thick nerves (possible transition zone); Permanent sections / IHC: Hypoganglionic myenteric plexus with hypertrophic nerves (40-55 µm): transition zone.

L4: Descending-sigmoid junction (seromuscular): Frozen section result (intraoperative): Ganglion cells present; normal-appearing density; no hypertrophic nerves; Permanent sections / IHC: Confirmed ganglionic, normal density; calretinin-positive fibres.

L5: Distal descending colon (full-thickness, 2 cm proximal to L4): Frozen section result (intraoperative): Ganglion cells present in myenteric and submucosal plexuses; no hypertrophic nerves; Permanent sections / IHC: Confirmed normal ganglionic bowel in both plexuses.

finalDiagnosis.label: Colon and rectum, intraoperative levelling biopsies L1-L5:
finalDiagnosis.text: L1 (rectum) and L2 (rectosigmoid): aganglionic, hypertrophic nerves. L3 (mid sigmoid): hypoganglionic with hypertrophic nerves, transition zone. L4 (descending-sigmoid junction) and L5 (distal descending colon): normal ganglionic bowel. Frozen and permanent diagnoses concordant.

comment.text: Seromuscular biopsies assess only the myenteric plexus. A single small biopsy can miss an asymmetric transition zone. L3 showed transition-zone features, so L3 must not be used for the anastomosis. The pull-through should reach normal bowel at or above L4/L5, transected 5-10 cm proximal to the first normal biopsy or confirmed with a circumferential doughnut (ERNICA 2020).

Frozen sections in infants can be limited by freezing artefact and immature ganglion cells. Permanent sections and IHC confirmed all levels here. The resection specimen should be sent intact and orientated for mapping.

containers.text: Five fresh specimens received sequentially for frozen section. L1, rectum 3 cm above the dentate line: 4 x 3 x 2 mm. Embedded on edge to show both muscle layers.
L2, rectosigmoid: 5 x 3 x 2 mm. Embedded on edge to show both muscle layers.
L3, mid sigmoid: 5 x 3 x 2 mm. Embedded on edge to show both muscle layers.
L4, descending-sigmoid junction: 5 x 4 x 2 mm. Embedded on edge to show both muscle layers.
L5, distal descending colon, full thickness: 6 x 4 x 3 mm. Embedded on edge to show both muscle layers.

exampleGross.sections: FS1-FS5: entirely frozen; residual tissue fixed in formalin after frozen section and processed as A1-A5 (three levels each); calretinin on A1-A5; Hu C/D on A3.

diagnoses.name: Hirschsprung Disease, Transanal Endorectal Pull-through Resection

micro.text: The distal segment (0-8 cm) is aganglionic in both submucosal and myenteric plexuses, with hypertrophic extrinsic nerve trunks (up to 80 µm) in the submucosa and between the muscle layers. Calretinin-positive mucosal fibrils are absent.

At 10 cm (calibre change) there is partial circumferential aganglionosis: myenteric ganglia are sparse and present over only part of the circumference, submucosal ganglia are rare, and nerves measure about 45 µm. At 12 cm ganglia are present but mildly reduced, with nerves of 40-45 µm. Together these are transition-zone features over about 4 cm.

From 14 cm, and in all four quadrants of the proximal margin ring, ganglion cells are present at normal density in both plexuses. Submucosal nerves are less than 40 µm and calretinin fibrils are present. The dilated proximal mucosa shows mild focal cryptitis without ulceration (mild enterocolitis). The table below maps the findings.
Mapping of Sections (H&E and Calretinin):
A1 distal margin (0 cm): Submucosal ganglia: Absent; Myenteric ganglia: Absent; Nerves (max diameter): Hypertrophic (80 µm); Calretinin: Negative.
A2-A4 (2, 4, 6 cm): Submucosal ganglia: Absent; Myenteric ganglia: Absent; Nerves (max diameter): Hypertrophic (60-80 µm); Calretinin: Negative.
A5 (8 cm): Submucosal ganglia: Absent; Myenteric ganglia: Absent; Nerves (max diameter): Hypertrophic (55 µm); Calretinin: Negative.
A6 (10 cm), calibre change: Submucosal ganglia: Rare; Myenteric ganglia: Sparse, partial circumference; Nerves (max diameter): Hypertrophic (45 µm); Calretinin: Patchy.
A7 (12 cm): Submucosal ganglia: Present, reduced; Myenteric ganglia: Present, mildly reduced; Nerves (max diameter): 40-45 µm; Calretinin: Positive.
A8 (14 cm): Submucosal ganglia: Present; Myenteric ganglia: Present, normal density; Nerves (max diameter): Less than 40 µm; Calretinin: Positive.

A9-A12 proximal margin ring, 4 quadrants (17 cm): Submucosal ganglia: Present in all quadrants; Myenteric ganglia: Present in all quadrants, normal density; Nerves (max diameter): Less than 40 µm; Calretinin: Positive.

finalDiagnosis.label: Rectosigmoid colon, transanal endorectal pull-through:
finalDiagnosis.text: Hirschsprung disease, short (rectosigmoid) segment: aganglionic segment at least 8 cm (from the distal margin to 8 cm), with hypertrophic nerves and absent calretinin innervation; transition zone at 10-12 cm (partial circumferential aganglionosis, hypoganglionosis, nerve hypertrophy). Proximal margin (circumferential, 4 quadrants): ganglion cells present in both plexuses at normal density, no hypertrophic nerves, calretinin positive, i.e. normally ganglionated. Mild enterocolitis in the dilated segment.

comment.text: The proximal margin meets the criteria for normal innervation. Ganglion cells are present around the entire circumference of the myenteric and submucosal plexuses, at normal density, with no submucosal nerve hypertrophy (40 µm or more). This makes a transition-zone pull-through unlikely. Mapping showed an asymmetric transition zone (partial circumferential aganglionosis at 10 cm), which is why the margin must be assessed circumferentially.

The aganglionic length is given as at least 8 cm because the distal end lies about 1 cm above the dentate line, within the physiological hypoganglionic zone. If obstructive symptoms persist after surgery, these margin findings and repeat rectal biopsies should be reviewed (ERNICA 2020).

containers.text: Received an orientated segment of rectum and sigmoid colon, 17 cm long, with a short mucosal cuff at the distal (transanal) end. The distal 9 cm is narrow (circumference 3.5 cm), with a cone-shaped calibre change at 9-12 cm to a dilated proximal segment (circumference 7 cm at 15 cm). The wall is thickened proximally (up to 4 mm). The mucosa is congested proximally with no ulceration. No perforation. The serosa shows levelling biopsy sites at about 8 and 13 cm. Mapping: a longitudinal strip was taken from the distal margin to the proximal end, with sections every 2 cm and an additional section at the calibre change. The proximal margin was taken as a complete circumferential ring and submitted in four quadrants (inked 12, 3, 6 and 9 o'clock).

exampleGross.sections: A1 distal margin; A2-A8 longitudinal strip at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (calibre change), 12 and 14 cm; A9-A12 proximal margin ring, quadrants 12, 3, 6, 9 o'clock; A13 dilated proximal mucosa (enterocolitis). Three levels each; calretinin on A1, A6, A7, A9-A12.

micro.text: Ganglion cells are absent from the submucosal and myenteric plexuses throughout the rectum, colon, caecum and appendix. Unlike rectosigmoid disease, the nerve trunks are not hypertrophic (less than 40 µm). Calretinin-immunoreactive fibrils are absent. Hu C/D confirms the absence of neurons.

The terminal ileum 5 cm from the ileocaecal valve shows sparse, small myenteric ganglia, absent submucosal ganglia, occasional 40-45 µm nerves and reduced calretinin, consistent with transition zone. From 15 cm, and in all four quadrants of the ileal margin, the ileum is normally ganglionated in both plexuses. The right colon shows healed enterocolitis-related changes. The table below maps the findings.
Mapping of Sections (H&E, Calretinin, Hu C/D):
Rectum (distal margin): Ganglion cells (submucosal / myenteric): Absent / absent; Nerves: Not hypertrophic (less than 40 µm); Calretinin: Negative.
Sigmoid, descending, transverse, ascending colon (2 sections each): Ganglion cells (submucosal / myenteric): Absent / absent; Nerves: Not hypertrophic; Calretinin: Negative.
Caecum: Ganglion cells (submucosal / myenteric): Absent / absent; Nerves: Not hypertrophic; Calretinin: Negative.
Appendix: Ganglion cells (submucosal / myenteric): Absent / absent; Nerves: Not hypertrophic; Calretinin: Negative.
Terminal ileum, 5 cm from ileocaecal valve: Ganglion cells (submucosal / myenteric): Absent / sparse, small ganglia; Nerves: Occasional 40-45 µm; Calretinin: Reduced (transition zone).
Ileum, 15 cm (prior levelling stoma site): Ganglion cells (submucosal / myenteric): Present / present, normal density; Nerves: Normal; Calretinin: Positive.
Ileal proximal margin ring (20 cm), 4 quadrants: Ganglion cells (submucosal / myenteric): Present / present, all quadrants; Nerves: Normal; Calretinin: Positive.

finalDiagnosis.label: Colon, appendix and terminal ileum, total colectomy (ileoanal pull-through):
finalDiagnosis.text: Total colonic aganglionosis: no ganglion cells in rectum, entire colon, caecum and appendix, without nerve hypertrophy and with absent calretinin innervation; extension into the terminal ileum as a transition zone (about 5 cm). Ileal proximal margin normally ganglionated (all quadrants). Healed enterocolitis changes in the right colon.

comment.text: Total colonic aganglionosis often lacks the hypertrophic extrinsic nerves of rectosigmoid disease, and AChE histochemistry can be falsely negative. Calretinin (and Hu C/D) are therefore important, as they were on the diagnostic rectal biopsy. An aganglionic appendix is a useful intraoperative clue. Transition zone in the terminal ileum is common, so the margin was assessed circumferentially.

The ileal margin is normally ganglionated. Total colonic aganglionosis carries a higher risk of enterocolitis and fluid or nutritional problems after pull-through, and a higher familial recurrence risk; genetic counselling is advised.

containers.text: Received a total colectomy specimen with the rectum and 20 cm of terminal ileum, and the appendix attached. The colon is 38 cm long, uniformly narrow and unused (circumference 2.5-3 cm), with no calibre change. The terminal ileum is dilated proximally (circumference 5 cm at 15-20 cm). The appendix is 5 cm long. The mucosa is unremarkable apart from flattened folds in the right colon. Serosal sites of previous biopsies are noted.

exampleGross.sections: A1 distal margin (rectum); A2-A9 sigmoid, descending, transverse and ascending colon (2 each); A10 caecum; A11 appendix; A12-A14 terminal ileum at 5, 10 and 15 cm; A15-A18 ileal proximal margin ring in 4 quadrants. Three levels each; calretinin on all blocks; Hu C/D on A9, A10 and A12.

micro.text: Sections show gallbladder wall with a markedly oedematous and congested lamina propria and muscularis. The mucosa shows erosions and ulcers covered by fibrin and neutrophils, with reactive atypia of the regenerating epithelium at the ulcer margins. A dense neutrophilic infiltrate is present in the mucosa, muscularis and perimuscular connective tissue, with microabscess formation in the wall. The lumen contains neutrophils, fibrin and cellular debris (suppurative exudate). The serosa and subserosa show oedema, dilated congested vessels and a fibrinopurulent exudate (fibrinopurulent serositis).

There is no transmural necrosis, vascular thrombosis, gas or haemorrhage. Background chronic changes are minimal. Dysplasia and malignancy are not seen. The cystic duct margin shows mild acute inflammation without dysplasia.

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Acute suppurative calculous cholecystitis (acute cholecystitis with empyema) with cholelithiasis. No dysplasia or malignancy identified.

comment.text: No gangrenous change is seen. Bile culture sensitivity correlation is suggested.

containers.text: Received a gallbladder measuring 10 x 5 x 3.5 cm, with a cystic duct stump 1.2 cm long. The gallbladder is tense. The serosa is congested and dull, with patchy yellow-white fibrinous exudate and loose adhesions. On opening, about 40 mL of turbid yellow-green purulent fluid escapes. One calculus 1.6 cm in diameter is impacted in the neck, and 6 further faceted yellow-green calculi measuring 0.5 to 1.2 cm are present in the lumen. The wall is thickened to 0.6 cm. The mucosa is hyperaemic with patchy ulceration. There is no perforation, necrosis, polyp or mass lesion.

exampleGross.sections: A1 cystic duct margin; A2 fundus; A3 body; A4 neck; A5-A6 ulcerated areas (6 cassettes). Not entirely submitted; no thickened or suspicious area apart from the ulcerated mucosa.

micro.text: Sections show gallbladder wall with patchy coagulative necrosis and sloughing of the mucosa (ischaemic change) with haemorrhage. The lamina propria and muscularis are oedematous and congested. Fibrin thrombi are seen in small vessels of the wall. Neutrophils are sparse to moderate and are mainly seen at the margins of the necrotic areas and in the lumen; the inflammatory response is less prominent than the degree of mucosal necrosis. There is no transmural necrosis.

There is no significant chronic inflammation, fibrosis, Rokitansky-Aschoff sinus formation or metaplasia. No viral inclusions, parasites or organisms are seen. Dysplasia and malignancy are not seen. The cystic duct margin shows mild congestion.
Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry:
CMV immunohistochemistry: Result: Negative; Interpretation: No cytomegalovirus infection.
PAS / GMS: Result: No organisms; Interpretation: No fungal infection.

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Acute acalculous cholecystitis with ischaemic mucosal necrosis (no gallstones). No dysplasia or malignancy identified.

comment.text: The picture is consistent with ischaemic injury in a critically ill patient. No gangrenous transformation is seen.

containers.text: Received a distended gallbladder measuring 12 x 5 x 4 cm, with a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosa is congested with patchy dusky areas. The lumen contains about 30 mL of thick dark green sludge-like bile. No calculi are present. The wall is 0.5 cm thick. The mucosa shows patchy dark red-brown discolouration with focal necrosis. There is no perforation, polyp or mass lesion.

exampleGross.sections: A1 cystic duct margin; A2 fundus; A3 body; A4 neck; A5 necrotic mucosa (5 cassettes).

micro.text: Sections show a gallbladder wall with a chronic inflammatory infiltrate of lymphocytes and plasma cells, subepithelial and perimuscular fibrosis, muscular hypertrophy and Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses extending into the perimuscular tissue. Focal pyloric metaplasia is present.

Superimposed on this are features of acute injury: oedema and congestion of the lamina propria and muscularis, a focal mucosal erosion covered by fibrin and neutrophils, and neutrophils infiltrating the lamina propria, muscularis and several Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses. The serosa shows fibrinopurulent exudate. There is no transmural necrosis or vascular thrombosis. Dysplasia and malignancy are not seen. The cystic duct margin shows mild chronic inflammation.

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Acute on chronic calculous cholecystitis with cholelithiasis. No dysplasia or malignancy identified.

containers.text: Received a gallbladder measuring 9 x 4 x 3 cm, with a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosa is congested with fibrinous exudate and dense adhesions. The wall is thickened to 0.7 cm. The lumen contains turbid, non-purulent bile and 9 mixed calculi, the largest 1.4 cm, with one calculus in the neck. The mucosa is hyperaemic with a small focus of erosion. There is no necrosis, perforation, polyp or mass lesion.

exampleGross.sections: A1 cystic duct margin; A2 fundus; A3 body; A4 neck; A5 area of erosion (5 cassettes).

micro.text: Sections show gallbladder wall with extensive full-thickness (transmural) coagulative necrosis, with ghost outlines of the muscle bundles and loss of nuclear staining. Haemorrhage is present throughout the wall, and the mucosa is largely sloughed. Fibrin thrombi are seen in small vessels of the wall and subserosa. A rim of neutrophils lies at the junction with the viable tissue, and bacterial colonies are seen within the necrotic areas. At the perforation site the wall is replaced by a full-thickness defect covered with fibrinopurulent exudate and acute inflammation.

Viable tissue in the neck shows oedema, congestion and a dense neutrophilic infiltrate with mild background chronic inflammation. The cystic duct margin is viable with mild acute inflammation. Dysplasia and malignancy are not seen in the viable mucosa; assessment of the epithelium is limited in the necrotic areas.

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Acute gangrenous cholecystitis with transmural necrosis, vascular thrombosis and fundal perforation, with cholelithiasis. No malignancy identified.

comment.text: Epithelial assessment is limited in the necrotic areas. Culture correlation and clinical follow-up for peritoneal or liver bed collections are suggested.

containers.text: Received a gallbladder measuring 11 x 5.5 x 4 cm with attached omentum, and a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosa is green-black and friable over the fundus and body, covered with fibrinopurulent exudate. A 1 cm perforation with ragged edges is present in the fundus. The lumen contains dark turbid bile and 3 calculi, the largest 1.8 cm. The wall is thickened to 0.8 cm. The mucosa is dusky green-black with extensive sloughing, and the neck is relatively preserved. No polyp or mass lesion is identified.

exampleGross.sections: A1 cystic duct margin; A2-A3 perforation edge; A4-A5 fundus; A6-A7 body; A8 neck (8 cassettes). Additional sections from the necrotic areas.

micro.text: Sections show gallbladder wall with numerous round to oval empty spaces (gas bubbles) in the lamina propria, muscularis and subserosa, some lined by compressed histiocytes and neutrophils. There is extensive coagulative necrosis of the mucosa and wall, haemorrhage and oedema, with fibrin thrombi in the wall vessels. Neutrophils are seen at the edge of viable tissue. Clusters of large Gram-positive bacilli are seen in the necrotic areas and around the gas spaces.

There is no perforation. Background chronic inflammation and fibrosis are minimal. Dysplasia and malignancy are not seen in the viable epithelium. The cystic duct margin shows acute inflammation with no necrosis.
Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry:
Gram stain: Result: Gram-positive bacilli in necrotic tissue; Interpretation: Large bacilli compatible with Clostridium species.
PAS / GMS: Result: No fungal organisms; Interpretation: -.

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Acute emphysematous cholecystitis with gangrenous change (acalculous). Gram-positive bacilli identified in tissue. No dysplasia or malignancy identified.

comment.text: Emphysematous cholecystitis is usually diagnosed radiologically; the histology confirms an acute, ischaemic and gas-containing wall. Correlation with culture results and early antibiotic therapy is advised.

containers.text: Received a distended, crepitant gallbladder measuring 9 x 5 x 4 cm, with a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosa is dusky with fibrinous exudate. On incision, gas escapes and about 20 mL of thin brown foul-smelling bile with sludge is present. No calculi are found. The wall is 0.5 cm thick and shows multiple pinhead to 0.4 cm gas-filled spaces giving a honeycomb appearance on the cut surface. The mucosa is dusky green-black with patchy necrosis. No perforation, polyp or mass is identified.

exampleGross.sections: A1 cystic duct margin; A2 fundus; A3 body; A4 neck; A5-A6 necrotic mucosa (6 cassettes).

micro.text: Sections show gallbladder wall with mucosa lined by columnar epithelium with focal flattening. Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses extend into the muscularis propria and perimuscular connective tissue. The lamina propria and muscular wall show a chronic inflammatory infiltrate of lymphocytes and plasma cells with scattered eosinophils, along with subepithelial and perimuscular fibrosis and muscular hypertrophy. Focal pyloric (gastric antral type) metaplasia and a small focus of intestinal metaplasia with goblet cells are present.
There is no significant neutrophilic infiltrate, necrosis, granuloma, dysplasia or malignancy. The cystic duct margin shows no significant inflammation.

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Chronic calculous cholecystitis with cholelithiasis. Focal pyloric and intestinal metaplasia. No dysplasia or malignancy identified.

containers.text: Received a gallbladder measuring 8 x 3.5 x 2.5 cm, with a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosal surface is dull and fibrotic, with focal adhesions. The wall is thickened, measuring up to 0.5 cm. On opening, the lumen contains 14 faceted yellow-green calculi, the largest measuring 1.3 cm, and dark green bile. The mucosa is flattened and focally velvety. There is no ulcer, polyp or mass lesion.

exampleGross.sections: A1 cystic duct margin; A2 fundus; A3 body; A4 neck (one cassette each). Entire wall not submitted; no thickened or suspicious area identified.

micro.text: Sections show gallbladder wall lined by columnar epithelium of normal height. The lamina propria shows a mild increase in lymphocytes and plasma cells with mild subepithelial fibrosis. A few shallow Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses are seen within the muscularis propria. Muscle thickness is within normal limits to mildly increased.
There are no neutrophils, prominent eosinophils, lymphoid follicles, granulomas, foamy macrophages, metaplasia, dysplasia or malignancy. The cystic duct margin is unremarkable.

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Mild chronic acalculous cholecystitis (no gallstones). No dysplasia or malignancy identified.

comment.text: The histological changes are mild and non-specific, and are compatible with the clinical diagnosis of functional gallbladder disorder.

containers.text: Received a gallbladder measuring 7 x 2.5 x 2 cm, with a cystic duct stump 0.8 cm long. The serosa is smooth and glistening. The wall measures 0.2 cm. The lumen contains about 8 mL of thin green bile. No calculi, sludge, polyp or mass lesion is present. The mucosa is green and velvety.

exampleGross.sections: A1 cystic duct margin; A2 fundus; A3 body; A4 neck (one cassette each). Not entirely submitted; no thickened or suspicious area identified.

micro.text: Sections show gallbladder wall with a chronic inflammatory infiltrate that includes numerous well-defined lymphoid follicles with reactive germinal centres in the lamina propria and extending into the muscularis. The germinal centres show polarisation, tingible-body macrophages and surrounding mantle zones. Interfollicular areas contain small lymphocytes and plasma cells. There is mild subepithelial and perimuscular fibrosis and a few Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses.

There is no lymphoepithelial lesion, no destructive sheets of monotonous lymphoid cells, no neutrophilic infiltrate, granuloma, dysplasia or malignancy. The cystic duct margin shows no significant inflammation.
Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry:
CD20 / CD3: Result: B cells in follicles; T cells interfollicular; Interpretation: Normal compartmentalisation.
CD10 / BCL6: Result: Positive in germinal centres; Interpretation: Reactive germinal centres.
BCL2: Result: Negative in germinal centres; positive in mantle zones and T cells; Interpretation: No follicular lymphoma pattern.
Ki-67: Result: High, polarised in germinal centres; Interpretation: Reactive.
Kappa / lambda (in situ hybridisation): Result: Polytypic plasma cells; Interpretation: No light-chain restriction.
IgG4: Result: Fewer than 10 positive cells per HPF; Interpretation: IgG4-related disease not supported.

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Chronic follicular cholecystitis (reactive lymphoid hyperplasia) with cholelithiasis. No evidence of lymphoma, dysplasia or malignancy.

comment.text: Immunohistochemistry supports a reactive follicular process; extranodal marginal zone lymphoma is not supported.

containers.text: Received a gallbladder measuring 7.5 x 3 x 2 cm, with a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosa is smooth with few adhesions. The wall is 0.3 cm thick. The lumen contains 3 yellow faceted calculi measuring 0.6 to 0.9 cm and green bile. The mucosa is velvety with fine granularity and tiny pale nodules measuring up to 0.1 cm. There is no ulcer, polyp or mass lesion.

exampleGross.sections: A1 cystic duct margin; A2 fundus; A3 body; A4 neck (one cassette each). Entire wall not submitted; no thickened or suspicious area identified.

micro.text: Sections show gallbladder wall with a dense transmural infiltrate involving the lamina propria, muscularis propria and perimuscular connective tissue. The infiltrate is composed predominantly of eosinophils, which account for more than 90% of the inflammatory cells, with more than 100 eosinophils per high-power field in multiple fields. Occasional intra-epithelial eosinophils and focal degranulation are seen. Lymphocytes are few and plasma cells are rare. The wall is oedematous with mild fibrosis.
There are no neutrophilic abscesses, necrosis, granulomas, vasculitis, parasites, ova or larvae. Dysplasia and malignancy are not seen. The cystic duct margin shows a few eosinophils only.
Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry:
PAS / GMS: Result: No organisms; Interpretation: No fungal infection.
Review of H&E sections: Result: No parasites or ova; Interpretation: Parasitic cause not found.

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Eosinophilic cholecystitis (acalculous), with transmural eosinophil-rich infiltrate exceeding 90% of the inflammatory cells. No parasites, dysplasia or malignancy identified.

comment.text: Correlation with allergic history, drug history and repeat peripheral eosinophil count is suggested. Systemic causes such as hypereosinophilic syndrome and eosinophilic gastroenteritis should be considered if eosinophilia persists.

containers.text: Received a gallbladder measuring 8 x 3 x 2.5 cm, with a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosa is dull. The wall is thickened to 0.6 cm and the cut surface is grey-white. The lumen contains dark green bile; no calculi are present. The mucosa is red-tan and velvety. There is no ulcer, polyp or mass lesion.

exampleGross.sections: A1 cystic duct margin; A2 fundus; A3 body; A4 neck (one cassette each). Entire wall not submitted; no thickened or suspicious area identified.

micro.text: Sections show gallbladder wall with extensive nodular and sheet-like collections of foamy (lipid-laden) histiocytes, accompanied by multinucleated giant cells, including Touton-type cells, and cholesterol clefts. Golden-brown bile and ceroid pigment are seen within macrophages and in the stroma. Scattered neutrophils, lymphocytes and plasma cells are present. There is dense fibrosis. The mucosa is focally ulcerated, and ruptured Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses with extravasated bile and mucin are seen. The process extends through the muscularis into the perimuscular tissue and adherent omentum.

No atypical glands, desmoplastic stroma, perineural or lymphovascular invasion is seen. No dysplasia or malignancy is identified in any of the 14 sections. The cystic duct margin shows chronic inflammation without xanthogranulomatous change or dysplasia.
Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry:
CD68: Result: Positive in foamy cells; Interpretation: Histiocytic nature.
Pan-cytokeratin: Result: Negative in foamy cells; entrapped benign glands only; Interpretation: No carcinoma.
PAS / von Kossa: Result: No Michaelis-Gutmann bodies; Interpretation: Malakoplakia excluded.
Ziehl-Neelsen (AFB): Result: Negative; Interpretation: No mycobacteria.
IgG4: Result: Fewer than 10 positive cells per HPF; Interpretation: IgG4-related disease not supported.

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis with cholelithiasis. No dysplasia or malignancy identified in the entire gallbladder.

comment.text: Xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis can mimic carcinoma clinically and radiologically. The whole gallbladder was submitted and no carcinoma is identified.

containers.text: Received a gallbladder measuring 9 x 4.5 x 3.5 cm, with a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosa is fibrotic with dense adhesions. The wall is markedly and diffusely thickened, up to 1.2 cm. The cut surface shows yellow-tan nodules up to 0.7 cm and bands within a grey-white fibrotic wall, with focal mucosal ulceration. The lumen contains 7 calculi, the largest 1.4 cm, and dark bile with sludge. No discrete mass lesion or polyp is identified.

exampleGross.sections: Entire gallbladder submitted in view of the marked thickening and clinical suspicion of malignancy: A1 cystic duct margin; A2-A4 fundus; A5-A9 body; A10-A12 neck; A13-A14 adherent omental tissue (14 cassettes).

micro.text: Sections show gallbladder wall with multiple confluent epithelioid granulomas with Langhans-type multinucleated giant cells and central caseous necrosis in the lamina propria, muscularis propria and subserosa. The granulomas are surrounded by lymphocytes and plasma cells, and there is focal mucosal ulceration and fibrosis. Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses are present. The adherent omentum shows similar granulomas.

Ziehl-Neelsen stain shows occasional acid-fast bacilli within the necrotic areas. There are no fungal organisms, ova or foreign material. There is no dysplasia or malignancy. The cystic duct margin shows chronic inflammation without granulomas.
Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry:
Ziehl-Neelsen (AFB): Result: Positive, occasional bacilli (1+); Interpretation: Mycobacterial infection.
PAS / GMS: Result: Negative; Interpretation: No fungal organisms.
Pan-cytokeratin: Result: Entrapped benign glands only; Interpretation: No carcinoma.

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Granulomatous (caseating) cholecystitis, consistent with tuberculosis (acid-fast bacilli positive), with cholelithiasis. Omental involvement present. No dysplasia or malignancy identified.

comment.text: Tissue TB PCR/culture and evaluation for other sites of abdominal tuberculosis are advised, with clinical correlation for anti-tubercular therapy.

containers.text: Received a gallbladder measuring 7 x 3 x 2.5 cm with attached omentum, and a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosa is congested with adhesions. The wall is thickened to 0.9 cm, with grey-white to yellowish areas and foci of soft cheesy (caseous) material. The mucosa shows a focal ulcer 0.6 cm in diameter. The lumen contains 2 calculi, the largest 0.8 cm, and bile. No discrete mass lesion is identified.

exampleGross.sections: A1 cystic duct margin; A2-A3 fundus; A4-A5 body; A6 neck; A7 ulcer; A8 omentum (8 cassettes).

micro.text: Sections show gallbladder wall with a dense transmural lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with scattered eosinophils and lymphoid follicles. There is storiform fibrosis in the muscularis and perimuscular connective tissue. Obliterative phlebitis is seen, with veins showing luminal obliteration by lymphoplasmacytic inflammation, highlighted by an elastic stain. The mucosa is preserved.

There are no significant neutrophils, granulomas or necrosis. There is no cytological atypia, dysplasia, infiltrating glands or perineural invasion. The cystic duct margin shows mild chronic inflammation with a few IgG4-positive plasma cells.
Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry:
IgG4: Result: Up to 62 positive plasma cells per HPF (hot-spot); Interpretation: Meets the count criterion (more than 10 per HPF).
IgG: Result: Positive in plasma cells; Interpretation: -.
IgG4 / IgG ratio: Result: About 55%; Interpretation: Meets the ratio criterion (more than 40%).
Elastic stain (EVG): Result: Obliterated veins; Interpretation: Obliterative phlebitis.
Pan-cytokeratin: Result: No infiltrating epithelium; Interpretation: No carcinoma.

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: IgG4-related cholecystitis (IgG4-related sclerosing cholecystitis). No dysplasia or malignancy identified in the entire gallbladder.

comment.text: The morphology together with the IgG4 count and ratio meets the pathological criteria for IgG4-related disease and is consistent with the clinical history of autoimmune pancreatitis and elevated serum IgG4. Correlation with imaging of the pancreas and bile ducts is suggested.

containers.text: Received a gallbladder measuring 8 x 3.5 x 3 cm, with a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosa is smooth. The wall is diffusely thickened to 0.8 cm, with a localised area in the body measuring 1.5 cm in thickness. The cut surface of the thickened wall is grey-white, firm and rubbery. The mucosa is smooth and intact. The lumen contains bile only; no calculi, ulcer, polyp or mass lesion is identified.

exampleGross.sections: Entire gallbladder submitted in view of the localised thickening and clinical suspicion of malignancy: A1 cystic duct margin; A2-A3 fundus; A4-A8 body including the thickened area; A9-A11 neck (11 cassettes).

micro.text: Sections show gallbladder wall with expanded villous tips and mucosal folds, in which the lamina propria is filled by aggregates of foamy (lipid-laden) macrophages beneath intact columnar epithelium. The epithelium shows mild lipid vacuolation. The inflammatory infiltrate is minimal, with only a few scattered lymphocytes. The muscularis propria is of normal thickness and there is no fibrosis, neutrophilic infiltrate, Rokitansky-Aschoff sinus proliferation or metaplasia.
There is no dysplasia or malignancy. The cystic duct margin is unremarkable.
Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry:
CD68: Result: Positive in foamy cells; Interpretation: Macrophages confirmed.
Pan-cytokeratin: Result: Positive in epithelium only, negative in foamy cells; Interpretation: Not epithelial.

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Cholesterolosis of the gallbladder (non-inflammatory; no cholecystitis) with cholelithiasis. No dysplasia or malignancy identified.

comment.text: Cholesterolosis is an incidental or associated lipid deposition and should not be reported as cholecystitis in the absence of significant inflammation. Symptoms are attributed to the gallstones.

containers.text: Received a gallbladder measuring 8 x 3 x 2.2 cm, with a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosa is smooth and glistening. The wall is thin, measuring 0.2 cm. The lumen contains 5 yellow calculi, the largest 0.9 cm, and green bile. The mucosa is bright red-green and velvety with numerous fine yellow flecks and streaks giving a "strawberry" appearance. There is no ulcer, polyp or mass lesion.

exampleGross.sections: A1 cystic duct margin; A2 fundus; A3 body; A4 neck (one cassette each). Entire wall not submitted; no thickened or suspicious area identified.

micro.text: Sections show extrahepatic bile duct mucosa with a flat and focally micropapillary epithelial lesion. The nuclei are elongated, mildly enlarged and hyperchromatic, with pseudostratification confined to the lower two-thirds of the epithelium. Nuclear polarity is preserved, and surface maturation is retained. Mitoses are rare and basal. There is no marked pleomorphism, no cribriform architecture, and no loss of polarity.

The peribiliary glands are involved by the same low-grade epithelial change. The gland contours remain rounded, a basement membrane is retained, and there is no desmoplastic stromal reaction. No invasive carcinoma is identified.

The background duct shows chronic cholangitis, with a lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate in the wall, fibrosis and pyloric gland metaplasia. The proximal margin is involved by low-grade biliary intraepithelial neoplasia. The distal margin is uninvolved. No high-grade biliary intraepithelial neoplasia is seen.

finalDiagnosis.text: Extrahepatic bile duct, segmental excision: Low-grade biliary intraepithelial neoplasia (BilIN, low grade), arising in chronic cholangitis. Proximal margin involved by low-grade BilIN. Distal margin negative. No high-grade BilIN or invasive carcinoma identified.

comment.text: Biliary intraepithelial neoplasia is a flat, non-invasive precursor of cholangiocarcinoma. In the current two-tier World Health Organization system it is graded as low grade or high grade. Low-grade BilIN corresponds to the former BilIN-1, and shows mild nuclear enlargement, hyperchromasia and pseudostratification with preserved polarity. High-grade BilIN, equivalent to carcinoma in situ, shows loss of polarity, marked nuclear atypia, frequent or atypical mitoses, and complex micropapillary or cribriform growth.

Reactive atypia in active cholangitis can mimic low-grade BilIN. Reactive nuclei are usually more uniform, with surface maturation, prominent nucleoli and an acute inflammatory background, and the change is limited to eroded or inflamed epithelium. The lesion here is more extensive than the inflammation and has the elongated hyperchromatic nuclei of low-grade BilIN.

Involvement of peribiliary glands by BilIN should not be reported as invasion when the glands retain smooth contours and a basement membrane and there is no desmoplasia. Low-grade BilIN at a resection margin is recorded, but it is not equivalent to a high-grade or carcinoma-in-situ margin. Clinical and imaging correlation is advised.

containers.text: Received a segment of extrahepatic bile duct measuring 3.5 cm in length and 0.8 cm in external diameter. The serosa is dull. The wall is thickened, measuring up to 0.3 cm. The mucosa is granular and focally flattened, without a polyp, ulcerated mass or papillary tumour. The proximal and distal margins are inked.

exampleGross.sections: The specimen is entirely submitted, including the proximal and distal margins en face and representative transverse sections of the intervening duct.

micro.text: Sections show biliary mucosa replaced by a flat, micropapillary and focally cribriform epithelial proliferation. The nuclei are markedly enlarged, hyperchromatic and pleomorphic, with irregular membranes and loss of polarity. Nuclei extend to the luminal surface. Mitoses are frequent, including atypical forms in the upper epithelium. Adjacent mucosa shows low-grade biliary intraepithelial neoplasia.

Peribiliary glands are colonized by the same high-grade epithelium. The involved glands retain smooth rounded contours and a basement membrane, and there is no desmoplastic stromal reaction, irregular angulated infiltration, or single-cell invasion. No invasive adenocarcinoma is identified in the submitted tissue.

The left hepatic duct margin is involved by high-grade biliary intraepithelial neoplasia. The right hepatic duct margin and the distal common hepatic duct margin are negative for high-grade BilIN and carcinoma. The wall shows chronic cholangitis and fibrosis.

finalDiagnosis.text: Biliary confluence and common hepatic duct, excision: High-grade biliary intraepithelial neoplasia (BilIN, high grade; carcinoma in situ), with adjacent low-grade BilIN, arising in chronic cholangitis. Left hepatic duct margin involved by high-grade BilIN. Right hepatic duct and distal margins negative. No invasive carcinoma identified.

comment.text: High-grade biliary intraepithelial neoplasia is the flat carcinoma-in-situ end of the BilIN spectrum in the current two-tier World Health Organization system, corresponding to former BilIN-3. It is distinguished from low-grade BilIN by loss of nuclear polarity, marked pleomorphism, mitoses high in the epithelium, and complex micropapillary or cribriform architecture. A two-tier diagnosis is preferred; intermediate (former BilIN-2) changes with loss of polarity are included in the high-grade category.

Colonization of peribiliary glands by high-grade BilIN is not invasion when gland contours remain smooth, a basement membrane is retained, and there is no desmoplasia. True invasion shows irregular angulated glands, single cells, or a stromal response. Deeper levels were examined and no invasion is seen in this sample. Because high-grade BilIN often coexists with an invasive carcinoma nearby, correlation with imaging and complete sampling of any residual stricture are advised.

High-grade BilIN at the left hepatic duct margin is a positive carcinoma-in-situ margin and is reported separately from low-grade involvement. Immunohistochemistry is not required for the diagnosis. Clinical and surgical correlation is advised.

containers.text: Received the biliary confluence with segments of the common hepatic duct and the origins of the right and left hepatic ducts, measuring 2.8 cm in length. The wall is firm and thickened, up to 0.4 cm. The mucosa is granular and finely papillary, without an ulcerated mass. The proximal right and left duct margins and the distal common hepatic duct margin are inked in separate colours.

exampleGross.sections: The specimen is entirely submitted, with the three margins en face and transverse sections of the confluence.

micro.text: Sections show a well-circumscribed polypoid mass with a lobular, pushing base. It is composed of closely packed, back-to-back pyloric-type glands lined by cuboidal to columnar cells with pale, foamy mucinous cytoplasm and small, round, basal nuclei with mild atypia. The surface shows a thin layer of foveolar-type epithelium with focal short papillary infoldings. Mitoses are rare and there is no necrosis. Architectural complexity is limited, with no cribriform or solid growth and no marked nuclear pleomorphism; overall cytoarchitectural atypia is low-grade. The stroma shows scattered chronic inflammatory cells and focal intestinal metaplasia. No glands infiltrate the muscular layer; glands in Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses are bland and lack a desmoplastic reaction. The background shows chronic cholecystitis with no flat dysplasia. The cystic duct margin is uninvolved.
Immunohistochemistry:
MUC6: Diffuse strong positive
MUC5AC: Positive (surface and superficial glands)
MUC2: Negative
CDX2: Negative
CK7: Positive
p53: Wild-type pattern (patchy weak to moderate)
Beta-catenin: Membranous (nuclear in <5% of cells)
Ki-67: About 3 to 5%

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Intracholecystic papillary neoplasm (ICPN), gastric subtype (pyloric gland type; formerly 'pyloric gland adenoma'), LOW-GRADE, fundus, 2.1 cm. No invasive carcinoma identified (entire gallbladder submitted). Cystic duct margin negative. Chronic cholecystitis.

comment.text: In the WHO 6th edition, pyloric gland adenoma is regarded as the gastric subtype of ICPN and mass-forming precursor lesions are graded low-grade or high-grade. Because these neoplasms may harbour foci of high-grade change or invasion, the entire gallbladder was submitted; none is seen. Clinical correlation is advised.

containers.text: Received an unopened gallbladder measuring 8 x 3 x 2.5 cm with a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosa is smooth and glistening. On opening, the fundic mucosa shows a short-stalked polypoid mass measuring 2.1 x 1.6 x 1.2 cm with a lobulated, finely granular surface. The cut surface is tan-white and glistening with a pushing base; the underlying wall is not thickened. The remaining mucosa is green and velvety. Wall thickness is 0.2 cm. No calculi or other polyps.

exampleGross.sections: Entire gallbladder submitted. A1: cystic duct margin (en face). A2: neck. A3 to A8: polyp serially sectioned in toto with underlying wall. A9: base of polyp. A10 to A14: remaining body and fundus, including a fundus-to-neck transmural strip. Total 14 cassettes.

micro.text: Sections show a tubulovillous to villous polyp lined by tall columnar cells with elongated, pencillate, stratified, hyperchromatic nuclei, a moderate amount of eosinophilic cytoplasm and admixed goblet cells. Nuclear atypia is mild to moderate, with preserved polarity and rare mitoses; there is no cribriform architecture, necrosis or marked pleomorphism. By the two-tier system these features qualify as low-grade (combining the former low and intermediate grades). The stalk contains thin fibrovascular and smooth muscle fibres without invasive glands. The adjacent mucosa shows intestinal metaplasia and mild chronic cholecystitis; no flat dysplasia is seen. The cystic duct margin is uninvolved.
Immunohistochemistry:
MUC2: Positive (goblet cells)
CDX2: Positive (diffuse nuclear)
CK20: Positive
CK7: Focal positive
MUC1: Negative
MUC5AC: Focal positive
p53: Wild-type pattern
Ki-67: About 8 to 10%

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Intracholecystic papillary neoplasm (ICPN), intestinal subtype, LOW-GRADE, body, 1.6 cm. No invasive carcinoma identified (entire gallbladder submitted). Cystic duct margin negative. Intestinal metaplasia with mild chronic cholecystitis.

comment.text: The intestinal subtype shows an intestinal phenotype (MUC2, CDX2, CK20). The entire gallbladder was submitted and examined for high-grade change and invasive carcinoma, which are not identified.

containers.text: Received an unopened gallbladder measuring 7.5 x 3 x 2.5 cm with a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosa is smooth. On opening, the body shows a villous, pedunculated tan-pink mass measuring 1.6 x 1.3 x 1.0 cm on a 0.5 cm stalk. The wall is 0.25 cm thick. The remaining mucosa is velvety. No calculi.

exampleGross.sections: Entire gallbladder submitted. A1: cystic duct margin (en face). A2 to A5: polyp with stalk, serially sectioned in toto. A6: base. A7 to A11: remaining neck, body and fundus including a fundus-to-neck transmural strip. Total 11 cassettes.

micro.text: Sections show a papillary neoplasm with delicate, branching fibrovascular cores lined by a single to focally pseudostratified layer of cuboidal to columnar cells with scant to moderate amphophilic to eosinophilic cytoplasm and little intracellular mucin. Nuclei are round to oval with mild to moderate enlargement, finely granular chromatin and inconspicuous nucleoli; polarity is largely preserved. Mitoses are infrequent and there is no necrosis. Complex fusion of papillae, cribriform architecture and marked pleomorphism are absent, and the lesion is graded as low-grade. The base is broad and pushing, and no invasion into the lamina propria or muscular layer is seen. Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses are present with bland epithelium. The cystic duct margin is uninvolved. Background shows chronic cholecystitis and cholelithiasis.
Immunohistochemistry:
MUC1: Positive (apical, luminal)
MUC5AC: Positive
MUC6: Focal positive
MUC2: Negative
CDX2: Negative
CK7: Positive
CK20: Negative
p53: Wild-type pattern
Ki-67: About 5 to 8%

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Intracholecystic papillary neoplasm (ICPN), pancreatobiliary subtype, LOW-GRADE, neck-body junction, 1.8 cm. No invasive carcinoma identified (entire gallbladder submitted). Cystic duct margin negative. Chronic cholecystitis with cholelithiasis.

comment.text: Entire submission of the gallbladder was performed to exclude high-grade areas and invasive carcinoma, as the pancreatobiliary subtype carries a higher risk of progression than the gastric subtype. None is found. Clinical correlation is advised.

containers.text: Received an unopened gallbladder measuring 8.5 x 3 x 2.5 cm with a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosa is smooth. On opening, the neck-body junction shows a papillary, friable, tan-pink mass measuring 1.8 x 1.5 x 1.0 cm attached by a broad base. The surrounding wall is 0.3 cm thick. Two cholesterol calculi, 0.4 cm each, are present. The remaining mucosa is velvety green.

exampleGross.sections: Entire gallbladder submitted. A1: cystic duct margin (en face). A2 to A7: mass with underlying wall, serially sectioned in toto. A8 to A13: remaining neck, body and fundus, including a fundus-to-neck transmural strip. Total 13 cassettes.

micro.text: Sections show a polypoid neoplasm composed predominantly of pyloric-type glands, back-to-back and focally fused, lined by cuboidal to columnar cells with mucinous cytoplasm. Most of the lesion shows low-grade cytoarchitectural atypia. A distinct area in the central and basal parts of the mass shows complex architecture with cribriform and fused glands, loss of nuclear polarity, nuclear enlargement and pleomorphism, vesicular chromatin, prominent nucleoli and a higher nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio. Mitoses number up to 6 per 10 high-power fields, including atypical forms. Focal intraluminal necrotic debris is present. The neoplasm is graded as high-grade. The lesion is sharply demarcated from the underlying lamina propria and muscular layer; no desmoplastic stromal reaction, single-cell infiltration or invasion beyond the basement membrane is seen after examination of the entire gallbladder. Background shows chronic cholecystitis. The cystic duct margin is free of neoplasia.
Immunohistochemistry:
MUC6: Diffuse positive
MUC5AC: Positive
MUC2: Negative
CDX2: Negative
CK7: Positive
p53: Overexpression (strong, >80% of nuclei) in the high-grade area
Beta-catenin: Nuclear in a subset of cells
Ki-67: About 25 to 30% in the high-grade area

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Intracholecystic papillary neoplasm (ICPN), gastric subtype (pyloric gland type), HIGH-GRADE (focal), body, 2.6 cm. No invasive carcinoma identified (entire gallbladder submitted). Cystic duct margin negative for high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia. Chronic cholecystitis.

comment.text: The overall neoplasm is graded by its highest-grade area (two-tier WHO 6th edition grading). Complete submission of the gallbladder was undertaken to exclude associated invasive carcinoma, and none is identified. As a high-grade ICPN can be accompanied by invasion in unsampled areas, thorough clinical follow-up is advised.

containers.text: Received an unopened gallbladder measuring 9 x 3.5 x 3 cm with a cystic duct stump 1.2 cm long. The serosa is smooth. On opening, the body shows a broad-based polypoid mass measuring 2.6 x 2.2 x 1.5 cm with a nodular, mucoid surface. The cut surface is tan-grey and glistening with small cystic spaces. The base appears well defined and the wall beneath is 0.3 cm thick. The remaining mucosa is velvety. No calculi.

exampleGross.sections: Entire gallbladder submitted. A1: cystic duct margin (en face). A2: neck. A3 to A10: mass serially sectioned in toto with underlying wall. A11: base of mass (perpendicular). A12 to A17: remaining fundus, body and neck, including a fundus-to-neck transmural strip. Total 17 cassettes.

micro.text: Sections show a villous and tubulovillous neoplasm with architectural complexity, including cribriform glands and areas of back-to-back growth, lined by stratified columnar cells with intestinal-type differentiation and variable goblet cells. Nuclei are markedly enlarged, hyperchromatic and pleomorphic with vesicular chromatin, prominent nucleoli, loss of polarity and apical mitoses (up to 12 per 10 high-power fields), with intraluminal necrotic debris ('dirty necrosis'). The lesion is high-grade. Mucin pools are focally present within the lumina but no extracellular mucin dissects stroma. Multiple sections of the base show a smooth epithelial-stromal interface; no invasive glands, desmoplasia, lymphovascular or perineural invasion is seen. The cystic duct margin is free of neoplasia. Background shows intestinal metaplasia and chronic cholecystitis.
Immunohistochemistry:
MUC2: Positive
CDX2: Positive (diffuse)
CK20: Positive
CK7: Focal / weak
MUC1: Negative
p53: Overexpression (strong, diffuse nuclear)
Ki-67: About 40%

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Intracholecystic papillary neoplasm (ICPN), intestinal subtype, HIGH-GRADE, fundus and body, 3.8 cm. No invasive carcinoma identified after submission of the entire gallbladder. Cystic duct margin negative for high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia.

comment.text: A large high-grade ICPN carries a significant risk of invasive carcinoma; the entire gallbladder (21 blocks) was examined with additional sections of the base, and invasion is not seen. Clinical follow-up is advised.

containers.text: Received an unopened gallbladder measuring 10 x 4 x 3.5 cm with a cystic duct stump 1.2 cm long. The serosa is smooth. On opening, the fundus and body contain a bulky, villous, tan-pink mass measuring 3.8 x 3.0 x 2.2 cm with a friable surface and focal mucoid areas. The cut surface shows soft fronds without gross necrosis; the base is broad and the wall beneath is 0.4 cm thick with an intact serosa. The remaining mucosa is velvety.

exampleGross.sections: Entire gallbladder submitted. A1: cystic duct margin (en face). A2: neck. A3 to A14: mass serially sectioned in toto with underlying wall, including four perpendicular sections of the base (A11 to A14). A15 to A21: remaining mucosa including a fundus-to-neck transmural strip. Total 21 cassettes.

micro.text: Sections show an exophytic papillary neoplasm with complex, arborizing, fused papillae and focal cribriform areas lined by stratified cuboidal to columnar cells with scant cytoplasm and little mucin. Nuclei are enlarged, hyperchromatic and pleomorphic with irregular contours, prominent nucleoli and loss of polarity; the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio is high. Mitoses are frequent (up to 10 per 10 high-power fields) with atypical forms, and there is focal necrosis in the luminal debris. These features constitute high-grade cytoarchitectural atypia throughout most of the lesion. At the base, epithelium extends into Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses without a desmoplastic reaction. Multiple levels and the entire sampled wall show no stromal invasion beyond the basement membrane, no single cells or irregular infiltrating glands, and no lymphovascular or perineural invasion. The cystic duct margin is free of high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia and flat dysplasia is not identified in the adjacent mucosa.
Immunohistochemistry:
MUC1: Strong positive
MUC5AC: Positive
MUC2: Negative
CDX2: Negative
CK7: Positive
CK20: Focal weak positive
p53: Overexpression (strong, diffuse nuclear)
Ki-67: About 30 to 40%

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Intracholecystic papillary neoplasm (ICPN), pancreatobiliary subtype, HIGH-GRADE, fundus, 3.2 cm. No invasive carcinoma identified after submission of the entire gallbladder. Cystic duct margin negative for high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia.

comment.text: The lesion corresponds to a high-grade ICPN (formerly ICPN with high-grade dysplasia / carcinoma in situ). Because up to two-thirds of ICPNs are associated with invasive carcinoma and invasion may be focal, the entire gallbladder was submitted and no invasion is found. Further levels are recommended if clinical suspicion persists.

containers.text: Received an unopened gallbladder measuring 9 x 4 x 3.5 cm with a cystic duct stump 1.3 cm long. The serosa is smooth with no adhesions. On opening, the fundus shows a friable, papillary, tan-white mass measuring 3.2 x 2.8 x 2.0 cm filling much of the lumen, attached by a broad base. The cut surface shows soft papillary fronds with foci of haemorrhage but no necrosis. The wall at the base appears focally thickened (0.5 cm) but the serosal surface is intact. The remaining mucosa is velvety. No calculi.

exampleGross.sections: Entire gallbladder submitted. A1: cystic duct margin (en face). A2: neck. A3 to A12: mass serially sectioned in toto with underlying wall (A3 to A10) and base, perpendicular to the wall (A11, A12). A13 to A20: remaining fundus and body, including a fundus-to-neck transmural strip. Total 20 cassettes.

micro.text: Sections show an arborizing papillary and nodular neoplasm, with focal complex fusion and cribriform architecture. It is lined by cuboidal to columnar cells with abundant finely granular, deeply eosinophilic (oncocytic) cytoplasm. Nuclei are round with prominent, centrally placed nucleoli. Intraepithelial lumina ('punched-out' spaces) are present and mucin is scanty. The cytology and architecture are high-grade. Mitoses are 4 per 10 high-power fields. There is no tumour necrosis. The neoplasm is sharply demarcated from the underlying wall; no stromal invasion, lymphovascular or perineural invasion is identified after total submission. The cystic duct margin is negative. Background shows mild chronic cholecystitis.
Immunohistochemistry:
MUC6: Positive
MUC5AC: Focal positive
MUC1: Positive
MUC2: Negative
CDX2: Negative
HepPar-1: Positive (granular cytoplasmic)
CK7: Positive
p53: Wild-type pattern
Ki-67: About 15 to 20%

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Intracholecystic papillary neoplasm (ICPN), oncocytic subtype, HIGH-GRADE, body, 2.4 cm. No invasive carcinoma identified (entire gallbladder submitted). Cystic duct margin negative.

comment.text: Oncocytic neoplasms are generally cytologically high-grade (prominent nucleoli) and parallel the intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasm of the pancreas and bile ducts. DNAJB1::PRKACA / PRKACB fusion testing was not performed.

containers.text: Received an unopened gallbladder measuring 8 x 3.5 x 3 cm with a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosa is smooth. On opening, the body shows a soft, mahogany-brown to tan, nodular and papillary mass measuring 2.4 x 2.0 x 1.4 cm on a broad base. The cut surface is homogeneous and fleshy with focal haemorrhage. The wall is 0.3 cm thick. No calculi.

exampleGross.sections: Entire gallbladder submitted. A1: cystic duct margin (en face). A2 to A8: mass serially sectioned in toto with underlying wall. A9 to A15: remaining neck, body and fundus including a fundus-to-neck transmural strip. Total 15 cassettes.

micro.text: Sections show a pedunculated polyp composed of compact, back-to-back small tubular and acinar-like glands of variable complexity with minimal intervening stroma, which shows focal amorphous, amyloid-like hyalinization. The tubules are lined by cuboidal cells with minimal cytoplasm and no significant intracellular mucin. Nuclei are round to oval with open chromatin and single prominent nucleoli, and some show a washed-out appearance. Squamoid morules and small neuroendocrine-type cell clusters are present. The cytoarchitectural complexity qualifies as high-grade, but the lesion is confined to the polyp: there is no invasion at the stalk or the underlying gallbladder wall. The background mucosa shows cholesterolosis and no dysplasia. The cystic duct margin is negative.
Immunohistochemistry:
MUC6: Diffuse positive
MUC5AC: Negative
MUC2: Negative
CDX2: Negative
CK7: Positive
Beta-catenin: Nuclear positivity in squamoid morules
p53: Wild-type pattern
Ki-67: About 10 to 15%

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder, cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Intracholecystic tubular neoplasm (ICTN), HIGH-GRADE, non-invasive, fundus, 1.6 cm. No invasive carcinoma identified (entire gallbladder submitted). Cystic duct margin negative. Cholesterolosis.

comment.text: ICTN is the second subcategory of intracholecystic neoplasm in the WHO 6th edition (with ICPN). ICTN is tubular, non-mucinous and MUC6-positive, usually arises in gallbladders with cholesterolosis, and is cytoarchitecturally high-grade but rarely invasive. The entire gallbladder was submitted and no invasion is found.

containers.text: Received an unopened gallbladder measuring 8 x 3 x 2.5 cm with a cystic duct stump 1 cm long. The serosa is smooth. On opening, the fundus shows a loosely attached, pedunculated, cauliflower-like tan-yellow polyp measuring 1.6 x 1.3 x 1.2 cm on a thin stalk 0.3 cm in diameter. The mucosa shows a yellow stippled (cholesterolosis) pattern. The wall is 0.2 cm thick. No calculi.

exampleGross.sections: Entire gallbladder submitted. A1: cystic duct margin (en face). A2 to A5: polyp with stalk, serially sectioned in toto. A6: stalk base with underlying wall. A7 to A12: remaining mucosa including a fundus-to-neck transmural strip. Total 12 cassettes.

micro.text: Sections show an intracholecystic papillary neoplasm (ICPN), pancreatobiliary subtype, with complex papillae lined by cuboidal cells showing marked nuclear atypia, loss of polarity and frequent mitoses — high-grade by two-tier WHO 6th edition grading. At the base, invasive adenocarcinoma of biliary type extends through muscularis into perimuscular connective tissue on the hepatic side (largest invasive focus 1.6 cm; two smaller foci 0.4 and 0.3 cm; aggregate 2.3 cm; invasive ~40% of gross tumour). No liver invasion; serosa intact. LVI present; PNI not identified. Margins free (cystic duct 3.8 cm; hepatic 1.1 cm). One of eight nodes positive (6 mm deposit). Adjacent mucosa: intestinal metaplasia.
Immunohistochemistry:
CK7: Positive (diffuse)
MUC1: Positive
CK20: Negative
CDX2: Negative
MUC2: Negative
MUC5AC: Focal positive in ICPN
p53: Aberrant (overexpression) in high-grade ICPN and invasive component
Ki-67: About 45% in invasive component
MMR proteins (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6): Intact nuclear expression

finalDiagnosis.label: Gallbladder with liver wedge and portal lymph nodes, radical cholecystectomy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Intracholecystic papillary neoplasm (ICPN), pancreatobiliary subtype, HIGH-GRADE, 4.0 cm, with associated invasive adenocarcinoma, biliary type, G2 (largest focus 1.6 cm; aggregate 2.3 cm), invading perimuscular connective tissue on the hepatic side (pT2b), with LVI. Margins negative. Metastatic carcinoma in 1 of 8 nodes. pT2b pN1, stage IIIB (AJCC 8th edition).

comment.text: Per WHO 6th edition (2026), mass-forming intracholecystic neoplasms are ICPN or ICTN with two-tier (low/high) grading. CAP requires reporting size of largest invasive focus, aggregate size, and/or percentage invasion when invasion is associated with ICPN. The deepest invasive focus determines pT.

micro.text: Sections show an exophytic papillary neoplasm with complex, fused papillae and cribriform areas lined by stratified cuboidal to columnar cells, with marked nuclear atypia, prominent nucleoli, loss of polarity, frequent mitoses and focal necrosis, representing a high-grade intracholecystic papillary neoplasm. The cystic duct margin shows no neoplasia and the nearest invasive focus is 6.0 cm from it. The cystic duct lymph node contains no metastatic tumour.

MUC5AC: Positive
CK7: Positive
MUC2 / CDX2: Negative
p53: Overexpression (strong, diffuse nuclear)

micro.text: Sections show an invasive adenocarcinoma composed of irregular, infiltrating glands, small tubules and cords lined by cuboidal to columnar cells with moderate nuclear pleomorphism, vesicular chromatin, prominent nucleoli and mucin-poor eosinophilic cytoplasm, embedded in a desmoplastic stroma. Three of nine regional lymph nodes show metastatic adenocarcinoma, the largest deposit measuring 7 mm, with no extranodal extension.
