A4–A8 tumour, including a full-face section with the tunica (A4) and with the rete testis / hilar soft tissue (A5), with tumour-normal interfaces (A6–A8). A9 epididymis. A10–A11 background testis away from the tumour. Tumour submitted at about 1 block per cm of greatest dimension, plus additional sections.

diagnoses.name: Reactive Fibroinflammatory Biliary Stricture, Common Hepatic Duct (SpyGlass Cholangioscopic Biopsy)

micro.text: Sections at three levels show:

Fragments: Five small, partly crushed fragments of biliary mucosa and fibrous stroma. Surface biliary epithelium is present in three fragments, focally eroded. Bile pigment and a little fibrinous debris on the surface.

Surface epithelium: A single layer of cuboidal to columnar biliary epithelium with mild reactive changes: slight nuclear enlargement, small regular nucleoli, and preserved polarity and nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio. No papillary or micropapillary architecture, no stratification to the luminal surface and no marked pleomorphism. No high-grade biliary intraepithelial neoplasia (BilIN).

Peribiliary glands: Scattered small peribiliary glands in a lobular arrangement around a central duct, with mild reactive nuclear enlargement and preserved polarity. No haphazard, infiltrative or single-cell glands, no incomplete glands, and no glands next to thick-walled vessels or within nerves. No prominent nucleoli and no intraluminal necrotic debris. No perineural invasion.

Stroma: Cellular fibro-inflammatory stroma with lymphocytes, plasma cells and occasional neutrophils and eosinophils. No storiform fibrosis, no obliterative phlebitis and no onion-skin periductal fibrosis in the sampled tissue (limited by fragment size).
Other: Crush artefact limits assessment of part of the tissue. No granulomas. No stone fragments or foreign material.
Immunohistochemistry (Illustrative):
p53: Wild-type pattern (scattered nuclei of variable intensity)
SMAD4 (DPC4): Nuclear expression retained in epithelium
IgG4: Under 10 IgG4-positive plasma cells per HPF (maximum 6 per HPF)
IgG: IgG4/IgG plasma cell ratio under 40% (about 15%)

finalDiagnosis.label: A. Common hepatic duct stricture, cholangioscopy-guided (SpyGlass) biopsies:
finalDiagnosis.text: Fibro-inflammatory tissue with reactive atypia of peribiliary glands. Negative for high-grade dysplasia (high-grade BilIN) or carcinoma.

comment.text: Sampling: SpyBite biopsies are small and superficial, and a desmoplastic cholangiocarcinoma may be mostly subepithelial. A negative biopsy does not exclude cholangiocarcinoma.
IHC: wild-type p53 and retained SMAD4 support a reactive process. Normal results do not exclude malignancy, because many cholangiocarcinomas show neither aberration.

Correlation: please correlate with brush cytology and FISH (if done), CA 19-9 after biliary decompression, cross-sectional imaging and EUS (with fine-needle aspiration or biopsy if a mass or wall thickening is targetable). Repeat sampling or close follow-up is recommended if clinical suspicion stays high.
Differential diagnosis of a benign-appearing stricture:
1. Primary sclerosing cholangitis: correlate with cholangiographic pattern and inflammatory bowel disease history. Onion-skin fibrosis is not seen in this limited material.

2. IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis: not supported here (IgG4 counts and ratio low, serum IgG4 normal). Note that biopsies are often non-diagnostic for this condition, so correlate with other organ involvement, such as autoimmune pancreatitis.
3. Stone- or stent-related injury: likely contributory given the recent plastic stent and prior gallstone disease. Stent injury can cause erosion and marked reactive atypia, a recognised pitfall.
Terminology follows the WHO Classification of Digestive System Tumours (BilIN two-tier grading). Illustrative sample report.

containers.text: Biliary stricture biopsies (common hepatic duct, SpyGlass cholangioscopy): Received in formalin: 5 tiny tan-white fragments, 0.1 to 0.2 cm each, aggregate 0.5 x 0.3 x 0.1 cm.

exampleGross.sections: A1 filtered through biopsy paper, wrapped (entirely embedded). Three H&E levels cut, with intervening unstained spare sections kept for ancillary studies.

diagnoses.name: Cystic Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumour, WHO Grade 1, Pancreatic Tail (EUS-FNB)

micro.text: Sections show:
Adequacy: Several intact core fragments with lesional tissue, total lesional area about 6 mm² (counted for mitoses), with blood clot and a little benign gastric-type contaminant (needle tract).
Architecture: Nests, trabeculae, cords and occasional rosettes of tumour cells in hyalinised fibrous stroma. In places the stroma lines the cyst wall.

Tumour cells: Small, uniform cells with moderate amphophilic to finely granular cytoplasm and round to oval nuclei with stippled, salt-and-pepper chromatin and inconspicuous nucleoli. No significant pleomorphism.
Necrosis: Not identified.
Mitoses: Fewer than 2 per 2 mm² (1 mitosis in about 6 mm² of evaluable tumour).

Negative findings: No mucinous or columnar epithelial lining and no ovarian-type stroma (against mucinous cystic neoplasm). No pseudopapillae, hyaline globules or foam cells (against solid pseudopapillary neoplasm). No acinar formations with granular apical cytoplasm (against acinar cell carcinoma). No clear-cell cuboidal serous lining (against serous cystadenoma).
Immunohistochemistry (Illustrative):
Synaptophysin: Diffuse strong positive
Chromogranin A: Positive (granular cytoplasmic)
INSM1: Diffuse nuclear positive
Pancytokeratin AE1/AE3: Positive (dot-like / cytoplasmic)
Ki-67 (MIB-1): About 2% (hotspot count, about 500 cells), WHO grade 1 range
β-catenin: Membranous only, no nuclear staining (against SPN)
CD10: Negative (against SPN)
E-cadherin: Retained membranous (against SPN)
Trypsin: Negative (against acinar cell carcinoma)
BCL10: Negative (against acinar cell carcinoma)

finalDiagnosis.label: A. Pancreatic tail cystic lesion, EUS-guided fine-needle biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumour, WHO grade 1 (Ki-67 about 2%; mitoses fewer than 2 per 2 mm²), consistent with a cystic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour.

comment.text: Grading: grading follows the WHO 5th edition (G1: Ki-67 below 3% and mitoses below 2 per 2 mm²; the higher of the two determines grade). Ki-67 can be heterogeneous in neuroendocrine tumours, and small biopsies may miss hotspots, so the grade on biopsy may be underestimated. Definitive grading and staging should be done on the resection specimen.
Differential diagnosis:
1. Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm: excluded by membranous-only β-catenin, retained E-cadherin and negative CD10. Note that SPN can show focal synaptophysin.
2. Acinar cell carcinoma: excluded by negative trypsin and BCL10. Acinar tumours may show focal neuroendocrine marker expression.
3. Serous cystadenoma: no glycogen-rich cuboidal lining.
4. Mucinous cyst (mucinous cystic neoplasm / IPMN): no mucinous epithelium or ovarian-type stroma.

Correlation: please correlate with cyst fluid analysis and imaging. Cystic neuroendocrine tumours typically have low cyst fluid CEA and a hypervascular rim. Somatostatin receptor imaging (for example 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT) is suggested for staging and receptor status. Consider MEN1 or VHL assessment if clinically indicated.
Illustrative sample report.

containers.text: Pancreatic tail lesion, EUS-FNB: Received in formalin: multiple tan-white, threadlike core fragments and clotted blood, aggregate 1.5 x 0.6 x 0.2 cm, with the longest core 0.8 cm.

exampleGross.sections: A1–A2 cores filtered and wrapped (entirely embedded). H&E levels cut, with unstained spare sections kept for immunohistochemistry.

diagnoses.name: Tuberculoid Leprosy (Ridley-Jopling TT), Left Forearm (Punch Biopsy)

micro.text: Sections show skin with the following features:
Epidermis: Mildly atrophic, with focal basal layer damage where granulomas abut it.

Granulomas: Well-formed, compact epithelioid cell granulomas with Langhans-type multinucleated giant cells and a dense peripheral cuff of lymphocytes. They involve the superficial and deep dermis in an elongated, linear distribution along neurovascular bundles and around eccrine glands, hair follicles and arrector pili muscles.
Grenz zone: Absent. The granulomas extend up to the dermo-epidermal junction and erode the basal layer.
Nerves: Dermal nerve twigs are infiltrated and partly destroyed by granulomas and lymphocytes. Several small nerves cannot be identified, and S100 shows fragmented nerve remnants within granulomas.
Necrosis: No caseation. Focal tiny fibrinoid foci only. No foamy macrophages (no lepromatous features).
Other: No interface dermatitis, no mucin and no foreign material on polarised light. No vasculitis.
Special Stains / Immunohistochemistry:
Fite-Faraco (modified acid-fast): No acid-fast bacilli identified in granulomas or nerves after a careful search (bacterial index, BI, 0)
Ziehl-Neelsen: No acid-fast bacilli
S100: Highlights fragmented, infiltrated dermal nerve twigs within granulomas
PAS / GMS: No fungal organisms

finalDiagnosis.label: A. Skin, left forearm, punch biopsy:
finalDiagnosis.text: Granulomatous dermatitis with nerve destruction, consistent with tuberculoid leprosy (Ridley-Jopling TT). Fite-Faraco negative for acid-fast bacilli (BI 0).

comment.text: Classification: TT is favoured over borderline tuberculoid (BT), for these reasons:
a) There is no grenz zone; granulomas reach and erode the epidermis.
b) The granulomas are compact, with a dense lymphocyte mantle.
c) Dermal nerves are destroyed.
d) No bacilli are found.
e) There is a single well-defined anaesthetic plaque.

BT usually shows a narrow grenz zone, less dense lymphocytes, swollen but identifiable nerves, occasional bacilli (BI 0 to 2) and several lesions clinically. The TT/BT distinction can be subtle, so clinical correlation is essential.

Ridley-Jopling vs WHO: the Ridley-Jopling spectrum (TT, BT, BB, BL, LL, plus indeterminate) is a clinicopathological classification that helps predict reactions. The WHO operational classification for treatment is clinical: paucibacillary (PB, 1 to 5 skin lesions with no bacilli on slit-skin smear) or multibacillary (MB, more than 5 lesions, nerve involvement criteria, or a positive smear). Final PB/MB assignment and treatment rest with the clinician. Slit-skin smear examination (BI and morphological index) is recommended to complete classification.
Differential diagnosis:
1. Sarcoidosis: naked granulomas with sparse lymphocytes, not nerve-centred, and no nerve destruction.
2. Cutaneous tuberculosis (lupus vulgaris / tuberculosis verrucosa cutis): caseation may be present, with no neurotropism. Consider culture or PCR if clinically indicated.
3. Granuloma annulare: palisading histiocytes around mucin and degenerated collagen, without well-formed epithelioid granulomas or nerve destruction.
4. Other: tertiary syphilis, deep fungal infection and leishmaniasis are considered less likely given the negative stains and the morphology.
Absence of bacilli on tissue staining does not exclude leprosy; TT is typically paucibacillary. Illustrative sample report.

containers.text: Skin punch biopsy, left forearm: A cylindrical skin punch biopsy, 4 mm in diameter and 0.6 cm deep, with a pale skin surface.

exampleGross.sections: A1 bisected longitudinally (entirely embedded). Levels cut, with spare unstained sections kept for Fite-Faraco staining.

diagnoses.name: Backwash Ileitis with Chronic Active Ulcerative Colitis, Terminal Ileum and Caecum (Colonoscopic Biopsies)

micro.text: A – Terminal ileum: Ileal mucosa from the distal terminal ileum with mild, diffuse and continuous active inflammation across all fragments. There is mild villous blunting (villus:crypt ratio about 2:1) and focal neutrophilic cryptitis without crypt abscesses. The lamina propria shows a mixed infiltrate of lymphocytes, plasma cells, eosinophils and scattered neutrophils. No granulomas on levels. No pyloric gland (ulcer-associated) metaplasia. No patchy (skip) involvement within the sampled fragments. No erosions, aphthous or deep fissuring ulcers. No viral inclusions. No dysplasia.

B – Caecum and ascending colon: Chronic active colitis. Architectural distortion includes branched, shortened and irregularly spaced crypts, with mild crypt atrophy and a villiform surface. There is diffuse transmucosal lymphoplasmacytosis with basal plasmacytosis, and focal Paneth cell metaplasia (abnormal in the ascending colon). Neutrophils in the lamina propria, with cryptitis in fewer than 50% of crypts. Occasional crypt abscesses. No erosion or ulceration. No granulomas, no CMV inclusions and no dysplasia.
Interpretation: Colonic disease is diffuse and continuous with the ileal changes, which are mild and limited to the distal ileum.

micro.label: Synoptic Report (Ulcerative Colitis Activity: Nancy Index And Geboes Score):
Site graded:
micro.text: B – Caecum and ascending colon.

micro.label: Chronicity / architecture:
micro.text: Architectural distortion present (moderate). Basal plasmacytosis present.

micro.label: Geboes grade 0: structural / architectural change:
micro.text: 0.2 (mild to moderate diffuse or multifocal abnormalities).

micro.label: Geboes grade 1: chronic inflammatory infiltrate:
micro.text: 1.2 (moderate increase).

micro.label: Geboes grade 2A: lamina propria eosinophils:
micro.text: 2A.1 (mild increase).

micro.label: Geboes grade 2B: lamina propria neutrophils:
micro.text: 2B.1 (mild increase).

micro.label: Geboes grade 3: neutrophils in epithelium:
micro.text: 3.2 (fewer than 50% of crypts involved).

micro.label: Geboes grade 4: crypt destruction:
micro.text: 4.2 (probable; occasional crypt abscesses).

micro.label: Geboes grade 5: erosion or ulceration:
micro.text: 5.0 (none).

micro.label: Geboes score (highest grade):
micro.text: Grade 4.2: active colitis.

micro.label: Nancy index:
micro.text: Grade 2: mild acute inflammatory cell infiltrate, no ulceration (moderate to severe chronic infiltrate).

micro.label: Overall histological activity:
micro.text: Mild to moderate active disease. Not in histological remission.

micro.label: Terminal ileum (A), not graded by these indices:
micro.text: Mild active ileitis in continuity with caecal disease (backwash pattern). No granulomas.

micro.label: Dysplasia:
micro.text: Not identified (negative for dysplasia).

micro.label: Note:
micro.text: Nancy index and Geboes score were developed for colorectal mucosa. Ileal changes are described, not scored.

finalDiagnosis.label: A. Terminal ileum, biopsies:
finalDiagnosis.text: Mild active ileitis with villous blunting, in continuity with caecal disease, consistent with backwash ileitis in the setting of ulcerative colitis. No granulomas. Negative for dysplasia.

finalDiagnosis.label: B. Caecum and ascending colon, biopsies:
finalDiagnosis.text: Chronic active colitis with architectural distortion, consistent with known ulcerative colitis (pancolitis). Moderate activity (Geboes 4.2; Nancy index 2). No granulomas. Negative for dysplasia.

comment.text: Backwash ileitis vs Crohn disease: these ileal changes support backwash ileitis, for these reasons:
a) They are mild, diffuse and continuous.
b) They are confined to the distal few centimetres.
c) They are in continuity with active caecal colitis in a patient with pancolitis.
d) The ileocaecal valve is patulous.
e) There are no granulomas, pyloric gland metaplasia, skip lesions or deep fissuring or aphthous ulcers.

Features favouring Crohn ileitis would include the following: patchy or skip involvement, aphthous or deep fissuring ulcers, pyloric gland metaplasia (chronicity), non-crypt-related epithelioid granulomas, and involvement out of proportion to caecal disease or with a normal caecum. Correlate with endoscopy, cross-sectional imaging (MR enterography if doubt persists) and the disease pattern.
NSAID-related injury: this can cause ileal erosions, ulcers and diaphragm-like strictures, often with increased epithelial apoptosis. The medication history should be reviewed.

Infection: infectious ileitis (for example Yersinia, Campylobacter, Salmonella, CMV and tuberculosis) can mimic or complicate UC. Stool studies are negative here. Consider further testing (for example CMV IHC on any ulcerated tissue) if clinically indicated.
Activity: the Nancy index and Geboes score describe histological activity in the colorectum. Histological remission is an emerging treatment target in ulcerative colitis. Illustrative sample report.

containers.text: Terminal ileum: Received in formalin: 3 tan mucosal fragments, 0.2 to 0.4 cm each. Oriented on filter paper.
Caecum and ascending colon: Received in formalin: 4 tan mucosal fragments, 0.2 to 0.5 cm each. Oriented on filter paper.

exampleGross.sections: A1 terminal ileum (entirely embedded); B1 caecum and ascending colon (entirely embedded). Levels cut on both blocks.

diagnoses.name: Endometrioid Carcinoma of Endometrium, FIGO Grade 2, pT1a pN0, FIGO 2023 IA2 (Total Hysterectomy)

micro.text: Sections from the endometrial tumour show an endometrioid adenocarcinoma composed of crowded, back-to-back and cribriform glands lined by stratified columnar cells with oval nuclei, moderate atypia and occasional nucleoli. Solid non-squamous growth forms about 20% of the tumour (FIGO grade 2; low grade in the WHO two-tier scheme). Foci of squamous morular differentiation are present and are excluded from the solid component. Mitoses are readily seen. No serous, clear cell or high-grade nuclear features.

The tumour invades the inner myometrium to a depth of 0.6 cm out of a 1.6 cm wall (about 38%, less than 50%), with an infiltrative glandular pattern and desmoplastic stroma. Lymphovascular space invasion is focal (a single vessel involved near the invasive front). Lower uterine segment shows surface involvement only. Cervical stroma is free of tumour. Uterine serosa is free.
Background endometrium is atrophic. Fallopian tubes and ovaries were not submitted and cannot be assessed.
Fourteen pelvic lymph nodes (right 0/7, left 0/7) show reactive changes and no metastatic carcinoma.
Immunohistochemistry:
ER: Result: Positive (strong, 90%); Interpretation: Supports endometrioid type.
PR: Result: Positive (moderate, 70%); Interpretation: Supports endometrioid type.
p53: Result: Wild-type (variable, heterogeneous); Interpretation: No TP53 aberration.
p16: Result: Patchy, non-block; Interpretation: Against serous carcinoma and HPV-associated endocervical adenocarcinoma.
Vimentin: Result: Positive; Interpretation: Favours endometrial over endocervical origin.
MLH1 / PMS2: Result: Retained; Interpretation: MMR proficient.
MSH2 / MSH6: Result: Retained; Interpretation: MMR proficient.
POLE: Result: Not tested; Interpretation: Sequencing not performed.

finalDiagnosis.text: Uterus with cervix (total hysterectomy) and bilateral pelvic lymph nodes:
- Endometrioid carcinoma of the endometrium, FIGO grade 2 (low grade), 3.2 cm.
- Myometrial invasion less than 50% (about 38%); focal lymphovascular space invasion.
- Cervical stroma and uterine serosa free of tumour. Adnexa not submitted.
- Fourteen pelvic lymph nodes negative for metastasis (0/14).
- MMR proficient, p53 wild-type, POLE not tested: NSMP. ER and PR positive.
- pT1a pN0; FIGO 2023 stage IA2.

comment.text: Low-grade endometrioid histology, less than half myometrial invasion and only focal LVSI place this tumour in FIGO 2023 stage IA2. Substantial LVSI (5 or more vessels) would have upstaged it to IIB, so the focal extent is specifically recorded. The ER/PR-positive, vimentin-positive, patchy p16 and wild-type p53 profile supports endometrioid carcinoma over serous carcinoma, HPV-associated endocervical adenocarcinoma and metastatic colorectal carcinoma. Tubes and ovaries were not received, so adnexal involvement (which would make the tumour stage IIIA) cannot be excluded pathologically; the stage assumes clinically and radiologically normal adnexa.

The molecular class is reported as NSMP on immunohistochemistry. Because POLE was not sequenced, a POLE-mutant tumour cannot be excluded; POLE testing may be considered if it would alter adjuvant therapy. MMR proficiency makes Lynch syndrome unlikely. Correlation in the gynae-oncology tumour board is advised.
